30 Years in 15 Microfilms 

For our fifth microfilm, we’re on the cusp of a prolific new psytrance era as the scene continues to gather pace into the new millennium. In Boom news, we’re dancing in Herdade do Zambujal one last time: 8,500 Boomers and a brand new convention area to feed our minds. But when one door closes, another one opens. What’s next?

Boom Festival is celebrating 30 years on planet Earth in 2027 – but how did it all begin? Come with us on a journey through time, space and Portugal to discover the depths of our psychedelic roots, and relive pivotal moments in our history along the way.

These 15 microfilms, soundtracked by an emblematic collection of music, explore the festival’s expansive odyssey across eras and oceans in search of a transformative new psychedelic experience. Featuring decades of vibrant archival footage, the series captures Boom’s cultural impact and the global community that has grown around the festival, offering a unique window into its past, present and future.

Annie Trevillian is an independent artist and designer with strong technical skills and experience in textiles design and printing including digital technologies.⁠

She has worked as a community artist, educator, freelance designer and practitioner. She taught in the ANU Textiles Workshop from 1992 – 2011. She has long been associated with Megalo Print Studio and Gallery as an access user, community project artist and board member.⁠
.⁠
Since 2010 her commissioned work allows her to explore new technologies in collaboration with other designers. Commissions include Sydney Harbour YHA, Australian National University, ACT Health and the Legislative Assembly of the ACT.⁠
.⁠
More recently Trevillian has collaborated with screenprinter Alex Lundy to produce a variety of screenprinted products including childrenswear and fabric lengths. She continues to draw and paint and immerse herself in digital design producing Canberra Cloths inspired by her love of Canberra nature. ⁠

Trevillian is represented in the National Gallery of Australia, ArtsACT, Canberra Museum and Gallery, Legislative Assembly of the ACT, National Library of Australia and State Libraries, Megalo Archive, RACV Print Collection and private collections in Australia and overseas.⁠

MEET THE MEMBER | Rosalie Rose @rosalie_rose__ | Maker Member of Craft + Design Canberra⁠
.⁠
Rosalie Rose is a textile artist. Her creative life prioritises the processes of slow stitching and botanical dyeing, creating large handstitched artworks, talismans, baskets and garments. Rosalie holds stitching and dyeing workshops for children and adults and has both past and forthcoming solo exhibitions of her slow stitched pieces.⁠
.⁠
'Creative inspiration arises from nature, from Mother Earth. Natural fibres and fabrics, shells, stones, and plant pigments resonate with me on a creative level, serving as both material and muse.'⁠
.⁠
‘Currently, I am exploring the idea of ‘home’ as both a physical place and an inner sanctuary. By using motifs that conjure shelter and the repetition of hand stitching I am reflecting on feelings of inner alignment, belonging, and connection to nature. This exploration is essentially a coming back to oneself.’⁠
⁠.⁠
'Through the work I create, I seek to establish a connection between material, maker, and viewer where the relationship between the contemporary inner experience and something ancient is honoured.'⁠
.⁠
Rosalie has an upcoming exhibition, earth + sea, with Member Anna Williams @silent.sea.ceramics at Strathnairn Arts @strathnairnarts from 25 August to 20 September 2026.⁠

30 Years in 15 Microfilms 

Boom Festival is celebrating 30 years on planet Earth in 2027 – but how did it all begin? Come with us on a journey through time, space to discover the depths of our psychedelic roots, and relive pivotal moments in our history along the way.

These 15 films, soundtracked by an emblematic collection of music, explore the festival’s expansive odyssey across eras and oceans in search of a transformative new psychedelic experience. Featuring decades of vibrant archival footage, the series captures Boom’s cultural impact and the global community that has grown around the festival, offering a unique window into its past, present and future.

🇵🇹 PT ⚠️ Faltam poucas horas. O PSZAER está em consulta pública apenas até amanhã, 15 de julho ⚠️

O PSZAER define onde se podem instalar novos parques solares e eólicos em Portugal, de forma acelerada, e onde poderão ser licenciados sem Avaliação de Impacte Ambiental.

Foram identificados 7% do território continental, mas ainda não há mapa final: só se saberá que terras serão afectadas, projecto a projecto, quando já não houver como travar.

Participar leva apenas alguns minutos e pode ajudar a garantir que o PSZAER seja revisto antes da sua aprovação.

👉 Usa os códigos QR nas imagens ou os links na bio para participar através do portal Participa.pt.

.

🇬🇧 EN ⚠️ Only hours remain. The PSZAER public consultation closes tomorrow, 15 July ⚠️

The PSZAER defines where new solar and wind farms may be built across Portugal, and where they may be approved without an Environmental Impact Assessment.

7% of mainland Portugal has been identified, but there is still no final map: the land affected will only become clear project by project, when it may already be too late to stop it.

Taking part takes only a few minutes and can help ensure that the PSZAER is revised before it is approved.

👉 Scan the QR codes in the images or use the links in our bio to take part via Participa.pt.

As the new year turns and the emotions settle in the ways they do, I reflect upon many years of music, dance, and celebration. I write to you from just before the official opening of @tropicalfruitsinc where this mix will play in the Sensorium. The Sensorium is a gorgeous sensory down regulatory space created by one of my oldest friends @river.moore.art that has been a place to find space for the body in a festive space that can be incredibly fast and pressured. It’s an honour to contribute my practice towards presence, truth, and rest.

I’ve embraced a lot of silence recently in order to listen and hear more clearly. Listening to my body, observing patterns, and revealing new paths as the seasons of my life change. In this humbling phase I’ve returned to many artists, sounds, and moments that have guided and shaped me off the dance floor.

I invite you to hear your slowness through a folding together of times - guidance out of isolation and despair towards resolve. These sounds are familiar to the bedrock of my soul and I hope they can assist you in your reflections moving into 2026 (or whenever you are journeying).

May you become all you need to be in the seasons to come.
May you be held.

MEET THE MEMBER | Phoebe Porter @phoebe.porter | Accredited Professional Member of Craft + Design Canberra⁠
.⁠
For more than 25 years, Phoebe Porter has developed a distinctive practice spanning studio production, commissioned jewellery and the creation of ambitious new work for exhibition. Strongly influenced by Bauhaus and Constructivist principles, Phoebe’s work explores structure, balance, proportion and materiality. She seeks to reduce each piece to its essential elements, creating jewellery that is sculptural and contemporary while remaining closely connected to the traditions of gold and silversmithing.⁠
.⁠
Since Graduating with a Bachelor of Arts (Gold and Silversmithing) from ANU, Phoebe has exhibited across Australia as well as exhibitions in Japan, Germany, the UK and USA. Her work is highly collectable and is represented in public collections including the National Gallery of Australia @nationalgalleryaus, the Art Gallery of South Australia @agsa.adelaide and the Powerhouse Museum @powerhousemuseum. Her awards include a Victorian Premier’s Design Mark, as well as grants from Creative Australia, Arts Victoria, and Arts ACT.⁠
.⁠
In 2026, Phoebe Porter will be a part of the 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Festival with her exhibition Raw and Refined in the Departures Lounge at Canberra Airport @canberra_airport from 5 to 15 November. As part of the exhibition, there will be an artist talk with Phoebe Porter in conversation with Kevin Murray @kmaustral on from 5:30pm on Thursday 12 November. Phoebe will also be an Undercurrent Design Market Stallholder at Ainslie Arts Centre @ainsliearts from 13 to 15 November. 30 Years in 15 Microfilms 

For our fourth microfilm, we pay a visit to the magical place that held us first: the forest of Herdade do Zambujal. Discover the surprising legacy and its mythical history where many communities have gathered over the decades in nature. In the 1990s, these gatherings were grounded in a love of Goa trance and psychedelic culture. 

Boom Festival is celebrating 30 years on planet Earth in 2027 – but how did it all begin? Come with us on a journey through time, space and Portugal to discover the depths of our psychedelic roots, and relive pivotal moments in our history along the way.

These 15 microfilms, soundtracked by an emblematic collection of music, explore the festival’s expansive odyssey across eras and oceans in search of a transformative new psychedelic experience. Featuring decades of vibrant archival footage, the series captures Boom’s cultural impact and the global community that has grown around the festival, offering a unique window into its past, present and future.

Boom by Bike Initiative: From One Ride to a Movement 🌎

In 2008, two cyclists, Joost and Stan, rode from Belgium to Boom. By 2010, Boom by Bike Initiative became an invitation to reach the festival in a more conscious way. In 2016, the Boom Bike Village gave that journey a home at Boom Festival.

Since then, we have followed the stories of Boomers who choose to arrive on two wheels.

This #FlashbackFriday, we celebrate the 106 cyclists who took part in Boom by Bike Initiative in 2025: over 80,000 kilometres cycled to Boom, and 11.2 tonnes of CO₂e avoided ✨

This week, we also unveil the identity of Boom 2027 – a special edition celebrating 30 years of Boom Festival. As we move towards this milestone, we return to a simple truth: the journey to Boom begins long before the gates open.

By its nature, big-wave surfing is often the epicenter of innovation in our sport. The high speeds, critical conditions and dangerous hazards mean that both athletes and equipment have to be in top form. 
⁠
“There is no limit to big-wave paddle surfing if we just improve the technology behind it” says Kai Lenny. “I think we can go faster, ride bigger waves, take off deeper, get longer barrels and ride smaller boards.”⁠
⁠
He goes on to explain that traditional guns have been relatively unchanged for most of their history – a thin nose, foiled to a thicker mid-section and then a thin tail. However, his craft bucks the trend with an extremely thick nose, a thinner tail and foiled equally all the way through.⁠

Paulo Lopes, the Portuguese DJ who was pivotal to the 1990s psy scene in Portugal, has passed away. 

Born in Portugal, he emigrated to France at an early age, where he studied Economics and History at university. It was there, in the early 1990s, that he connected with the emerging Goa trance scene. 

Due to a genetic condition, he lost his sight as a child, which granted him an extraordinary sensitivity to music. In the mid-1990s, he became a DJ and a major driving force in the Portuguese scene during that decade, as well as in Trancoso, Brazil, where he lived part-time. His sets were always defined by a unique experimentalism. 

Paulo is, and always will be, an example of strength, culture, and an inspiration to many people. 

Obrigado, Paulo. Fly high, irmão.

The Daily Creative Challenge celebrates artistic expression and encourages mindfulness through daily creative practice. This exhibition presents selected works by the award recipients from the 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Daily Creative Challenge.  ABOUT THE CHALLANGE 
The 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Daily Creative Challenge celebrates Canberra as a vibrant centre of creativity while connecting a wider community of makers across Australia and beyond. 
Each July, creatives from around the world respond to a series of daily word prompts, sharing new work via Instagram. Working across ceramics, textiles, photography and mixed media, participants embrace experimentation, process and connection through creativity. 
Now in its fifth year, the 2026 theme Dissent advocates for creativity as a powerful tool for questioning, challenging, and reshaping ourselves and the world around us. 
Over the three week challenge, participants generated thousands of artworks and posts. The result is a diverse and series work that reflects the energy, imagination and collective spirit of the Challenge.

I’ve been working with so many fascinating raw materials for my upcoming exhibition RAW AND REFINED @canberra_airport for @craftdesigncanberrafestival.

The exhibition brings together native Australian gold, copper and uncut sapphires with materials sourced from further afield, including pieces of the Campo del Cielo meteorite from Argentina. Some of the gold has a personal history from my grandfather, a surveyor who worked for a time in Papua New Guinea.

Other materials have been found through fossicking, gem merchants and the Canberra Lapidary Club’s Rock Swap, where I sourced many Australian copper specimens and met people who had fossicked for them across the country. 

I see the beauty in raw materials and appreciate them for their inherent beauty and their imperfections. They also remind me of natural landscapes. There’s something about the specimens that makes you think about these materials being found and collected; they come from natural landscapes that are so beautiful, and the materials become even more valuable because they’re finite.

Images @pew.pew.studio for @artsact and @craft_design_canberra

EXHIBITION CLOSING THIS SATURDAY 24 OCTOBER | HOW WILL THEY KNOW IT’S ME | ZOE BRAND⁠ @zbrandbrand 
.⁠
Plan your visit to see the exhibition before it closes on Saturday 24 October. The Craft + Design Canberra Gallery is open from Wednesday to Saturday from noon to 4pm.⁠
.⁠
HOW WILL THEY KNOW IT'S ME is a new exhibition by artist Zoe Brand that explores the performative nature of jewellery as a device for communication. Using jewellery archetypes, ready mades and text, Zoe collects mundane and throwaway statements from casual conversation, examining their ambiguity and transforming them into objects to be worn.⁠
.⁠
For this exhibition, Zoe draws on homemade banners, sporting pennants, flags and quilts, considering both their forms and cultural and social contexts. These references inform a new series of SOFT TEXT works, developed through quilting techniques and screen printed text. The large scale works are designed to be worn by multiple people, either as a single piece with multiple points of attachment or as separate pieces worn collectively. ⁠
.⁠
Through these works, Zoe continues to explore the ambiguity and slippages of language, transforming everyday statements into physical, wearable objects. By subverting familiar forms and phrasing, HOW WILL THEY KNOW IT'S ME asks how jewellery can communicate, and what happens to meaning when words move from casual conversation onto the body and into public space. ⁠
.⁠

Icons of Cuisine 
These two have been hosting and preparing our VIP Icons of Foam dinner for years. Aaron and Pam Schwartz have now opened a new restaurant/event space in Encinitas. BLANK SLATE 101 (right next to Mark and John at world famous Encinitas Surfboards!) 

In 2019, the couple co-founded Ranch 45 with Brandt Beef co-owner Eric Brandt, giving Solana Beach a top-notch butcher and bottle shop. They left the concept in late 2023/early 2024 and launched their own catering and consulting company—APS Hospitality Group. They’d use a commercial kitchen space, and bring Aron’s signature style of hyper-local, farm-to-table dishes into people’s homes and various venues. Over time, that pack-it-in, pack-it-out process started to make them miss the stability of a stationary kitchen and a one-on-one connection with regular guests and consistent employee interaction.

So the duo are opening Blank Slate in Encinitas, a chef-driven private event space slated for this spring. 

“We are going to be providing a space that’s going to feel like a home,” says Pam. “You can come in and take that stress out of hosting an event at your house and bring it to us.” 

Whether an intimate dinner for six people or reception for 50, Blank Slate will customize the experience from the menu to the linens to lights and flowers—“really create the space to be what you want it to be,” Pam says. They’re still working out the interior design, but the space will fit around 50 people seated with a 12-seat chef’s counter, plus up to 75 people on the patio, and 300 people if they use an outdoor parking lot for large events. 

Reservations Strongly Suggested!

Our hearts are aching here at the Surfing Heritage and Culture Center as we say goodbye to Paul Strauch, our dear friend, longtime supporter, board member, and former Executive Director.
Paul had a smile that lit up every room. He carried himself with style, charm, and grace, and he touched everyone he met with warmth, humor, and generosity. At SHACC, he became a beloved storyteller, educator, and true ambassador of the aloha spirit. He held us spellbound with stories of Tom Blake shaping his first balsa board, of sitting front row with Duke Kahanamoku at a Sammy Davis Jr. concert in Las Vegas, and of asking Buffalo Keaulana to catch his favorite fish, which Buff somehow delivered.
As one of Duke’s students and team riders, Paul honored that lineage in the way he lived. He was among the finest surfers of his era, winning at Makaha and Peru, placing second at the Duke Invitational, and third at the 1965 World Championships. More than results, it was his style during surfing’s great transition that earned him the respect of his peers.
We will miss his electric smile and contagious laugh. We send our deepest sympathy to his family and friends. Thank you for the joy, Paul. Catch a few for us.

Winter at Boomland ❄️ 

This Winter, the Iberian Peninsula was hit by two major storms. Kristin and Leonardo swept across the land with winds reaching 200 km/h, while persistent rain and flooding reshaped the landscape entirely.

At @boomlandofficial, the impact is tangible:

👉 Trees lost and artworks damaged
👉 A solar array destroyed
👉 Rising water levels that left parts of Boomland submerged

The Lake Portal and the Meniroid Stones almost disappeared beneath the water, as rising water levels came close to both the Alchemy Circle and the Dance Temple. Dive into Boomland in January in 📸 1-9.

Despite this, work continues. At the Dance Temple, maintenance of the bamboo structure, designed using biomimetic principles, remains ongoing, while a new canopy is taking shape, to be revealed at @‌beingathering from 1 to 5 July 2026 (📸 10).

But the work extends beyond those areas. New camping swales for short-term staff and new camping zones for Being Gathering are being built. On top of providing additional camping space, swales also improve water retention (📸 11).

At Being Gathering, the first feminine urinal made with hemp at a festival will also be introduced, developed during the Boomland School Natural Building Course in 2025 (📸 12).

The final images show the Green Corridor at the Dance Temple - our new reforestation project designed to create shade, cool the area and increase biodiversity by linking trees, pathways and gardens into a unified ecological landscape. A living corridor that reconnects the ecosystem and brings new life to the heart of the Dance Temple area (📸 13-14). 

You make all of this possible, Boomers. Thank you. ♥️

See you at @beingathering 👉 1-5 July 2026 🌀

🍂 As temperatures rise and landscapes grow drier, nourishing the soil becomes essential, so that this land never turns into desert.

Our commitment is simple: working with nature, never against it. ❤️

Guided by the principles of agroforestry and permaculture, and saying no to chemical fertilisers, we actively regenerate the land for a richer, life-filled ecosystem.

🌱 Continuous care - Regular soil analysis carried out by certified external entities confirms that the land remains free from contamination.

🌿 Minimal disturbance - By avoiding unnecessary soil movement, we protect organic matter - the foundation of long-term fertility and resilience.

♻️ Closing the nutrient loop - Organic compost, safely processed through ecological sanitation systems, is returned to the soil, nourishing it naturally and completing the cycle.

This is the foundation of our long-term ecological path. 🌳

J. Warx @j.warx (Valencia, España)

J. Warx (València, 1994) es un artista plástico que interviene en las calles desde 2013 a través del graffiti. En 2020 comienza a realizar murales que buscan una comunicación directa con quien los observa. Crece en la ciudad de València, donde los solares y casas tapiadas aportan espacios que permiten hacer intervenciones sin la necesidad de un permiso, atendiendo a sus consecuencias.

Sus murales destacan por el tratamiento de temas actuales desde discursos críticos e irónicos, a través de composiciones sencillas en un dibujo acompañado de un texto. 
Desde 2021 forma pareja artística con Os Gat, llevando a cabo intervenciones en Oaxaca (México), Madrid, Barcelona, Finestrat, Fanzara, Murcia, entre otras.

So much more than a tool, the surfboard is the philosophical icon, a sacred craft, a culturally pervasive symbol of freedom, adventure and enduring youth. This is why the surfboard builder was once the primary arbiter of surfing culture, from those early Hawaiian kahunas to the first wave of board manufactures. Think back: Hobie, Hansen, Bing, Weber, Larkin, Noll, Jacobs, Haut, et al. These surfboard builders shaped surf culture, both literally and figuratively. It was all about the ride–what you wore came second. Since 2007 THE BOARDROOM SHOW has reasserted and maintained this philosophy. To put the surfboard — and the modern day kahunas who craft and design them — back at the forefront of surf culture. Today the international surfboard building community places surf culture, its influence, its importance, its responsibility, back in the hands of the artisans who shape our sacred craft – and ultimately our future. Please join us as we showcase builders, designers, craftsman, surfboards, essential surf equipment, gear, art, music & more.

Uncle Chris Thorne is an Aboriginal artist living in the bush near Lima, Victoria, and is well known throughout the Benalla region for his paintings. His work as an artist and activist is a bridge to the Dreamtime stories shared by his Elders. For Chris, art is a journey of identity and "finding his way home"—a journey he is now sharing as a mentor to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students in Benalla.

This year, he is joined by Bryan, Chantay, Shanaih, Jobe, Indi, and Haylee. These young artists are bringing their commitment, their energy, and their own connections to Country to a collaborative mural that celebrates culture and community.

Come witness this powerful exchange of knowledge and see history in the making on the walls of Benalla.

Cristina Reyes @cristina_reyes__ (Santa Cruz de Tenerife, España)

La obra de Cristina Reyes es una invitación a abrazar la imperfección y a encontrar belleza en lo que suele ser rechazado. Reyes indaga en el trauma y se nutre de su energía para transformarla, trascendiendo lo aparentemente negativo desde el juego. Sus murales integran los elementos ambientales y arquitectónicos del lugar, creando nuevas realidades imaginarias. Reyes juega con las formas, buscando despertar la curiosidad y abrir la mente a nuevas maneras de ver el mundo. A través de la creación de su propia mitología, explora símbolos visuales y escritura automática. Sus pinturas representan seres híbridos que, con el tiempo, se convierten en arquetipos dentro de su universo visual.

Artista interdisciplinar, desarrolla su práctica entre Londres y Tenerife, y participa regularmente en exposiciones y residencias internacionales. Colabora periódicamente con diseñadores cómo Miista e instituciones como la Hayward Gallery, el Palacio de Kensington y el Museo V&A de Londres.

©Cristina Reyes

Catch them in two ways over the festival weekend:

🎤 ‘So To Speak’ Q&A: Join us for a rare, deep-dive session into the grit and history of the early Melbourne and Australian scene with Peril & Paris. They’ll be discussing their new book by Puzle Press (https://www.instagram.com/elzup/) - Claim 2 Fame, featuring their personal archive of over 600 images documenting the birth of a movement.

This is a piece of Australian history you don’t want to miss.

Manolo Mesa @manolo_mesa (Puerto de Santa María, España)

En lo material existe un significado intrínseco y otro que proyectamos. Pero Es el acto de mirar que nos sirve para entender su artificio en la pintura. Enfrentarse a objetos inertes, contemplar su belleza y esperar que revelen ese sentido que se resiste, un motivo aparentemente neutro como una forma autónoma de ser. 

Manolo Mesa comienza a pintar grafitis en 2002. Mientras cursa Bellas Artes en la Universidad de Sevilla, desarrolla su camino en la pintura. Posteriormente realiza un máster en Cerámica y cursa el master de Pintura en la misma Universidad del País Vasco. Sus intervenciones murales se encuentran en numerosos países de Europa, África, Asia y Estados Unidos. Su obra ha sido presentada en exposiciones individuales, colectivas y ferias de arte en ciudades como Madrid, París, Berlín, Los Ángeles, Nueva York, Miami, Herning, Aalborg y Londres, entre otras ciudades nacionales e internacionales.

Malditas Ternura @malditas.ternura (Buenos Aires, Argentina)

Malditas Ternura es un dúo de artistas originarias de la ciudad de Buenos Aires, Argentina. Formadas en Artes Visuales y Diseño Gráfico en la UNA (Universidad Nacional del Arte) y en la UBA (Universidad de Buenos Aires); trabajan como artistas visuales, docentes y muralistas.
Trabajan en el campo del arte urbano desde hace más de diez años de manera individual y, en 2021, decidieron conformar este colectivo. Actualmente, gestionan un estudio artístico en la ciudad de Buenos Aires desde donde impulsan residencias y exhibiciones para artistas.
Son miembros fundadoras de la Asociación Argentina de Mujeres Muralistas (AMMURA) y han participado en numerosos festivales internacionales de arte urbano en Europa y Latinoamérica, entre los que se destacan Vigo Cidade de Cor (Galicia), Asalto (Zaragoza, España), Urban Act (Atenas, Grecia), Ms Artville (Hamburgo, Alemania), Calle Libre (Viena, Austria), Pictopia (Medellín, Colombia) y 33 Grados (Mercedes, Uruguay), entre otros.

【ベイブレードについて】

『ベイブレード』は1999年に誕生した、ベーゴマを現代風にアレンジした対戦玩具である。第1世代『爆転シュート ベイブレード』、第2世代『メタルファイト ベイブレード』、第3世代『ベイブレードバースト』、第4世代『BEYBLADE X』の4つのシリーズを通して、世界80以上の国と地域で累計5.6億個以上（2025年9月時点）が出荷されている。最新の『BEYBLADE X』は、ベイブレード（コマ）の軸についている“ギヤ”とスタジアムの“レール”がかみ合うことで、超加速を生み出す新ギミック「X（エクストリーム）ダッシュ」を搭載し、プレイヤーだけでなく観客をも魅了するGEAR SPORTSへと進化している。

Your personal details are linked to your My UTMB profile. To update them, log in to My UTMB here. Please note - it may take a few hours for your updated details to show on your registration.

At Boom, we are dedicated to regenerating and nurturing the Earth.

Ecological consciousness is woven into every stage of the festival: before, during and after the event.

Giulio Vesprini @giuliovesprini (Civitanova Marche, Italia)

Giulio Vesprini (1980, Civitanova Marche, Italia) es un artista formadoen  la Academia de Bellas Artes y el Departamento de Arquitectura. Grafitero entre 1994 y 2000, desde 2004 desarrolla su práctica en el campo del arte urbano.
Su trabajo ha sido ampliamente difundido en publicaciones especializadas como “Abitare, Architecture Suisse”, “Graffiti Art Magazine” y “Stuart Magazine”, y ha participado en numerosos festivales internacionales, entre los que destacan Le MUR (Saint-Étienne), Goldmine Festival (Gante), Asalto Festival (Zaragoza), LookUp Festival (Portsmouth) y el proyecto PlankSidan (Gotemburgo).
Es fundador de Vedo a Colori – Urban Art Museum y del Tabula Rasa Visual Arts Festival. En 2013 creó el estudio creativo Asinus in Cathedra e inició una investigación en torno al concepto de Archigraphy, una práctica que transforma muros, zonas de juego y espacios públicos mediante el arte urbano, en diálogo con tácticas urbanas.
Es profesor de Teoría del Color y Obra Artística, imparte clases sobre técnicas antiguas de impresión y utiliza la fotografía como herramienta de investigación urbana. Ha desarrollado importantes proyectos creativos en colaboración con marcas y entidades como Ikea, Antonio Lupi, Bruno Barbieri, Il Sole 24 Ore, Enel, Rag & Bone NYC, EA Sports, ENI, entre otras.

Artist Feature 🎨

@fork_one  is a Moscow-based artist who emerged from the Russian graffiti movement of the early 2000s, becoming known for character-driven street works across Moscow, Barcelona, Paris and Osaka. A pivotal injury in 2017 prompted a shift from walls to canvas, transforming his street language into a distinctive studio practice. 

He is the founder of “plasticine realism” — hyperrealistic paintings that mimic hand-moulded plasticine, fusing childhood nostalgia with technical precision and three- dimensional illusion. Balancing irony, colour and dynamism, Fork creates works that are playful yet profound, bridging street culture and contemporary art through a universal visual language.

Llega la 21ª edición del Encuentro de Arte Urbano PolinizaDOS 2026 @polinizados 🥳

🗓️ Del 11 al 15 de mayo en los espacios del Campus de Vera de la @instaupv 

El Encuentro propone una reflexión en torno a la espacialidad, con el objetivo de ir más allá del mural como formato pictórico y contribuir a la construcción de un sentido espacial y arquitectónico. Para ello, se plantea una aproximación expandida desde la investigación artística, entendida como una herramienta para la configuración de espacialidades propias, cargadas de sentido discursivo.

En este contexto, PolinizaDOS vuelve a invitar a artistas vinculados a una ciudad del ámbito iberoamericano. En esta ocasión, la ciudad invitada es Lisboa, representada por el colectivo Os Espacialistas @os_espacialistas . 

El cartel se completa con los y las artistas seleccionadas mediante convocatoria pública: Malditas Ternura @malditas.ternura , cuyo trabajo explora la sensibilidad de las historiografías colectivas; Manolo Mesa @manolo_mesa , centrado en la relación entre objeto y la tradición de los espacios íntimos; Giulio Vesprini @giuliovesprini , que investiga la abstracción a través de composiciones de fuerte carácter gráfico; Alexandros Simopoulos @this_is_opium , cuya práctica se sitúa entre la pintura y el conceptualismo referencial al espacio; y Cristina Reyes @cristina_reyes__ , que aborda el mural desde una aproximación narrativa y simbólica, como nuevas maneras de ver el mundo.

Asimismo, retomando la línea de apoyo al talento interno de la Facultad de Bellas Artes, el jurado ha concedido un accésit a J. Warx, cuyo trabajo destaca por su aproximación discursiva sobre coyunturas contemporáneas.

Con la colaboración de @pinturas_joseantoniogarcia , ECSA , @gvacultura

The psychedelic community is buzzing and we are here for it! 🚀 After years of pushing boundaries, psytechno is finally getting the spotlight it deserves. Now a well-known music platform and many outlets are officially recognising it. The Alchemy Circle has been championing this sound since 2012 🌪️

Inspired by the Alchemy theme of Boom 2012, we wanted to create something unique. We wanted to bring on a brand new concept to follow up the Groovy Beach stage (2008 and 2010 - where sounds from a pioneer label of psytechno, Boshke Beats, were common). Back then, stages outside the psytrance / chill-out dichotomy were simply labelled the “Alternative Stage”. We wanted more.

We turned the Alchemy Circle into a melting pot of psytechno, dark prog, psytrance, progressive, breakbeat, and drum’n’bass - all wrapped up in that signature Boom magic:

✨ Mind-blowing architecture
💃 Insane stage designs
🎨 Immersive art & gardens
🌈 The wildest, fun and high vibes global dancefloor provided by YOU, the Boomers ❤️

Since 2012, this has been one of our temples of fusion, alongside the heartbeat of Boom, the Dance Temple. Helping young artists find their voice at Alchemy and watching our psychedelic music scene expand in so many directions has been the ultimate trip, and the evolution continues 🍄

🟠 Get to know the UTA50 course 🟠

Sharing the second half of the iconic UTA100, the UTA50 delivers big scenery, big moments and serious Blue Mountains beauty.

Starting at Scenic World in Katoomba, you’ll head straight out along the dramatic clifftops, taking in breathtaking views of Mt Solitary and the surrounding escarpments early in the run.

Around the halfway mark, Wentworth Falls provides a standout moment before the course flows into the long descent of the epic Kedumba Pas.

From there, there’s only one way to finish.

Up you go, tackling the infamous 951 Furber Steps and climbing your way back to the finish line at Scenic World - tired legs, full hearts and a true sense of accomplishment.

Extreme weather? This is our reality at #Boomland.

From heatwaves and droughts to water scarcity, swirling winds, sudden heavy rainfall, and springs and summers with hundreds of days above 30ºC - sometimes surrounded by fire. This is our normal.

Resilience, humility, and learning to work with Mother Nature are at the core of everything we do. Always with love. ♥️

After a winter of almost non-stop rain at Boomland, bringing much-needed and blessed water, the Iberian Peninsula is now facing Storm Kristin. Intense rainfall and winds between 140 and 200 km/h have been reported.

At @boomlandofficial, the impact is real:
🌳 Trees lost, including century-old holm oaks
🌬️ A full solar array destroyed
🎨 Artworks damaged

Losing century-old living beings is always heartbreaking. We remain deeply grateful for the oxygen, shade, and life they offered.

Working with Nature is a blessing. Moments like these only strengthen our commitment to continue our environmental and regenerative programme, with even more dedication.

A word of solidarity to everyone in Portugal and Spain facing difficult situations right now.

We Are With You. 💚

#OnlyLoveBringsLove

caption:
Did you know that our work in Boomland is an all-year process, rooted in care and presence? 🌱✨

It’s not only about envisioning and bringing to life @boomfestivalofficial, @beingathering, and the Boomland School. Since 2010, this land has been nurtured through every season. 🌀

Winter is a time for grounding the future. A season dedicated to regeneration: replanting biodiversity meadows, caring for compost systems, maintaining waterlines and networks, planting new trees, and shaping new ecological initiatives. 🌳💧

One example is the Green Corridor at the Dance Temple, a new intervention designed to bring shade and biodiversity through living connections between trees, paths, and gardens (photos 7; 8; 9). 🌿

It is also a time when structures evolve. At the Dance Temple, work continues with bamboo, guided by biomimetic principles that teach us how to build lightly, intelligently, and in harmony with the land (photos 1; 2; 3; 4; 5). 🌍

Boomland is not just a place. It is a living ecosystem. And you are part of it. ✨

Thank you, Boomers. Muito Obrigado. ❤️

Eco Letter to the Boomers II: The Second Chapter ✨

Every edition, our regenerative efforts take into account the need to restore and improve biodiversity but also to act on the impact of the festival production. We measure, we act, we improve. And this year we are supporting a pioneering project to restore seagrass meadows with @ocean_alive_org 💫

2016年結成。打楽器奏者のみで構成された”熱狂打楽器集団”。
ハンドサインを用いた即興演奏法“Rhythm with Signs”を取り入れた日本初のグループ。
大編成で打ち鳴らされる轟音。即興演奏ならではの予測不能な展開。伝統的かつ革新的な音楽。大迫力のパフォーマンスは、聴くもの全てを”熱狂の国”へと誘う。
その演奏は世代や人種の壁を超えて好評を博し、ライブハウス、野外フェス、クラブ、学校の体育館から児童に向けたワークショップまで場所を問わず活動している。
テレビ朝日「EIGHT-JAM」打楽器特集回に出演、打首獄門同好会.日食なつこ.KenKen(RIZE).小川慶太(Snarky Puppy)など国内外で活躍するアーティストとのコラボ、Yahoo!ニュースに取り上げられる等、各方面で注目を集めている。
2021年9月に1st EP｢La｣、同年12月に2nd EP｢Señas」をリリース。2024年1月には1stアルバム「Country of Frenzy」を全国流通リリース。同年東名阪ツアーを開催。ツアーファイナルのShibuya WWWはSold Out。
2025年3月には2ndアルバム「熱狂は全てを超えて」を携え、実施半年前には渋谷WWWX公演含む全4公演ソールドアウトの中、東名阪ツアーを開催。
2026年5月には3rdアルバム「熱狂の彼方へと紡ぐ」をリリースし同年5月より自身最大規模の全国ツアーを開催。ツアーファイナルは恵比寿LIQUIDROOMにて大盛況の中幕を閉じた。

★Rhythm with Signsとは★
アルゼンチンの音楽家であり作曲家のSantiago Vazquezが2005年に発案した演奏方法。
指揮者が繰り出す100種類以上のハンドサインを元に演奏者が即興でアンサンブルを構築する。2024年のSantiago Vazquez来日時にはコラボレーションライブ及びワークショップを開催した。

🔴 Get to know the UTAMiler course 🔴

Grose Valley, Grand Canyon, Perrys Lookdown, Blue Gum Forest, Lockleys Pylon - just to name a few of the incredible place's part of 100 mile journey.

Alongside Narrow Neck, Ironpot Ridge, Leura Forest, Wentworth Falls, Kedumba Pass and Furber Steps - this is the race trail runners across Australia dream about.

Starting in Blackheath, the UTAMiler immediately draws you into the dramatic beauty of the Grose Valley, where long descents and climbs set the tone for what lies ahead. The course winds through the Grand Canyon, climbs toward the sweeping 360‑degree views at Lockleys Pylon, and passes through the lush tranquillity of Blue Gum Forest.

A memorable stop at the Hydro Majestic Hotel, overlooking the Megalong Valley, before the course connects with the iconic UTA100 route at Narrow Neck Lookout.

From here, the journey continues through the heart of the World Heritage listed Blue Mountains, flowing across mostly single track, wide trails, ridgelines and escarpments.

After around 99 miles, one final challenge awaits.

At the bottom of trail running’s most famous staircase, 951 Furber Steps stand between you and the finish line at Scenic World - a fitting end to an epic adventure.

*For the most accurate distance, please refer to the Strava maps on our website.

＜PUSHIM＞ @shinoyama_pushim
1995年に地元大阪で活動を開始。
その歌声を聞くと、誰もが“Feel The Soul (=魂を感じる)”“Strong Voice!(=力強い声)”“One &Only(=誰にも真似できない)”と形容されるプレミアム・シンガー。 “クイーン・オブ・レゲエ”として、今やジャパニーズ・レゲエ・シーンNo.1シンガーの座を確固たるものにしたと同時に、日本の音楽シーンの中でも圧倒的な歌唱 力を誇るシンガーとして高い評価を受け続けている。
2015年には自身のレーベル“Groovillage”を設立させるなど、更に活動の幅を拡げている。
2019年3月にはオリジナルアルバムとしては10枚目となる「immature」をリリース。
Zepp5箇所全10公演のPUSHIM 20th ANNIVERSARY LIVE TOUR”immature”や大阪JOULEと渋谷VISIONで行われたTHE MIDNIGHT PARTYも超満員で終える。
2021年には Mini Album 『深呼吸』をリリース。リリースに伴い、PUSHIM LIVE TOUR 2021 ”深呼吸”と題した東名阪Zeppツアーを開催し大成功を収めた。2年後の2023年にはMEDZ MUSIC協力の元、アルバム「Dialogue」をリリース。今年2024年はデビューから25周年のアニバーサリーイヤーを迎え、GrooPeePartyと題し自身のファンサイトをリニューアル。その唯一無二の歌唱力にエンパワーメントのメッセージを乗せ、円熟味を増しつつも「REBEL」の精神を貫くその姿は多くの人々の心を掴み、勇気付け続けている。

＜韻シストBAND＞ @in_sistagram
生々しく独創的でグルーヴィーなサウンドと極上のライブパフォーマンスが圧倒的な評価を受け続ける、大阪をベースに活動するファンキーグルーヴマスターと称される唯一無二のヒップホップバンド。数度のメンバー・チェンジを経て、MC（サッコン)、Gtr. (TAKU)、Bass (Shyoudog)、Drs.(TAROW-ONE)からなる現メンバーとなる。1998年の結成当初から大阪を拠点として活動し、日本におけるヒップホップ・バンドのパイオニア的存在として、またミュージシャンズ・ミュージシャンとして高い評価を受け続けている。

🟢 Get to know the UTA100 course 🟢

Narrow Neck, Ironpot Ridge, Leura Forest, Wentworth Falls, Kedumba Pass and Furber Steps.

This is the race many trail runners dream of tackling at least once… and for those who do, once is often never enough.

Starting at Scenic World in Katoomba, the course takes you deep into the heart of the World Heritage listed Blue Mountains, weaving through single track and wide trails.

Lush bushland, dramatic escarpments and epic ridgelines roll by, until, after around 99 kilometres, you arrive at one final challenge.

Waiting at the bottom: the most famous staircase in trail running. 951 Furber Steps stand between you and the finish line back at Scenic World.

Building with nature. 🌿 

Work continues at Boomland - in the Dance Temple we are maintaining the bamboo structure designed using biomimetic principles: intelligent material use, deep ecological integration, and natural forms.

As a fast-growing, renewable resource with remarkable structural properties, bamboo teaches us how to build lightly, intelligently, and in harmony with the ecosystems we all belong to. 🌍

🧚 We introduced dry compost toilets at Boomland back in 2006.

No water. No chemicals. A system that turns waste into nutrient-rich soil, closing the loop and contributing to the regeneration of the Earth. 🌍

Nearly two decades of research, testing and real-world use have allowed us to refine a compost toilet designed for our ecosystem, and adaptable to festivals and events anywhere.

🌳 No water is used, and everything left behind is transformed into high-quality biological compost.

🌀 This is part of our ongoing work in @boomlandofficial: applying ecological principles in practice, year after year.

Toilets can make or break the festival experience, but they are also a powerful symbol of global challenges and opportunities. Our goal is simple: to provide high-quality facilities while saving water and turning waste into soil.

Proof that festivals can be more than celebration.
They can educate, inspire, and contribute to global solutions. ✨❤️

#8 on our best moments from 2026 ✨🔦

There’s something special about watching the trails come alive in the dark.

Hundreds of head torches lighting up the Blue Mountains, all chasing their own finish line 😍

Fortress Ridge in all its glory 🤩

Clouds rolling in, runners flowing along the ridgeline - this is the UTAMiler.

Raw, rugged, and unforgettable. Who's ready to take it on in 2027? 🙌🏻

From where you would rather be...

The Blue Mountains is calling your name for 2027 😍

General Entries open 11:00am AEST, 17 September.

#UltraTrailAustralia

As we look ahead to 2027,  let’s take a moment to relive the magic of an incredible 2026 💙✨

From the breathtaking cliff-top escarpments to the depths of the bush-clad valleys, the cheers of the crowds filling your ears to the sounds of the yidaki echoing for miles - the sights and sounds of 2026 HOKA Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB were truly unforgettable!

As we get ready for 2027 #UTA entries to open, we’re taking a moment to relive the magic of 2026 by counting down our top 10 moments!
 
Kicking things off at #10: welcoming home our final UTA100 finisher, Louise Pontello 💙
 
Taking on her first ever 100km race, it was nothing but magnificent and breathtaking. What made it even more special was crossing the finish line with her kids by her side 🥹

5am in the Blue Mountains. Fog hanging low, rain in the air, the sun still not up. 160 kilometres of trail waiting.

It takes a special kind of courage to stand on this start line before the world wakes up, to chase something bigger. This is where the extraordinary journeys begin.

The #UTAMiler, a race like no other!

The moody Blue Mountains 💙

From epic ridgelines to valleys wrapped in fog, every turn reveals a new side of this iconic landscape.

Could this be your view from Govetts Leap in 2027? 😶‍🌫️
From misty mornings to jaw‑dropping viewpoints, nothing compares to running at #UTA through the Blue Mountains 💙

Little legs, big adventures! 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️💙

The UTA Kids Run is all about fun, smiles and creating unforgettable trail memories. Watching the next generation cross the finish line never gets old.

As we continue counting down our top 10 moments from 2026... #9 is the McKenzie family pit crew 💙

Returning for another year at UTA, the McKenzie family were back in action at the Fairmont Resort checkpoint. With all the fuel, fishing vests, and kids on board, they had everything covered 🙌🏼

We love seeing UTA become more than just a race. It’s a weekend where the whole family can get involved, cheer from the sidelines, and be part of the journey.

Don’t forget to lock in your support crew for 2027. At #UTA, it’s always a team effort 💪🏼

The mountains are feeling moody 💙

UTAMiler runners descend into Govetts Leap as fog rolls through the valley - what a sight 😶‍🌫️

🏃🏼‍♀️ 51% 🏃🏼‍♀️

In 2026, 43% of runners at HOKA Ultra-Trail Australia by UTMB were female. In fact, women outnumbered men in both UTA11 and UTA22 🙌🏻

Tanya, Regional Director for UTMB Oceania and a 10-time UTA100 finisher, is putting the call out to women everywhere to make their mark at 2027 #UTA.

She says starting trail running can feel daunting, but that quickly changed when she connected with a community of women who offered support, training advice, and became lifelong training partners.

Project 51% - let's make it happen! 💥

Vibram was once again part of the #UTA experience this year, supporting runners and connecting with the trail running community throughout race week.

A reminder of Vibram's long-standing connection to the mountains - globally through nearly 20 years of UTMB support.

With athletes from New Zealand and Japan on course, and Vibram outsoles trusted by runners throughout the Blue Mountains, UTA once again demonstrated why confidence in every step is non-negotiable when tackling technical (and wet) terrain.

#ConfidenceInEveryStep #VibramMegaGrip #UTMB

This is what “see you at the front” looks like 👀

#hiddenvalley #hiddenvalleyfestival

How lucky are we to run and explore these incredible destinations 😍

Happy International Running Day to all our trail runners - we hope you get out there today and explore some beautiful trails.

We might be biased, but we think these are some of the best places you could possibly run ✨

10/4(日)「PES」出演!!
@pepes_jp

2001年、RIP SLYMEのMCとしてメジャーデビュー。
日本のHIP HOPグループとしては初の武道館公演・海外公演・野外5万人ライブなど数々の記録を作り続けてきた。
2012年には本格的にソロ活動を開始し独自の表現を追求し、柔らかなフロウと感性豊かなリリックを武器に、ヒップホップを軸とした自由な音楽スタイルを展開している。
日常に寄り添う言葉と心地よいグルーヴで、多くのリスナーを魅了。
音楽だけでなくアートや植物、サーフカルチャーにも深く関わり、自身ならではの世界観を発信し続けている。

Artist Feature 🎨

Mur0ne is a largely self-taught artist whose career spans graphic design, graffiti and muralism. Beginning casually before evolving into a profession, his background in design strongly informs his contemporary practice. Working between geometric abstraction, expressionism and psychedelic figurative imagery, he creates bold, immersive works defined by primary colours, sharp contrasts and high saturation. 

Muralism is his preferred medium, with large-format works across public spaces worldwide, including fields, stands, tunnels and ceilings. His monumental approach has established him as a reference point for immersive art. As he explains, “Abstract geometry and illustration are my passion, broadly defining my work.”

Artist Feature 🎨

@juzpop  is a Melbourne-based Australian artist and muralist known for large-scale murals and surreal, introspective paintings. Her work explores identity, mental health, and hidden emotional landscapes, centring women as symbols of strength. Drawing from her own photography, she merges portraiture with elements of nature to create layered, dreamlike compositions reflecting the connection between humanity and the natural world. 

After discovering muralism during a residency in Oaxaca, Mexico, her work has appeared across Australia, Mongolia, Amsterdam and Mexico. Her 2024 solo exhibition, Morphe, marked a milestone in her evolving exploration of transformation and self.

We're thrilled to have Gus Eagleton at this year's festival! Gus is a Brisbane-based contemporary mural artist delivering public and private commissions across Australia and internationally. A 2013 graduate of the Queensland College of Art and Design, he has over a decade of experience in large- scale painting and has earned international recognition, including the Lord Mayor’s Brisbane Portrait Prize. His practice explores the lives of everyday people, blending imagery from diverse times and perspectives into compelling figurative narratives. Eagleton has completed projects for councils nationwide and organisations including Hutchinson Builders, Mirvac, Queensland Rail, Scentre Group, IBM and Alder Constructions, with works spanning 30 metres high and 200 metres long.

caption: 10 years, and what a show it was 🪩 . We thank you for all the support over the years. We are truly grateful. See you next year 🌴

THE WOMEN WHO PAINT OUR WORLD. 🎨💪

This #InternationalWomensDay, we’re celebrating the incredible creativity, resilience, and vision of women in street art.

At the upcoming festival, we are honoured to feature a lineup of extraordinary women who bring diverse perspectives, unmatched skill, and vibrant life to our town. 

One such artist is @jasmine_crisp. Jasmine Crisp (she/her) is a painter and muralist from Adelaide, South Australia. Working with traditional techniques, she creates highly detailed murals using only brush, roller and hand-mixed colours. Her practice draws on lived experience, depicting local figures, spaces and personal belongings through original imagery and references. 

Blending reality with fantasy, she produces playful genre paintings of the imagined familiar. Since beginning her public art practice in 2020, Crisp has delivered large-scale murals internationally, including Street Art Boulogne Sur Mer (France); Without Frontiers Lunetta (Italy); Muralia (Vienna) and LOOKUP Festival (Portsmouth, UK), alongside major commissions and festivals across Australia.

We can't wait to see her work at the festival 🙌

📸 @flashstudio

2016年結成。打楽器奏者のみで構成された”熱狂打楽器集団”。
ハンドサインを用いた即興演奏法“Rhythm with Signs”を取り入れた日本初のグループ。
大編成で打ち鳴らされる轟音。即興演奏ならではの予測不能な展開。伝統的かつ革新的な音楽。大迫力のパフォーマンスは、聴くもの全てを”熱狂の国”へと誘う。
その演奏は世代や人種の壁を超えて好評を博し、ライブハウス、野外フェス、クラブ、学校の体育館から児童に向けたワークショップまで場所を問わず活動している。
テレビ朝日「EIGHT-JAM」打楽器特集回に出演、打首獄門同好会.日食なつこ.KenKen(RIZE).小川慶太(Snarky Puppy)など国内外で活躍するアーティストとのコラボ、Yahoo!ニュースに取り上げられる等、各方面で注目を集めている。
2021年9月に1st EP｢La｣、同年12月に2nd EP｢Señas」をリリース。2024年1月には1stアルバム「Country of Frenzy」を全国流通リリース。同年東名阪ツアーを開催。ツアーファイナルのShibuya WWWはSold Out。
2025年3月には2ndアルバム「熱狂は全てを超えて」を携え、実施半年前には渋谷WWWX公演含む全4公演ソールドアウトの中、東名阪ツアーを開催。
2026年5月には3rdアルバム「熱狂の彼方へと紡ぐ」をリリースし同年5月より自身最大規模の全国ツアーを開催。ツアーファイナルは恵比寿LIQUIDROOMにて大盛況の中幕を閉じた。

SNEAK PEEK: A work-in-progress look at “Shared Waters” by @stephaniecartledge, located at the Benalla Visitor Information Centre, which will be exhibited from the 27 March to 19 July 2026.

Shared Waters highlights the often-unseen native animals living in Lake Benalla. While many people walk around the lake daily, species such as the platypus, rakali, nankeen night heron, and long-necked turtle often go unnoticed because they are most active at dawn and dusk.

Benalla Rural City Council is inviting individuals, community groups, schools, businesses and organisations to consider hosting an event as part of the 2026 Benalla Street Art Festival from 17–19 April 2026.

Events should celebrate street art, showcase local talent, support local businesses and encourage more people to visit Benalla and the High-Country region.

Events could include music, installations, galleries, workshops, or other creative activities.

Events will be promoted through the festival’s program, highlighting activities across Benalla and surrounding townships.

It is with heavy hearts that we say goodbye to a dear friend and true titan of our tribe, Don Hansen. Don was a founding member of SHACC and a lifelong friend to our founder, Dick Metz.
“He was one of the sweetest guys I’ve ever known,” says Metz. “And one of the smartest, too.”
Hansen arrived in California from South Dakota in 1958 while stationed at Fort Ord. After seeing surfing in Santa Cruz, he forged a friendship with Jack O’Neill, who taught him the shaping basics. Following his service, he moved south to refine his skills under Hap Jacobs and Hobie Alter, which is where he first met Metz.
“Hobie loved Hansen because he was very straightforward about his plans,” Metz recalls. “He said he wanted to learn the business from us and open his own shop down south. Hobie respected that. And that’s exactly what Don did!”
But not before Hansen made a detour to Hawaii, where he famously landed the cover of Surfer Magazine in 1962. Upon returning to California, he opened the first Hansen Surfboards in Cardiff, and business boomed. The former farm boy, mink trapper, boxer, and track star arrived in North County San Diego loaded with ambition. By 1965, he was one of the ten legendary shapers featured on the cover of Surfing Magazine.
His team was stacked, with Mike Doyle, Rusty Miller, Margo Godfrey, and Linda Benson among his riders. While he helped usher in the “signature model” era, his retail prowess made him a cornerstone of California’s coastal identity. No other 60s shaper and retailer endured like Hansen. His Encinitas landmark has thrived through six decades of surfing’s boom-and-bust cycles.
“He diversified better than any of us,” says Metz. “You walk into his shop today and you still find skis, snowboards, skateboards, and surfboards. He did it all. He was a real industry leader, and I already miss him.”
We are forever grateful for Don’s friendship, support, and contributions to our culture. Our deepest condolences go out to his wife, Shirley, sons Josh and Christian, and daughter Heidi, who are all proudly carrying Don’s legacy forward.
Rest easy, Don. We love you!

The quiet and reserved Pete Peterson was also a first-rate craftsman. He designed and built a popular line of surfboards and paddleboards for Pacific System Homes in the late ‘30s, working mainly with balsa and redwood, and also made and sold boards out of his own house for $35 (or $45 with a five-coat spar varnish finish). As surf photographer Don James later noted, Peterson was particular, almost neurotic, about the condition of his own boards. “He was a neat freak,” James remembered, “who never used any wax on the surface of his board for traction because he felt it violated the pristine look he so admired.” Peterson dominated the Pacific Coast Surf Riding Championships, early modern surfing’s biggest event, winning four times between 1928 and 1941—nobody else won more than once. Peterson didn’t surf competitively in the ‘50s, then returned with spectacular results in the early and mid-‘60s as a tandem rider. ⁠

1963 Surfboards Hawaii #149 shaped by Dick Brewer in Hawaii. ⁠
⁠
This big-wave gun is one of the few survivors of the North Shore in the early 1960s. There are some gorgeous “modern classics” in the marketplace, but this board was actually in the water and being ridden alongside big wave pioneers such as Buzzy Trent, George Downing, Wally Froiseth, Pat Curren and the like. The name of the original owner is unknown; the board was found washed up on the North Shore in the early 1960s after a huge swell, stored away, and then brought to Randy Rarick to restore in the 1990s.  Brewer’s initials “RB” and “# 149” are written on the stringer just below the Surfboards Hawaii logo. The board is 10’-4” long and has a 1.5” wide old-growth redwood stringer and tailblock, along with a Dick Brewer mahogany speed fin. The board is in absolutely mint condition.⁠

👀 It's the Rakali Treasure Hunt Trail! Are you going to be lucky enough to grab the Rakali Rocks by Linleigh Rocks? 👀
The Rakali is the Aboriginal name for the Australian Water-rat (Hydromys chrysogaster). It is native and an iconic inhabitant of Lake Benalla and surrounding water-ways, most often glimpsed swimming on the surface of the water in the early morning or late afternoon. It is similar in size and colour to the platypus.

Hint: Rakali can be found where there is water all year round; the species' only habitat requirement is clean water and plenty of vegetation. Make sure you're paying attention so you don't miss out on spotting one of the beauties.
‼️When you pick one up make sure to tag @benallastreetartfestival and Linleigh Rocks (on Facebook) for their generous contribution 🙏

Sea Otter Australia is a lot of festival packed into one weekend. Here's how to make sure you get the most out of it.

📋 Grab the festival schedule ahead of time and plan your day - there's a lot on and clashes happen fast.
🏁 Lock in your race and ride times so you know exactly where you need to be and when.
🏆 Don't miss the ceremonies. The atmosphere when riders cross that finish line is one of the best parts of the whole weekend.
🍔 Refuel between sessions at the food trucks, you'll need the energy.
🎪 Make time for the Expo. New gear, exhibitor activations and product drops happen all weekend, not just on one day.
🎁 Keep an eye out for onsite activations and promotions. Some only run once, so don't sleep on them.

Design, art and good times. We asked Rebecca Birrell how to find them at Junction.

Bec’s connection to the festival runs deep. A fixture since its early days, she’s been part of Junction’s story and evolution over the years, witnessing the festival grow into the creative gathering it is today, a history and legacy reflected in the images she pulled from her archives for us.

caption:
We’re peering behind the curtains to meet some of the artists making bold new work for this year’s Junction 👀

First up: Freyja from ROOKE 🎤 A contemporary circus company bringing not one, but two very different shows to the Festival.

🎪 Dream Job: a funny, silly and heartwarming family show about finding your dream job, even if you’re 45.

🥵 NOOK: ridiculously high-level circus, very good times and an offering to the gods of party. Come for the circus, stay out all night.

When asked what makes creating work in lutruwita special, Freyja says: “It’s quiet here. Grounded. Close to nature.” Giving artists space to make richer, more connected work.

And what makes a good audience? “The sounds they make.” When a room cheers together, or falls completely silent at just the right moment, that’s magic.

Three words for Dream Job: Fun. Silly. Heartwarming.

Three emojis for NOOK: 🥵🤯🍑

Discover ROOKE and the full Junction program via the link in bio.

Junction Arts Festival
17–20 September
In and around Prince’s Square, Launceston

#JunctionArtsFestival #Launceston #WhatsOnTasmania

We’re kicking off our How To Junction series with familiar faces from the festival community sharing their pathways through this year’s program.

First up: Emily-Rose Wills, Creative Producer of Junction Arts Festival.

ONE THING WE CAN’T MISS?

‣ I’m going to cheat and say two: Malcolm Johnson in The Secret Life of Eels with Where Water Meets, an ecologist, geographer and self-described eel advocate; and KATTLEYA at Resonance Rising with The Yoga Loft Launceston. One explores eel skin instruments and our relationship with rivers, the other brings movement and live music together in the morning light, high above the city.

HOW WOULD YOU DESCRIBE THIS YEAR’S PROGRAM?

‣ Considered is the word I keep coming back to. Junction is intentionally interdisciplinary, with loud nights and quiet mornings, ticketed and free events, work that challenges and work that’s simply fun. We’re taking over unexpected spaces too - an old menswear shop, empty offices, a church, backyard and stables.

YOUR PERFECT JUNCTION ITINERARY?

‣ Pick one or two key events each day and build around them. Start at the Festival Hub in Prince’s Square, then explore: A Stretch of the Imagination Thursday; Making at Design Tasmania and Nook (ROOKE) Friday; hands-on workshops, Art Walk and Emily Sanzaro Tasmanian Harpist’s Mixtape Marathon Saturday; and the Great Junction Dog Show, The Secret Life of Eels and a final night at the Hub on Sunday.

AN ICONIC JUNCTION MEMORY?

‣ Dan Koop’s The Stream / The Boat / The Shore / The Bridge, 2013. You made your own way around and over the river, handing your thoughts and choices over to the artists. I remember sitting in a rowboat talking about my mum’s death, and still have the Polaroid I was given on the bridge thirteen years later.

The work asked you to give as much of yourself to it as you hoped to get out of it. I did. It changed the way I see Launceston and live art - and that’s what I hope first-time Junction audiences find too ❣️

Feeling inspired?

From Monterey to Batemans Bay: The Torch is Lit.

As the world's cycling family gathers in Monterey this week for @seaotterclassic, we're reminded that this brand was built around a simple but powerful vision - to be the heartbeat of an entire industry. 

Our crew is on the ground at Laguna Seca with a profound sense of pride and responsiblity to continue the legacy that's been built on 35 years of of authenticity, community, and the simple joy of being on two wheels. 

In 2025, we saw that spirit ignite in Batemans Bay and proved that the Sea Otter heart beats just as strong in the Eurobodalla as it does in Monterey. We saw the same smiles, the same participation-first inclusivity, and the same industry-shaping energy that makes the original so iconic.

To our "Big Cousin" in the Northern Hemisphere: we’re here soaking up the vibes, connecting with the global team, and carrying that fire back to the NSW South Coast. 

From the action on the trails at @mogotrails and @mtbnarooma to the event hub races, the inspiring Summit, the massive expo and the community that comes with it, we're creating something the whole Australian cycling world can call its own. 2026 is going to be something special. Will you be there?

Batemans Bay, 21–25 October | Register for racing now via link in bio or visit www.seaotter.au

caption:
宝台樹でのキャンプはLabyrinthの大きな魅力のひとつです。2018年まで10年間にわたって開催してきた苗場からこの宝台樹に会場を移した一番の理由は、キャンプ場としての充実した設備でした。

みなかみの標高は1,000メートル。白樺やカラマツの森に囲まれ、空を背景に武尊山を望むこの場所は、キャンプ場として国内でも類稀な美しさだと感じております。場内は森の中にキャンプエリアが広がり、設備として24時間利用できるコインシャワー（3分200円）、各所に水場や水洗トイレ、調理に使える屋根付きのBBQスペース、また管理センター・売店である「しらかばハウス」では薪以外にもキャンプに必要な一通りのものが購入できます。

キャンプで過ごすことで、シャトルバス等で移動することなく、会場内で音楽と共に3日間を過ごすことができます。ただし夜は冷え込むので、インナー、フリース、ジャケットなど、防寒着を必ず用意してください。雨具や靴、ソックスのスペアも忘れずに。

私たちはキャンプそのものがLabyrinthという体験の根幹だと考えているため、チケットには火曜までの延泊を含む3泊分のキャンプ料金が含まれています。時間が許すなら最終日の音楽が終わった後、もう一晩泊まってみてください。そこで過ごした3日間の体験が自分自身の奥深くまでゆっくりと染み込んでいくのを感じることができると思います。

私がこのイベントで体験してきたことでも好きな時間のひとつが、夜に音楽が終わったあと、キャンプ場をあてもなくぶらぶら歩くことです。それぞれのキャンプサイトで焚き火を囲む姿や、森の中で談笑し、響く笑い声が森の中で溶け合ってる様子は、私にとって「帰る場所」でもあります。

—

Camping at Hodaigi Campground is one of the Labyrinth’s highlights. When we moved from Naeba after a ten-year run, the main motivation was to host the event at a campground with full facilities.

1000 meters up in Minakami, in a forest of birch and larch trees, with Mt. Hotaka framed against the sky, Hodaigi is a jewel in the world of Japanese campgrounds. Facilities include coin showers running 24 hours (¥200 / 3 min), flush toilets across many buildings, covered BBQ areas for cooking, and shaded camping space in the forest. Shirakaba House, the management center, has a small store for firewood, equipment, and many basics. And of course the main highlight is its natural beauty.

If you camp, you don’t need to worry about catching the shuttle bus. Just please come prepared for the cold at night with layers: inner layer, fleece and a jacket. Proper rain gear with an extra pair of shoes are also required. 

It’s standard for festivals now to charge a separate camping ticket, but we see camping as a fundamental part of the experience, so three nights of camping is included with tickets. Camp one more night after the music finishes to let the whole experience seep down into your roots. There’s no rush.

One of my favorite parts of the event is stumbling around the campground well after the music is done, hearing laughter echo through the forest mixed with nature sounds. To me, it sounds like home.

SO

Mindgamesの一員で、Labyrinthにおいて長年に渡りレジデントDJを務めるSoは、まさにこのイベントの中心にいる存在だ。主催者として、また出演者として、常に二足の草鞋を履きながらこのイベントに取り組む中、その合間を縫って数時間だけDJとしてステージに立つ姿は不思議でさえもある。

SOのDJとしての音楽スタイルは野外フェスとの相性が良い。時間帯や天気、フロアの温度感を感じながら、ゆったりとスムーズに物語を綴る展開力は、自然環境の中でとりわけその能力が発揮される。近年は毎年のLabyrinthでの活動に加え、ポルトガルのWaking LifeやVinculum、スペインのParallel、ポーランドのGarbicz Festival、ドイツのNacht Digital、ベルギーのLa Natureなど、欧州各所の良質なフェスからもそのスタイルが評価され、オファーが絶えない。

昨年のLabyrinthでは、長年担当して来た昼すぎの時間帯から、サンセットをまたぐ夕刻の時間帯へとスロットをシフトし、これまでにはないエネルギッシュなプレイを披露する機会となった。本日は、その素晴らしいセットを皆さんにもシェアするので、是非聴いて欲しい。

—

As both co-organizer and Mindgames resident dj, So is right at the core of the event. Every year he somehow manages to set aside the organizers’s hat for a few hours to perform the dj’s role.

So’s dj style is particularily well-suited to the outdoors, where his patience and sense of space and time can shine. Beyond his annual set at Labyrinth, he is a frequent guest to many intimate European festivals, such as Waking Life and Vinculum in Portugal, Parallel in Spain, Garbicz Festival in Poland, Nacht Digital in Germany, and La Nature in Belgium.

At last year’s Labyrinth, So shifted from his regular early afternoon role to the Sunday sunset set, giving him a chance to up the BPM and energy. We are happy to share that excellent set today on our SoundCloud.

「Hinata Rental」は、The Labyrinthの公式キャンプ用品レンタルサービスです。

利用方法はとても簡単。オンラインで予約し、会場でレンタル用品を受け取り、宝台樹の森でキャンプを満喫したら、最後にそのまま返却するだけです。シャトルバスや電車で重いテントを持ち運ぶ必要はありません。

【利用方法】

Hinata Rental is the official camping-gear rental service for The Labyrinth at Minakami Hodaigi Campground. 

The process is super simple: Reserve online, pick everything up at the venue, enjoy the magic of camping in the forest of Hodaigi, and then drop everything off at the end. No need to haul a tent on the shuttle or trains.

How it works:

- Choose what gear you want on the Hinata site (use browser translation to translate to English).
- Select the rental dates.
- Pick up your gear at the campground center building (next to the entrance) in a labeled delivery bag.
- Before you leave, pack it back in the same bag and return it to the same building.

No washing required. Travel light. Choose sets specifically chosen for Minakami autumns. 

What you can rent:

- Light festival sets: tent + bedding + lantern (solo from about ¥8,700; 2–4 person versions available).
- Full comfort sets: tent, chairs, table, sleep system (starter and family versions for 1–4 people).
- Just tents: types include dome, 2-room, and teepees, and brands include Snow Peak, Zane Arts, Coleman, and Logos.
- Other items include: sleeping bags, inflatable mats, cots, Helinox-style chairs, lanterns, coolers, stoves and cookware.

The deadline is Sunday, October 4.

ATOM™ & TOBIAS. (live)

「これは猫とネズミのゲームではなく、ネズミたちとチーズのゲームだ」

前回、Atom™とTobiasがLabyrinthで、今や伝説となったロング・ライブセットを披露したとき、私の頭にはある光景が浮かんだ。二匹のトリッピーなネズミが、サイケデリックなヒゲをぴくぴくさせながらステージ上で知恵を絞りながらゲームをしている姿だ。

そのゲームとは「狩り」であり――私が迷宮の奥深くに隠したチーズを探す狩りだった。

AtomとTobiasは、このゲームを実に30年以上にわたって続けてきた。そのなかで二人の間には、直感的で、言葉を必要としない独自のコミュニケーション言語が育まれてきた。彼らの演奏は完全な即興で流れは誰にも予測できず、どこへ辿り着くのかもわからない。チーズを探す途中、ときには二人が別々の方向へ漂うこともある。だが、やがて再び二人の歯車が徐々に噛み合い始め、「ひとつになる瞬間」へとどんどん近づいていく。

私自身、長年ダンサーとして様々なDJやライブを見てきたつもりだが、それでもこの二人の天才が、あの「ひとつになる瞬間」が生まれる圧倒的な音楽体験は他にない。

迷宮の中に隠されたチーズを見つけた瞬間。
二人自身もその瞬間を認識している。そしてフロアにいる誰もがそれを感じ取っている。

Labyrinthにおける彼らの壮大な歩みは2011年に始まり、これまでに7回のパフォーマンスを数えるが、Mindgamesからその録音された音源をリリースしたことはない。何故ならそのパフォーマンスは、その場所その瞬間に立ち会ってこそ意味があり、あの場で鳴っていたサウンドシステムの質感や音圧とあまりにも深く結びついているからだ。

体験したいのであれば、その場にいるしかない。
そして今年はこのふたりが初めてLabyrinthでクロージングセットを披露する。
尚更、この瞬間を体感して欲しい。

---

It's not a game of cat and mouse. It's a game of mice and the cheese.

The last time Atom™ and Tobias played one of their legendary live sets at Labyrinth, I had a vision of these two as trippy mice, psychedelic whiskers twitching, playing a clever game on stage. The game was a hunt for the cheese hidden deep inside the labyrinth.

Atom and Tobias have been playing versions of this game for three decades, developing an intuitive non-verbal language of communication. They play in an improvised form, where the flow is unpredictable and destination unclear. At times they drift apart in the hunt, but then you feel them lock back in as they get closer and closer to that moment of union.

As dancers for many years, we have seen many magic moments, but we have never experienced anything like when these two sonic geniuses collide in one of those moments of union. They know it, and everyone on the floor knows—that moment where they find the cheese.

Their epic run together at Labyrinth began in 2011 and consists of seven performances. We haven't released these recordings because their performance is so much tied to the texture and sound pressure of the system in that place and time. 

To experience it, you must be there.

And this year in particular you must be there, for Atom™ and Tobias are, for the first time, playing the closing set on the final day.

年々ダンスフロアに持ち込まれるキャンピングチェアや簡易ベッドが増えており、近年はより一層深刻な状況になりました。

あまりにも多くの椅子が放置されているため、ダンスフロアは前方と後方で分断されてしまい、また夜になるとそれらを避けながらフロア最前列に向かうのはかなり難しい状況です。

昼間に椅子を持ってきて、そのまま放置する人が多いため、無人の椅子によってフロアの広い部分が使えなくなってしまっており、今年からはその対策が必要だと考えており、今年からLabyrinthではフロアのステージに向かって右側に旗で目印を付けた「チェアエリア」を設けます。椅子を使用する場合はこのエリア内に置いてください。それ以外の場所に置かれている椅子については、移動をお願いするか、スタッフがこのエリアへ移動させていただきます。

ダンスフロアは文字通り、ダンスのための場所だと考えております。みんなが気持ちよく踊れるスペースを確保するためご協力をお願いします。一緒に行く友人たちにもこのルールをお伝え頂けると幸いです。また夜間は清掃が入るため、椅子や荷物をフロアに置きっぱなしにせず、ご自身のキャンプサイトへ持ち帰るようお願いします。（後から何らかのクレームを受けても対応し兼ねます）
音楽を楽しむためのフロアをできるだけ広く確保したいため、皆さんのご理解とご協力をよろしくお願いします！

Every year the number of camping chairs on the dance floor has increased, and this has increasingly become a problem.

Last year the dance floor became split between front and back because so many chairs were left unattended. At night it became difficult to navigate the floor without stumbling over camping chairs or cots.

Many people bring chairs during the day and then leave them there for the entire event, so large parts of the floor become unusable. We have decided to address this problem this year.

This year, there’s a designated “Chair Area” on the right side of the floor as you face the stage. The area will be marked by flags. If you use a chair, please place it inside this area. Chairs left elsewhere on the dancefloor need to be moved by you, or staff will move them into this area.

We consider the dancefloor a place for dancing, not for storing your belongings. Please help us keep enough space so everyone can dance comfortably. And please let your friends know about this rule.

If you do bring chairs to the floor, please bring your things back to your camping spot or hotel at night. We clean the floor at night, so you cannot leave stuff on the floor overnight. (We will not be able to respond to complaints received later about items left unattended on the floor overnight.)

We want the floor to feel as open and clean as possible for the music. Thank you for your cooperation and understanding.

caption:
ARCHITECTURAL

—

Juan RicoによるソロプロジェクトArchitectural長年にわたり、ベールに包まれた正体不明のアーティストとして活動して来たが、その正体はスペイン・アストゥリアス出身で、Reekoとして知られるJuna Ricoである。

2010年に自身のレーベルArchitecturalから一連の作品を発表し、その後、R&S、Music Man、Semantica、Delsin、Non Seriesといった名門レーベルからもリリースを重ねて来た。

その音楽性は、クラシカルなテクノやシネマティックな要素を基盤としながら、それらを非常にモダンで洗練された感覚で再解釈したものだ。テクノからアンビエントまで幅広く、深い没入感を伴い、ダビーな作品もあれば、感情的でメランコリックな作品もあるが、共通して言えるのはヒプノティックで尚且つアトモスフェリックな雰囲気を纏っていることだ。

Reeko名義では重厚感のあるインダストリアルなサウンドで知られていたJuanだが、Architecturalは彼にとって、より感傷的で内省的、そして抽象的な音楽の側面を探求するためのプロジェクトであり、それは同時に彼の内に本来備わっている二面性の、もうひとつの顔を表現するための場所だ。

Architectural名義でのDJセットもまた、同じように幅広い表現を見せる。まるで包み込むような心地よさ、繊細なニュアンス、そして力強い推進力―それらが共存する体験となるだろう。

—

Architectural is Juan Rico.

For years, the Architectural project remained anonymous until it was revealed to be a new side of Juan Rico, the Asturian artist behind Reeko.

Launched in 2010 with a series of releases on the label of the same name, Architectural has had releases across seminal labels such as R&S, Music Man, Semantica, Delsin, and Non Series. Architectural blends classic techno and cinematic influences with his very modern and stylish interpretations. The music covers a wide spectrum from techno to ambient with a deep bent. Some releases are dubby while others are emotional and melancholy, but all are hypnotic and share an atmospheric vibe. 

As Reeko, Juan was known for a heavy, industrial sound, but Architectural gives him a place to explore a more sentimental, introspective, and abstract side. A place to explore the other side of an inherent duality.

Architectural dj sets cover a similarly wide range: a comforting embrace, a nuanced touch, and a powerful drive...
MAKING: Some nights are for the curious...…

JONATHAN FITOUSSI (LIVE)

フランスの電子音楽史を語る上で欠かせない存在であるJonathan Fitoussi。キャリアの初期は磁気テープのアーカイブ修復に携わり、GRM(音楽研究グループ)の資料を扱う中で、かつての巨匠たちの膨大な作品群に触れることとなる。歴史的録音を保存するという緻密な作業を通して、ミュージックコンクリートや初期の電子音響音楽を形づくった過程と深く向き合うことになった。

かつての伝統を掘り起こし未来へと受け継いで行く活動は、自身のレーベルTransversales Disquesの設立へと繋がる。同レーベルからは、Pierre HenryやLuc Ferrari、Bernard Parmegianiといった巨匠たちが残し、長い間失われていたテープや知られざる音源をリリースしてきた。こうした音源との出会い、そしてFrançois BayleやEliane Radigueといった巨匠たちとの交流は、卓越したプロデューサー／演奏家としての彼の創作に深い影響を与えている。

Fitoussiはアナログ／モジュラー・シンセシスの名手として知られ、さまざまなBuchlaシステムやEMS Synthi AKSといった偉大なマシンを自在に操る優れたライブパフォーマーでもある。彼の音楽は、繊細な音のテクスチャーへの拘りと、リズミックなループ、そしてシネマティックなエモーションを融合させている。

2019年のLabyrinthでは、美しい満月のもと、Synthiを駆使した天空を思わせるクロージングセットを披露した。それは、20年以上にわたる私たちのイベントの歴史のなかでも、最も忘れがたい瞬間のひとつとなった。

そして今年、彼が再び帰ってくる。
今度は新月の夜——何も描かれていない、真っさらなキャンバスへ。
夜空を埋め尽くす星空にシンセサイザーの音が響き渡るだろう。

---

Jonathan Fitoussi occupies an important place in the history of French electronic music. Early in his career, he restored magnetic-tape archives, working with GRM material and absorbing the catalog of key composers. Performing the meticulous task of conserving historical recordings brought him into contact with the practices that defined musique concrète and early electroacoustic work.

This curation of a grand tradition continued with the launch of Transversales Disques, his label that releases lost tapes and obscure recordings from masters such as Pierre Henry, Luc Ferrari, and Bernard Parmegiani. His encounters with this material and the greats–such as François Bayle and Eliane Radigue–have deeply informed his work as a distinguished producer and performer.

Fitoussi is recognized as a master of analogue and modular synthesis and accomplished live performer of the great machines such as various Buchla systems and the EMS Synthi AKS. His work combines a respect for fragile textures of sound with rhythmic looping, cinematic emotion, and vivid color. At the 2019 Labyrinth he performed a celestial closing set with his Synthi to a magnificent full moon, one of the most memorable moments in our two decades plus of events.

This year he returns to play on a new moon night, an empty canvas.

Synths across the stars of a dark-night sky.

caption:
HIYOSHI

ホテルに泊まらずに、Labyrinthの会場内でキャンプする楽しみのひとつは、朝ゆるやかに流れるHiyoshiの音に包まれて目を覚ますことだ。テントで目を覚まし、前夜の疲れでぼんやりした頭を振り払い、コーヒーを飲む。そして「Hiyoshiが始まった。気持ち良いね。今日はきっといい一日になりそうだね」そんな会話があちこちで聞かれる。

HiyoshiはMindgamesを代表するアンビエントDJであり、これまで開催されたすべてのLabyrinthに出演してきた唯一のDJでもある。毎年恒例となった彼の朝のセット、フロアから静かに歌いかけてくる、やさしい目覚ましのような音楽は、Labyrinthの大切な伝統のひとつとなっている。

音楽活動の傍らで、Hiyoshiは病院で働いている。それはアンビエントDJとしての彼の音楽性や役割にも不思議なほどよく似合っている。今年のLabyrinthでもHiyoshiは我々を癒し、労り、私たちはまた新しい一日を迎え入れる。

—

One of the joys of camping at Labyrinth instead of staying at a local inn or hotel is waking up to the sounds of Hiyoshi gently flowing through the campground. Stir from your sleeping bag, shake off the cobwebs from the previous night's exertions, make yourself a coffee. Thinking to yourself—nice, Hiyoshi has started. Today is going to be a good day.

Hiyoshi is the the Mindgames resident ambient dj, the only dj to have played every Labyrinth. His annual morning sets—a gentle alarm clock that sings from the floor—are an important part of the Labyrinth tradition. 

In his other life Hiyoshi works as staff in a hospital, a fitting compliment to his role as an ambient dj. Curing ills, treating tired heads, welcoming the day.

The countdown is ON—we are less than 200 days away from the ultimate bike fest, Sea Otter Australia 2026! To celebrate, Rocky Trail turned the iconic Mogo Trails—the official Home of Sea Otter Australia—into a massive Easter scavenger hunt with a prize pool over over $4,000 AUD! 🐾🥚

Whether you’re a big shredder chasing the ultimate Sea Otter Australia Entry Ticket (race any event!) or have little legs just finding their flow, this is for everyone!

Here’s the play:

PETAR DUNDOV (live)

私たちの多くが、人生において非日常的な「超越体験」を求めている。それは自身の存在を超えた巨大な何かの一部かのような感覚で、宗教や芸術、日々の仕事や人間関係など、さまざまな場面で起こりうるその体験だが、とりわけ音楽を通して得られる「超越体験」はより強く、誰しも気心の知れた仲間たちと同じ音楽に身を委ねて共に高揚する瞬間が記憶に刻まれた経験があるだろう。

エレクトロニック・ミュージックの世界で、そのような「超越」の感覚を呼び起こすアーティストのひとりとして名高いのがクロアチア出身のプロデューサー／DJ、Petar Dundovだ。

彼はこう語る：
「プロデューサー、そしてミュージシャンたる究極の目標は、インスピレーションの世界と現実世界との境界を限りなく曖昧にし、聴き手をその区別できなくなる領域まで持ち上げることだ。音楽には、私たち誰もが本来持っている深い感情を伝える力があるが、私の探求は、その感情を呼び覚まし、ひとつになって共鳴できる場所まで再び導くことである。」

彼がMusic Man Recordsから発表した4枚のアルバムは、その哲学を体現する傑作ばかりだ。複雑に絡み合い、絶えず変化していくメロディによって聴く者を魅了し、深い催眠性へと誘う。

私たちが最後にThe Labyrinthで、Petarのライブを体験してから早くも10年が経ったが、それでも彼の楽曲は、その後も幾度となく誰かのDJセットの中で使われ、フロアにマジックをかけ続けてきた。その瞬間を言葉で説明するのは容易ではないが、空気が変わり、時間の流れが変わり、あたかも全員がひとつの方向に引き寄せられるかのように一気にフロアの一体感が増す。

長い時を経て再びこの場所に戻ってくる私たちのスター、Dundovの帰還を心から歓迎したい。

---

At the end of the day, transcendence, in one form or the other, is what we are all after. That sense of being a part of something above and beyond the self.

We find it in community, religion, and art, but most profoundly we find in it music. And we best find it while listening to live music surrounded by friends.

In the world of eletronic music, few artists trigger feelings of transcendence like the Croatia producer and dj, Peter Dundov.

He says: “My ultimate goal as a producer and musician is to bridge the world of inspiration and physical world to the extent where the listener wouldn't be able to distinguish between the two. Music has this unique property to communicate deep emotions that are inherently in all of us. We just forgot how to use them, and my search is an attempt to revive those emotions where we all resonate as one.” His four albums on Music Man Records are each masterpieces of this philosophy. Hypnotic techno that mesmerizes with complex, shifting melodies.

It's been ten years since we had a chance to hear Petar Dundov live at The Labyrinth surrounded by friends, but he has been present every year with his music. Every time a dj drops a Petar Dundov track, something magical happens on the floor. It's difficult to explain these moments. The atmosphere changes. Time shifts. And people move in different ways, towards one. We celebrate Dundov's long-awaited return.

What a summit! 🤘🚵‍♀️

Before the official racing kicked off, the Sea Otter Australia Industry Summit brought together riders, trail builders and outdoor leaders from across the country for two massive days of ideas, inspiration and connection in Batemans Bay.

From thought-provoking talks to future-focused discussions on trails, tourism, sustainability and innovation, it was all about celebrating the power of two wheels and the people driving the MTB community forward!

A huge thanks to everyone who joined us and helped make it an unforgettable start to Sea Otter Australia. The future of mountain biking is looking stronger than ever, and we can't wait to see what comes next 🔥
