TOBIAS. DOLTZ. (live)

Tobias. Doltz.はドイツと日本の間の新たな邂逅によって生まれたTobiasとDoltzのふたりによるプロジェクトである。

TobiasはこれまでもSieg Über Die SonneとのDandy Jack、Max Loderbauerとの実験的ユニットNSI、すでにLabyrinthでは馴染みとなったAtom™との即興ライブテクノプロジェクトなど、数々の先駆的プロジェクトを生み出し、これらのコラボレーションは長年彼の活動の中核を形成してきた。ミュージシャン、パフォーマー、サウンドエンジニアとして、音を「共有された探求の実践」と捉える思想の持ち主で、30年以上にわたりドイツのエレクトロニックミュージックシーンの中心で活動を続け、音の可能性と境界を絶えず押し広げてきた存在だ。

一方で日本を拠点とするDoltzは、ハードコアパンクバンドのドラマーとして活動を開始。その後、繊細なアンビエント作品を手掛けるプロデューサーへと歩みを進めた。実験的アンビエント作品には脈動する生命感が宿り、その感覚はDJ Nobu主宰レーベルBittaから発表したInception EPや最新アルバムFinal Traceといった力強いテクノ作品にも受け継がれている。近年はパワフルで表現力豊かなライブパフォーマンスによって、国内外で熱心な支持を獲得し続けている。

そんなふたりによるTobias. Doltz.としては、DelsinよりVersus、Frontiers of Scienceの2作品を発表。エレクトロニックミュージックにおけるリズム、空間、サウンドのあらゆる領域を探求した傑作と言える。卓越したライブパフォーマーでもある二人が、今年のLabyrinthではサウンドシステムの限界へ挑むパフォーマンスを披露することになるだろう。

---

Tobias. Doltz. is a new collaborative project between two new friends, Tobias and Doltz.

Collaboration has long formed a core for Tobias, leading to numerous projects such as Dandy Jack with Sieg Über Die Sonne, his live improvised techno project with Atom™, and his experimental work with Max Loderbauer as NSI. As a musician, performer, and sound engineer, he believes deeply in sound as a shared exploratory practice. For over three decades, Tobias has worked at the center of the German electronic scene, constantly exploring and pushing the boundaries of sound.

Doltz, based in Japan, began exploring his boundaries of sound first as a drummer in a hardcore punk band and then as a producer in delicate ambient albums. His experimental ambient releases have a pulsating sense of life to them, a trait he then applied to techno, such as on his “Inception EP” and new album “Final Trace”, two fierce records for DJ Nobu’s label Bitta. Over the past few year Doltz has won a loyal following in Japan and abroad for his powerful and expressive live performances.

As Tobias. Doltz., these two highly instinctive producers have released two brilliant albums for Delsin, “Versus” and “Frontiers of Science”, albums that explore the full spectrum of electronic rhythm, space, and sound. And as brilliant live performers, they are sure to push the Labyrinth sound system to its limits.

PETER VAN HOESEN

Peter Van Hoesenは数十年に渡るキャリアの中で、エレクトロニックミュージックのあらゆる領域を横断してきたが、この1年で更に野心的にプロジェクトに挑んでいる。そのひとつとして、クラブミュージック以外のシーンでも映画史に残る名作「ターミーネイター2・ジャッジメントデイ」のサウンドトラックを新たにスコアリングし、Melbourne Electronic Sound Studio（MESS）Synthesiser Ensembleと共に豪州メルボルン、シドニー、キャンベラで開催された上映会でライブ演奏を行ったりと、表現の幅を更に広げている。

Mindgamesでも2008年の初出演以来、レジデントDJとして全てのLabyrinthに出演し、その他クラブでのプレイも含め説明不要の多くの軌跡を残して来た存在だが、一昨年はAtom™とのユニットSYNC.として、イベント最終日を締めくくる伝説的な7時間のライブ・パフォーマンスを敢行。昨年のLabyrinthでは実験的なドラムンベースへの嗜好性を強調し、ブロークンリズムにフォーカスしたセットを披露。その進化は止まらない。SYNCとしてライブのために制作された楽曲の一部は現在3部作のEPとしてリリース予定で、その第一弾”One out of Three”がBandcampで公開されている。

そして今年、Peter Van Hoesenは、今回の核とも言えるピークタイムに登場する。
2日目、日曜日の夜にフロアの熱気が最高潮となり、まさにレイヴとなるだろう。

—

Peter Van Hoesen's multi-decade career spans the full spectrum of electronic music, but this past year he expanded his repertoire for perhaps his most ambitious project yet. He re-scored the soundtrack for the iconic film, "Terminator 2: Judgment Day", and then conducted live performance of this new soundtrack with the Melbourne Electronic Sound Studio (MESS) Synthesiser Ensemble at series of screenings in Melbourne, Sydney, and Canberra.

In a way, Peter has been providing the soundtrack for Mindgames for almost 20 years now. Since his initial performances in 2008, Peter Van Hoesen has been a resident dj for Mindgames, playing every Labyrinth event in addition to a number of Tokyo clubs shows. Last year he showcased his interest in experimental drum & bass with a set tightly focused on broken rhythms, and the previous year he closed the final day with Atom™ as SYNC. in a legendary 7-hour live performance. (Some of that music that was created for that set is now being released as a series of three EP's on Bandcamp, and the first release, "One out of Three," is now available.)

This year Peter Van Hoesen is returning to play a style right at the core of the event: Sunday night peak-energy rave.

KAITO (live)

—

ドイツを代表する伝統的な音楽レーベルKompaktを知ってるのであれば、KaitoことHiroshi Watanabeの名前もご存知でしょう。トランス〜ハウスを横断する作品となったSpecial Life、Hundred Million Light Years、Trust、Until the End of Timeは当時の名盤であり、またアンビエントのシリーズであるSpecial Love、Hundred Million Love Years、Trust Less、Less Time Until the Endもまた同様に名作と言える。彼のシグネチャーサウンドは旋律に溢れ感情豊かであり、アンビエントなサウンドスケープの中にダンスリズムが織り込まれている。

2019年には自身のレーベルCosmic Signaturesを立ち上げ、アンビエント作品を中心に数多くの素晴らしいリリースを発表した。

卓越した実力のミュージシャンであり、名門Berklee College of Music卒業生でもあるHiroshi Watanabeは、多彩なシンセサイザー、ハードウェア・シーケンサー、エフェクト、ライブキーボードの演奏を駆使した素晴らしいライブパフォーマンスを披露する。

その近年の活動に感銘を受け、Balance 2025にKaito名義でのライブ出演を依頼したが、根源的なリズム、ハーモニーを駆使し、月が煌々と輝く夜に、オーディエンスと共に探求したライブセッションは、個人的には2025年のアクトの中でもって最も純粋な音楽体験だった。

本日、その日の特別な録音音源をSouldCloudよりリリースする。

“As we gather for this live session...”

—

If you know the history of the legendary German music label Kompakt, you know Kaito, aka Hiroshi Watanabe. The trance-house albums Special Life, Hundred Million Light Years, Trust, and Until the End of Time are classics of the day, as are the ambient versions of these albums: Special Love, Hundred Million Love Years, Trust Less, and Less Time Until the End. His signature sound is melodic and deeply emotive, with dance rhythms embedded in ambient soundscapes.

In 2019 he set up his own label, Cosmic Signatures, where he has put out a large number of wonderful releases with a focus on ambient albums.

A deeply accomplished musician and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music, Hiroshi Watanabe creates superb live performances, where he utilizes a wide range of synths, hardware sequencer, FX units, and live keyboard playing.

Inspired by his recent work, we invited him to play live as Kaito at the Balance 2025.

Just speaking personally, his Balance live session was my purest musical memory of 2025. He tapped into a fundamental rhthym and key, which he then explored with the audience on that beautiful moon-lit night. We are happy to share a recording of that very special live session with all of you today on our SoundCloud. Thank you everyone.

“As we gather for this live session...”

鏡民 / Kyomi 

東京のシーンを代表する若き才能のひとり、鏡民（Kyomi）は、音楽通や玄人の間で急激にファンを増やしている注目のアーティストで、卓越したセンスを持ち、ジャンルの枠に囚われず自由にジャンルを行き来する。

彼女が素晴らしいとされる理由は、ダンスフロアからの期待値やトレンドに縛られることなく、常にサイケデリックな感覚を失わずに自身のプレイするところであり、私たちもそこに魅力を感じている。

昨年のBalanceに出演し、ノンビートのアンビエントからゆったりとしたグルーヴのFunkへと幅広い展開のサウンドジャーニーを披露したが、その非常に印象深いセットを今回共有するので是非聴いてほしい。

The Labyrinthへ初の出演となる鏡民を心から歓迎したい。

—

鏡民 (aka Kyomi) is a young, new talent in Tokyo who is quickly building a fan base here among true music heads. She has a natural musician’s ear for music and hovers in a genre-less space without borders. We love how she isn’t tied down by expectations or trends and is always psychedelic.

She played for Mindgames for the first time at last year’s Balance, and that deeply impressive set showed off her skills going from beatless ambient beginnings to a wide-ranging journey of slow-grooving funk. We loved what she did that day, and are pleased to share the recording of that set today.

This will be her Labyrinth debut. Welcome, Kyomi.

DONATO DOZZY

説明不要ながら、Donato Dozzyは単なるMindgamesのレジデントDJではなく、2007年に初めてLabyrinthへ出演して以来共に歩み、築き上げてきた大切な家族であり、かけがえのないパートナーである。出会った頃から今に至るまで、Donatoは個人でテクノを制作する時も、多彩なコラボレーションで幅広いジャンルを探求する時も、エレクトロニック・ミュージックを代表する最も個性的な表現者のひとりとして飛躍的に成長を遂げてきた。

ご存知の通り、彼の最もよく知られたプロジェクトは、朋友NeelとのユニットVoices of the Lakeである。アンビエントとヒプノティック・テクノを自在に横断するこのプロジェクトは高い評価を得ている。一方、Batuとの新たな共作では、!K7 RecordsからアルバムExhaleをリリース。現在の彼が強く魅了されている、サウンドシステム・カルチャーをルーツに持つブロークンリズムやビートを探求した作品となっている。

レジデントDJとして、毎年異なる時間帯で新たな表現領域に挑戦することがその役割とも言えるが、Donatoが近年実に幅広いジャンルや創作へと活動の幅を広げてきたことを踏まえ、今年はジャンルの垣根を取り払った、完全に自由なセットを披露してもらう絶好のタイミングだと考えている。

今回のDonato Dozzyは、日曜の午後にフリースタイル・セットを披露。ディープ・テクノやディープ・ハウスから、変拍子を駆使したフラクチャード・リズムまで、あらゆる音楽が自由に行き交う、境界のない空間を楽しませてくれるだろう。

REEKO

—

...そして、Juan RicoはReekoでもある。

25年以上にわたってDJとして活動しており、世界的にも屈指のテクノDJのひとりとして知られている。2003年には自身の作品を発表する場としてレーベル Mental Disorderを設立し、2010年には Oscar Mulero、Christian Wünsch、Exium とともにスペインのコレクティブPoleGroupを立ち上げた。

近年のReekoは、DelsinやSamuraiからの作品に代表されるように、変則リズムや実験的なブロークンリズムを追求しており、これらの作品は、テクノ、ドラムンベース、エレクトロニカが交差する実験的な領域、という位置付けだ。儀式的とも言える雰囲気を纏いつつ、直感的では捉えにくい重厚なエネルギーを引き出している。

最新アルバムCrytophonyについて、Reekoは次のように語っている。

「Crytophonyは、音がどのように情報を隠し、示唆し、あるいは明らかにするのかを、象徴的・感覚的・儀式的な観点から探求した作品だ。実際のところ、音楽の中に隠された意図したメッセージは無い。しかしながら最終的なプロセスを経て変容した奇妙な声が存在している。」

私たちにとって、近年のReeko作品は、この数年間のテクノにおける最も独創的で刺激的な探求のひとつだ。そして彼のDJセットは、精密でありながら幻覚的な感覚を伴い、強烈なインパクトを与える。

Reekoは長年に渡り独特の技術を極めたマスターとして評価されてきたが、近年さらに新たな芸術的高みに到達したと感じている。今年のLabyrinthではその創造性を形作る二つの側面を、互いに結びついた二つのセットとして披露してもらうという特別な企画を依頼した。

Reeko = Juan Rico = Architectural

彼の中に存在する、二つの異なる表情を是非体験して欲しい。

—

...and Juan Rico is Reeko.

Reeko has been dj’ing for 25+ years and is one of the world’s elite techno dj’s. He founded Mental Disorder in 2003, a platform first for his own work, and launched the Spanish collective PoleGroup in 2010 together with Oscar Mulero, Christian Wünsch, and Exium.

Recently Reeko has been exploring alternative time signatures and experimental broken rhythms on records for Delsin and Samurai. These records sit at the experimental intersection of techno, drum & bass and electronica. Their ritualistic vibes tap into non-obvious forms of heavy energy.

Of his most recent album Crytophony, Reeko says “Crytophony explores how sound can conceal, suggest or reveal information in a symbolic, sensory or ritualistic way….There are no hidden messages in the music, but there are strange voices that, after the final process, sound transformed.”

The recent Reeko records represent, for us, the most distinctive and exciting explorations in techno over the past few years. And Reeko dj sets are precise and hallucinatory–they hit hard.

Reeko has been recognized as a master of his craft for decades, but we feel he recently has hit new artistic peaks, so we asked him to do something very special for Labyrinth: share both sides of his creative equation via two connected sets.

Reeko = Juan Rico = Architectural.

caption:
The Labyrinthでは長年ほぼ同じ音響システムを使い続けて、細かなアップデートを重ねて参りましたが、今年はサウンド面で大幅なアップグレードが実施される予定で、非常にワクワクしております。これは10年以上を振り返っても、サウンドシステムに施す最大の変更になります。

まず、昨年のLabyrinthでは、Funktion-Oneの最新モデルをインフィル（補助的スピーカー）として試験的に導入したところ、その自然で滑らかな音質に大きな感銘を受けました。本来であれば、システム全体をEVOシリーズに置き換えたかったのですが、国内関連会社と英国のFunktion-Oneチームと数週間に渡り調査と議論を重ねた結果、必要なスピーカーが現状日本には存在しないという結論に至りました。

しかしながら、今回は幸いなことに、日本のMeta Audioが不足していた機材を特別に追加発注してくれたことにより、Funktion-Oneの本社が我々のイベントに間に合うよう、迅速に製造と配送を行い、そして今、すべてのスピーカーが無事に日本に到着し、来週に向けて開梱作業が進められております。

低音域については、従来のF218とInfrabassのベース・ビンを、F121とF124を非対称に組み合わせたスタックに置き換えます。各スタックが異なる周波数帯にフォーカスすることで、干渉を最小限に抑える設計です。中高域は、従来のRES5に代わってEVO7とEVO6を導入。そしてセンターのインフィルには、Funktion-Oneの最新モデルであるEVO2を使用します。

イベントのあらゆる瞬間に完璧な音を届けることは最も難しく、同時に最も楽しい要素のひとつです。完全に新しいシステムに刷新された来週末、どんな音響体験が創出されるでしょう？　この新しいスピーカーで組み上げられたサウンドシステムと3日間のストーリーを、皆さんと共有できることを心から楽しみにしております。

—

After many years of using essentially the same speakers, we are excited to make a huge sonic upgrade this year. This will be the biggest change we have made to the system in over a decade.

We experimented with Funktion-One EVO’s as infills at Labyrinth last year and were impressed by how natural and smooth they sounded. We wanted to replace the entire system with EVO’s, but after weeks of brainstorming with teams here and with the Funktion-One team in the UK, we realized that the combination of speakers we needed were simply not here.

Fortunately, Meta Audio put in a special order for the missing pieces of the puzzle, and Funktion-One put these speakers into rush production and delivery in time for the event. We are happy to report that all the speakers have arrived in Japan and are being unboxed for next week!

For the bass, we are replacing the F218/Infrabass bass bins with an asymmetrical stack of F121/F124 bass bins with each stack focusing on a different frequency range for minimal interference. For the mid-highs, EVO7’s and EVO6’s will be replacing the RES5’s. And for center infills, we will be using the newest models, the EVO2’s.

Getting the sound just right for every moment of the event is one of our most challenging and enjoyable responsibilities, so we’re excited to see what we can accomplish next weekend with this new system...

Green Art es un reconocido proyecto de artesanía botánica liderado por Sandra Guinart y Oscar Gallego, especializado en el diseño de mini jardines autónomos y kokedamas. 
Con base en Azuqueca de Henares y una intensa actividad en Madrid capital, su propuesta se centra en crear experiencias de desconexión y bienestar que enseñan a modelar la naturaleza con las manos. 
En esta edición de BROCANTE, impartirán dos experiencias vegetales únicas: el taller “Kokedama”, donde los asistentes descubrirán este arte japonés sostenible aprendiendo a diseñar paso a paso un ecosistema único con musgo y barro; y el taller “Kusamono”, una técnica tradicional japonesa que transforma pequeñas plantas silvestres, musgos y elementos naturales en auténticos paisajes en miniatura cargados de poesía visual.
El taller es gratuito, pero se paga un pequeño importe de 15€ para cubrir los materiales.

The Labyrinth is a Collaborative Art Project.

It could never be designed or planned. It could only be built organically by an entire community who believe, more or less, in the same thing.

We believe in the power of ritual and myth, the purity of sound, and the magic of fairy tales.

We believe in you. And we thank you for believing in us.

Collaborative art projects built to celebrate life by local communities united in shared beliefs have a name in Japanese.

Matsuri.

And fairy tales are whimsical stories of enchantment.

Thank you for joining and building our matsuri together.

And thank you for listening to our little fairy tale...

...we look forward to the next telling.

---

The Labyrinthは、共創によるアートプロジェクトです。

誰かひとりがデザインしたり計画するものではなく、同じ想いを共有するコミュニティによって形成され、まるで生き物かのように有機的に形作られます。

私たちは、音楽に対する純粋な気持ちや、フェスティバルにおける儀式や神話性、そこで起きる魔法のような御伽話など、スピリチュアルな出来事や精神を信じてます。

それと共に、コミュニティを形成した皆さんのことも信じてますし、信じて参加してくれた皆さんには心から感謝しております。

日本では、共通の信念で結ばれたコミュニティが、何かを祝うために共創することを「祭」と呼びますが、The Labyrinthはまさに「祭」であり、共に築いて頂き、ありがとうございました。

また、気まぐれで魔法と幻想に満ちた御伽話を最後まで聴いて頂き、ありがとうございました。

✨TALLER EXPERIMENTAL ✨
“TRAMAR EL CUERPO”
Isabel Moltó es una artista visual e investigadora cuya práctica se sitúa en la intersección entre la materia, la memoria y la reparación, explorando el gesto del remiendo como un acto tanto poético como político. 
Es la creadora detrás de CASAMADRE, un proyecto conceptual que dialoga con materiales como el textil, la cerámica y los objetos encontrados para entrelazar lo íntimo con lo estructural. 
En esta edición de BROCANTE, además de contar con su propio espacio expositivo donde mostrará su particular universo plástico, impartirá el taller experimental “Tramar el cuerpo”. En esta sesión, los asistentes aprenderán técnicas de creación textil enfocadas en diseñar joyería de autor (broches, amuletos o collares) a partir de hilos, cordones y tejidos. Una propuesta íntima y reflexiva para elegir qué partes del cuerpo mostrar u ocultar, creando una pieza única lista para llevar puesta.

THE LABYRINTH 2025 TIMETABLE

Laneway Festival is committed to creating a welcoming, safe, and accessible space for everyone. Thank you to everyone who shared feedback from previous Laneway events. It’s helped shape the work we’ve been doing to improve our access services across all sites.

WHAT’S CHANGING FOR 2027
→ Access & Inclusion leadership: Building on our work with access consultants, we’ve added a dedicated Access & Inclusion Manager to our national team. They bring lived experience and extensive event operations expertise, and they’re involved in production and planning at every stage.
→ Expanded on-site support: Friendly, disability-aware trained Laneway Helpers and Crowd Car stationed at Info Hubs, Accessible Viewing Platforms, accessible entry & exits and roving the site to assist you.

We continue to build on our access services and infrastructure. To see the start of our evolving plans, head to the Accessibility page on the Laneway website:
→ Low Sensory Space: Dedicated low-lit, quiet spaces for patrons experiencing sensory overload to decompress and self-regulate. 
→ Viewing Platforms & Viewing Areas: Elevated viewing decks at key stages providing clear sightlines and space for mobility-aid users, accompanied by ground-level Accessible Seating Viewing Areas enclosed for safety.
→ Maps & Planning: City-specific accessibility maps & info guides published before the festival to help you plan your day.

caption: Just two more days til Grinduro PA… ✌️

💜😈🇮🇹It is with great sadness 💔 that we have decided to cancel Grinduro Italia.

Unfortunately, this format simply hasn’t attracted enough interest or commitment from the riding community it is meant for.

One question will always stay with us: would people have signed up at the last minute? Maybe they would have, maybe not. We’ll never know. What we do know is that it’s impossible to build an event without the support of the very people it’s created for.

Over the past few years, we’ve shared so many unforgettable moments together, and for that we are truly grateful.

Don’t worry, everyone who has already registered will be refunded.

Thank you all for being part of the Grinduro Italia journey. We really hope to see you again soon.💜😈🇮🇹

We are pleased to be introducing two new designers today as unfortunately two others have pulled out /

Studio Liinea, directed by designer Silvia Kostandini is an emerging spatial practice in Aotearoa, New Zealand, that develops limited-edition collectible pieces and spatial compositions that blur the line between function and art. 

Through considered production, material poetics, and spatial sensitivity, Silvia designs objects that prioritise connection, narrative and innovation. The exhibited collection Isola, in Italian 'Island' draws from the heritage of the designer and the landscape of Aotearoa, shaped by volcanic grounds, black sand beaches, and tectonic formations. Monolithic forms are reinterpreted through contemporary geometry, creating a sense of presence rooted in everyday rituals. 

Each piece uses locality as a conceptual framework, grounding the design in context through form and material memory. Objects such as Vaso, Vassoio, and Luce support rituals of holding, containing, and illuminating, quietly reshaping atmosphere through sculptural presence and encouraging slower interaction within domestic spaces. All pieces are handmade locally.

Rupert Herring is exhibiting with us for Makers Market Edition 3.0 /

Rupert is a designer and artist whose practice explores transformation, material potential and the value of what already exists. Drawing on his skills as a cabinetmaker and his knowledge of materials, Herring creates distinctive objects from discarded timber, offcuts and found materials.

Central to his practice is the process of deconstruction and reconstruction. Through cutting, shaping and reassembling, Herring transforms society’s cast-offs into considered new forms, challenging preconceived ideas around waste, usefulness and value. His work often carries a sense of nostalgia, responding to a culture of disposability and excess while considering how objects can remain 
relevant over time.

Rather than imposing a predetermined outcome, Herring allows the qualities and limitations of each material to help guide the final form. This approach creates a dialogue between an object’s past life and its new purpose.

At its core, Herring’s practice is about minimising waste and making use of what already exists, 
revealing unexpected beauty and potential through thoughtful material transformation.

@hollidayherring

caption:
Featuring at next weekend's event – Talking Chairs explores the dynamic of interaction; reframing a set of two seats into an active dialogue within a space.

Designed by Klaus Todt as part of Collection 42, the pair challenges traditional seating by examining how geometry can express relationship, connection, and shifting perspective.

Defined by clean angles and a bold, block-like silhouette, each chair is built from complementary pastel forms that play off one another. The design’s true distinction lies in its adaptability: depending on how the pair is positioned, the backrests lean intentionally toward each other or angle away. This duality invites quiet interpretations of affection or aversion, allowing the arrangement to change the energy of the room.

Designed for interiors, Talking Chairs offers an expressive seating pair for open living areas,
galleries, or foyers. It brings a sculptural presence to the floor while proving that furniture can spark conversation through form alone.

Adia Ma of Studio Yun joins us at Makers Market Edition 3.0 this weekend /

Studio Yun is an independent ceramic studio in Orewa, north of Tāmaki Makaurau, founded by Adia and Yuan, partners originally from China whose practices bring together hand-building and wheel-throwing.

Adia came to ceramics after studying in the UK and Switzerland and working in events and marketing across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia. Exposure to different cultures and approaches to design shaped a perspective not tied to any single tradition. After settling in New Zealand, she taught herself ceramics through experimentation in her home studio. Since 2022, her work has received awards and finalist selections across New Zealand and was exhibited at 1000 Vases in Paris in 2024.

Yuan’s practice is grounded in tradition. Trained in Jingdezhen, China’s historic porcelain centre, he apprenticed under Master Yu, developing a disciplined approach to throwing, proportion and finishing.

In 2025, their practices came together as Studio Yun, combining experimentation with traditional ceramic knowledge. Every piece is built or thrown, glazed and fired in Orewa in small batches, using glazes developed in-studio. 

Their current Cloud collection celebrates subtle variations between individual pieces, creating functional objects designed to be used, lived with and kept.

We are thrilled to welcome jeweler and designer Shannen Young to Makers Market /

Based in Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland, Shannen Young is a multidisciplinary artist working across jewellery, fashion and textile-based adornment. Her practice is guided by intuition, experimentation and play, resulting in tactile works that explore the possibilities of material, form and personal expression.

Young’s pieces move freely between object and accessory, costume and sculpture. Her approach embraces the unexpected, allowing materials and processes to influence each work as it develops. This sense of spontaneity gives her pieces a distinctive character, balancing considered craftsmanship with a playful and exploratory sensibility.

Drawing from the languages of jewellery, fashion and contemporary craft, Young is interested in how objects interact with the body and transform through wear. Her multidisciplinary practice challenges traditional ideas of adornment, creating expressive 
pieces that can be worn, handled or appreciated as sculptural objects in their own right.

We are pleased to add returning designer Ian Lawson to Makers Market in October /

Ian is a woodturner and wood carver based in Tūranganui-a-Kiwa/Gisborne and Tamaki Makaurau / Auckland. His practice is deeply shaped by a strong family legacy in woodworking, art, and arboriculture. 

Ian’s approach balances tradition and innovation. He honours time-tested woodturning techniques passed down through generations while confidently exploring contemporary forms and finishes. This blend of heritage craftsmanship and modern experimentation allows him to create pieces that feel both grounded and fresh.

Working primarily with locally sourced timber – often from fallen trees – Ian emphasises sustainability and respect for the natural environment. His work celebrates the inherent beauty of wood, highlighting distinctive grain patterns, textures, and natural imperfections.

Returning designer Ian Lawson joins us again at Makers Market next weekend /

Ian is a woodturner and wood carver based in Tūranganui-a-Kiwa/Gisborne and Tamaki Makaurau / Auckland. His practice is deeply shaped by a strong family legacy in woodworking, art, and arboriculture. 

Ian’s approach balances tradition and innovation. He honours time-tested woodturning techniques passed down through generations while confidently exploring contemporary forms and finishes. This blend of heritage craftsmanship and modern experimentation allows him to create pieces that feel both grounded and fresh.

Working primarily with locally sourced timber – often from fallen trees – Ian emphasises sustainability and respect for the natural environment. His work celebrates the inherent beauty of wood, highlighting distinctive grain patterns, textures, and natural imperfections. 

@lawsonwoodturning

Jino Jeong's presentation in March at Good Form included polished and raw vessels and teapots with his signature neutral finishes and hand painted colour glazes. 

Jino’s work has been widely recognised through major awards, most notably winning the Premier Award at the 2023 Portage Ceramic Awards – Aotearoa’s foremost national ceramics event – for his piece Celestial Thread: A Tapestry of Sunshine and Spiderwebs. He has also received honours including Portage awards and national prizes at the Royal Easter Show and Wai Clay National Ceramics Award, reflecting his sustained excellence and evolving practice.

In addition to his studio work, Jino contributes to the wider ceramic community as a tutor, sharing his skills and passion for clay with students and enthusiasts across Auckland.

Alongside her studio practice, Soo Jeong has facilitated jewelry workshops that encourage

caption:
Designer Klaus Todt joins us the upcoming October event /

After 16 years of designing and crafting bespoke interiors throughout New Zealand through his joinery practice, Living Design, Klaus Todt returns to his first passion: furniture. With this comes K.TODT Design, a practice he originally established in Germany more than 35 years ago.

Guided by a lifelong fascination with materials, proportion and craftsmanship, Klaus thoughtfully designs each piece to outlast trends and be lived with for generations. K.TODT Design approaches furniture as functional sculpture, balancing purpose with a strong architectural and sculptural presence, the collection reflects a commitment to craftsmanship, architectural thinking and enduring design. Created to be both lived with and admired, each piece is conceived as a lasting object rather than a response to temporary trends.

Alistair is a cross-disciplinary design and maker from Tāmaki Makaurau. His creative practice is driven by a keen interest in materiality and process, along with a deep appreciation for the value of collaboration in the design process.

With a background in studying architecture, he practices across a wide range of disciplines from small, tactile product design to large experiential public installations. Being directly engaged with the fabrication of pieces at any of these scales is a critical factor in his process.

In this context, Alistair has been working with other designers and directly with clients on bespoke furniture pieces since 2017. At Makers Market he will be sharing a handful of recent designs that mark a shift into made-to-order pieces.

caption:
Jeweler and designer Shannen Young joins us at this weekend's Makers Market /

Based in Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland, Shannen Young is a multidisciplinary artist working across jewellery, fashion and textile-based adornment. Her practice is guided by intuition, experimentation and play, resulting in tactile works that explore the possibilities of material, form and personal expression.

Young’s pieces move freely between object and accessory, costume and sculpture. Her approach embraces the unexpected, allowing materials and processes to influence each work as it develops. This sense of spontaneity gives her pieces a distinctive character, balancing considered craftsmanship with a playful and exploratory sensibility.

Drawing from the languages of jewellery, fashion and contemporary craft, Young is interested in how objects interact with the body and transform through wear. Her multidisciplinary practice challenges traditional ideas of adornment, creating expressive 
pieces that can be worn, handled or appreciated as sculptural objects in their own right.

caption:
Craig Spencer will be presenting a new range of bespoke lamps at Makers Market next month /

Craig is a New Zealand–born ceramicist based in Auckland, working across New Zealand and Australia. With over 20 years’ experience in interior design throughout Australasia and Singapore, his ceramic practice is grounded in a refined understanding of space, proportion, and materiality.

Since discovering ceramics in 2018, he has developed a distinctive body of wheel-thrown and slab-built work characterised by clean architectural lines and quiet restraint. His inspiration draws from both architecture and the natural environment — from modernist structures and built form to landscape, light, and organic texture. Rather than being defined by a single influence, his work evolves through accumulated experience, learned traditions, and an ongoing exploration of material.

Now working as a qualified metal fabricator supporting the architectural and interior design 
industries, he launched Studio Thackeray in 2026 as an experimental outlet to create with unconventional methods free from client constraints.

His design practice focuses on celebrating the inherent beauty in metal through texture, raw 
finishes, and traditional forms. He draws inspiration from Japanese and American woodworking, aiming to apply the same grounded design language to metal objects. He works with steel, brass, and aluminium to create unique sculptural furniture pieces and 
homewares.

Particularly interested in tactility, Roy's practice explores how weight, temperature, and texture

Introducing Adia Ma of Studio Yun who joins us at Makers Market Edition 3.0 /

Studio Yun is an independent ceramic studio in Orewa, north of Tāmaki Makaurau, founded by Adia and Yuan, partners originally from China whose practices bring together hand-building and wheel-throwing.

Adia came to ceramics after studying in the UK and Switzerland and working in events and marketing across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia. Exposure to different cultures and approaches to design shaped a perspective not tied to any single tradition. After settling in New Zealand, she taught herself ceramics through experimentation in her home studio. Since 2022, her work has received awards and finalist selections across New Zealand and was exhibited at 1000 Vases in Paris in 2024.

Yuan’s practice is grounded in tradition. Trained in Jingdezhen, China’s historic porcelain centre, he apprenticed under Master Yu, developing a disciplined approach to throwing, proportion and finishing.

In 2025, their practices came together as Studio Yun, combining experimentation with traditional ceramic knowledge. Every piece is built or thrown, glazed and fired in Orewa in small batches, using glazes developed in-studio. 

Their current Cloud collection celebrates subtle variations between individual pieces, creating functional objects designed to be used, lived with and kept.

caption:
Introducing designer Rupert Herring who joins us for Makers Market Edition 3.0 /

Rupert is a designer and artist whose practice explores transformation, material potential and the value of what already exists. Drawing on his skills as a cabinetmaker and his knowledge of materials, Herring creates distinctive objects from discarded timber, offcuts and found materials.

Central to his practice is the process of deconstruction and reconstruction. Through cutting, shaping and reassembling, Herring transforms society’s cast-offs into considered new forms, challenging preconceived ideas around waste, usefulness and value. His work often carries a sense of nostalgia, responding to a culture of disposability and excess while considering how objects can remain 
relevant over time.

Rather than imposing a predetermined outcome, Herring allows the qualities and limitations of each material to help guide the final form. This approach creates a dialogue between an object’s past life and its new purpose.

At its core, Herring’s practice is about minimising waste and making use of what already exists, 
revealing unexpected beauty and potential through thoughtful material transformation.

Roy Duyndam is a California-born, Aotearoa-raised furniture maker and designer based in Ōtautahi. After studying illustration at Whitman College in Washington, USA, he returned to NZ and apprenticed as a fabricator.

Now working as a qualified metal fabricator supporting the architectural and interior design 
industries, he launched Studio Thackeray in 2026 as an experimental outlet to create with unconventional methods free from client constraints.

His design practice focuses on celebrating the inherent beauty in metal through texture, raw 
finishes, and traditional forms. He draws inspiration from Japanese and American woodworking, aiming to apply the same grounded design language to metal objects. He works with steel, brass, and aluminium to create unique sculptural furniture pieces and 
homewares.

Particularly interested in tactility, his practice explores how weight, temperature, and texture can influence emotion. He designs, fabricates, and finishes each unique piece by hand.

Josephine Jelicich is the maker behind these stunning walnut chopping boards, designed with a strong profile and endearing form. We are excited to see some of these at the upcoming October market. 

Josephine has built a diverse career spanning furniture making, teaching, exhibition installation, and arts production. She has worked as a technician for galleries and institutions, taught woodworking at The Warren Workshop, and now runs her own independent furniture and object-making practice. 

Alongside commissioned furniture, she develops personal projects that investigate sculptural form and domestic space and has exhibited her work in galleries including @objectspace, Precinct 35 and Laree Payne Gallery. We are pleased to announce that Craig Spencer will return to Makers Market in October, featuring lamps and limited edition pieces. 

@spencerceramics

Craig is a New Zealand–born ceramicist based in Auckland, working across New Zealand and Australia. 
With over 20 years’ experience in interior design throughout Australasia and Singapore, his ceramic practice is grounded in a refined understanding of space, proportion, and materiality.

Since discovering ceramics in 2018, he has developed a distinctive body of wheel-thrown and slab-built work characterised by clean architectural lines and quiet restraint. His inspiration draws from both architecture and the natural environment — from modernist structures and built form to landscape, light, and organic texture. Rather than being defined by a single influence, his work evolves through accumulated experience, learned traditions, and an ongoing exploration of material.

Grounded in the natural qualities of clay, each piece balances precision with the visible trace of the maker’s hand. By bringing together contemporary design sensibilities with time-honoured techniques, Craig creates ceramic collections, art objects, and bespoke lighting for a variety of private clients as well as large international brands, including Aesop. His work is guided by craftsmanship, material integrity, and a genuine love of making, resulting in pieces that are purposeful, enduring, and harmonious within interior spaces.

Introducing Giora Dan, who joins us for Makers Market Edition 3.0 in October

Giora Dan moved to Aotearoa in 1997 and soon made it his home. An avid traveller with a deep interest in people and place, Giora worked as a freelance photographer for more than two decades, both in New Zealand and internationally. His social documentary photography has been published in titles including Smithsonian, Geo and New Zealand Geographic. His 
commitment to social and environmental issues also led him to produce work supporting organisations such as UNESCO, Save the Children and Fair Trade.

During the Covid pandemic, Giora embraced a new direction, retraining as a joiner and cabinet maker before establishing BurntWood, a small creative woodwork studio based in Ōtautahi, Christchurch.

Every BurntWood piece is handcrafted using sustainably sourced timber. Much of the wood is 
reclaimed, bringing its own history and character, while other timber comes from residential tree 
removals or sustainably managed forests certified by MPI.

Using lamination techniques, Giora creates furniture and objects inspired by the braided rivers, mountains and dunes of Aotearoa. His stitched timber works introduce a bolder, more organic quality, while thoughtful lighting adds depth to lamps and sculptural pieces. His work balances craftsmanship with a strong connection to the natural landscape.

caption:
We are pleased to add returning designer Sara Santoro, who joins us for the October Makers Market /

Sara Santoro is a Hawke’s Bay–based creative whose naturally dyed woven art and homewares are crafted from her small garden studio. With a Bachelor of Design in Communication Design from Victoria University of Wellington (1996) and further study in Landscape Design since 2019, Sara’s practice reflects a thoughtful blending of disciplines, grounded in a deep respect for landscape, materiality, and sustainable processes.

Her discovery of botanical dyeing became a pivotal moment, uniting her long-held passions for colour, interiors, and the natural world. Working primarilywith undyed, New Zealand–grown and processed wool—often repurposing thread waste—alongside raw European flax linen yarns, Sara embraces a slow, considered approach to making. Each fibre is naturally dyed by hand using plant materials harvested from her garden or foraged locally, ensuring every piece carries a strong connection to place.

Sara’s process is intuitive and exploratory. She delights in the alchemy of dyeing and weaving—
blending tones, layering textures, and allowing the materials to guide the final form. The result is work that is both beautiful and functional, designed to bring quiet, everyday joy. Alongside her Loom Studio practice, she continues her landscape design work, balancing digital precision with tactile creativity.

Introducing Sha Ganjali who joins us for Makers Market Edition 3.0 /

With a background in interior design and painting, Sha Ganjali’s creative foundation has always been rooted in form, space, and materiality. Over time, she found her deepest connection through working with clay — a medium that continues to challenge and ground 
her.

Her practice is centred around hand-building sculptural forms, often led by intuition rather 
than predetermined design. She works closely with the clay’s natural responses – coiling, folding, collapsing – allowing each piece to evolve through a quiet collaboration between hand and material. The process is both contemplative and physical, shaped by presence and spontaneity.

Each piece carries the imprint of the moment it was made. The emotional landscape she brings into the studio – whether stillness, unrest, or reflection – becomes part of the work itself. No two forms are ever alike, because no two moments are ever the same. What emerges is often unexpected: a translation of something felt, rather than planned – shaped 
by what she is experiencing at that particular point in time.

In addition to her studio practice, she offers sculptural hand-building workshops where she shares this intuitive approach with others.

Craig Spencer's presentation at Makers Market in March showed an extensive selection of his ceramic works displayed with vintage storage pieces. He created a tonal space with small vessels and jewellery as well as larger investment objects. 

@spencerceramics

Craig is a New Zealand–born ceramicist based in Auckland, working across New Zealand and Australia. 
With over 20 years’ experience in interior design throughout Australasia and Singapore, his ceramic practice is grounded in a refined understanding of space, proportion, and materiality.

Since discovering ceramics in 2018, he has developed a distinctive body of wheel-thrown and slab-built work characterised by clean architectural lines and quiet restraint. His inspiration draws from both architecture and the natural environment — from modernist structures and built form to landscape, light, and organic texture. Rather than being defined by a single influence, his work evolves through accumulated experience, learned traditions, and an ongoing exploration of material.

Grounded in the natural qualities of clay, each piece balances precision with the visible trace of the maker’s hand. By bringing together contemporary design sensibilities with time-honoured techniques, Craig creates ceramic collections, art objects, and bespoke lighting for a variety of private clients as well as large international brands, including Aesop. His work is guided by craftsmanship, material integrity, and a genuine love of making, resulting in pieces that are purposeful, enduring, and harmonious within interior spaces.

Introducing Finnzarby Richwood who joins us for Makers Market Edition 3.0 /

Finnzarby Richwood is a trained furniture maker running a one-man design and make furniture studio in Henderson. The studio – Zarby Designs – is both commission-based, taking on design and manufacture work, as well as an outlet for Finn’s prospective pieces and products.

Finnzarby trained under Rowan Dicks and has since broadened his work and experience into a number of mediums and styles, though his heart is taken by timber. Conceptually driven, his furniture pieces are explorative in form, and try to play on the line between practical craft and art.

“My goal is to create much more than just functional furniture items, but pieces that influence the feeling of the space they’re in. I would love a world where people are more willing to push the boundary on the stylistic choices they consider for their spaces.”

Photo / @hanna.shim

We have taken a breath for the last month after Makers Market, school holidays and the Art Fair. So it seems we've vanished from social here! 

Rekindling this page – below, some thank yous and reflections. A new event announcement for Edition 3.0 will follow. 

We hope you all enjoyed Makers Market in March. For Edition 2.0 we brought together 19 new makers from across the country and the talented @hannahleejade from Edition 1.0. We spread the event further into the gallery so visitors could enjoy more of a spacious layout and we tried a few new presentation methods for signage and awareness. 

We've also started more of a connection with New Zealand Design Week and next year our March event will tie in with this. @nzdesignweek

There are still plenty more ideas we have to explore in future events and we hope you will come back for more! It's encouraging to see our usual customers and a new audience coming through on these weekend events. 

Thanks to everyone who visited and invested in designs from this talented group of designers. And such a huge thank you to the designers. Exhibiting for the weekend and sharing a piece of themselves in their work and showing up to meet our guests is not easy! We are grateful for everything you gave to the event /

You all are amazing and we look forward to seeing what happens next in your world. 

#gooodformmakersmarket 
Photo by @abigaildellavo

We loved how many of the designers supported each other through the weekend and quite a lot of sales were made between them. 

Ceramicist Jino Jeong of @jino_ceramic_studio is here buying a piece from Geri Wang of @theririlab with objects in the foreground by @salysi_official. 

Good Form supports the stands with items from our own collection which suit the space and needs of the designer. It was our pleasure to see a vintage wall shelving piece from @mrbigglesworthy used by @theririlab and brought to life. 

#gooodformmakersmarket

Photo : @abigaildellavo

Some notes on the Saturday shoot we did with @abigaildellavo from Emma Eagle. 

James Klein @jamesklein__ was one of the first designers to join Makers Market 2.0, when I saw his work during his time at the gallery buying a contemporary metal chair. This is his Span Chair, which needed a sitter to properly show the recline angle. Saddle leather and steel, minimal lines per his aesthetic, we loved it. 

This ended up being the only photo I'm in and it shows the heat on my face of the super humid weather we had that weekend. We were having so much fun but it was a packed day and the time to capture 20 designers and our gallery went so quickly! I can't wait to do this all again in a few months. 

#gooodformmakersmarket

Este 12 y 13 de septiembre, @rociogmu.art  nos trae a Mercado de Motores un taller de pintura abstracta para crear un abanico completamente único.

Durante el taller partirás de un abanico de tela blanca con una base de pintura abstracta y aprenderás a intervenirlo jugando con el color, las formas y diferentes herramientas. La idea es experimentar, dejarte llevar y descubrir tu propia manera de crear.

caption:
🍄 ¿Y si esta vez creamos con hongos?

El Reino Fungi esconde mucho más de lo que imaginamos. En este taller descubriremos el micelio con @miceliarte_ceramica_micologia_ , una red de filamentos capaz de crecer y transformar materiales orgánicos en nuevos biomateriales.

Aprenderemos cómo funciona, cómo se utiliza en diseño, arte y artesanía y, sobre todo, pasaremos a la práctica: crearás tu propio objeto de micelio. ✨

Una experiencia para descubrir, experimentar y ver cómo la naturaleza, la creatividad y la innovación pueden convertirse en una misma cosa.

Y sí, tu creación seguirá evolucionando después del taller. 🍄

caption:
Please welcome Paul Errington to the Gravel Cycling Hall of Fame!!⁠
@paule78 @the_dirty_reiver @grinduro⁠
-⁠
While modern gravel cycling has its roots firmly planted in the USA, it has quickly become a global phenomenon. One of the key figures in the global proliferation of gravel events has been Paul Errington. He recognized the potential of gravel cycling as a unique and accessible form of outdoor adventure. As an early advocate for the sport, he’s inspired countless cyclists to explore the world on gravel, both in Europe and beyond. He hosted his first gravel event –– The Dirty Reiver –– in 2016 and was a key figure in the global expansion of the Grinduro gravel series. Today, as the Grinduro series owner, Paul hosts thousands of riders each year at multiple events across the globe.⁠
-⁠
Read more at www.GravelCyclingHOF.com

Rick Struthers' presentation at Makers Market 2.0 in March included four designs which demonstrated his immense skill and patience in creating furniture. The piece which captured a lot of attention was the tall liquor cabinet with its secret drawer to the back and elegant curved form. 

Rick’s work draws on traditional techniques and the considered use of hand tools, which remain an important part of his process. His furniture takes inspiration from the Federal period, interpreted through a contemporary lens with an emphasis on elegance, proportion, and refined detail.

Anna Cuthbert and Amanda Neill of Design Alchemy Collective have designed a collection of handcrafted bedlinen and accessories which blur the line between functional object and textile art.

At the heart of the collection is an unexpected material story: reclaimed textile underprints. 
Traditionally discarded during the block-printing process, these excess-ink fabrics are 
reimagined and crafted by artisans processes into statement pieces that celebrate irregularity, tonal variation, and the quiet beauty of the handmade.

Ready means never getting stuck for long. 🧭 
 
We're closing out the 2026 Ultimate Overland Vehicle series with the gear that keeps you self-reliant when it counts. @FreedomRecoveryGear, @Wilco_Offroad, @onXOffroad, @RotopaXOfficial and @ForrestTool cover every angle: a full recovery kit and traction boards for the tough spots, a sturdy hitchgate for carrying a spare tire, trusted navigation off the grid, water and fuel storage, and a multipurpose tool kit for whatever the trail throws at you.
 
A build that proves what's possible when a proven vehicle meets the best in adventure gear.
 
The 2026 Ultimate Overland Vehicle heads to the Bring a Trailer auction this fall—and every dollar raised goes straight to the @OverlandExpoFoundation. Stay tuned for details.

As a standout double header, the festival hosts the UK leg of Grinduro, while also delivering racing that counts towards Round 4 of the GrALBA Series.

With its vast network of forest roads, quiet backcountry routes and flowing gravel tracks, South Scotland has become widely recognised for exceptional gravel riding. The combination of scale, solitude and scenery makes it equally appealing to competitive racers, endurance riders and those discovering gravel for the first time.

This is not just an event location - it’s a region shaping the future of gravel riding in the UK.

Discover the routes. Ride the landscape. Be part of it.

The son of Swiss artist Eva Aeppli and the stepson of renowned sculptor Jean Tinguely, Felix was a natural-born rebel. At just sixteen, he ran away from his father’s home in 1961 to pursue a life of travel, adventure and artistic freedom.
That bohemian dream truly took flight when he met painter Loretta Buscaglia in New York City in 1965, beginning a remarkable creative partnership and life together.
An inspiring and beautifully crafted documentary about art, freedom, love and living life on your own terms.

Hark Handmade is the beaded botanical practice of Auckland-based artist Hollie Ryan. Working primarily with glass seed beads and fine wire, Hollie creates sculptural flowers and still-life arrangements that explore memory, tenderness, and the quiet rituals of care.

Through slow, repetitive making, Hark Handmade reflects on themes of permanence, grief, intimacy and beauty, offering contemporary heirlooms that invite closer looking. The work embraces imperfection and labour as part of its narrative, celebrating the tactile and emotional qualities of handmade objects in an increasingly digital world.

Que os parecen estas espectaculares lámparas procedentes del mítico Hotel Ritz de Madrid, uno de los hoteles con más historia y glamour de nuestro país.

El Hotel Ritz abrió sus puertas en 1910, impulsado por el rey Alfonso XIII, con la intención de convertir Madrid en una capital con un hotel de lujo comparable a los grandes establecimientos europeos. 👑

Durante más de un siglo, sus habitaciones y salones fueron testigos del paso de reyes, artistas, políticos y algunas de las personalidades más importantes de la historia.

Estas lámparas formaban parte de sus estancias antes de la gran reforma del hotel. Y ahora, después de haber iluminado uno de los edificios más emblemáticos de Madrid… ¡han terminado en una tienda de antigüedades! 😱

Porque hay objetos antiguos que son bonitos… y otros que, además, han sido testigos de la historia. ❤️

Muchas gracias a Juan de @palatiumantique por su amabilidad.

👇 ¿Tendrías en casa una pieza original procedente del Hotel Ritz?

#HotelRitzMadrid #Antigüedades #HistoriaDeMadrid #Coleccionismo #ToyHunterSpain

Así vivimos la última edición de la temporada de Mercado de Motores 🚂💛

Un fin de semana rodeados de artesanos increíbles, música en directo, talleres, food trucks y miles de personas que hicieron que, una vez más, el mercado cobrara vida.

@nintendoes nos hizo volver a ser niños con su zona de juegos, donde pudimos probar la nueva Nintendo Switch y disfrutar de títulos como Mario Kart World, Super Mario Bros. Wonder, Super Mario Party Jamboree, Princess Peach: Showtime! y muchos más. 🎮

También vivimos una experiencia diferente con la @comisioneuropea y su reto #EyesOpen , una iniciativa para invitarnos a mantener los ojos abiertos ante las víctimas de cualquier tipo de violencia y reflexionar sobre la importancia de actuar, informar y apoyar. 👀💙

Y, por supuesto, no faltaron los brindis con @aperolspritzes , el de @vermutzarro y los buenos momentos compartidos con @mahou_es , que hicieron que el aperitivo supiera todavía mejor. 🍊🍷🍻

También disfrutamos de un espectáculo de adiestramiento para perros de @cucuradog 🐶 (volverán en septiembre 🐾)

Gracias a todos los que habéis formado parte de esta temporada: artesanos, visitantes, músicos, colaboradores y equipo. Sin vosotros, Mercado de Motores no sería lo que es.

Ahora toca hacer una pequeña pausa… nos vemos en septiembre con muchas más ganas y muchas sorpresas.

¡Gracias por acompañarnos una temporada más! 💛🚂

Sí, has leído bien. Nos hemos venido arriba y, de la mano de Mercado de Motores, vamos a sortear UNA GAFA CADA DÍA de lunes a sábado. 

¿Quieres elevar tu lookazos de verano? Tienes 6 oportunidades distintas para ganar. Lo mejor de todo es que si participas hoy, ¡sigues teniendo opciones de ganar el resto de días de la semana!

PASOS PARA PARTICIPAR:

1️⃣ Sigue a @martisoneyewear y a @mercadodemotores (revisaremos que sigas a ambas cuentas).
2️⃣ Deja un comentario en este post mencionando a un amigo.
3️⃣ Comparte este post en tus Stories.

¿Cómo conseguir más posibilidades de ganar?
¡Cuantos más comentarios dejes mencionando a amigos diferentes, más papeletas tienes! No hay límite. Además, todos los comentarios se acumulan cada día, así que si comentas mucho el lunes, ¡puedes acabar ganando el sábado!
¿Cómo elegimos a los ganadores?
Cada día, del lunes 22 a sábado 27 de junio, sacaremos un ganador/a entre TODOS los comentarios acumulados en este post hasta ese momento y lo anunciaremos en nuestras Stories. ¡El contador no se pone a cero, la bola sigue creciendo!
¡Mucha suerte a todos!

(Sorteo válido solo para en España: en Península y Baleares)

Jino Jeong is an Auckland-based ceramicist. Jino was born in Seoul and trained in ceramics at Kyunggi University in South Korea. He then spent a year at the highly prestigious Jingdezhen Ceramic Institute in China, the only dedicated university to ceramic arts in China.

Jino's work can be found in galleries and private collections here and overseas. He has been residing in New Zealand for 10 years and has received many recognised awards for his work during this time. Jino works from his studio experimenting with scale and glaze to create a unique body of work. 

Image / Portage Award 2023 Premier Award winning work Celestial Thread: A Tapestry of Sunshine and Spiderwebs. Jino also creates smaller versions of this design which will be at the market.

Since discovering ceramics in 2018, Craig Spencer has developed a distinctive body of wheel-thrown and slab-built ceramic work characterised by clean architectural lines and quiet restraint. 

Craig's inspiration draws from both architecture and the natural environment — from modernist structures and built form to landscape, light, and organic texture. Rather than being defined by a single influence, his work evolves through accumulated experience, learned traditions and an ongoing exploration of material.

Matt Coldicutt is a furniture maker and sculptor based in Tāmaki Makaurau working under the name of rough.house.project. His practice investigates the ecologies of urban development and convoluted social-spatial crisis and seeks to find balance through restorative making processes.

At present he is Head of the Technology Department at Nga Puna O Waiorea Western Springs College teaching Design. From 2020-2023 he was AUT’s Technology Curriculum Specialist Lecturer for their Faculty of Education. During 2014-17 he co-established and curated Rockies ARI (now The Frog) at 454 Karangahape Rd. 

Image features the Parquet Stool/Side Table made from Kauri.

Rick Struthers is an Auckland-based furniture maker who has spent over 20 years developing his craft. After discovering a passion for woodworking in his final year of secondary school, encouraged by a supportive teacher, he went on to complete a furniture making apprenticeship.

He particularly enjoys creating contrast through the use of different timbers and inlays, often working with species such as American cherry, maple, walnut, and ebony. Over the years Rick has produced a wide range of one-off pieces that reflect both traditional craftsmanship and a modern sensibility.

Image features a liquor cabinet design which is a reinterpretation of a design by a contemporary American furniture maker, reflecting Rick’s interest in studying and learning from established masters of the craft.

Drawing on both traditional craft methodologies and contemporary techniques, Kynan creates furniture that is thoughtful in proportion, honest in construction and expressive in form – each piece a testament to disciplined making and refined design.

caption:
Introducing Sara Santoro of Loom Studio /

Sara Santoro is a Hawke’s Bay–based creative whose naturally dyed woven art and homewares are 
crafted from her small garden studio. With a Bachelor of Design in Communication Design and further study in Landscape Design, Sara’s practice reflects a thoughtful blending of disciplines, grounded in a deep respect for landscape, materiality, and sustainable processes.

Her discovery of botanical dyeing became a pivotal moment, uniting her long-held passions for colour, 
interiors, and the natural world. Working primarily with undyed, New Zealand–grown and processed 
wool—often repurposing thread waste—alongside raw European flax linen yarns, Sara embraces a 
slow, considered approach to making. Each fibre is naturally dyed by hand using plant materials 
harvested from her garden or foraged locally, ensuring every piece carries a strong connection to 
place.

Sara joins us at Makers Market /

arboriculture. 

Ian honours time-tested woodturning techniques passed down through generations while confidently exploring contemporary forms and finishes. This blend of heritage craftsmanship and modern experimentation allows him to create pieces that feel both grounded and fresh. Working primarily with locally sourced timber – often from fallen trees – Ian emphasises sustainability and respect for the natural environment.

caption:
GreazeFest Presents: Psychomatic Kustom

Psychomatic Kustom is the creative partnership of husband and wife team Tash and Brenton, who are cruising to Queensland in their custom Thunderbird to showcase their kustom kulture creations at GreazeFest.

Meeting through a shared love of kustom art and classic cars, the Melbourne couple quickly found common ground in their passion for all things lowbrow. Since joining forces, they have honed their skills across pinstriping, airbrushing and metal shaping, becoming the talent behind many standout pieces in the GreazeFest Art Show in recent years.
Their work captures the true spirit of kustom kulture, and they generously share behind the scenes footage of their projects on social media, inviting others into their fascinating world.

Stop by and welcome Psychomatic Kustom when you are at GreazeFest, and be sure to bring something for them to pinstripe.

Emma La Rocca's designs for her label Emroce aim to inspire positive change in response to the environmental and social impacts of modern production and consumption. Her swimwear is created to stay secure in the surf, encouraging women to feel confident, adventurous, and connected to the water while fostering greater respect for rivers, lakes, and oceans.

Sustainability sits at the core of Emma’s process. She focuses on thoughtful pattern making and zero-waste lay plans, while continually researching innovative, environmentally responsible fabrics. Her swimwear concept was first developed in Italy and is now produced in New Zealand using high-quality recycled Italian fabrics. Each design is refined to its essential elements, prioritising function, durability, and a precise fit. Emma believes consumers hold real power: every purchase supports the values and companies people want to see thrive in the world.

caption:
Accomplished New Zealand designer Neal Smith is known for his minimal, clean aesthetic and proficient work with progressive wood based materials. Neal has focused on occupying a space between mass production and individual handcrafting, creating unique designs for leading architects and high-profile clients.

This prototype recliner was designed as an entry into the Carter Holt Harvey 2003 Metaform design competition. The goal was to demonstrate and promote the use of hardened NZ Pinus Radiata, a process of infusing cellulose into pine under pressure. Hardened pine is significantly denser and stronger than normal pine, hence the opportunity was taken to maximise the cantilevers of the recliner to showcase these qualities.

Neal joins us at Makers Market /

Ian Lawson is a woodturner and wood carver based in Tūranganui-a-Kiwa/Gisborne and Kirikiriroa/Hamilton, Aotearoa New Zealand. His practice is deeply shaped by a strong family legacy in woodworking, art, and arboriculture. 

Working primarily with locally sourced timber – often from fallen trees – Ian emphasises sustainability and respect for the natural environment. His work celebrates the inherent beauty of wood, highlighting distinctive grain patterns, textures, and natural imperfections. His creations range from finely crafted functional ware such as bowls and vases to expressive artistic pieces.

This piece was an award winning entry for @artofwoodnz

Belinda Marshall is a ceramic artist based in Tāmaki Makaurau, Auckland, whose practice is grounded in material exploration, intuition, and a deep respect for process. With a background spanning visual arts, film, and fashion, Marshall brings a multidisciplinary 
sensibility to her work in clay, where form, texture, and surface become vehicles for storytelling and cultural memory.

Travel and lived experience play an integral role in shaping her aesthetic. Encounters with different landscapes, architectural forms, and craft traditions inform the quiet strength and tactile richness of her hand-built vessels and sculptural objects. 

Each work is individually constructed by hand, resulting in pieces that feel intimate and singular. Through this balance of control and surrender, Belinda creates ceramics that are both grounded and expressive, celebrating imperfection, process, and the enduring beauty of the handmade.

Salysi is a design studio based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, New Zealand, founded by Sam Fox and Siobhan Seifert. The studio designs and produces furniture and homewares that balance playful expression with restrained minimalism., from brightly coloured statement pieces, to pared-back raw metal, or timber forms with subtle detailing. Each piece 
is carefully considered in both construction and material selection, with the intention that it 
will endure daily use and be kept, repaired, and passed on rather than replaced.

Sam holds a Bachelor of Design Innovation in Industrial Design and Siobhan a Bachelor of Architectural Studies, both from Te Herenga Waka | Victoria University of Wellington. Their combined backgrounds inform a process that brings together product design and spatial thinking, resulting in objects that are functional, distinctive, and built to last.

Since relocating to Aotearoa over a decade ago, ceramicist Jino Jeong has developed a distinctive body of work that explores form, scale and glaze in expressive and often meditative ways. His pieces 
are held in galleries and private collections both in New Zealand and overseas, and are celebrated for their refined surfaces and thoughtful engagement with materiality.

Jino’s work has been widely recognised through major awards, most notably winning the Premier Award at the 2023 Portage Ceramic Awards – Aotearoa’s foremost national ceramics event – for his piece Celestial Thread: A Tapestry of Sunshine and Spiderwebs. In addition to his studio work, Jino contributes to the wider ceramic community as a tutor, sharing his skills and passion for clay with students and enthusiasts across Auckland.

Emma La Rocca's designs for her label Emroce aim to inspire positive change in response to the environmental and social impacts of modern production and consumption. Her swimwear is created to stay secure in the surf, encouraging women to feel confident, adventurous, and connected to the water while fostering greater respect for rivers, lakes, and oceans.

Sustainability sits at the core of Emma’s process. She focuses on thoughtful pattern making and zero-waste lay plans, while continually researching innovative, environmentally responsible fabrics. Her swimwear concept was first developed in Italy and is now produced in New Zealand using high-quality recycled Italian fabrics. Each design is refined to its essential elements, prioritising function, durability, and a precise fit. Emma believes consumers hold real power: every purchase supports the values and companies people want to see thrive in the world.

Neal Smith's presentation at Makers Market 2.0 included furniture objects from his extensive catalogue and recent jewelery designs. One of the most accomplished and connected designers we know, it was a pleasure to host Neal for the weekend. 

Neal's independent practice has produced iconic pieces that have been celebrated within New Zealand’s design community. His 1989 ‘RYB’ chair was featured in Objectspace’s exhibition The Chair: A Story of Design and Making in Aotearoa, underscoring his enduring influence. Works such as his Olives Stool, inspired by traditional milking stool forms and crafted in timber, demonstrate his ability to blend functional simplicity with poetic form.

Throughout his career, Smith has championed the values of material integrity, refined proportions and enduring design, making him a respected figure in New Zealand’s furniture design community.

Belinda Marshall's presentation at Makers Market 2.0 in March featured ceramic works to elevate the every day – vases and vessels that offer a soft, organic presence. 

Central to Belinda's philosophy is an embrace of unpredictability. Clay resists total control; shifts in 
temperature, atmosphere, and glaze during firing introduce subtle variations in tone and texture. Rather than seeking perfection, Belinda honours these transformations, viewing them as evidence of collaboration between artist and element.

Each work is individually constructed by hand, resulting in pieces that feel intimate and singular. Through this balance of control and surrender, Belinda creates ceramics that are both grounded and expressive, celebrating imperfection, process, and the enduring beauty of the handmade.

GreazeFest Presents: All Star Tribute to Johnny Burnette

Long before rock'n'roll reached the mainstream, Johnny Burnette and The Rock and Roll Trio were forging a raw and electrified sound in the mid-1950s, that would shape the direction of modern music and the birth of rock. Their ground-breaking songs and recordings laid the foundation for generations to follow, influencing many bands from Robert Gordon to The Yardbirds to Led Zeppelin.

This special tribute brings together a talented line-up of guests at GreazeFest including Dave Cantrell, Kid James, Toto, Laura Palmer and more, to pay tribute, with classics such as Train Kept A Rollin', Lonesome Train, Rock Billy Boogie, Lonesome Tears In My Eyes, Sweet Love On My Mind and more!

Get ready, get dressed, for the Pinup Party at GreazeFest!

Join us on Saturday August 1 at 1.00pm for a celebration of pinup, style, fashion, and creativity at the GreazeFest Pinup Party!

All pinup enthusiasts are invited to step onto the stage to showcase their outfit and personal style. Whether your look is vintage, rockabilly, glamour, retro-inspired, or completely original, everyone is welcome.

Hosted by Hilly Monroe and Bettie Butcher from Pinups of Australia, the Pinup Party is all about fun, fashion, friendship, and fabulous photo moments.

Special guest speakers include Miss Chrissy, the vintage stylist and from the Lindy Charm School; Maizie May, the vintage girl in a modern world; international pinup Valentina Volupte; photographer Paul Pugh from Pandom Images; plus fashionista Vicki Martin.

Group Photo Themes

Saturday – Leopard Spots Forever
Celebrate the impact of leopard print on fashion through the decades, from vintage style to modern times. Whether it's subtle accents or head-to-toe leopard print, this is your chance to unleash your inner cool cat and break out the leopard spots for a magical group photo.

Sunday – Rock the Boat
Our nautical fashion theme sets sail with a celebration of timeless seaside style. From crisp white outfits to classic navy stripes, think sailor collars, high-waisted shorts and slacks, red lipstick, and windswept coastal glamour. This group photo is inspired by classic maritime pinup photography and mid-century seaside fashion.

Dates and Times:

Saturday Pinup Party & Group Photo - Sat August 1 at 1.00pm
Sunday Group Photo - Sun August 2 at 12.30pm

Both events are being held on the outdoor dance floor stage at GreazeFest. See you there!

GreazeFest Presents: Kieron McDonald Combo

The Kieron McDonald Combo create a distinct rockabilly sound while remaining true to the traditions of the genre. Hailing from Melbourne, Kieron McDonald has been celebrated across international rockabilly circles for two decades. During that time, Kieron has written and performed a strong catalogue of original songs, releasing eight full-length CD albums and three vinyl EPs. The Kieron McDonald Combo bring a cool collection of original songs and a reputation as one of Australia’s most authentic keepers of the 1950s rockabilly flame. Their sound is tight and is brimming with boppers, jivers and strollers.

GreazeFest Presents: Smokin' Firebirds

Heavily distilled in the rockabilly goodness you’d expect from the calibre of this hefty three-piece roots-rockabilly outfit, Smokin’ Firebirds bring together a unique combination of musicianship, talent, and fortitude.

Front-man Dan Fargo brings true grit on guitar and vocals and is well known in the Australian rockabilly scene, through his other outfits 'A Band Called Twang' and 'Palomino III'. The rhythm section, featuring Dale Berends on upright bass and Jeffrey Enchelmaier on drums, add depth and energy to the band's dynamic sound. With lightning-quick bass and powerful percussion, Smokin' Firebirds exudes finesse and personality, creating a very cool live music show.

GreazeFest Presents: The Linelockers

Nestled in the town of Lismore, New South Wales, The Linelockers have emerged as a dynamic force in the realm of authentic rockabilly. This trio isn't just about music; they walk the walk and talk the talk: a testament to the enduring spirit of this bygone era. Boasting an impressive variety of high energy roots rock'n'roll, rockabilly and honky-tonk songs, their grass roots approach to traditional rockabilly and hillbilly standards, along with authentic original material, is sure to keep the dance floor boppin'. Their album "Shake It Till You Break It" solidifies their status as ambassadors of the genre.

Tidal Orchestra by Lindisfarne Anglican Grammar School @lindisfarnegrammar

Tidal Orchestra is a collaborative ceramic installation created by Creative Industries students and inspired by 
the fluid motion of the ocean. Individually hand-built and glazed in soft pastel sea tones, each fish reflects the 
shifting colours of water and sky. Mounted on slender stainless-steel rods, the fish move gently with the coastal breeze, forming a unified school across the Currumbin dunes. The work symbolises unity, resilience, and interconnection, encouraging viewers to reflect on collaboration, environmental harmony, and the delicate 
balance between human creativity and the marine world.

Littoral Lantern by Brent Grainger & Jai McCartney

Littoral Lantern begins as a distant marker at the festival, a simple form that draws people toward it. As visitors approach, it opens, shifting from an object to a space to be experienced. Framed openings offer moments to pause and view the surrounding coastline from within. As daylight fades, a soft glow emerges, filtering through timber panels and spilling across the ground. The sculpture becomes a lantern—gathering people, light, and movement. Littoral Lantern invites interaction, reflection, and memory, creating an engaging spatial experience.

caption:
Salute to the Sun by Patricia Piccnini @patricia.piccinini

Salute to the Sun continues my long fascination with the boundary we draw between the natural and the artificial — and how readily that line dissolves once you look closely. This new bronze sculpture is a chimera, seamlessly moving between deer, tree, fungus, human and motorcycle. It evolves out of a machine base into an organic form whose arms, or perhaps antlers, unfurl like budding leaves.

The pose comes from the sun salute and from the way plants quietly rotate to face the light. I love that it stands on a beach, an obvious artificial construct, yet entirely at home in that archetypical natural place. Its materiality also reflects this: Bronze is mostly copper, a metal that was laid down in the earth eons ago, but shaped entirely by the manipulation of elemental fire by human activity.

In earlier work I looked at imagining machines with the tenderness, balance and yearning of living things. These machines are the wild creatures of a world where we are all intertwined with technology. ‘Salute to the Sun’ presents a creature of modern mythology: an hybrid chimera drawing its energy from the sun, more vulnerable than threatening, asking us where we fit into this world.

Rota Fortunae by Emily Hastie @emilyrosehastie

Rota Fortunae visualises the role of chance in life's most defining outcome: where on Earth we are born. Fortuna, ancient deity of chance, blindly holds out her hand to reveal a fate on the spinning wheel. Around its edge sits the true distribution of global population, drawn from current United Nations data. Australians are only ~0.34% of that population, yet inherit stewardship of a megadiverse country home to 10% of Earth's known 
species, over 80% found nowhere else on the planet. Such extraordinary fortune begets equal responsibility.

Reflections by Oliver Mabbutt @_mabart_

Reflections invites participants to move through and around the structure, encountering their own image as it 
fragments and multiplies. The work explores the human need to reflect on the past while remaining oriented 
toward what lies ahead. While reflection is essential for growth, lingering too long can obstruct forward momentum. By framing both the participant and the surrounding landscape, Reflections balances inward 
contemplation with outward projection, encouraging awareness of self, context, and future direction.

Fathom By Anna Bonshek

Fathom's a geometric form made of metal might remind us of a protective entity, a frame of a home or shelter, or the basic idea of an architectural structure standing 
as a symmetrical presence but seeming to dissolve in space. Fathom’s lightness resists desire for solidity arising in space and time. Its reflective surface allows for the play of light, edging on transparency and dematerialising itself as it demarcates and affirms its own boundaries, eventually converging on top, pointing to the unbounded sphere of the sky.

Still Room for Sentiment by Wendy Tanner @wentan

In a contemporary world of white walls and grey restraint, this work asks whether nostalgia and sentimentality still belong in our homes. Glass cabinets and ornament collections have given way to flat-packs and single statement pieces. Grandma’s blue-and-white porcelain, once treasured, dusted, and displayed, now drifts to op shops and garage sales as generations pass on. Gathered here, these figurines resist disappearance, asserting the quiet value of memory, care and excess in an age that prefers less.

Beyond the Bin by Sam Gowing @gowing.sam

This installation presents a colony of life-sized Ibis in motion, depicting walking and feeding behaviours within increasingly constrained spaces. The work responds to habitat loss caused by urban expansion and environmental degradation. Once revered as the “Sacred Bird” and now colloquially labelled the “Bin Chicken,” the Ibis has adapted to human-altered environments. The fluorescent colour functions as a visual warning and a strategy for heightened visibility, reflecting resilience and collective survival within human-altered landscapes. The work invites reconsideration of human impact, waste culture, and coexistence with native species.

#LaMasíaGallery La cuarta muestra en La Masía Gallery presenta la obra de @esthermiquel, bajo el título 'Interlude'. La obra de esta artista parte del silencio, entendido este no como el vacío, sino con un espacio de percepción. A través del mismo, explora la tensión entre presencia y ausencia, entre lo visible y aquello que permanece apenas perceptible. Su pintura ofrece un espacio de pausa en la a flagship de @nudeproject, en contraste con el ritmo frenético del entorno urbano.⁠
⁠
El lenguaje visual de Miquel se construye a través de la reducción, la materia y la repetición. Elementos mínimos, interrupciones y espacios de silencio generan composiciones en las que la imagen aparece, se desvanece o queda suspendida en un estado de ambigüedad. Con formación en diseño gráfico y diseño de interiores, Esther ha desarrollado una práctica marcada por la precisión visual y la economía de recursos. ⁠
⁠

Formations in Time by Natalie Yates & Jasmine Ivett-Crabtree
@natalieyatesdesigns @beautifulthingsbyjasmine

Yates and Ivett-Crabtree have captured the quiet choreography and beauty of nature. Their organically shaped forms, treated using the Obvara technique, evoke the gentle shaping of rock and earth by flowing water over hundreds of years, capturing the rhythm of fluvial erosion. Through surface, texture, and form, Yates and Ivett-Crabtree celebrate impermanence, transformation,
and the subtle poetry of the natural world.

Kern by Al Phemister @alphemistersculpture

During travels in Cornwall, UK, Al Phemester was mesmerized by the circles of ancient stone forms that remain resilient within the modern world. The artist invites viewers to experience a sense of this ancient mystery, with the  work finding its place as a quiet sentinel in the landscape or surrounding spaces, speaking with subtlety and grace.

Too Many Fish in the Sea? by Ged McCormick & Rusty Linane

This sculpture uses the mullet form to explore ecological excess: invasive weeds, plastic waste, and the 
consequences of human intervention. The body is built from environmental weeds, symbolising the relentless 
cycle of growth and control. Inside, soy sauce fish form the intestines, reflecting how plastics infiltrate living 
systems and accumulate unseen. Together, these materials imagine a creature shaped by imbalance, a fish literally filled with pollution and held together by what we struggle to manage. The work invites reflection on consumption, control, and the ecologies we unintentionally create.
