caption:
🎙️ Sexta é sinónimo de novo episódio do podcast Portugal Manual.

Ao longo das próximas semanas, continuamos a partilhar as conversas gravadas ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão hoje a pensar, criar e transformar o design em Portugal.

Neste episódio conversamos com Bárbara Coutinho, diretora do @mudemuseu , Ana Lia Santos, responsável pela Young Design Generation e pela ligação à comunidade académica da Lisbon Design Week, e Inês Continelli, responsável pelo Atelier Daciano da Costa.

A partir da exposição Young Design Generation e do lançamento da reedição da cadeira Osaka, refletimos sobre o papel das novas gerações, a importância da preservação da memória do design português e os desafios de transformar boas ideias em projetos sustentáveis.

Como se constrói uma cultura de design? Que responsabilidade têm os museus, as instituições e a indústria no apoio aos jovens designers? E como pode o legado de autores como Daciano da Costa continuar a inspirar quem está hoje a começar?

Uma conversa sobre continuidade, património, educação, indústria e sobre a necessidade de criar pontes entre o passado e o futuro do design português.

caption:
🎙️ Sexta é sinónimo de novo episódio do podcast Portugal Manual.

Estamos a chegar ao fim dos episódios gravados ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão hoje a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

Neste episódio conversamos com Vasco Fragoso Mendes.

Partindo da exposição Premature Retrospective. Not There Yet., apresentada no Lisbon Air durante a Lisbon Design Week, refletimos sobre o processo criativo enquanto espaço de experimentação, erro e descoberta, e sobre a importância de mostrar aquilo que normalmente permanece invisível.

O que significa fazer uma “retrospectiva” quando sentimos que ainda estamos no início do caminho? Como se constrói uma linguagem própria sem ficar preso a uma estética? E de que forma materiais como a madeira, o metal, a cortiça ou até o papel podem transformar-se em ferramentas para pensar o design?

Ao longo da conversa falamos ainda sobre o crescimento de um atelier independente, os desafios de construir uma equipa, a experiência em feiras internacionais e a liberdade de experimentar sem seguir um percurso pré-definido.

Uma conversa sobre processo, matéria, risco e sobre a curiosidade como força motriz da criação.

🕘 09h00 (Lisboa)

Ao longo das próximas semanas, continuamos a partilhar as conversas gravadas ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão hoje a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

Neste episódio conversamos com Thayra Correia e Lia Raquel Marques, membros do coletivo Sotaque, que reúne designers com raízes nas antigas colónias portuguesas e que apresentou a sua primeira exposição durante a Lisbon Design Week.

Partindo deste projeto coletivo, refletimos sobre identidade, pertença e sobre a forma como o design pode abrir espaço para novas narrativas, cruzando diferentes geografias, referências culturais e experiências de vida.

Ao longo da conversa exploramos temas como a descolonização do design, a valorização dos saberes locais, o papel das instituições culturais e a importância de criar espaços de representação para novas gerações de designers.

Como pode o design contribuir para um diálogo mais aberto sobre identidade e memória? De que forma se constroem novas linguagens sem esquecer as suas origens? E que lugar ocupam hoje estes criadores na construção do design contemporâneo?

Uma conversa sobre diversidade, representação, cultura e sobre a capacidade do design para criar pontes entre pessoas, territórios e histórias.

Quando a inovação material encontra o design de autor, surgem novas formas de pensar cada produto. 🙌
 
Foi neste espírito que nasceu Light Stone, a coleção cápsula desenvolvida por @tonigrilodesign para a Cosentino e apresentada, na @lisbondesignweek 2026. Composta por quatro peças escultóricas produzidas integralmente em Dekton 4 mm, a coleção desafia a perceção tradicional do material, explorando conceitos de leveza, movimento e aparente suspensão através de formas que evocam a delicadeza de uma folha de papel.
A coleção reafirma o potencial criativo do Dekton, demonstrando como a inovação tecnológica pode abrir caminho a novas possibilidades para o design contemporâneo. 💡
 
Este projeto resulta da colaboração entre o designer @tonigrilodesign, @lxrocks.pt, responsável pela transformação técnica das peças, e @oflex3_, que apoiou o desenvolvimento e execução das estruturas metálicas, numa parceria que evidencia a excelência e o know-how português.
 
Na sua primeira participação na Lisbon Design Week, a Cosentino reforçou assim o seu compromisso com a promoção do design, da inovação e da colaboração entre criadores e parceiros. 
 
#DektonByCosentino #CosentinoPortugal #LisbonDesignWeek 📷 by @martapoppefotografia

We're excited to carry on in our Collab interview series over here at Graffiato Media! 😉
This time we'll hear from @micastill & @paulyb.art about how they created the new mural on the side of Noel Leeming.  IMO, these two could not have done collaboration better.

How did you approach this collab?
From Mica:
"I started off stocking Paul's past work to get an idea of what he enjoyed painting. We decided video chats worked best. We could communicate our ideas quickly. We created a shared google doc and dumped a bunch of drawings - we met up three times and decided we could redraw what each of us contribute. We both hold no ego and wanted to be playful with the approach. We played around with various elements of our sketches like a collage until something came together. Colour is something important to both of us, so we had fun with choosing colours. We decided early on to melt our vibes rather than have separate elements. I think it worked out well as the image become a magical new representation of Paul and Mica as a team rather than any individual artist."

From Pauly B:
"Mica and I decided from the beginning that we wanted to take a fully collaborative approach - in the sense that we didn’t want people to be able to tell who’d done what. We both are present in all aspects of the design. 

We started by having a conversation about general themes and then both doing a lot of pencil drawing which we would upload to a shared drive. We would then make more drawings based on these and on our Zoom conversations. Then we started drawing over and redrawing each other's drawings. Finally, we both worked on combining the elements into the layout of the wall as one composition. There was a final process of discussion and redrawing until we arrived at the layout that we went with. Then we both made coloured versions, compared notes, and deciding together on the final colour scheme."

More to come from these two before we give you the final wall!

📸credit to @thatgreenolive

Ao longo das próximas semanas, continuamos a partilhar as conversas gravadas ao vivo no Bica do Sapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

Neste episódio conversamos com Sam Baron, Joana Teixeira, Sebastian Filgueiras e Tiago Ferreira sobre identidade, património, direção criativa e aquilo que permite a uma marca permanecer relevante ao longo do tempo.

Entre uma marca centenária de sabonetes, uma das mais antigas casas comerciais de Lisboa, uma companhia de chá profundamente ligada à cidade e o olhar de um designer internacional, exploramos diferentes formas de construir significado, pertença e continuidade.

Como se preserva uma identidade sem ficar preso ao passado? Como se atualiza uma marca sem perder aquilo que a torna única? E que papel podem o design, a curadoria e a experiência desempenhar nessa construção?

Uma conversa sobre memória, narrativa, cultura material e sobre a capacidade das marcas portuguesas se reinventarem sem perder a sua essência.

🎙️ Sexta é sinónimo de novo episódio do podcast Portugal Manual.

Conversas gravadas ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão hoje a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

Neste episódio conversamos com a curadora @almeida_felipa , que apresentou na Lisbon Design Week a exposição na Farmácia Gomes e lançou o livro que reúne cinco anos das suas emblemáticas feiras temáticas.

Partindo deste projeto, refletimos sobre o papel da curadoria enquanto prática de investigação, mediação e construção de comunidade, e sobre a forma como uma ideia nascida durante a pandemia acabou por reunir cerca de 60 artistas ao longo de cinco anos.

Como se constrói uma linguagem curatorial reconhecível sem limitar a liberdade criativa dos artistas? Que desafios existem na valorização do trabalho artesanal contemporâneo? E o que acontece quando um projeto pensado para ser efémero decide fechar um ciclo e transformar-se?

Ao longo da conversa falamos ainda sobre coleção, memória, processos criativos, colaboração e sobre a importância de criar tempo e contexto para que o trabalho artístico possa ser verdadeiramente visto e compreendido.

Uma conversa sobre curadoria, comunidade e sobre a capacidade de um projeto criar ligações duradouras entre artistas, objetos e públicos.

🎙️ Novo episódio do podcast Portugal Manual.

Ao longo das próximas semanas, continuamos a partilhar as conversas gravadas ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

Neste episódio conversamos com Sam Baron, Joana Teixeira, Sebastian Filgueiras e Tiago Ferreira sobre identidade, património, direção criativa e aquilo que permite a uma marca permanecer relevante ao longo do tempo.

Entre uma marca centenária de sabonetes, uma das mais antigas casas comerciais de Lisboa, uma companhia de chá profundamente ligada à cidade e o olhar de um designer internacional, exploramos diferentes formas de construir significado, pertença e continuidade.

Como se preserva uma identidade sem ficar preso ao passado? Como se atualiza uma marca sem perder aquilo que a torna única? E que papel podem o design, a curadoria e a experiência desempenhar nessa construção?

Uma conversa sobre memória, narrativa, cultura material e sobre a capacidade das marcas portuguesas se reinventarem sem perder a sua essência.

Ao longo das próximas semanas, continuamos a partilhar as conversas gravadas ao vivo no @bicadosapato durante a Lisbon Design Week, reunindo algumas das vozes que estão hoje a pensar, criar e transformar o design contemporâneo.

 e do Studio @further_ther 

A partir de Integrity of Form, exposição apresentada na Basílica da Estrela durante a Lisbon Design Week, falamos sobre o desafio de reunir treze designers com práticas, linguagens e percursos distintos e sobre o que acontece quando a função, a beleza e a expressão artística deixam de ocupar lugares separados.

Como se constrói uma exposição coletiva sem apagar a identidade de cada autor? De que forma um espaço com a história e a arquitetura da Basílica da Estrela influencia a seleção e a apresentação das peças? E o que significa criar uma plataforma dedicada aos designers que trabalham hoje em Portugal?

Ao longo da conversa refletimos também sobre curadoria, colaboração, identidade e diversidade cultural, mas também sobre o trabalho menos visível necessário para construir e manter um projeto coletivo.

Uma conversa sobre aquilo que se ganha e aquilo de que se abdica quando se investe tempo e energia na criação de espaço para o trabalho dos outros.

Part 2 of our interview series with @paulyb.art & @micastill telling our avid listeners about how this collab came together.

What did you feel you achieved during this process?

From Pauly:
"I have performed a lot with bands and to me the best collaborations push people in new directions with their artform while still keeping a strong sense of who they are and what they do. The sum should be greater than the parts.

Mica and I vibed really well - we had robust conversations, but always moving in the same direction, and discovering we have a really similar creative sensibility to each other. Even when we were painting, we were often having the same ideas about what we wanted to edit and how. 

Ultimately, we achieved what we both think is a really great mural that blends both of our work very well. We also went from knowing each other a little bit to being great mates."

From Mica:
"I feel like I achieved letting go of ego and therefore having a great time. It was a real trust exercise and it could have gone badly.  @sean_duffell was thoughtful in his pairing, not just visually but who could work as a team. 
I was appreciative of the experience as there are not a lot of opportunities to collaborate on such a scale."

We love this story of shared achievement! 

More collab stories to come before we give you the final wall experience.

PINKIR_ chair II — Maud Téphany & Rodolphe Renou

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

What I love about PINKIR_ chair II is that it represents something very close to the spirit of Lisbon Design Week: collaboration.

Maud Téphany and Rodolphe Renou bring together two very different crafts,ceramics and woodworking, without one becoming secondary to the other. You can still clearly see each maker’s hand and personality.

I also love that it sits somewhere between a functional object and a sculpture. It’s unexpected, slightly playful, and the first time I saw it , I wanted to walk around and look at it from different angles.

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

caption:
The Memory of the Walls — 3TWINS

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

This piece immediately spoke to me when I saw it in the apartment where it was shown because it is so connected to Lisbon.

The starting point is something we see everywhere in this city,the azulejos. 3TWINS have taken original early 20th-century tiles recovered from a Lisbon building and given them an entirely new life.

I love this idea of not simply preserving the past, but using it to create something new.

There is architecture, memory and contemporary art all within one object and somehow it still feels unmistakably Lisbon.

That made it a natural choice for our first LDW Edit.

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

Available now for purchase through The LDW Edit. Discover the piece via the link in bio.

A new setting for ‘Wool, a Forgotten Material’

After first presenting the project during @lisbondesignweek earlier this year, I’m very happy to see a selection of the works now finding their place at @quintaamala in Melides.

‘Wool, a Forgotten Material’ explores the potential of local sheep wool, a natural material that is increasingly overlooked and often treated as waste. Through felting and working directly with the raw qualities of the fibre, I create tactile artworks and objects that bring wool back into the interior in a contemporary way.

At Quinta Amala, the works feel remarkably at home, surrounded by natural materials, calm interiors and the landscape of Alentejo.

A selection of wool artworks and felted sheepskins will remain on view here throughout the autumn.

Thank you Karine for the warm welcome, your enthusiasm and for giving the work such a beautiful new setting.

During Lisbon Design Week 2026, the Molteni&C Flagship Store welcomed Alma Mater, a limited-edition functional art collection by Arianna Bavuso, co-founder of AB+AC Architects.

For this period, the showroom entered a meditative rhythm of stillness. The warm scent of hand-poured beeswax candles and the quiet precision of stainless steel created a delicate contrast in the space: soft, sensorial, clear, and architectural. Together, they invited each visitor to slow down, breathe deeper, and notice how light, material, and silence could gently reshape perception.

Thank you to all those who came by, paused, listened, and allowed themselves to enter this meditative moment with us. In a way, what stays with us is not only what we see, but what we share.

This week, @LisbonDesignWeek brought together Lisbon’s design and architecture community at @aethoslisbon for the first Lisbon screening of The Maximization of the Circumstance.

Created by @manutoro.work with designer @lucasmunozm, the film follows the transformation of Antonio Lamela’s iconic O’Donnell 34 building in Madrid and the creation of @sancal’s CO-LAB.

At its heart: what happens when we design with what already exists?

Through recovery, repair and experimentation, the project opens up a wider conversation around circularity, heritage and the creative potential of constraint.

Thank you to Lucas and Manu for joining us, to @acecultura and its PICE Mobility Programme for supporting their participation, and to @aethoslisbon for hosting the evening.

A special way to begin a new season as we move towards Lisbon Design Week’s 5th anniversary edition.

Un último paseo por Feria Aparte 2026 antes de empezar a pensar en todo lo que viene 🍡.

Celebramos tres días de cientos de obras, encuentros entre artistas, agentes del arte y diversos públicos, conversaciones, música, actividades y más de 7.500 personas recorriendo la Ex Cervecería Ebner en el @mallbarrioindepe 🏭

Ahora queremos saber de ustedes: 
¿Con qué te quedaste de esta edición? 🧸

ᴄᴇʀʀᴀᴍᴏꜱ ᴜɴᴀ ɴᴜᴇᴠᴀ ᴇᴅɪᴄɪóɴ ᴅᴇ ꜰᴇʀɪᴀ ᴀᴘᴀʀᴛᴇ 🐬🪄🧸

Esta quinta edición no fue fácil de levantar. Hubo momentos durante el año en que incluso nos preguntamos si iba a ser posible hacerla. Feria Aparte sigue siendo un proyecto independiente y autogestionado, que cada año tiene que volver a buscar los recursos y las personas necesarias para existir. Nada está asegurado de una edición a otra.
Por eso, ver la Ex Cervecería Ebner llena durante tres días tuvo un valor muy especial.

Más de 𝟳.𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝘀 🔮 pasaron por la feria este fin de semana, recorrieron, preguntaron, conversaron con artistas, participaron, compraron obras o simplemente entraron a mirar.

Hace cinco años comenzamos este proyecto justamente con esa idea: hacer del arte contemporáneo un espacio más cercano, donde distintas formas de producir y circular pudieran encontrarse y donde no fuera necesario saber de arte o tener intención de comprar para sentirse parte.

Cinco ediciones después, seguimos intentando defender esa misma idea.

Gracias a las galerías, talleres, colectivos, artistas y proyectos que confiaron en esta edición. A las instituciones, colaboradores y aliados que decidieron apoyarla. A quienes aportaron recursos, tiempo, trabajo, ideas y energía para que pudiéramos volver a abrir las puertas nuevamente. Y especialmente a todo el equipo que estuvo detrás y delante de la feria haciendo posible algo que durante meses solo existió en planillas, reuniones, correos y muchas conversaciones.

Y gracias a quienes llegaron este fin de semana. A quienes vienen desde la primera edición y a quienes entraron por primera vez. Que más de 7.000 personas hayan decidido dedicar parte de su fin de semana a encontrarse con el trabajo de más de 200 artistas es algo que no damos por sentado.

Feria Aparte cumplió cinco años. Y después de esta edición, quizás la respuesta a la pregunta de por qué seguir haciendo todo esto está un poco más clara.
Gracias por estar acá ❤️‍🔥.

Ou-Mun Screen — Mariana Rola Pereira & Rival

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

I was immediately drawn to the story behind this piece.

Mariana Rola Pereira brings together references to Macau, where she was born with the very Portuguese tradition of Arraiolos embroidery, while Rival brings another layer through its amazing woodworking skills.

I find the result incredibly elegant, but what interests me most is the idea behind it: tradition doesn’t have to remain frozen in time. It can travel, meet another culture or another craft, and become something completely contemporary.

That dialogue between cultures, materials and makers is one of the reasons I wanted Ou-Mun to be part of our first Edit.

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

Graffiato: Taupō Street Art Festival returns this Labour Weekend, and 2026 is bringing something new 🎨
 
For the first time in its history, this vibrant annual event will see every artist complete their mural within the same laneway, maximising their impact.
 
This year will feature 11 incredibly talented artists, including two internationals, two emerging locals and seven artists from around New Zealand whose backgrounds span the globe.
 
The artists will transform this single laneway into a living canvas, showcasing live the incredible effort and unbelievable skill that is required to paint at scale. With 10 murals being painted over this coming Labour Weekend, Taupō’s 85+ existing works will be joined by several more in their ever-growing expansion.

Looking back through the archives, I believe this will be his 4th or even 5th Graffiato mural, and to see his evolution as an artist from his first mural in Taupō to this one will be quite a trip.

Practically a local, our next artist intro is for @razortaserlaser, who is coming all the way down SH5 from Roto-vegas to see us!  Razor cut his teeth with stencil art in Bristol, UK, before returning to NZ, and has been making his mark on home soil ever since. 

His art does sneakily appear around Taupō already, but this will be his first official Graffiato festival.  Razor has also been working hard with other Rotorua artists to establish their street art scene, and we're excited to see what's coming soon just up the road.

caption:
You Can’t Hold It, but You Can Touch It — Teresa Nunes with Ricardo Leal

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

There is something very sensitive about this piece that stayed with me from the moment I saw it at ROCA.

Teresa Nunes works with textiles, memory and reuse, and here she takes something almost impossible to capture, water and translates it through fabric, colour and touch.

I love the subtle variations created by botanical dyes, the hand embroidery and the use of existing textiles. And then there is the beautiful dialogue with Ricardo Leal’s wooden structure.

It is quiet, tactile and very human. It is multifunctional and can easily be used in a room as a divider or simply as a decorative piece. And it is green (my friends will understand….)

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

Available now for purchase through The LDW Edit. Discover the piece via the link in bio.

O Roca Lisboa Gallery esteve presente no mapa da @lisbondesignweek, com a exposição The Beauty in Everyday Rituals.⁣
⁣
Em parceria com a artista têxtil @teresa_nunes_, apresentámos uma instalação concebida especialmente para o nosso espaço, explorando a relação entre memória, água e os rituais quotidianos associados ao espaço de banho. 🧵🫧⁣
⁣
Ao longo destes dias, houve momentos de encontro, partilha e novas ligações que tornam esta semana ainda mais especial. 🤍⁣
Obrigado a todos os que nos visitaram e fizeram parte desta edição. ⁣
⁣

Lines with Earth — Ludivine Billaud

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

This is perhaps one of the most joyful pieces in the Edit.

I love the freedom with which Ludivine Billaud works with ceramics. There is drawing, colour, texture and experimentation, but it all comes together in an object that you can actually live with.

What particularly attracts me is the element of unpredictability. Ludivine creates her own experimental glazes, but the firing also has its say so the final surface can never be entirely controlled.

It gives each piece its own personality.

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

Available now for purchase through The LDW Edit. Discover the piece via the link in bio.

ADRO — Frederico Oliveira Vaz

WHY I CHOSE IT FROM LDW26

What attracted me to ADRO is its simplicity but also everything that sits behind that apparent simplicity.

Frederico Oliveira Vaz approaches furniture with an architect’s eye, bringing together Portuguese limestone and industrial aluminium: two materials that seem almost opposed in weight, history and character.

I particularly like this contrast between something deeply rooted in Portugal and something very contemporary and precise.

It feels architectural without being imposing, and distinctly Portuguese without relying on the obvious.

That balance is what made me want to include it in the Edit.

Michele Fajtmann, Founder of Lisbon Design Week

En su quinta edición, Feria Aparte vuelve a la Ex Cervecería Ebner, ubicada en el barrio Independencia de Santiago, con más de 40 expositores y una programación de conversatorios, talleres, música, recorridos y actividades de mediación, todos con acceso gratuito. Creada en 2022 como una iniciativa independiente y autogestionada, la feria llega a este aniversario con una pregunta que excede su propia continuidad: ¿cómo sostener un proyecto cultural sin que las condiciones de su financiamiento terminen definiendo aquello que le da sentido?

Feria Aparte se celebra del sábado 3 al domingo 4 de octubre de 2026, con entrada gratuita.

Now in its fifth edition, Feria Aparte returns to the former Ebner Brewery, located in Santiago’s Independencia neighborhood, with more than 40 exhibitors and a program of talks, workshops, music, tours, and outreach activities—all with free admission. Created in 2022 as an independent, self-managed initiative, the fair reaches this anniversary with a question that goes beyond its own survival: How can a cultural project be sustained without its funding conditions ultimately defining what gives it meaning?

Feria Aparte will be held from Saturday, October 3, to Sunday, October 4, 2026, with free admission.

Housed in an old shoe store dating back to 1880, @companhia.portugueza.do.cha is one of those places that feels like a journey in itself. Tea sommelier Sebastian Filgueiras has been sharing his knowledge and love for tea here for over two decades and every year for Lisbon Design Week, with a limited-edition tea created for the occasion.

This year, Lisbon-based illustrator @carolina.celas designed the packaging for our LDW tea box, turning it into a little story you can hold in your hands. 
Extending the narrative beyond the box, the four windows of the iconic Lisbon shop have been transformed into handmade paper scenographies by architect-designers Catarina Fragoso Mendes and Maria Luís Ferraz of @sanucurated, reflecting the colours and storytelling of Carolina’s illustrations.

We sat down with Carolina to talk about the ideas and creative process behind the project.

¿Te gustaría conocer el edificio de la antigua Cervecería Ebner? 🏛️

Muy pocas veces al año este edificio abre sus puertas, y esta es una de ellas.

Con más de 140 años de historia, aquí nació la icónica Pilsen Ebner, se impulsó la producción de Bilz, que incluso fue recomendada por la primera médica de Chile, Eloísa Díaz por sus propiedades “curativas”, y se escribió una parte clave de la historia cervecera de Chile.

Hoy es Monumento Histórico y uno de los patrimonios industriales más importantes de Santiago.

Months of preparation, collaboration, and sleepless nights led to this moment for these Burning Man artists. Fueled by their passion for creativity, artists bring their work as a gift that Black Rock citizens can explore, inhabit, and enjoy. Later, they will come to life in cities and parks around the world. Read more about art that travels in this Journal post, written by a member of Black Rock City’s Art department.

Many of these awe-inspiring works were funded by Black Rock City Honoraria grants and the generosity of the Burning Man community. In 2026, Burning Man Project invested more than $6 million in bringing art and artists through grant funding and extensive equipment and logistical support. Of this, more than $1.5 million was granted to artists through the Black Rock City Honoraria and Temple programs.

Burning Man has a powerful impact on oh so many delightful humans. Burning Man Project’s social media crew took to the Black Rock City streets to ask “Why do you Burn?” The answers were whimsical, profound, and unexpected.

caption:
Flying For Our Freedom is the story of Petit Muharto Kartodirdjo, who as a child in 1930s East Java was fascinated by the planes he glimpsed above his home, never dreaming he would one day fly one for his nation, and Bobby Freeberg, a former U.S. Navy pilot from Kansas who chose to fly for the Indonesian Republic after World War II as Dutch forces tightened their blockade on republican-held territories. 

Freeberg’s plane, registered RI-002, became so vital to the revolution that foreign press labelled it a “one-man air force,” carrying officials, supplies, and funds across blockaded territory to keep Indonesia’s scattered republican territories connected. In October 1948, Freeberg and RI-002 disappeared over southern Sumatra with a cargo of gold, a mystery that led Muharto to write this story of friendship and courage in Indonesia’s fight for freedom.

📍 Rumah Kayu at Taman Baca Ubud
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October
⏰ 2.30 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist

Flying For Our Freedom adalah kisah Petit Muharto Kartodirdjo, yang semasa kecil di Jawa Timur pada tahun 1930-an terpesona oleh pesawat-pesawat yang sesekali ia lihat di atas rumahnya, tanpa pernah bermimpi bahwa suatu hari ia akan menerbangkan salah satunya demi bangsanya, serta Bobby Freeberg, mantan pilot Angkatan Laut AS asal Kansas yang memilih untuk terbang bagi Republik Indonesia setelah Perang Dunia II, ketika pasukan Belanda memperketat blokade atas wilayah-wilayah kekuasaan republik. 

Pesawat Freeberg, yang terdaftar dengan nomor RI-002, menjadi begitu vital bagi revolusi hingga pers asing menjulukinya “angkatan udara satu orang”, membawa pejabat, perbekalan, dan dana melintasi wilayah yang terblokade untuk menjaga wilayah-wilayah republik yang terpencar tetap terhubung. Pada Oktober 1948, Freeberg dan RI-002 menghilang di atas Sumatra bagian selatan bersama muatan emas, sebuah misteri yang kemudian mendorong Muharto untuk menuliskan kisah persahabatan dan keberanian dalam perjuangan Indonesia meraih kemerdekaan ini.

Introducing the Burning Man 2027 theme 🔮 Spellbound.

Every year as Black Rock City draws to a close we say goodbye to what was, and hello to the future we build together. With this renewal comes the Burning Man 2027 theme ~ Spellbound.

The next 12 months invite you to plumb the mysteries of playa magic — from the serendipity of resonant coincidence to the gobsmacked awe of seeing things that cannot possibly be, and yet somehow are. It is an invitation to consider the nature of enchantment itself; to delve into the enigmatic depths of your own psyche, where belief and disbelief collide and the stories we are told bleed into the stories we tell ourselves, and in turn into the realities we construct for others.

Read the Burning Man 2027 theme announcement! Link in bio

This book launch features two bilingual books, 200 Voices, One Climate Story and Through the Lens: Stories of Climate and Sustainability, presented through readings, visual works, and conversation, bringing together more than 250 contributors from across Indonesia who respond to climate change through art, poetry, personal narratives, and photography. 

Contributors range from primary and secondary students to university students and adults from diverse professional backgrounds, many non-professional, bringing lived experiences across generations that create a sense of closeness and honesty. 

Four contributors will share their work alongside project initiator Amanda Katili Niode PhD as facilitator, drawing on her seventeen years of collaboration across cultures and communities, rooted in the idea that lasting environmental engagement begins not with facts alone, but with noticing what has long been overlooked.

Peluncuran buku ini menampilkan dua buku dwibahasa, 200 Voices, One Climate Story dan Through the Lens: Stories of Climate and Sustainability, yang dipersembahkan melalui pembacaan, karya visual, dan perbincangan, menghadirkan lebih dari 250 kontributor dari seluruh Indonesia yang merespons perubahan iklim melalui seni, puisi, narasi pribadi, dan fotografi. 
Empat kontributor terpilih akan berbagi karya mereka bersama inisiator proyek, Amanda Katili Niode PhD, sebagai fasilitator, dengan mengangkat pengalaman kolaborasinya selama tujuh belas tahun lintas budaya dan komunitas, berlandaskan gagasan bahwa keterlibatan lingkungan yang bertahan lama tidak dimulai dari fakta semata, melainkan dari kepekaan untuk melihat apa yang selama ini terabaikan.

Telanjang Kaki: Poor Privilege Life from a Poverty Graduate explores the paradox of “poor privilege,” a concept resonating with those who have risen from humble beginnings to navigate life’s challenges with unique grit, inviting readers into a life marked by resilience, heartbreak, and the relentless pursuit of success. 

Through a kaleidoscope of allegories mirroring the author’s journey, the narrative moves from the freedom of a kite to the scripted existence of an NPC, a non-player character bound by a role it never chose, to the absurdity of performing for a world that demands the unreasonable, and finally to an ode to authenticity and the bravery to choose solitude over compromise. Written with emotional depth and unflinching honesty, it is a guide for those seeking to understand privilege, ambition, and identity, and a celebration of resilience and owning one’s narrative.

📍 Powder Room by R4D
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October
⏰ 5 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist

Telanjang Kaki: Poor Privilege Life from a Poverty Graduate mengeksplorasi paradoks “poor privilege” (keistimewaan dari kemiskinan), sebuah konsep yang menggema bagi mereka yang bangkit dari awal yang sederhana untuk menghadapi tantangan hidup dengan keteguhan yang khas, mengajak pembaca masuk ke dalam kehidupan yang diwarnai oleh ketangguhan, luka hati, dan perjuangan tanpa henti menuju kesuksesan. 

Melalui kaleidoskop alegori yang mencerminkan perjalanan sang penulis, narasi ini bergerak dari kebebasan sebuah layang-layang menuju eksistensi yang telah ditentukan sebagai NPC, karakter non-pemain yang terikat pada peran yang tidak pernah ia pilih, lalu ke absurditas berpura-pura demi dunia yang menuntut hal-hal yang tidak masuk akal, dan akhirnya menuju penghormatan terhadap keaslian diri dan keberanian untuk memilih kesendirian daripada berkompromi. Ditulis dengan kedalaman emosi dan kejujuran tanpa kompromi, buku ini menjadi penuntun bagi mereka yang ingin memahami keistimewaan, ambisi, dan identitas, sekaligus perayaan atas ketangguhan dan kepemilikan atas kisah hidup sendiri.

A month in the desert helping build the “Temple of the Moon”🌙 @2026temple alongside 100+ people from around the world to bring this sacred space into existence.

The Temple tradition began at @burningman in 2000 with  David Best and Jack Haye’s Temple of the Mind. What began as a memorial for a friend became something much larger: a non-denominational sanctuary where anyone can come to grieve, remember, celebrate, pray, forgive, hope, dream, or simply sit in silence.

More than 25 years later, we were entrusted with building another chapter of that tradition.

That gave every bracket, every screw, every long day and night in the dust a different weight. We weren’t just building a structure. We were building a place to hold what thousands of people would eventually bring to it.

@annielocke the architect said something that stayed with me:

“Grief is love with nowhere to go. The Temple gives it somewhere to go.”

Deep respect to @gwertzman and the @the.moonlight.collective for the vision and leadership, Annie for the extraordinary architecture, Gravity for keeping us well fed, and leads: Boots, Priest, Sarah, Bobbie, Tony, Mamma Squirrel, Kama, Elke, Daphne, Doc, Peter, Morgan, Amazing, Muffins, and every heart and pair of hands that brought this offering to life. So many brought so much care and effort to this project and they did so as volunteers! I’m blown away. What an honour to build this powerful community and sacred structure together ❤️

One of the hardest and most transformative things I’ve ever been part of.

And somewhere between building a Temple and gifting butterflies across the playa, a few seeds were planted for the future. 🦋🌙

And to everyone who put a story, memorial, name(s), photo, prayer, a thought , a wish, or memory, into the Temple—I hope the fire brought forth some healing , solace, or release. 

With all my heart,

Callen

Conversatorio: Gestión cultural - desafíos para construir otros modelos

Sostener un proyecto cultural implica mucho más que conseguir financiamiento. Supone a su vez, construir vínculos, generar comunidad, adaptarse a los cambios y encontrar formas nuevas de colaboración que permitan que las ideas puedan permanecer y crecer en el tiempo.

Frente a este escenario, ¿cómo podemos construir modelos de gestión cultural más sostenibles? ¿qué lugar ocupan la autogestión, la colaboración, el territorio y las redes en estos procesos?

Te invitamos a participar al conversatorio junto a Ana Carolina Tapia (@feria.aparte ), Agustina Margotta (@criptagaleria ), Nay Jiménez (@barriotriana.cl ) Carolina Caimanque y Pablo Gutiérrez (@mapamapa.cl ) y Natalia Stipo (@tramagc) quienes compartirán distintas experiencias y reflexiones sobre las formas de sostener proyectos culturales y construir otros modelos de gestión.

La conversación será moderada por Mauricio Cifuentes, gerente de Chilecreativo

A warm-hearted robot inside a reality simulation called “Life X,” a life-game resembling contemporary Earth, receives the most complex mission it has ever been given: to play a human avatar named Sugi and rediscover his Life Purpose within the Battlefield. 

From the start, Sugi is trapped by the mistaken belief that success means becoming influential, wealthy, and renowned, modelling himself on Silicon Valley visionaries even as his avatar struggles with social awkwardness, doubt, and a fragile sense of identity. His pursuit of financial gain briefly pays off, building a media empire, fame, and love, until the system detects the imbalance, locking his progress and collapsing everything he has built through betrayal and family discord. Only by unlocking Third Eye mode, allowing him to observe his life from outside, does Sugi discover his true purpose: not conquest, but giving.

Sejak awal, Sugi terjebak pada keyakinan keliru bahwa kesuksesan berarti menjadi seseorang yang berpengaruh, kaya, dan bernama besar, menjadikan para visioner Silicon Valley sebagai panutannya, meski titisan yang ia mainkan bergulat dengan kecanggungan sosial, keraguan, dan identitas diri yang rapuh. Pencariannya akan keuntungan finansial sempat membuahkan hasil, membangun kerajaan media, ketenaran, dan cinta, hingga sistem mendeteksi ketidakseimbangan itu, mengunci progresnya dan meruntuhkan segala yang telah ia bangun melalui pengkhianatan dan perpecahan keluarga. This complete collection of poems draws together works scattered across books, zines, bulletins, and notes from a fugitive period, long fragmented and now, for the first time, gathered as a whole. It grew from a handwritten testament dated 1987, in which the poet granted permission for his words to be collected, and took shape over more than a decade of compiling and translating, becoming, in time, a capsule of history. 

More than a document, it stands as a quiet call to look after one another from below, an act of solidarity with those who have never felt safe within the state. It keeps hope alive, inviting us again and again to reread the relationship between words and the movement of time. Deepened by a photographic archive, it becomes a sanctuary for slowing forgetting, healing trauma, and reaching toward true freedom, offered from and for the families still waiting for certainty.

Berangkat dari wasiat penulis, yaitu surat ketikan pada 1987 yang mempersilakan puisi-puisinya dikumpulkan, kumpulan ini terbentuk melalui lebih dari satu dekade penyusunan dan penerjemahan, hingga menjadi kapsul sejarah. 

Lebih dari sekadar dokumen, ia hadir sebagai penanda waspada untuk saling menjaga dari bawah, sebentuk solidaritas bagi sesama yang merasa negara tidak pernah menjadi rasa aman. Ia menjaga harapan tetap hidup, mengajak kita berulang kali membaca kembali hubungan antara kata-kata dan gerak zaman. Diperkuat oleh arsip foto, kumpulan ini menjadi ruang suaka untuk memperlambat kelupaan, menyembuhkan trauma, dan memperjuangkan kemerdekaan sejadi-jadinya, dipersembahkan dari dan untuk keluarga yang masih menanti kepastian.

Uncovering a largely overlooked chapter of history, The Battle for Bali chronicles the violent guerrilla war that erupted on Bali when the Dutch colonial army returned after World War II, placed within the Indonesian Revolution and Dutch colonial politics. Drawing on extensive archival and field research, Anne-Lot Hoek reveals stories of oppression, betrayal and hidden terror camps, but also of fierce resistance and friendship.

Join the launch of Merebut Bali and a conversation with Anne-Lot Hoek and journalist Ni Ketut Sudiani, featuring AA Nanik Suryani, granddaughter of national hero I Gusti Ngurah Rai, and artist Mangu Putra.

📍 Bar Luna at Casa Luna
🗓️ Friday, 23 October
⏰ 6.30 PM
🎟️ Free Entry

Mengungkap babak sejarah yang selama ini terabaikan, The Battle for Bali mengisahkan perang gerilya penuh kekerasan yang pecah di Bali ketika tentara kolonial Belanda kembali setelah Perang Dunia II, ditempatkan dalam konteks Revolusi Indonesia dan politik kolonial Belanda. Berbekal riset arsip dan lapangan yang mendalam, Anne-Lot Hoek mengungkap kisah penindasan, pengkhianatan, dan kamp-kamp teror tersembunyi, sekaligus kisah perlawanan yang gigih dan persahabatan.

Hadiri peluncuran Merebut Bali dan perbincangan bersama Anne-Lot Hoek dan jurnalis Ni Ketut Sudiani, menghadirkan AA Nanik Suryani, cucu Pahlawan Nasional I Gusti Ngurah Rai, serta seniman Mangu Putra.

Brought to #UWRF26 with Suchi Rangaswami, this book by the late Michael Morrissey follows Captain Bligh’s second breadfruit mission, this time carrying a mysterious Tahitian stowaway tasked with keeping the plantlings alive, a man whose obituary strangely appears in Jamaica’s Royal Gazette within months of his arrival. 

Set against Jamaica in 1792, as the Apprenticeship system ends and the formerly enslaved build new settlements amid ongoing tensions and injustice, it follows Quashie and his grandfather as they travel to spread word about breadfruit, while unravelling the story of a Tahitian friend whose desire for vengeance carried him halfway around the world. 

Michael Morrissey’s imaginative exploration moves between eighteenth-century Tahiti and nineteenth-century Jamaica, filling in the gaps left by an official history, and telling a story of love, resistance, and the colonial-era obsession with a single, humble fruit.

Music presented by Celtic Room

Bersama Suchi Rangaswami, buku karya almarhum Michael Morrissey ini mengisahkan misi kedua Kapten Bligh membawa buah sukun, kali ini dengan seorang penumpang gelap misterius asal Tahiti yang bertugas menjaga bibit tanaman tetap hidup, seorang pria yang berita duka wafatnya secara aneh muncul di Royal Gazette Jamaika hanya beberapa bulan setelah kedatangannya. 

Berlatar Jamaika tahun 1792, ketika sistem Apprenticeship berakhir dan mereka yang sebelumnya diperbudak membangun permukiman baru di tengah ketegangan dan ketidakadilan yang terus berlangsung, kisah ini mengikuti Quashie dan kakeknya dalam perjalanan menyebarkan kabar tentang sukun, sembari mengungkap kisah seorang sahabat asal Tahiti yang dendamnya membawanya menempuh setengah dunia. 

Eksplorasi imajinatif Michael Morrissey ini bergerak antara Tahiti abad kedelapan belas dan Jamaika abad kesembilan belas, mengisi celah yang ditinggalkan sejarah resmi, serta menuturkan kisah cinta, perlawanan, dan obsesi era kolonial terhadap satu buah yang sederhana.

The Forgotten Words That Saved the World is a magical adventure for readers aged 7 to 9, following bickering siblings Thomas and Alexandra as they discover a hidden realm tucked behind their garden hedge. At first they are delighted, enjoying a place where steaming baos grow on trees and leaves taste like lollipops, but these treats come with an unexpected responsibility: they have not found a carefree playground, but have been chosen to restore balance to a dying world. 

To succeed, they must master the one thing they dread most, the ‘Forgotten Words’ of the Mandarin language, decoding ancient characters to activate magical powers, solve environmental puzzles, and track down a missing dragon. This debut fantasy blends high-stakes adventure with relatable sibling chaos, serving as a mirror and window for Third Culture Kids and young adventurers everywhere.

The Forgotten Words That Saved the World adalah petualangan magis untuk pembaca usia 7 hingga 9 tahun, mengikuti kisah kakak-beradik Thomas dan Alexandra yang sering bertengkar saat mereka menemukan dunia tersembunyi di balik pagar tanaman kebun mereka. Pada awalnya mereka senang, menikmati tempat di mana bakpao kukus tumbuh di pohon dan daun-daun terasa seperti permen lolipop, namun kelezatan ini datang dengan tanggung jawab yang tak terduga: mereka bukan menemukan taman bermain yang bebas dari beban, melainkan telah terpilih untuk memulihkan keseimbangan dunia yang sekarat. 

Untuk berhasil, mereka harus menguasai satu hal yang paling mereka takuti, yaitu ‘Kata-Kata yang Terlupakan’ dari bahasa Mandarin, dengan menerjemahkan aksara kuno untuk mengaktifkan kekuatan magis, memecahkan teka-teki lingkungan, dan melacak keberadaan seekor naga yang hilang. Debut fantasi ini memadukan petualangan penuh risiko tinggi dengan kekacauan khas hubungan kakak-beradik, menjadi cerminan sekaligus jendela bagi Third Culture Kids dan para petualang muda di mana pun.

Poetry and music are fruits of the same tree. Verse united with voice creates music on the page and is transformed in performance; where there is rhythm and melody, there is poetry. In the grounds of Honeymoon Garden, under the stars and in the shadow of an almighty statue of Shiva, poets and musicians gather as verse takes on rhythm, from song to spoken word to hip-hop, chasing themes of nature, identity and emotion. 

In this magical setting, artists from across the globe collide, with indigenous music meeting contemporary spoken word for a night charged with reflection. Meanwhile, two empires meet in the garden kitchen: Chef Aman Lakhiani’s Lamuri brings the deep spice of South India face to face with the fire of Sumatra, cauldrons steaming as the poets take the stage. Chilled drinks and food are on sale throughout the evening.

Di halaman Honeymoon Garden, di bawah langit berbintang dan dalam naungan patung Siwa yang agung, para penyair dan musisi berkumpul saat larik-larik puisi menemukan iramanya, dari lagu hingga spoken word dan hip-hop, menyusuri tema alam, identitas, dan emosi. 

Dalam suasana magis ini, para seniman dari berbagai penjuru dunia saling bertemu, musik tradisi berjumpa dengan spoken word kontemporer, untuk sebuah malam yang sarat perenungan. Join this mighty conversation between father and daughter, Frank and Saoirse Connolly, exploring the scandals that shook history and women’s stories of revolution that reimagine the future. Frank, a veteran investigative journalist, has dedicated his life to exposing corruption at the heart of Irish politics, while Saoirse has spent the past decade publishing the stories of those impacted by that corruption and building bold alternatives for a better future. 

Moderated by midwife, author and CNN Hero of the Year Robin Lim, alongside co-authors from the award-winning Rebel Ma anthology series, this panel explores the role of the writer in times of collapse through storytelling, spoken word and creativity as an act of resistance, as we grapple with what comes after Empire.

What if unity and diversity were never opposites at all? In Samarasā: The Ocean of Unity, Drs. I Ketut Suardana, M.Fil.H offers a rare philosophy of wholeness, rooted in the Sanskrit union of sama (balanced, one) and rasa (essence, feeling), where difference converges in harmony without losing its shape. The book moves through Citta (mind), Rasa (heart), and Karsa (action), guided by Dharma, revealing that truth must not only be known, but felt and lived. 

Drawing on the Upaniṣads, Bhagavad Gītā and Balinese tradition, Suardana widens the lens from the individual to civilisation, asking how nations and Bali’s own future might hold difference without fracturing. Like waves never separate from the ocean, this book invites us to see the unity beneath difference, and finally act on it.

⏰ 3 PM

Bagaimana jika kesatuan dan keberagaman sebenarnya tidak pernah bertentangan? Dalam Samarasā: The Ocean of Unity, Drs. I Ketut Suardana, M.Fil.H menawarkan sebuah filosofi keutuhan yang jarang ditemukan, berakar dari perpaduan bahasa Sanskerta antara sama (seimbang, satu) dan rasa (esensi, perasaan), di mana perbedaan menyatu dalam harmoni tanpa kehilangan bentuknya. Buku ini bergerak melalui Citta (pikiran), Rasa (hati), dan Karsa (tindakan), yang dituntun oleh Dharma, mengungkap bahwa kebenaran tidak hanya perlu diketahui, tetapi juga dirasakan dan dijalani. 

Berpijak pada Upaniṣad, Bhagavad Gītā, dan tradisi Bali, Suardana memperluas sudut pandang dari individu ke peradaban, mempertanyakan bagaimana bangsa-bangsa dan masa depan Bali sendiri dapat menampung perbedaan tanpa terpecah. Seperti ombak yang tak pernah terlepas dari lautan, buku ini mengundang kita untuk melihat kesatuan di balik perbedaan, dan akhirnya bertindak atasnya.

This book invites readers, young and old, to rediscover childhood as a treasure trove of joyful memories, gems ready to light up our darkest days.

Gestora cultural y fundadora de Feria Aparte, feria de arte contemporáneo que articula galerías de arte, colectivos y proyectos de artistas en un espacio de encuentro gratuito y abierto a la comunidad. Su trabajo se ha orientado a la creación, desarrollo e implementación de proyectos culturales, poniendo especial énfasis en la circulación del arte contemporáneo, la descentralización territorial y la activación de espacios patrimoniales a través de modelos independientes y colaborativos.
Con formación como artista visual en la Universidad Diego Portales, su trayectoria se ha nutrido tanto de la práctica artística como de la gestión cultural. Ha trabajado en galerías de arte, proyectos independientes y marcas, desempeñándose en áreas de producción, comunicaciones y vinculación institucional. Entre sus experiencias se encuentran colaboraciones con Galería AFA, Metro 21, Hasta Pronto Brewing, Galpón Independencia, así como en proyectos de curaduría, coordinación de exposiciones y desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas con entidades culturales y privadas.
A lo largo de su camino, ha impulsado instancias de colaboración interdisciplinaria, construyendo puentes entre artistas, instituciones y públicos diversos. Su interés se centra en repensar los formatos de exhibición, fortalecer la profesionalización de artistas y gestores, y generar espacios de encuentro cultural accesibles y sostenibles.
Actualmente, desde Feria Aparte, lidera un equipo de trabajo que busca ampliar las redes de circulación artística en Chile, consolidando la feria como un referente para la visibilización de proyectos emergentes y consolidados en el ámbito de las artes visuales y la cultura contemporánea.

Anna @byronbayrandr is a naturopath, acupuncturist and therapeutic bodyworker with more than 30 years’ experience in natural health and wellness. 

Anna weaves together natural medicine, bodywork, lifestyle practices, vibrant nutrition and compassionate care to help people restore balance, strengthen resilience and reconnect with their inner joy.

Guided by a deep calling to help others through this medicine, Anna’s personal journey led her into the jungles of Gabon, where she spent several months immersed in traditional Bwiti training, ceremonies and rituals with Iboga. She was profoundly touched not only by the plant, but by the Bwiti teachings of truth, self-knowledge, personal responsibility, connection with nature and learning to genuinely understand and love oneself.

At the Byron Wellness Festival, Anna will share how her experience with Iboga and Bwiti has deepened and expanded her lifelong work in natural medicine, aftercare and integration. She will explore Iboga as a traditional African plant medicine, the wisdom of Bwiti, and the growing international interest in ibogaine—particularly in the areas of substance dependency, trauma, brain injury and concussion, and psycho-spiritual wellbeing.

Central to Anna’s presentation is the respect and responsibility required when approaching such a powerful traditional medicine. She will honour Iboga’s Indigenous African roots while discussing the importance of traditional knowledge, careful preparation, health assessment, ECG and blood screening, medical safeguards and ongoing integration. This is an educational offering designed to open a respectful and informed conversation, not to encourage the unauthorised use of Iboga or ibogaine.

Anna will be presenting an educational talk on Saturday at 11.30am on the Bruns Stage. The full schedule will be out early October!

caption:
This book traces the life of Tjokorda Gde Raka Soekawati, a Balinese prince born in Ubud in 1899, caught between the traditions of his kingdom and a world reshaped by Dutch colonial rule. It follows his rise as punggawa of Ubud and member of the Volksraad in Batavia, and his role as a cultural bridge-builder who helped found the influential Pita Maha artists’ movement in 1936 alongside Rudolf Bonnet, Walter Spies, and his brother. 

In 1931, he carried Balinese art and dance to the Paris Colonial Exposition, introducing the island’s traditions to Europe. The book builds towards his most consequential chapter: his 1946 election as President of the State of East Indonesia, a role he held until 1950. Ultimately, it’s the story of how one prince helped shape the Bali the world knows today.

📍 Puri Kantor Legacy The Heritage Palace

⏰ 3 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist

Buku ini menelusuri kehidupan Tjokorda Gde Raka Soekawati, seorang pangeran Bali yang lahir di Ubud pada tahun 1899, yang berada di antara tradisi kerajaannya dan dunia yang berubah akibat pemerintahan kolonial Belanda. Buku ini mengisahkan perjalanannya sebagai punggawa Ubud dan anggota Volksraad di Batavia, serta perannya sebagai penghubung budaya yang turut mendirikan gerakan seniman Pita Maha yang berpengaruh pada tahun 1936 bersama Rudolf Bonnet, Walter Spies, dan saudaranya. 

Pada tahun 1931, ia membawa seni dan tari Bali ke Pameran Kolonial Paris, memperkenalkan tradisi pulau ini kepada Eropa. Buku ini mengarah pada babak paling penting dalam hidupnya: terpilihnya ia sebagai Presiden Negara Indonesia Timur pada tahun 1946, jabatan yang diembannya hingga tahun 1950. Pada akhirnya, ini adalah kisah tentang bagaimana seorang pangeran turut membentuk Bali yang dikenal dunia saat ini.

People with mental conditions, called as ODGJ, have rarely been treated as a major issue, struggling to attract attention from human rights advocates. Some conditions are visible while others go unseen, their cries for help suppressed and ignored; poverty and hostile environments leave many cast aside, confined, and even physically restrained. 

Through his poetry collection Soto Otak, Tan Lioe Ie gives voice to these experiences, drawing on references from Chairil Anwar to Led Zeppelin, mythology, and the tragedy of 1965, tears within a Bali often called “the last paradise.” His own experience living with mental illness offers a rare, valuable way into understanding this hidden world.

⏰ 2.30 PM

Orang-orang dengan kondisi mental, disebut sebagai ODGJ, jarang dianggap sebagai isu utama, dan masih kurang mendapat perhatian dari para pembela hak asasi manusia. Beberapa kondisi terlihat jelas, sementara yang lain tidak tampak, jeritan minta tolong mereka diredam dan diabaikan; kemiskinan dan lingkungan yang tidak bersahabat membuat banyak dari mereka tersisih, dikurung, bahkan dipasung. 

Melalui kumpulan puisi Soto Otak, Tan Lioe Ie menyuarakan pengalaman ini, dengan referensi dari Chairil Anwar hingga Led Zeppelin, mitologi, dan tragedi 1965, air mata di dalam Bali yang sering disebut “surga terakhir”. Pengalaman pribadinya hidup dengan gangguan mental menawarkan cara yang langka dan berharga untuk memahami dunia yang tersembunyi ini.

Night Before Nyepi is a poem inspired by the Balinese people and the pride they take in their traditions. It offers a window into the author’s gratitude and admiration for their Balinese community. It also serves as a reminder that our experience of time is shaped by how present and aware we choose to be as we move through this ever-evolving world. 

The author has collaborated with a young Balinese artist, Agus Ramantha, who, after nearly two months of talent and dedication, has created the 17 images you see.

caption:
This book marks a shift in Oka Rusmini’s artistic voice, moving from explosive expression toward a more contemplative and restrained form. Where her earlier work foregrounded open protest against custom and patriarchy, this collection instead works through the archiving of memory, weaving the trauma of 1965 survivors into a quiet, intimate personal narrative. 

Here, the female body is no longer solely a locus of wounds, but a space for producing meaning: an ecosystem of memory, language, and a more subtle yet still political and dignified resistance.

⏰ 5 PM

Buku ini menandai pergeseran suara artistik Oka Rusmini, dari ekspresi yang eksplosif menuju bentuk yang lebih kontemplatif dan terkendali. Jika karya-karyanya sebelumnya menekankan gugatan terbuka terhadap adat dan patriarki, kumpulan ini justru bekerja melalui pengarsipan ingatan, merajut trauma penyintas 1965 ke dalam narasi personal yang sunyi dan intim. 

Di sini, tubuh perempuan tidak lagi semata menjadi locus luka, melainkan ruang produksi makna: sebuah ekosistem ingatan, bahasa, dan resistensi yang lebih subtil, namun tetap politis dan bermartabat.

This story is set against the brutal backdrop of 16th-century North Sulawesi, long before the shadow of the VOC, the Dutch trading company that would later colonize the region, reached Indonesian shores. Pingkan Matindas is a legendary epic of devotion amidst tribal chaos. 

In an era defined by greed and relentless territorial conquest, Pingkan and Matindas represent the ultimate rebellion, a love that chose poverty and peril over the whims of tyrants. When Pingkan’s beauty caught the dangerous obsession of a powerful King, her loyalty remained unshakable, and though Pingkan and Matindas’ journey ended in a tragic sacrifice, their blood became the soil from which the Minahasa people grew. Today, their legacy stands tall in Manado, North Sulawesi, not as mere myth, but as a monumental testament to a love that ended centuries of war.

📍 The Elephant
🗓️ Sunday, 25 October
⏰ 3 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunches

Kisah ini berlatar belakang Sulawesi Utara yang keras pada abad ke-16, jauh sebelum bayang-bayang VOC, perusahaan dagang Belanda yang kelak menjajah wilayah ini, tiba di tanah Indonesia. Pingkan Matindas adalah kisah epik legendaris tentang pengabdian di tengah kekacauan antarsuku. 

Di era yang dipenuhi keserakahan dan penaklukan wilayah tanpa henti, Pingkan dan Matindas mewakili pemberontakan sejati, sebuah cinta yang memilih kemiskinan dan bahaya daripada tunduk pada kehendak para penguasa lalim. Ketika kecantikan Pingkan menarik obsesi berbahaya seorang Raja yang berkuasa, kesetiaannya tetap tak tergoyahkan, dan meskipun perjalanan Pingkan dan Matindas berakhir dengan pengorbanan yang tragis, darah mereka menjadi tanah tempat masyarakat Minahasa tumbuh. Kini, warisan mereka berdiri kokoh di Manado, Sulawesi Utara, bukan sekadar mitos, melainkan sebagai bukti nyata akan cinta yang mengakhiri perang selama berabad-abad.

We’re peering behind the curtains to meet some of the artists making bold new work for this year’s Junction 👀

Up next is Travis Hennessy, whos show @zoeskillerinstinct opens tonight! 

+ describe what makes a killer thriller: 
Mystery, murder, mayhem, melodies and music and a killer Queen ready to take on the world! 

+ tell us about your practice:
This year has been busy locally with my work at Black Box Theatre Co and as MD for LC’s production of We Will Rock You. I also composed the piano score for Mudlark Theatre’s Enough before heading to Syd for our first season of ZKI. I first started writing songs when I was in my teens so I’ve been a composer now for about 30 years, but this is the first time I have composed for the Cabaret format.

+ what makes creating in lutruwita so special/different? 
Tassie artists take our creative practice very seriously. We have dedicated audiences who appreciate the craft, so when creating works for local audiences it’s important that we really honour that shared love of theatre and really leave no stone unturned as we create a work that’s deserving of people’s time and money. That’s definitely been front-of-mind for us and I can safely say that our lutruwita has never seen anything like this before!! 

+ who is Zoe? [from Zoe’s Killer Instinct]
Zoe is eternal. A superstar – of course – but she is so much more than that. She is the aurora and the eclipse. A force of nature who bestows her light on only those she deems worthy. And if you are unworthy? Then heaven (or anyone) help your black little hearts! 

+ describe your show in 3 emojis
❤️🔪🎹

+ what makes Tasmanian theatre so unique?
I think there is always a level of fearlessness that drives theatre in Tas, especially in the creation of new work. We never take for granted the opportunity to create and share and so I think that allows makers to take more risks and swing a bit wider and push the boundaries. That’s certainly what we’ve done with ZKI and the work is so much better for it!

This darkly comic horror novel follows Dion Sobarna, who escapes to Bali hoping to heal his broken heart after his ex marries someone else, only to find himself haunted by two things at once: memories of his former love and a very real ghost. 

Together with Khimah, a fellow victim of heartbreak, he ends up stranded at Pondok Ki Amat, a mysterious place of healing that only the desperate can find. But rather than recovering, Dion is dragged back into the trauma of his past, and as the line between memory, hallucination and reality blurs, he confronts a terrifying question: what if Pondok Ki Amat is not a place where wounds are healed, but a place where they are nurtured… to be devoured?

Bersama Khimah, sesama korban remuk hati, Dion terdampar di Pondok Ki Amat, tempat penyembuhan misterius yang hanya bisa ditemukan oleh orang-orang yang putus asa. Namun, bukannya pulih, Dion justru terseret kembali ke dalam trauma masa lalunya, dan saat batas antara kenangan, halusinasi, dan kenyataan makin kabur, ia dihadapkan pada satu pertanyaan mengerikan: bagaimana jika Pondok Ki Amat sebenarnya bukan tempat menyembuhkan luka, melainkan tempat luka dipelihara… untuk dimangsa?

SOUND AND FREQUENCY WITH TANYA ALIJANI
Melbourne based @tanyaalijani is a sound healing practitioner, meditation teacher and breathwork facilitator. For more than fifteen years, she has been immersed in her own healing and spiritual practice, following a deep curiosity about the body, consciousness and the many ways we find our way back to ourselves. What began as a personal search gradually became the work she now holds for others.

Her studies have taken her across sound healing, meditation, breathwork, Hatha Yoga, Kundalini Yoga, Himalayan Kriya and embodied spiritual traditions, and this breadth of learning forms the foundation of her approach. Her work brings together ancient wisdom, modern science and lived experience, with a particular interest in the relationship between intention, the heart, the nervous system, breath and sound.

At Byron Wellness Festival @byronwellnessfestival Tanya will share Soulchemy™, her signature journey weaving guided meditation, heart-led intention, conscious breathwork, alchemy crystal bowls and frequency. The experience begins with an inner journey to connect with the heart and set a powerful intention, followed by breathwork to open the body and create space for movement, release and greater receptivity. Sound then becomes the place of integration, carrying the intention through the body and guiding participants into a deeper state of alignment, presence and connection.

When faced with everything that’s going wrong in the world, it’s easy for cynicism to be the default mode.

When cynicism is so mainstream, we think it’s actually more punk to be optimistic and work toward building the future we want  ☀️

This year at Burning Man, a coalition of burners proved what’s possible when you lean in:

- the first 100% solar-powered art car gathering with @robotheartfoundation 
- a free clean energy alternative to Hell Station for Black Rock City citizens, open 24/7

This test demonstration goes beyond the playa and is intended as a blueprint for quickly deploying large-scale solar for disaster relief, live music, construction, large events and beyond.

Cynicism didn’t build this. Community did. ⚡

Jasmine Crisp | Tell me I'm pretty, tell me I'm good.
📍22 Carrier Street, Benalla

Jasmine Crisp’s mural, Tell me I’m pretty, tell me I’m good , delivers a witty critique of decorative public art, pairing lush floral imagery with a cascade of gold stars to parody our hunger for validation. Beneath the humour sits a celebration of her love for painting shiny things and the quiet joy she finds in nature. Created at a massive scale under a tight deadline, the work showcases her technical rigour and determination, transforming a challenging wall into a bold, self‑aware statement about beauty, originality and artistic confidence.

Vero Coya | Interwoven
📍5-9 Bridge Street East, Benalla, rear wall

Vero Coya’s mural creates a powerful dialogue between the organic world and the built environment, scaling microscopic rhythms of sun and rain into a striking, wall‑sized meditation on connection. Through rich texture and flowing forms, the work becomes a call for stewardship - a reminder that we are inseparable from the cycles that sustain us, and responsible for the future we help shape.

Across 84 square metres of brick, Juzpop captured intimate human emotion you can feel from the street.

Juzpop | Open your eyes
📍44 Bridge Street East, Benalla (Laneway through to Fawckner Drive)

JUZPOP’s mural stretches across 6×14 metres, pushing the boundaries of scale and intimacy through her signature double‑exposure technique. The collision of textures and narratives brings raw vulnerability to the surface, transforming photographic process into paint to articulate profound human emotion.etched across an entire wall. Western Australian roots, Victorian landscape, and a burst of colour that stops you mid-step.

Sarsar | Field Notes
📍107 Bridge Street East, Benalla

Sarah McCloskey (SARSAR) shifts from her intricate realism to a bolder, more painterly approach for her mural, Field Notes, using the textured brick surface as a space for experimentation. Framed like an open sketchbook, the work features Eucalyptus preissiana and Hakea laurina - native species that connect her Western Australian roots to the Victorian landscape. With an amplified colour palette and a radiant neon orange backdrop, she transforms a quiet side street into a vibrant moment of discovery, inviting passersby to pause and appreciate the often‑overlooked beauty of their own local flora.

A veces, crear comienza simplemente por aprender a mirar de otra manera.

Grinduroooooooooo!!!! 💜💜 

Holy smokes it’s crazy to think that exactly 10 years ago was my first time rolling into little old Quincy! The magic that @sierratrails has been building up here, and all across the Lost Sierra, has shaped me so much as a person and rider!! This event has meant so much to me over the years and getting the opportunity to have a teeny-tiny part of fostering that magic is incredible. 

Which is why it’s such a bummer and honestly downright confusing as to why none of you want to come hang out and ride some of the most picturesque trails in California! This event had one of the lowest turnouts I’ve seen, particularly after leaving last year with so much stoke and a real feeling of starting something great. I know the world is a crazy place these days, but to me, there is nothing better to block out the crap than disappearing into the mountains to race bikes all weekend! So let me know, what WILL get you out here?? It’s my goal to see this event succeed and spread the word of the magic that @sierratrails has built up on Mt. Hough!! So reach out, how can we get YOU out there in 2027?? 

Ok, enough event talk, onto the racing!! Coming in as defending champ for both @grinduro and the Mt. Hough Enduro was pretty wild, especially when real hitters like @danlikesbikes and @mctubbbin turn up to steal my lunch money. Had an absolute blast out there all weekend, partying it up at the back and ripping the stages! Snuck myself into second place 🥈 for grinduro, once again emptying the tank going up and hooning my @revel__metal El Jefe on the way down. Too dang fun. It may not be a full defense but regardless, proud to hold my own against legit pros! 

Sunday was all about the Downcountry bikes and I was ready to let the @revelbikes Ranger go to work! Seeing Dan and Tobin in Lycra and road shoes on the start line, I knew I couldn’t let the roadie boys take my title 😂. Left it all out there and stoked to hold it down and take the win 🏆!!! I guess we were having too much fun going party pace at the back as we didn’t get a single riding shot 😂. I’d call that a proper party-to-race ratio🤙

DUSTOPIA is the next independently produced art film by Ayni and Severin Koller of @unisonofilms 

A gift for the Burning Man community, Part II, into the visual world of DUST. 

Their vision was to dive deeper into the paradox of this temporary city, during one of the most punishing storms the Playa had seen. A place where destruction and creation coexist, where art is built by many hands, only to be reclaimed by nature in a single breath.

The result is DUSTOPIA — a cinematic descent into the heart of Burning Man’s global culture, capturing the storm, impermanence, ritual, and the electric force of human connection in the vastness of the Black Rock Desert.

If you haven’t experienced DUST, now may be the perfect time to enter the story before DUSTOPIA arrives —

Free clean power to the people, 24/7. 

Introducing Black Rock City’s first megawatt-scale clean energy power plant - SOLAR STATION. 

This gift from @solarpunks.club, Solaris and Burning Man returns with 4x the generation capacity of last year: Over 1 MW of solar (DC), 5.4 MWh of battery storage, and free clean electrons for all BRC citizens to charge art cars, e-bikes, phones, art installations, batteries and more. 

For the first time in Burning Man history, @robotheartfoundation’s iconic art car will be charged at SOLAR STATION and deliver a fully solar-powered DJ set to the playa as a celebration of what a clean energy future looks like - today. 

This year, SOLAR STATION also powers a large theme camp hub and six art installations entirely from the sun. 

This gift is made possible by a coalition of burners who have pooled resources, skills, and conviction to overcome the initial cultural and economic inertia that has kept large-scale clean energy from displacing diesel for temporary applications.

What we test & demonstrate on playa doesn’t stay here. This technology is a solution for disaster relief, construction, large events, live music and more - anywhere portable energy currently means portable pollution. 

Come plug in at 2+K, see what community clean energy looks like in action, and BYOC (bring your own cable) to ensure compatibility!

Video by: @damien.blue & @solarpunks.club

🍂October is one of the most exciting months of the year for the climbing community in the Gunks.

We're looking forward to welcoming climbers from near and far as both Flash Foxy Mini Fest (October 2-4) and GunksFest x Gunks Climbers' Coalition (October 9-12) bring people together to build new skills, share knowledge, and strengthen connections within the climbing community. From climbing clinics and educational workshops to panel discussions, adventure films, guest speakers, and community gatherings, these events celebrate the many ways people connect through climbing while experiencing the unique landscapes of the Shawangunk Ridge.

As the steward of these climbing landscapes, Mohonk Preserve is proud to support opportunities that inspire connection to nature, stewardship, and community. We know the cliffs, carriage roads, and trails will be busy, vibrant, and full of energy, and we can't wait to see people enjoying this special place together💚

Interested in attending? Visit the event websites or check out the tagged accounts in this post to learn more about schedules, registration, and programming.

If you're visiting the Gunks this month, please help protect the places that make these experiences possible. Stay on designated trails, respect wildlife, pack out everything you bring in, and follow Leave No Trace principles. Small actions make a big difference in protecting the cliffs, forests, and habitats we all love.
Have a great climb, look out for one another, and enjoy an amazing month in the Gunks! ✨

K Y L E.  L I O N H A R T

Kyle Lionhart @kylelionhart has honed his craft and built an extremely loyal fanbase by busking on the streets and beaches of his hometown Byron Bay. Musically, Kyle’s sound has raised comparisons to the likes of Ben Harper and Matt Corby. His honest and poetic songwriting explores relationships of love, death, friendships and the often harsh realities around them.

In February 2015, Kyle self-released his debut EP Keep In Mind. At a time when even major labels were struggling to sell CDs, Kyle sold out more than 10,000 copies. His music and reputation soon spread around the world thanks to the enthusiastic reviews of impressed tourists, and it wasn’t long before record labels began to notice the young busker, who was drawing crowds in the hundreds on the main street of Byron Bay.

Kyle signed to Ivy League Records in 2016 and a year later released his second EP entitled Eleven & Two. The EP generated over 10 million streams and lead to a sold out national Australian tour, a European tour with Xavier Rudd and a debut London headline show that sold out within a week of going on sale.

Following EPs Keep In Mind and Eleven & Two, Kyle released his acclaimed 2019 debut album Too Young, featuring streaming hits Sorry I’m Gone (feat. Emily Reid, Holding On and So Close. 2020 revealed standalone singles Beautiful Life, Dream It Right and a stunning cover of the Cranberries’ classic, Dreams.

In May this year, Kyle released the single Shelter, his first new music in nearly 2 years, with extensive accompanying tour dates taking him right across the country.

Kyle has amassed more than 60 million streams to date and has enjoyed sold out headline shows across Australia, also playing festivals such as Splendour In The Grass and Bluesfest and opening for Xavier Rudd, Foy Vance, and Niall Horan.”

In what may be the most stirring city on earth, there is always room for stillness.
Offering spaces for meditative calm, we are thrilled to congratulate these Honoraria peace practitioners.
A 17-foot-tall lotus shaped bud, "The Sanctuary of the Silent Star" is activated by quiet: rewarding those who arrive in silence with an immersive celestial experience.
"1/1000 — A Wish for Recovery" is a luminous steel paper crane inspired by the Japanese tradition of folding 1,000 cranes — each one a wish, handmade through community.
200 year old salvaged rosewood panels from a Thai Buddhist temple construct "Pandora's Eye," inviting you to look through the aperture of myth itself.
"Cocoon" is an enveloping sculptural shelter — a crocheted refuge to remind that before transformation, we must first slow down and experience stillness.

📸 1: “The Sanctuary of the Silent Star” by Michael McIntosh
📸 2: “1/1000” – A wish for recovery by Steel Tigerlillies 
📸 3: “Pandora’s Eye” by Joe Di Marco and Hannah Yata
📸 4: “Cocoon” by Jillian Culver and the Pilot Hill Art Collective

Participants joined Mohonk Preserve staff Andrew Reynolds, Senior Manager of Volunteer Programs; Cheryl Elsinger, Managing Ranger & Trailhead Operations; Justin Key, Associate Director of Facilities & Grounds; and Carmen Acuna, Ranger in removing litter and caring for the lands we all share.

Stewardship takes many forms, and every piece of trash removed helps protect the health and beauty of the landscape for visitors, wildlife, and future generations.

💚 Thank you to Flash Foxy and everyone who participated in this cleanup and demonstrated that caring for the outdoors is part of every adventure.

Claudia Heredia es la creadora detrás del proyecto Para un roto y un descosido, una firma dedicada a la belleza del diseño natural y la decoración botánica. 
En esta edición de BROCANTE, impartirá el taller práctico “Crea tu centro con flores preservadas”. En esta experiencia de desconexión, diseñada para crear sin prisas y sin necesidad de experiencia previa, los participantes aprenderán a mirar el arte floral desde una nueva perspectiva. 
A través del juego con diferentes volúmenes, texturas y tonalidades, cada asistente descubrirá cómo conectar con la materia vegetal y plasmar su huella personal en el diseño, llevándose a casa un centro floral único, duradero y lleno de vida listo para conservar.
El taller es gratuito, pero se paga un pequeño importe de 15€ para cubrir los materiales.
📅 Fechas: 17 y 18 de octubre
📍 Lugar: Brocante by Mercado de Motores (Museo del Ferrocarril)
🔗 Descubre su trabajo: @paraunrotoyundescosido

caption:
American-born, Berlin-based artist fumi is rapidly emerging as one of the most exciting new voices in the techno scene 🌀

Under the guise of her grandmother’s name, fumi’s eclectic selection and musical background bellows a playful rendition of old and new school techno, and comes together through quick, high energy mixing.

As a member of 240 KM/H, fumi is not only influenced by the techno scene, but draws ideas from many other genres and bubbles, including jazz, hip hop, and RnB. With a dedication to the craft of track selection and mixing, the artist treats her setup as an instrument, composing a new sound through layering. 

Characterized by fast mixing and multi-deck construction, fumi’s sound is one of it’s own.
