Some of the most visionary technology has been conceptualized on the playa. These Black Rock City 2026 Honoraria artworks fit right in.

"The Portal of Collective Imagination" is a 20-foot aluminum, bamboo, and mycelium arch — a luminous geometric halo that transforms voice, breath, and movement into poetry and generative visuals.
"Harmonic Orbiter" is a kinetic sculpture balanced on a single point, powered by the people inside it. As participants shift weight, the structure orbits, turning strangers into a single shared system.
"Spectral Scarab," Inspired by Egyptian sun god Khepri, transforms throughout the day and night, symbolizing rebirth in an evolving radiant display. 

1 📸: “The Portal of Collective Imagination” by Kim Carson (Photo courtesy of Kim Carson) 
2 📸: “Harmonic Orbiter” by Linda Qian and the Harmonic Orbiters (Photo courtesy of the Harmonic Orbiters)

Invisible by day, illuminated by night⚡ Meet Marc Pascal, the artist behind the main stage lasers and lighting décor woven throughout the Wildlands 🌀 

Through suspended spirals, sweeping arcs of LED light and lasers cutting through the night, Marc creates glowing pockets of connection and moments of magic across the festival site. 

“The cool thing about Strawberry is they are not afraid to mix things up, there is always change afoot to keep things fresh. This is perfect for us artists, as it keeps us on our toes, so much thinking and visualising goes into this event way before we reach the site. And the site! The best! So inspiring! Some of those trees are 100’s of years old, I love trees, all of my site lighting decor uses trees as the anchor.” 

We invite you to take a moment to pause, look up at the trees and watch the Wildlands transform after dark this November.

Burning Man is everywhere — 365 days a year, around the world creative beings bring the culture to life in their home communities. But once a year, a uniquely dusty tradition ignites the Communal Effort that becomes Black Rock City. 
On a ridge several hundred feet above the Black Rock Desert, you can feel the heat coming off the dry lakebed that stretches five miles from east to west here and nearly 50 miles north to south. With a vibe reminiscent of Road Warrior, ribbons of dust are rising off the playa as numerous vehicles converge on a common destination — the Golden Spike, an Axis Mundi that will soon draw creative beings from across this vibrant global cultural movement. 
So begins Black Rock City 2026. On Saturday, August 1, hundreds of city builders converged and took a moment to drive the Golden Spike into the dust, marking the spot where the Man and Man Pavilion will be lovingly hand built over the next three plus weeks. Out of this nothingness a city will rise — built through love, strength, perseverance, and tenacity by crews with names like Shade, Gate, Perimeter & Exodus, Solar, HEAT, and dozens more. 
Then, Black Rock City will welcome the world. For eight days it will serve as a nexus for connection, awe, and creativity — a city built and ignited by its inhabitants, sending ripples of wonder and innovation into the cosmos. 

Photos and prose by @campimp from Profiles in Dust

It may seem ironic that an event with so many impactful tentacles in the world begins with the collective raising of a nine-mile fence. But the annual construction of the Trash Fence is as symbolic as it is functional. Yesterday was Fence Day, when hundreds of people came together to build the fence that circumnavigates Black Rock City. The fence delineates the physical boundaries of Black Rock City, and serves the practical purpose of catching windblown trash that escapes despite participants' best efforts.
 
“It's the day that all the different departments break off from the different things that they do, hand, foot, head, heart. We all move as one body. And nobody's more important than the other. It's more true to what we actually are.” explained Barbarella, one of the builders. 
 
They do it the old-fashioned way. By hand, pounding in fence posts. Rolling out miles of orange trash fence, and tying it with twine to lines that have been strung between the posts. The Trash Fence is intentionally built by hand, an early morning ritual that sets the tone for an ephemeral city built through the Communal Effort of its citizens, and a global cultural movement that arises through more than one million people bringing their dreams and ideas to life around the world.
 
Photos and prose by Terry Pratt from Profiles in Dust. Thank you for documenting the faces behind this enduring tradition.

MANOA
Manoa @musicofmanoa is an Australian multi-instrumentalist, singer-songwriter, breathwork facilitator and Native American flute teacher whose work invites people to slow down, reconnect with nature and rediscover a sense of presence. Blending original folk music with the Native American flute, handpan, guitar and immersive nature soundscapes, Manoa creates experiences that foster reflection, creativity and connection.

Drawing on a PhD in Ecopsychology and years of experience in environmental education, his work bridges music, nature and wellbeing through performances, workshops and immersive experiences that encourage deeper listening—to ourselves, to each other and to the natural world. He has supported artists including Nahko and Satsang, and has performed at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival and Pranafest.

Manoa will host a 60-minute workshop at Byron Wellness Festival with a relaxed introduction to the Native American flute. Participants will explore mindful breathing, learn foundational breath and finger techniques, experiment with expressive embellishments, and play a simple melody together. No musical experience is needed, and flutes are available for those who don’t have their own. The workshop is designed to give participants a fun, inspiring first experience with the instrument and build confidence to continue their musical journey with the flute.

atmos pink別注モデルとして、'47（フォーティーセブン）の定番「CLEAN UP（クリーンナップ）」キャップが登場。

ネイビーをベースにしたストライプ柄が目を引く、洗練されたデザイン。クラシックな雰囲気を残しながら、ストリートやカジュアルスタイルにも自然に馴染み、いつものコーディネートにさりげないアクセントを添えてくれます。

caption:
Temple of the Moon by James Gwertzman, the Moonlight Collective and the Temple Build Crew from Oakland, CA: The official design selected for the 2026 #BlackRockCity #Temple . Designed alongside architect Annie Locke Scherer, the concept takes its inspiration from the Queen of the Night—a rare desert cactus flower that blooms for just a single night each year. Using parametric design and algorithmic modeling to shape straight timber pieces into sweeping, organic curves, the structure features a radial flower geometry with winding, deflected pathways that encourage visitors to slow down as they transition into a quiet space for reflection.

This project builds on years of playa installations created by James Gwertzman and @the.moonlight.collective . His earlier Burning Man works include #PrairieOfPossibilities (2022/2023) and #TheMoonlightLibrary (2025)—a beloved interactive wooden library and event space that has since found a more permanent home at @fly_ranch .

Physically, the @2026temple is anchored by a 30-foot-tall central tower crowned with wooden petals engineered to hinge open at night, enclosing a central tree-like "stamen" that reaches up to 52 feet into the sky. Extending outward from this core are five curving wooden arms, surrounded by 20 free-standing slatted petals and an outer perimeter fence spanning roughly 170 to 220 feet in diameter with eight "moon gates" representing the phases of the moon. 

The last parts of #2026temple are currently being built by the wonderful temple crew with the Moonlight Collective and the @templebuildersguild in Oakland, CA. It burns in less than 50 days!

Jonathan Hanson ( @explorationquarterly ) on Writing, Overland Conservation, and Land Cruisers 🎙️

Overland Journal Podcast host Ashley Giordano ( @desktoglory_ash ) interviews writer, ecologist, and @overlandjournal Co-founder Jonathan Hanson for the publication’s 20-year anniversary. Hanson discusses his favorite expedition vehicles, including his 1973 FJ40 and a 1993 Land Cruiser Troopy that has traveled across Australia, Africa, and the US. He shares how early field-biology work and outdoor exploration shaped his approach to conservation and travel, leading to the creation of Overland Journal and @overlandexpo alongside @scott.a.brady and Stephanie Brady. Reflecting on his editorial philosophy, Hanson recounts collaborating with Tom Sheppard on the Vehicle-dependent Expedition Guide, highlights memorable journeys in Southern Africa and Egypt, introduces his new publication, Exploration Quarterly, and offers practical advice on vehicle modifications, low-impact driving, and essential overlanding gear.

【JASPER ZIONIC “Bee Nice”】

KEENとの2026年別注第二弾。
蜂からインスパイヤーされた一足。
蜂がいなくなったら世界から果物、植物は絶滅する。蜂に優しく、BEE NICE。

私たちが当たり前のように楽しんでいるものの多くは、ミツバチをはじめとする花粉媒介者の存在に支えられています。
世界中の植物の受粉を支える、小さなヒーロー。
そんなミツバチへのリスペクトと、「蜂に優しくしよう」というシンプルなメッセージから生まれたのが、KEEN Jasper Zionic “Bee Nice”です。

アッパーには柔らかなヘアリースエードを採用し、フラッフィーシューレースを組み合わせることで、ミツバチを思わせる温かみのある表情に仕上げました。
ヒールにはお花のアイコンとともにハニカムロゴを配置。さらに、Jasper Zionicを象徴するサイドパネルの波線には、蜂のグラフィックと、花から花へと飛び回る蜂の軌跡を忍ばせています。

インソールには、今回のコラボレーションのために制作したオリジナルの“ハニードリップ”ロゴをプリント。
足元から、ちょっとだけ自然を意識する。
Be Nice to Bees.

【Saucony Omni 9 "Pink Flamingo"】

ピンクフラミンゴそのものをインスピレーション源に、カラー・姿勢・存在感のすべてを落とし込んだ逸足。ピンク色は、食べたもの（藻やエビ）からにじみ出る色であり、自分で“色”を作り出している鳥です。「自分らしい生き方から、自然とその人だけの色がにじみ出てくる人」へ向けた逸足です。人と違っていい。目立っていい。ピンクフラミンゴのように、鮮やかに、堂々と立ち続けてほしいという想いを込めてデザインしました。ライニングにはToo Fly to Blend in. (馴染むにはイケすぎている・誰とも違う、だから埋もれない)というメッセージが隠れて入っています。自分の個性を受け入れ、周囲との違いをポジティブに楽しめる。そんなメンタリティを持つ方へ向けたシューズ。

【ZX8000 atmos G-SNK 13 "Chlorophyll"】

「atmos」と「adidas Originals」が手掛ける名作別注シリーズ”ZX 8000 G-SNK”より、シリーズ第13弾となる”Chlorophyl”が登場。
今作のデザインソースとなるのは、1999年に登場したオリジナルカラー”Chlorophyll”。アイコニックなカラーリングが、2020年に発売された”G-SNK 3”以来、約5年ぶりにG-SNKシリーズへとカムバックします。
まさに”Chlorophyll（葉緑素）”を思わせる鮮やかなグリーンカラーをベースに、”G-SNK”を象徴するスネークスキンパターンを随所に配置。生命力溢れる植物を彷彿とさせる鮮烈なグリーンと特徴的なテクスチャーが融合し、”ZX 8000”のアイコニックなシルエットに新たな存在感を与えています。
さらに、”G-SNK 3”ではハラコ素材を使用していたパーツには、今回はオリジナルモデルに忠実なメッシュ素材を採用。1999年のオリジナルカラーが持つディテールを踏襲しながら、G-SNKならではのエッセンスを加えた仕上がりとなっています。
オリジナルへのリスペクトとG-SNKシリーズのDNAを融合させた、コレクター心をくすぐる一足。長年”ZX 8000”を追い続けてきたファンにとっても、見逃せない一足が完成しました。

La discapacidad no es el conflicto ni el desenlace en BEAUTY. Es el punto de partida de una historia colectiva sobre deportistas que se mueven, compiten, viajan y construyen comunidad.

Nos entusiasma dar la bienvenida a BEAUTY, dirigida por Eduardo Muñoz y José del Corral, y producida por @toma_cafe_films 

El documental sigue a Alejandro Marín, ingeniero mecánico y referente en ortoprótesis, en su llegada a Vigo para hablar sobre inclusión y deporte adaptado en O Marisquiño, uno de los principales festivales de cultura urbana de Europa.

Durante cuatro días en la playa de Samil, Alejandro se encuentra con skaters y riders de BMX adaptado de todo el mundo. Entre ellos están Marcelo Lusardi, Julián Molina, Dan Butler, Santiago Lozano, Ryusei Ohuchi, Vinicius Sardi, Ítalo Romano y Daniel Amorinha.

Cada uno tiene una relación diferente con la discapacidad y los deportes de acción. Juntas, sus experiencias componen un retrato más amplio de la identidad, el movimiento, la representación y la importancia de encontrar a otras personas que comprendan lo que vives.

En lugar de presentar a sus protagonistas a través de los relatos convencionales de adversidad y superación, BEAUTY se centra en quiénes son, qué hacen y la comunidad que han creado alrededor del skate y el BMX.

“Born To Burn” is a gorgeous new book by Miguel Arraiz García, the architect and artist behind “Temple of the Deep” in Black Rock City 2025. Miguel tells the story of the creation of the Temple, but also explores his journey with fire, art, and community — from Las Fallas in Valencia, Spain, to Burning Man. Filled with photographs, sketches and stories, “Born To Burn” reflects on how art can bring people together, help process loss, and forge meaningful connections.

If you’ve followed the Temple project, love Burning Man, or are simply curious about the power of community and creativity, this is one you’ll enjoy. Purchase your copy here: https://borntoburn-book.com/ 🔥

As many of you may know, the Heathcote Lowerlands is currently undergoing an exciting redevelopment by the City of Melville. 🚶 Walk, ride or take public transport if you are able to - the 30 minute river walk from the station is one of our favourite ways to arrive on a Sunday morning.

♿ Fully wheelchair accessible, accessible toilets on-site

This isn’t about dancing perfectly.

Feeling deeply.
And coming home to yourself.

Complex発のフードカルチャープラットフォーム「Family Style」が、日本初上陸！『atmoscon 2026』に登場！

「Family Style」は、フードを起点に、ストリートカルチャー、ファッション、音楽、アートなどを横断しながら、その都市でいま注目すべきレストランやシェフ、ブランドを独自の視点でキュレーションするフードフェスティバル。

日本初開催となる今回は、Family Styleが東京のフードカルチャーを独自にキュレーション。長く街やカルチャーに根づいてきた店から、新たなスタイルを生み出している注目のフードプレイヤーまで、全7組が参加します。

会場には、ジャンルもバックグラウンドも異なるフードが集結。それぞれの店が持つストーリーや作り手のこだわりを、Family Styleならではの視点でひとつのカルチャー体験としてつなぎます。
さらに、フードを提供するだけではなく、参加者とのコラボレーションによる限定メニューやパッケージ、マーチャンダイズ、ビジュアル表現なども展開予定。

「何を食べるか」だけではなく、「誰が、なぜそれを作っているのか」「その店がどんなカルチャーをつくってきたの
か」まで含めて体験する場を目指します。

SOUND AND FREQUENCY 
Tanya Alijani @tanyaalijani is a sound healing practitioner, meditation teacher and breathwork facilitator. For more than fifteen years, she has been immersed in her own healing and spiritual practice, following a deep curiosity about the body, consciousness and the many ways we find our way back to ourselves. What began as a personal search gradually became the work she now holds for others.

Her studies have taken her across sound healing, meditation, breathwork, Hatha Yoga, Kundalini Yoga, Himalayan Kriya and embodied spiritual traditions, and this breadth of learning forms the foundation of her approach. Her work brings together ancient wisdom, modern science and lived experience, with a particular interest in the relationship between intention, the heart, the nervous system, breath and sound.

At Byron Wellness Festival @byronwellnessfestival Tanya will share Soulchemy™, her signature journey weaving guided meditation, heart-led intention, conscious breathwork, alchemy crystal bowls and frequency. The experience begins with an inner journey to connect with the heart and set a powerful intention, followed by breathwork to open the body and create space for movement, release and greater receptivity. Sound then becomes the place of integration, carrying the intention through the body and guiding participants into a deeper state of alignment, presence and connection.

TEA CEREMONY
Tea has an extraordinary way of inviting us back to ourselves. It asks nothing of us except our presence.

This offering is a unique collaboration between Byron Bay facilitators Heidi Lampard and Troy Abraham, where two distinct streams come together to create a third, an experience that neither tea nor sound could create alone.

The tea gently opens awareness, while the sound provides a supportive landscape for the nervous system to soften, the mind to quieten and the body to settle into a place of effortless being.

Heidi Lampard @heidi.lampard has spent many years immersed in the practices of yoga, meditation, tea ceremony and retreat facilitation. A senior yoga teacher, meditation guide and tea ceremony facilitator, she is passionate about creating spaces that invite people back into presence, authenticity and embodied awareness. Drawing on both ancient wisdom traditions and lived experience, her work gently supports the nervous system to soften, the heart to open and a deeper connection with self and life to emerge.

Troy Abraham @troysplayground has spent decades immersed in the worlds of yoga, music and sound. A senior yoga teacher, teacher trainer, retreat facilitator and lifelong musician, he brings a rare depth of experience to every space he holds. His intuitive approach weaves together live meditative sound, breath, movement and presence to create experiences that are deeply grounding, expansive and profoundly moving. Whether guiding a yoga practice, facilitating a retreat or creating immersive soundscapes, Troy’s work is rooted in authenticity, simplicity and a genuine invitation for people to reconnect with themselves.

Together, they create a space where tea and sound meet, allowing something subtle yet profound to emerge, a shared experience that is unique for every person in the room.

Murray Kyle @murraykylemusic is a Byron Bay based singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and sound healer whose music is known for its heartfelt lyrics, soothing melodies, and uplifting presence. Blending folk, world, and devotional influences, his songs create spaces for connection, reflection, and collective singing.

With a career spanning more than two decades, Murray has performed at festivals, retreats, and wellness events around the world, sharing music that inspires presence, authenticity, and a deeper connection to self and community. His performances weave together original songs, mantra, storytelling, and moments of stillness, inviting audiences into an experience that is both intimate and expansive.

Whether performing solo or collaborating with other musicians, Murray’s warm and grounded style has made him a much-loved presence within the conscious music community. His offerings encourage audiences to slow down, open their hearts, and rediscover the healing power of music shared together.

Nama sang GOAT @leomessi diabadikan jadi nama spesies tumbuhan di Peru. Diberi nama “Salvia messii”, tumbuhan yang ditemukan di kawasan Pegunungan Andes ini dinamai oleh peneliti dari Peru dan Argentina sebagai bentuk penghormatan buat Lionel Messi. Apalagi, bunganya punya perpaduan warna biru muda dan putih yang mirip sama jersey Timnas Argentina.

Masih satu keluarga sama mint dan rosemary, Salvia messii bisa tumbuh sampai sekitar 1,5 meter dan biasa ditemukan di lereng berbatu pada ketinggian 2.000–2.400 mdpl. Tumbuhan yang keberadaannya udah tercatat sejak 2009 ini akhirnya resmi dideskripsikan sebagai spesies baru lewat penelitian yang terbit di jurnal ilmiah Phytotaxa pada 2 Oktober 2026. Sayangnya, Salvia messii juga dinilai terancam punah karena persebarannya yang terbatas, ditambah ancaman kekeringan, kebakaran, sampai perubahan iklim.

[📷: AP Photo / Gustavo Garello / Jean Capcha-Ramos / Paúl Gonzáles / Phytotaxa]

K Y L E.  L I O N H A R T

Kyle Lionhart @kylelionhart has honed his craft and built an extremely loyal fanbase by busking on the streets and beaches of his hometown Byron Bay. Musically, Kyle’s sound has raised comparisons to the likes of Ben Harper and Matt Corby. His honest and poetic songwriting explores relationships of love, death, friendships and the often harsh realities around them.

In February 2015, Kyle self-released his debut EP Keep In Mind. At a time when even major labels were struggling to sell CDs, Kyle sold out more than 10,000 copies. His music and reputation soon spread around the world thanks to the enthusiastic reviews of impressed tourists, and it wasn’t long before record labels began to notice the young busker, who was drawing crowds in the hundreds on the main street of Byron Bay.

Kyle signed to Ivy League Records in 2016 and a year later released his second EP entitled Eleven & Two. The EP generated over 10 million streams and lead to a sold out national Australian tour, a European tour with Xavier Rudd and a debut London headline show that sold out within a week of going on sale.

Following EPs Keep In Mind and Eleven & Two, Kyle released his acclaimed 2019 debut album Too Young, featuring streaming hits Sorry I’m Gone (feat. Emily Reid, Holding On and So Close. 2020 revealed standalone singles Beautiful Life, Dream It Right and a stunning cover of the Cranberries’ classic, Dreams.

In May this year, Kyle released the single Shelter, his first new music in nearly 2 years, with extensive accompanying tour dates taking him right across the country.

Kyle has amassed more than 60 million streams to date and has enjoyed sold out headline shows across Australia, also playing festivals such as Splendour In The Grass and Bluesfest and opening for Xavier Rudd, Foy Vance, and Niall Horan.”

Dylan Blackstone has been part of the Strawberry Fields story for 13 years, creating immersive installations that blur the lines between art, architecture and experience. 

Inspired by the patterns and forms found throughout the natural world, his work invites you to slow down, look closer and get lost in the details. Shapes repeat, colours shift and familiar forms transform as you move through them, revealing something new from every angle.

“I’ve been building for Strawberry Fields for 13 years, and for all of those years it has been one of the major highlights of my year. Strawberry was the first festival that truly trusted me in my creative process, half-finished drawings, bamboo skewer models, hand gestures paired with funny noises to try to explain what was happening inside my head. I’ve made some of my best friends, met my wife and even moved to a new country because of the experiences I’ve had and the relationships I’ve formed at Strawberry Fields. I’m forever grateful to my Strawberry family.”

We’re excited to see what Dylan dreams up for Strawberry this November 🍃 

📷 @duncographic @will.hamiltoncoates @allegramazzella

Dystopia is compelling. What’s the opposite? Hope.

Xtina Chu and Corey Johnson talk in Black Rock City about all things interesting with our solar future happening now! They share how in an age of cynicism, optimism is the ultimate punk rock rebellion.

What started as a DIY experiment has evolved into a megawatt array gifting clean-energy to EV art cars and fuel-free theme camps. Meanwhile, back in California, they deploy rapid disaster-relief. They’re rewriting the rules of power, even large-scale event power. 

The future doesn’t stink. 
Moving away from individualism, they view "self-reliance" as a collective resilience network. They shine a light on the engineering — and cultural engineering — happening now and forever, more and more.

【Design Comment】 
I envisioned a “PLAYGROUND” where fashion, music, and street culture—all stemming from sneakers—naturally blend together. I aimed to create a visual where the entire venue becomes a single cultural scene, allowing each visitor to discover new inspirations.

L U L U &. M I S C H K A

Lulu & Mischka @luluandmischka are musicians, guides and lovers of life dedicated to creating space for the deep remembrance of who we are through collective song, prayer and silence. Their music has brought them a global following and seen them tour the world from festival stages, to grass roots gatherings, ceremonial spaces and high end retreats. Lulu’s crystalline voice enchants listeners and blends sweetly with Mischka’s gentle strength and musical guidance.

To sing, to express, to hold a space for everyone to find freedom is their intention.

The married couple has been sharing music in this way since 2010 together, released various albums and regularly holds transformational retreats to remember
the truth of who we are.

From the natural beauty of this world, to the elemental forces, from contemporary sages to indigenous lineages and other human wisdom keepers, Lulu & Mischka
draw upon many pathways and traditions in their offerings and music.

Their music is inspired by their personal life, authentic and real enquiry of what it means to be human in this life. 

Heart-opening and inspiring lyrics meet hypnotic
chants of various languages. No experience is needed as you melt into the magic ride of their welcoming offerings.

Como dice nuestro querido Kepa Acero: “El mar me ha enseñado a fluir.” 🌊

Y fluir también significa entender que las condiciones no siempre son favorables. Que hay veces que toca adaptarse, aceptar los contratiempos y cambiar el plan, pero que lo verdaderamente importante se queda con nosotros.

El diluvio del sábado dejó inutilizados todos nuestros equipos eléctricos y nos obligó a parar antes de tiempo. Pero nos quedamos con los abrazos bajo la lluvia y, sobre todo, con una certeza: WIPEOUT no son solo luces, pantallas o amplificadores. WIPEOUT es su gente.

De parte de todo el equipo, solo podemos decir GRACIAS. Por cada mensaje de APOYO, por estar ahí, incluso bajo la lluvia… y por las ganas inmensas de que este proyecto que nos acerca al mar siga creciendo entre todo. 

Esta 5ª edición iba camino de ser inolvidable… y, de alguna manera, lo ha sido… pero nos quedamos con más ilusión y más ganas para la siguiente! Ojalá podamos seguir🙏🏽💪🎬🎶💙 Nos vemos en la próxima ola! 🌊

INSPIRED KIDS YOGA
Stacey Louise from Inspired Kids Yoga @inspired.kids.yoga offers playful, heart-led yoga and mindfulness sessions for children where they can explore movement, breath and mindfulness through storytelling, imagination and sensory play. With over 20 years’ experience teaching yoga to children, Stacey has trained hundreds of educators and yoga teachers across Australia and New Zealand and shared kids yoga at festivals; in kindergartens; schools and through her Calm Fairies hospital program. Parents can feel at ease knowing their child is in safe, experienced hands. 

Kids Yoga (Ages 2-7) Each session is thoughtfully designed to be invitational and engaging. Using storytelling, imagination and sensory play, children are offered a space to move, rest and reset their nervous systems amidst the buzz of the festival. It’s also a chance for parents to take a moment to themselves or join in and reconnect through simple, childlike joy- either way, it’s a little pocket of magic in the day for your little love. 

Tween Partner Yoga (Ages 8-12)  Move, stretch and laugh with a friend – or come and make a new one! This fun-filled session includes group yoga, partner yoga and beginner-friendly AcroYoga, where you’ll safely explore balancing together. Along the way, you’ll learn calming breathing and mindfulness techniques to help you feel relaxed, connected and ready to enjoy the festival.

A space to pause, breathe, release, and reconnect.

Blending conscious breathwork, yoga, sound healing, meditation, and emotional integration, their sessions create powerful shifts that are felt long after you leave the room.

Ben combines breath science, trauma-informed practices, meditation, and sound therapy to support deep nervous system regulation and emotional healing.

Sarah brings a rare blend of strength and compassion through her work in breathwork, yoga, nutrition, sound healing, and voice activation, creating a space where transformation feels both safe and possible.

Together, they guide experiences that are grounding, empowering, and deeply restorative.

『SEPARATION 空間をほどく』は、未来へ資源をつなげていくために、設計の段階から解体後やその先のことまで見据えるプロジェクトです。
 
私たちが携わる空間づくりの中には、つくってから壊すまでのサイクルが短いプロジェクトも多く、そのたびに廃棄物が発生します。なかでも、さまざまな素材が複合的に使われ、解体時の分別が難しい「混合廃棄物」は、再利用や再資源化を難しくし、資源循環を進めるうえでの課題の一つになっています。
 
混合廃棄物量を低減し、より持続的な空間づくりを実現するためには 、空間を構成する壁や家具を解体時に素材へと分離できるような設計の視点も必要だと考えました。
 
今回の取り組みでは、これまで培われてきた合理的な納まりやものづくりの知恵を異なる視点から捉え直し、さらに現代の科学技術を手掛かりとすることで、空間を構成する素材が次の循環へとつながる、新たなデザインの可能性を探ります。

SEPARATION — Designed to Come Apart looks past demolition from the very first stage of design, so that resources can carry on into the future.
 
Many spaces are built and taken down in a short cycle, and each time, waste is left behind. Mixed waste is made of combined materials that are hard to sort, and it is one of the biggest obstacles to reuse and recycling.
 
So we asked a different question: what if walls and furniture were designed to separate back into their materials? We revisit time-tested joinery and craft knowledge and draw on modern science and technology. In doing so, we explore new design possibilities that let materials go on to their next life.
 
Turn it, soak it, dissolve it, light it. Come see a space come apart in Daikanyama.

American journalist Kade Krichko has written an article for *Adventure Journal* inspired by the protest movement that took place at the ATXARTE climbing paradise in the 1990s.
He crafted the story of that peaceful yet effective movement againts the mines by interviewing figures such as Guillermo "Willy" Bañales, Jabi Berasaluze, and Edu Gomez.
The piece has been named a finalist in the Mountain Article category of the @banffmountainfestival Mountain Book Competition.
The winners will be announced in mid-October.

The Wallas is a collective of musicians and yogis who come together to share the ancient practice of Kirtan — the devotional music of yoga. There is no better way to end two days of practice than with our voices united. The Kirtan with The Wallas will close the 5th edition of the Wander Yogi Festival — a collective offering of sound, presence, and gratitude. 🤍

I get a little emotional writing this right now. 🥹

Looking at these pictures from last weekend’s @thewanderyogi_official fills my heart with so much gratitude.

Gratitude for every single person who joined, opened their hearts, stayed curious and dared to explore a different way of connecting with themselves and others.

We spend so much of our lives thinking, analysing and doing. And sometimes so little time actually EXPERIENCING life with presence and joy.

Understanding mentally that something needs to change is one thing. But inviting your whole body onto that journey? Creating new experiences that help your nervous system learn that something unfamiliar doesn’t necessarily mean something unsafe?

That’s a whole different story.

Because our nervous systems don’t learn through understanding alone. They also learn through experience, repetition and the relationships we feel safe enough to explore within.

And honestly? I will always be grateful for following my heart four years ago. For daring to take that first step towards a life that actually feels like mine.

Today, I get to speak about and facilitate so much of what I needed most back then.

Rebuilding a sense of safety in a body that learned to function in a society where overwhelm and overachievement are often celebrated.

Reintegrating playfulness, trust and the courage to dream again.

Learning to meet life from a place of love rather than fear.

And remembering that life isn’t just something we’re supposed to manage, optimise or survive. We’re here to LIVE it. To feel it. To play with it.

I guess that’s why we share what we share.
At least that’s why I do. ❤️

この作品は、越前工芸をもっと身近な存在として、多くの人に知ってもらうための試みです。完成された工芸品をそのまま届けるのではなく、越前和紙や越前漆、越前打刃物、越前焼など、それぞれの工芸をかたちづくる素材や制作の痕跡を「部分」として取り出し、5cm角の小さなパーツにしました。
このパーツには、職人の手仕事や制作の時間、その土地で出会った人や活動の記憶を抽象的に重ねています。そして、身近な量産品に一枚ずつ貼り重ね、工芸の不均一なテクスチャをまとわせます。
新しい工芸品をつくるのではなく、すでに存在する物を越前の工芸によってアップデートする。安価で均一につくられ、交換されていく量産品に手仕事の痕跡を加えることで、もう一度愛着を持つきっかけをつくります。
5cm角という単位は、越前の記憶を残す記録であり、物や空間に愛着を生み出すためのルールでもあります。小さな「部分」から物へ、物から空間へ。越前工芸を日常へ広げ、新しい出会い方をつくる作品です。

This project is an attempt to make Echizen crafts more familiar and accessible to a wider audience. Rather than presenting finished craft objects as they are, materials and traces of making from Echizen washi, Echizen urushi lacquer, Echizen forged blades, and Echizen ceramics are extracted as “fragments” and transformed into small 5 cm square pieces.

Each piece abstractly carries traces of the artisans’ hands, the time involved in making, and memories of the people and activities encountered in Echizen. These pieces are then applied one by one to familiar mass-produced objects, allowing them to take on the irregular textures of traditional craft.

長年にわたりソファの可能性を探求してきたフランチェスコ・ビンファーレにとって、「Anywhere」はその研究のひとつの到達点ともいえるプロダクトです。
「どんな状況でも、最もパーソナルな方法で座る喜びを提供するためのデザインです。その開放感は、海の上に広がる空に向かって真っ白な帆が開かれているかのようです。」
——フランチェスコ・ビンファーレ——

 使う人の身体や振る舞いによって、その形や使い方が変化する「Anywhere」。あらかじめ決められた用途や姿勢を求めるのではなく、使い手自身がその可能性を引き出すことで完成する、自由で詩的なソファシステムです。
「Anywhere」には、Edraが創業以来追求してきた「Art of Living（アート・オブ・リビング）」の思想が凝縮されています。　CEOヴァレリオ・マッツェイと副社長モニカ・マッツェイは、「Anywhere」を人間のウェルビーイングと、これまでにない快適性を追求したプロダクトとして位置づけています。独自のファブリック研究によって生み出される視覚的な美しさと、触れた瞬間に感じられる心地よさ。そして、量ではなく質を重視し、流行に左右されることなく長く愛されるものを生み出すというEdraの姿勢。「Anywhere」は、家具という枠を超え、身体と空間、そして人の過ごし方に寄り添いながら、新しい「座る」という体験を提案します。

For Francesco Binfaré, who has spent years exploring the possibilities of the sofa, Anywhere represents a culmination of his ongoing pursuit.
“It is a design conceived to offer the pleasure of sitting in the most personal way, whatever the situation. Its sense of openness is like a pure white sail unfurled towards the sky stretching above the sea.”
— Francesco Binfaré
Shaped by the body and movements of its users, Anywhere is a poetic sofa system that invites freedom of expression and comfort. It embodies Edra’s philosophy of Art of Living, combining innovative fabric research, exceptional comfort, and a commitment to timeless quality. Going beyond conventional furniture, Anywhere redefines the experience of sitting in harmony with the body and space.

＝(イコール)
私たちは日常の中で「資源」と「ゴミ」を異なるものとして捉えています。
資源は自然が生み出した必要なもの、ゴミは人間が生み出した不要なもの。そのように区別する考え方は、私たちの暮らしの中で当たり前になっています。しかし、本当にゴミは不要で価値がないものなのでしょうか。

私たちが「ゴミ」と呼んでいるものの多くは、役割を終えただけであり、物質自体の価値まで失われたわけではありません。つまり、ゴミとは「価値を失ったもの」ではなく、「価値を見失った資源」と捉え直すことができます。

REFINVERSEは独自の技術によって、これまで廃棄物とされてきたものを新たな素材へと再生し、「ゴミ＝資源」という価値観を提案しています。

本展示では、「＝（イコール）」をコンセプトに据えることで「すべてのモノは等しく価値を持つ」という考え方を表しています。「資源」と「ゴミ」を分けているのは人が与えた価値の違いです。その境界を取り除くことであらゆるものは次の循環を担う資源となり、それぞれが等しい価値を持つ存在として捉えることができます。
「＝」という記号を通して、「資源」や「ゴミ」だけではなく、すべてのモノが等価であるという価値観を提案します。

= (Equals)
We treat resources and waste as opposites. A resource is finite, given by nature; waste is what human activity leaves behind, and it is unwanted. The division is so familiar that we rarely stop to question it. But is waste really without value?

Most of what we call waste has only finished a role. The material itself has lost nothing. Discarded fishing nets, waste plastics, textiles, carpet — seen differently, each can return to circulation as a new material. Waste, then, is not something that has lost its value. It is a resource whose value we have stopped being able to see.

For over twenty years REFINVERSE Group has built a business on exactly this: turning what could only be thrown away into materials and products, and making it commercially work. That success is itself the argument. If a discarded fishing net can be sold as material, its value was never absent — only unrecognised. What finishes one role does not lose its worth; it carries forward into the next cycle.

This exhibition takes a single symbol as its concept: =. What separates a resource from waste is not the substance but the value people assign to it. Remove that boundary and everything becomes a resource for the cycle that follows, each thing equal to every other.

Through one simple sign, = (Equals) proposes a way of seeing in which nothing is worth less than anything else.

This one means a lot.

We’re very happy to finally share that Wild Horses has been granted a three-year permit to continue doing what we love in the Northern Grampians.

For a small independent festival that started 10 years ago, built around Melbourne’s underground music community, getting to this point is something we’re genuinely proud of. Festivals aren’t getting any easier to run — costs keep going up, regulations keep growing — so having the certainty of the next three years is a pretty big moment for us.

A massive thank you to Northern Grampians Shire Council, and especially the communities of St Arnaud and Stuart Mill, for trusting us and welcoming our slightly unusual Wild Horses family into your part of the world each year.
We want that relationship to go both ways. When you’re heading to the festival, stop in town, grab some food, fill up the car, buy your supplies and support the local businesses whenever you can. 
Please look after the land, respect the locals and remember that for one weekend this is our playground, but for the rest of the year it’s their home.

We’ll also keep doing our part throughout the year to support local businesses and the community that has given Wild Horses a home.

And finally, this simply wouldn’t have happened without our crew. There’s a small army of people behind Wild Horses who put an ridiculous amount of time, love and energy into keeping this thing alive — and a community that has backed us for the last 10 years.
So thank you.

Three more years. Same wild spirit. Plenty more memories to make. 🐎❤️

─────────────
エリア：代官山
会場名：ヒルサイドフォーラム 
住所：東京都渋谷区猿楽町18-8 ヒルサイドテラス F棟
会期：10/30 - 11/3
時間：10:00 - 20:00 (11/2：10:00 - 17:00 / 11/3：10:00 - 18:00)
─────────────

工業素材であるアルミニウム。

私たちの営みの中に当たり前に存在するこのマテリアルは、近代工業社会の中で、人間の目的に合わせて均質に制御されてきました。

いつしかアルミは、硬質で均質な「動かない工業素材」という印象を私たちに与えるようになりました。

しかし、それは加工によって制御された、アルミの一状態に過ぎません。

水のように溶け、
布のように曲がり、
水面のように光を揺らしながら反射する。

そこには、ある種有機物のように自由に動き出すアルミの姿があります。

「アルミは動き出す」は、そんな自由で、まるで意思を持つかのようなアルミの瞬間に焦点を当て、素材に正面から向き合い、その可能性を模索するプロジェクトです。

私たちから一方的に形を与えるのではなく、ときに素材の動きを受け入れながら、
アルミそのものが持つ性質や振る舞いに目を凝らすことで、これまで見過ごされてきたさまざまな表情が見えてくる。

そして、役割を終えれば、溶かされ、姿を変え、再び私たちの営みへと戻っていく。

本展示では、私たちがアルミと向き合う中で見つけた、柔らかさ、揺らぎ、偶然性、そして循環していく性質を、ひとつの試行としてひらいていきます。

まだ知らないアルミの姿を探し、その魅力と可能性を少しずつ拡張していく。
その小さな試みの中に、人とアルミとの新たな対話と、これからの持続可能な素材との付き合い方につながる、ひとつの片鱗を見つけることができるかもしれません。

Aluminum: an industrial material, shaped by industry to be uniform and controlled. We came to see it as hard and still.
Yet that is only one of its states.
It melts like water,
bends like cloth,
and reflects light that ripples across its surface.
Here, aluminum begins to move, almost as if alive.
""Aluminum Begins to Move"" captures these moments. Rather than imposing form, we let the material lead, and overlooked expressions come into view. When its work is done, it is melted down and returns to our lives once more.
This exhibition shares what we found: softness, flux, chance and the way it keeps returning. In this small experiment may lie a new dialogue between people and aluminum.

「人生は、住まいで変えられる」
 わたしたちLIXILは、360°あらゆる「空間」と
365日すべての「時間」をデザインする「Lifescape Design」を通じ、
豊かで新しい住体験を追求し続けています。

本展示は、加速する現代において、
効率や合理性だけでは辿り着けない、
「これからの時代に必要な豊かさ」へのひとつの試みです。

キッチン、バスルーム、ガーデン ── 
私たちが目指すのは、固定化された「住まい」への概念の再構築。
使う瞬間とただ佇む瞬間、行為と没入、
静寂と賑わいがシームレスに交差する。
空間や役割の境界を解放し、新たな景色を描くことで、
日常の豊かさを拡張します。

それをかたちづくるのは、
暮らす人を考えた理由のある機能やかたち、
なめらかにつながり生まれる空間の調和と、
変化に寄り添い流れる時間。

光が移ろう空間演出のなかで、
コンセプトモデル含む4つのプロダクト空間を
ご覧いただけます。

""Life can be transformed through our living spaces.""
At LIXIL, through ""Lifescape Design""—the art of designing every spatial dimension (360°) and every moment of time (365 days)—we continuously pursue richer, new living experiences.

In an ever-accelerating world, this exhibition is an endeavor to discover the true richness needed for the era ahead—a quality that efficiency and rationality alone cannot reach.

Kitchens, bathrooms, gardens—our goal is to reconstruct rigid, conventional concepts of the home. Moments of practical use seamlessly intersect with moments of quiet lingering, action with immersion, and stillness with vibrancy. By liberating the boundaries of space and function to paint new landscapes, we expand the richness of daily life.

This vision is given form by purposeful functions and shapes crafted for everyday living, spatial harmony born from seamless connections, and time that flows gently alongside change.

Set within an environment of shifting light, you are invited to explore four distinct product spaces, including concept models.

TRAIN：列車、引き連なるもの。あるいは、本来備わっている力を引き出すこと。

重ねる、連ねる、整える。形状が似た2つ以上のモノを手にしたとき、人は無意識にそれらを揃えようとする。TRAIN CHAIRは、そうした人の所作に着想を得てデザインされた、「綺麗にしまいたくなる」感覚を呼び起こすスタッキングチェアである。角度のついた座面と肘掛けの間にもう一脚が入り込む仕掛けにより、前後方向へとどこまでも連ねることができる。従来のスタッキングチェアに見られるような、椅子を高く持ち上げる動作は不要であり、身体への負担を軽減すると同時に、収納時の所作そのものも美しいものとなる。また、主な構成をステンレスの曲げ、穴あけ、溶接といったシンプルな加工で成立させることで、特定の設備や技術に依存しない高い再現性を備えている。オフィス内の集会スペースのためのデザインであり、少人数のレクチャーからワークショップ、さらには200人規模のイベントまで幅広い用途に対応する。使用しない時には、壁際や天井の低い階段下にも無理なく収まり、会場設営や撤収の動作もスムーズに行うことができる。美しく連なった状態は、整然としたリズムを生み出し、空間の質までも引き締める。

Stacking, aligning, arranging: faced with similarly shaped objects, people instinctively line them up. TRAIN CHAIR is a stacking chair built on that instinct, evoking the urge to tidy things away neatly. One chair slides into the angled gap between the seat and armrest of the next, letting chairs link endlessly front to back. Unlike conventional stacking chairs, it needs no overhead lifting, easing physical strain while making storage itself a beautiful motion. Its structure relies on simple stainless steel work, bending, drilling, welding, so it needs no special equipment, giving high reproducibility. Designed for office gathering spaces, it suits small lectures and workshops through events of 200. Unused, it fits neatly against a wall or under a low staircase, keeping setup and teardown smooth. Linked together, the chairs form an orderly rhythm that sharpens the space itself.

オーバル型バランスボール MALLOW の新作発表とともに、多様なテクスチャーを纏った限定アートピースが一堂に会します。進化した MALLOW 2.0 には、身体の動きに応じて揺れながら、自然と起き上がる新たな機能が加わりました。
実際に触れたり、座ったりすることで感じる、生き物のような柔らかな反発と、マテリアルがもたらす知覚の揺らぎ。それらと身体が響き合う体験を通して、この世界を身体で感じるよろこびを、改めて呼び覚まします。

ー

Void Skin／空洞の表皮

空洞は、表皮という境界によって生まれる。
内と外の力が釣り合うことで、そのかたちは存在している。
僕らもまた、身体という表皮を通して世界を知覚し、
その内側にそれぞれの世界が立ち現れる。
世界は、僕らの内側にある。

デザインディレクション： 橋倉 誠
展覧会デザイン： MAKOTO HASHIKURA DESIGN
企画・制作コーディネート： 藤原 彩花

The newly evolved MALLOW 2.0, an oval-shaped balance ball, is presented alongside a collection of limited-edition art pieces featuring a diverse range of textures. MALLOW 2.0 introduces a new self-righting function that allows it to sway in response to the body’s movement and naturally return to its upright position.
Through touching and sitting on MALLOW, visitors can experience its soft, almost living response and the subtle shifts in perception created by different materials. Through this resonance between body and object, the exhibition seeks to reawaken the joy of feeling the world with the whole body.

—

Void Skin

A void comes into being
through the boundary of a skin.

Its form exists
in the balance of forces
within and without.

We, too, perceive the world
through the skin of our bodies,
and within us, our own worlds emerge.

The world is within us.

Design Direction: Makoto Hashikura
Exhibition Design: MAKOTO HASHIKURA DESIGN
Planning & Production Coordination: Sayaka Fujiwara

今回展示する新コレクションは、ロンドンを拠点とするデザインスタジオ Industrial Facility（インダストリアル・ファシリティ）に加え、イトーキの和田光平、田幸宏崇が参画した3製品。Industrial Facilityによる「HAKUSAN」、和田による「BIWA」、田幸による「ALLROUND」で構成されています。本ラインアップは、人と人をつなぐことを起点に、ワークや会議、コミュニケーションといった多様な行為に寄り添います。独創的でありながら空間に自然と溶け込み、人の動きや関係性を引き出しながら、新たな椅子の在り方を提示します。

NII is a furniture brand that transforms the office into an attractive and vibrant stage. Working closely with designers active in both Japan and around the world, NII develops innovative collections with quality, comfort and craftsmanship in every last detail. The ingenious design is a source of energy and inspiration, creating magnetic spaces where people naturally gather, connect and inspire one another.
At this exhibition, NII present its 2026 collection—highlighting the brand’s design philosophy through three new collections: HAKUSAN by London-based design office Industrial Facility, BIWA by ITOKI’s Kohei Wada, and ALLROUND by Hirotaka Tako.
Designed for today’s evolving workplaces, the new collection reflects the brand’s philosophy of Ingenious Design, combining functionality, comfort and clarity for how people meet, work and interact today.

El Salto del Nervión, con más de 200 metros de altura, es el mayor salto de agua de la península ibérica y acota el cauce del río Nervión en sus primeros pasos tras su naciminento, formando un inmenso cañón.  
Un equipo de motivados highliners ha conseguido un valioso pero limitado permiso para tender una línea que atraviese el inmenso cañón. 
Acostumbrados a montar líneas de entre 50 y 300 metros, será la primera vez que este equipo tenga que montar una línea de casi 1 kilómetro. Y con un poco de suerte, habrá agua en la cascada. 
Una historia de compañerismo y trabajo duro. Un equipo fuerte, forjado entre la comunidad highline de Guipuzkoa y de Bizkaia. Además, nadie antes ha montado una línea sobre el cañón del Nervión pero sí se ha soñado con ello. 

Nerbioiko ur-jauzia, Iberiar penintsulako ur-jauzirik haundiena da 200 metroak gainditzen dituen altuerarekin. Nerbioi ibaiaren jaiotza markatzen du arroil erraldoi bat osatuz.

Besapean linea bat montatzeko baimenarekin, gogotsu ekingo diote highline zale hauek arroila zeharkatzeko erronkari.
50-300 metroko lineatara ohituta, ia kilometro bateko tartea zeharkatu beharko dute, eta zorte pixkatekin beraien aurrean urez gainezka ari den ur jauzia dutela.

Elkarlana eta lan gogorra dira protagonistak istorio honetan. Gipuzkoa eta Bizkaian errotutako highline komunitateak amestu bakarrik egin den abenturari ekingo dio, Nerbioiko jauzian kilometroko linea montatu eta zeharkatzea.

今まで見えなかったもの、失われつつあるもの、気づかれずにいたもの。
歴史あるものづくりの中で培われてきた技術や知恵。その裏側にあり目に触れなかったもの、途絶えかけた工芸技法、そして現代の技術との掛け合わせから生まれる新しい工法。
見えていなかった潜在的な価値を“サルベージ”し、出会うことのなかったもの同士をつなぎ、時代を超えて新たな表現へとつむぐ試みである。

01｜イグサを編む
畳の衰退とともに減少するイグサ。畳に使えないB品を日用品へ編み替える産地の技法に着目し、本来床に敷く素材を垂直面へ転換。編むことで生まれる表情から、現代の暮らしに新たな「間」を提案する。

02｜普段見えない型にこそ
伝統的な提灯の制作過程にのみ存在する「型」に着目。代々継承されてきた型の仕組みと現代の光源を掛け合わせ、異なるかたちの照明として可視化した。

03｜木の歪
寸法変位が敬遠される木材の「歪み」に着目。紙のように薄く裂いた木板を加工し、二度と同じ形にならない有機的な歪みを引き出した。自然素材の偶然性を、異なる陰影を生む照明へと昇華している。

04｜曲木とシワ
木を曲げる技術は、生産環境の変化とともに切削へと置き換えられ、いつしか曲木と曲木風が混在するようになった。敬遠され削ぎ落とされてきた、木を曲げることでしか表れないシワに着目し、新たな表現として引き出した。

Things once invisible, lost, or unnoticed: wisdom from generations of craft. This project salvages hidden value, revives dying techniques, and merges them with modern tech to weave new expressions.

01 | Weaving Igusa
Reweaving sub-standard igusa grass into daily wares, this approach shifts tatami from floor to wall, offering a new spatial sense for modern living.

02 | The Unseen Molds
Focusing on molds hidden inside Japanese lanterns, this work merges inherited logic with modern light, revealing unseen structures.

03 | Natural Distortion
Reinterpreting wood warping, paper-thin timber yields unique organic distortions, turning natural chance into shadow-casting light.

04 | Bentwood Wrinkles
Focusing on wrinkles unique to steam-bending, once shaved away, this project draws them out as a bold new expression.

FLUX TABLEは、1964年創業の大阪のサインメーカー・株式会社ダイカンと、日本の3Dデザインブランド130（ONE THIRTY）が共同開発したコレクタブルオブジェクトです。

天板素材「FLUX METAL」は、積層された構造用アルミニウムパネルの断面を露出させ、職人がミクロン単位で手鏡面研磨したもの。光と視点の変化によって、静水のようにも溶融した銀のようにも見える、液体的な表情が立ち上がります。

この仕上げは機械研磨では到達できません。圧力で積層断面がずれてしまうため、表面を読み取り必要な仕上がりへ導けるのは職人の手だけです。ラグジュアリーブランドのサイン製造で60年にわたり培われた判断と感性が、そのまま素材の表現になっています。

台座は130（ONE THIRTY）が設計・製作。1本の連続したフレームから複雑な立体を構築する独自の手法により、幾何学的な厳密さとフレームならではの軽さを両立しました。液体的な天板と構造的な台座——その対比が作品全体に緊張感を与えています。

本作は、ミラノデザインウィーク2026で発表した展示「Return to… — The Beauty of Resilience」（Palermo 18／Brera Design District）の中心作品。DESIGNART TOKYO 2026では、その凱旋展示として日本初公開します。

FLUX TABLE is a collectible object developed by DAIKAN Co., Ltd. — an Osaka-based signage manufacturer founded in 1964 — in collaboration with 130 (ONE THIRTY), a Japanese 3D design brand.

The tabletop is made from FLUX METAL: engineered aluminium panels whose cross-sectional planes are exposed and mirror-polished by hand to the micron level. The result is a surface that appears liquid, shifting between still water and molten silver as light and viewing angle change.

This finish cannot be achieved by machine. Mechanical polishing causes the laminated sections to shift under pressure; only a craftsperson’s hand can read the surface and bring it to the required finish — judgement accumulated over sixty years of precision work for luxury brand signage.

DEKEL OPEN TO CLOSE - TICKET LINK IN BIO! 🔥
We’re closing out our 10th anniversary year the only way it could — with DEKEL , open to close, for six and a half hours straight.

There are only a handful of artists who know how to unite a crowd like this — to bring an entire dancefloor together as one, to align a room fully into the moment. Dekel is one of them.

Dekel isn’t just headlining this one. He’s played five Wild Horses festivals, and this November will mark his sixth. His sound has become part of what Wild Horses sounds like — woven into the sonic signature that’s carried this festival through a decade. 
There’s no better way to close our 10th anniversary chapter than with an artist we resonate with this deeply. Now he takes over an entire night, start to finish, no one else on the decks.

This will be the final event of our 10th anniversary year, and one of the biggest city shows Wild Horses has ever staged — inside a room built for sound. Northcote Theatre has hosted some of Melbourne’s most legendary events and artists, with soaring ceilings and acoustics few venues can touch. It’s also the first time a psychedelic production of this scale will take over this stage: full lighting design, immersive projection, and a sound system as clear as it gets.

Expect a night unlike anything Wild Horses has done before — one artist, one journey, six and a half hours, and a production to match the occasion.

Opening this weekend: Sally Smart’s ‘The Space of Inventory’ at Gallery Sally Dan-Cuthbert will transform the gallery into a shifting landscape of painted, stitched, printed and sculptural forms.

Extending her longstanding language of cutting and collage beyond the canvas, Smart treats the gallery itself as a space for making, with works overlapping, moving through the grid and inviting the viewer to navigate the exhibition from multiple perspectives.

Here, Smart discusses the ideas behind the exhibition, the influence of performance and choreography on her practice, and how working across materials, places and cultural contexts continues to reshape the work.

The Space of Inventory opens Saturday, 19 September

IAMF GRAND PRIZE
The International Alliance for Mountain Film is proud to inform that its 2026 Grand Prize has been awarded to Australian director Jennifer Peedom @jenpeedom !

Writer, director and producer creating movies combining documentary realism with cinematic grandeur, Jennifer Peedom developed an extremely personal style that, over the years, has made her one of the most authoritative voices in contemporary documentary cinema, particularly in the fields of nature and mountaineering. A journey that began long ago and at high altitude: in 2008 "Solo" won many prestigious awards. The turning point came in 2015 with "Sherpa", which was the third highest-grossing Australian documentary of all time and was internationally acclaimed, as well as winning at some International Alliance for Mountain Film festivals. Two years later, in 2017, she made "Mountain" in collaboration with the Australian Chamber Orchestra. The film surpassed "Sherpa" and became the most viewed documentary of all time in Australia and was released in cinemas in 26 countries worldwide. With "River" in 2021 and "Deeper" in 2025, she shifted her focus from the peaks to the water and the depths of submerged caves. The elements changed, but not the quality and style.

After the IAMF Grand Prize awarded in 2022 to Michel Dillon, this new recognition testifies to the vitality and importance of Australian filmmakers on the scene of mountain cinema.

On Now - Pedro Wonaeamirri at STATION, Sydney

Awirankini Jilamara kapi purinjirringuwi: new designs on wood brings together new ochre paintings, bark works and sculptural forms rooted in Tiwi living culture.

Working across plywood, stringybark and tunga (bark bags), Wonaeamirri’s refined geometric language speaks to Tiwi knowledge, Country and Japarra, the moon man, whose presence connects ideas of life, death, water and sea.

A quiet, deeply considered exhibition where material, cultural knowledge and contemporary practice meet.

Exhibition on until 3 October

Abdul Abdullah’s 𝚃𝚘 𝙱𝚎 𝚄𝚗𝚐𝚘𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚗𝚊𝚋𝚕𝚎 series explores what it means to resist the forces that seek to define, contain and control us. This painting, presented with Ames Yavuz at ꜱʏᴅɴᴇʏ ᴄᴏɴᴛᴇᴍᴘᴏʀᴀʀʏ this year, plays with language, absurdity and the idea of animals as inherently ungovernable.

The painting began with a linguistic joke: in Thai, the word for seal, maew nam, translates literally as “water cat”. Abdullah brings the two animals together, using the absurdity of a domestic cat among a family of seals to consider agency, freedom and the limits of our attempts to possess or control the world around us.

After taking Laneway Festival somewhere new in 2026, our Queensland edition is headed to the Brisbane Showgrounds for 2027. Thank you to Southport Sharks for welcoming us in 2026 and giving us the opportunity to share Laneway with the Gold Coast’s incredible music community.
To our Adelaide and Perth friends, we know this will be disappointing. In 2027, Laneway will be taking a break in your cities.
For over two decades, we’ve had the pleasure of bringing Laneway to Australia and New Zealand, with stints in Singapore and Detroit too. Running so many shows, so close together, across so much ground is a logistical feat we are proud of, but it also asks a lot of our lineup and crew.
Taking a pause allows us to focus on making the festival the best it can be, while freeing up time for more artists to bring headline shows to cities beyond our festival stops.
Adelaide and Perth, we love you! We are incredibly grateful to every single person who has shown up for us over the years.
This isn’t goodbye, just see you soon.
More info on Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, and Auckland coming soon, stay tuned!

¡Un beso enorme Josep Manuel Anglada y Eli Vergés, en vuestro reencuentro!

In 2024 we established a partnership with Milano Off to begin exploring opportunities for exchange between Darwin and Italy. 

In 2025 after presenting her one woman show We Keep Everything at Brown's Mart as a part of their Main Stage program we put Lisa Pellegrino in touch with our lovely Fringe Family over in Milan and Catania.

Now in the year 2026 we are excited for Lisa as she prepares to take this work on the road, a full circle moment for a show about Italian and Scottish immigration to Australia.

As an independent artist Lisa is funding this work alone purely out of her passion to share family stories and inspire discussion around legacy. You can help her out but donating to the journey today.

Compartir esta historia en un festival de montaña, tan cerca de casa y con un público que entiende y valora la montaña, la memoria y el compromiso colectivo, nos llena de motivación para seguir contando historias.

Art enthusiasts, assemble. Australia’s biggest contemporary art event is back at Carriageworks in Redfern from September 3-6.

Sydney Contemporary has returned with a Champagne-fuelled bang, featuring stunning works by more than 500 artists from 33 countries, represented by 100 galleries.

The ambitious program is made up of large-scale installations, impressive works, photographs, performances and talks. And for the first time ever, Sydney Contemporary has spilled beyond the walls of Carriageworks, with public artworks popping up across the city.

Fair director Zoe Paulsen says this year’s massive 10th edition is filled with “celebration and discovery, the familiar and the unexpected.”

Tickets start at $40 per person.

Keen? Click the link in bio to find out more. And we will see you there 😎

📸 : Wes Nel; Avril Treasure for Time Out Sydney

Billy Apple®’s iconic statement transforms Carriageworks 

A pioneering figure of pop and conceptual art, Billy Apple® (1935–2021) spent his career challenging the conventions of art, identity and the art market. First in London and New York, then across Australasia, his work continues to question the economic structures that shape the contemporary art world.

Now, the declaration makes a bold statement across Carriageworks – bringing Billy Apple®’s work into the heart of Sydney. 

This project is presented as part of Installations, curated by José Da Silva (Director UNSW Galleries), with the support of NSW Government through Destination NSW.

We are thrilled to introduce the following artists that are joining the Brisbane Illustration Fair October 2026! Check out their bios below & give them a follow! 

@chubbycalico_: chubbycalico (Jade) is an analogue collage artist based in Meanjin/Brisbane. Using scissor and glue, Jade takes entries from her diary, and transforms emotions and thoughts into layered compositions, blending images, textures, and handwritten notes to explore memory, identity, and self-reflection.

@dossyexe: DossyEXE is an independent digital illustrator selling original art prints, vinyl stickers, and other illustrated creations. Most well known for their frequent use of computer motifs, they blend retro technology, nostalgia & a graphic style to create art that captures their experiences with gender, neurodivergence & what it is to be human.

@alexwiltonart: Alex is a Brisbane-based multi-disciplinary artist and musician specialising in imaginative realism illustration. Working primarily digitally and in oils, but branching recently into inks and watercolour; Alex’s creative practice is inspired by the ways music and art evoke narrative

@richard.scott.draws: Richard Scott is a Gold Coast based printmaker inspired by the city’s architecture and signage. His works capture the essence of Queensland's humble small businesses, from snack bars and take-aways, to motels and massage parlours, with a focus on bold graphics, colours, and typography.

The closing day of the first A3 was something to write home about. The heavens opened, and the Forest stage really came into its own. Patrick Topping delivered the closing set to end all closing sets. But really, you were the highlight.

Something clicked on Sunday. The site felt familiar, there was no getting lost on the way back from the loo or grabbing a snack, and the crew was; Locked. In. We were all in a groove, and we weren’t getting out of it until close.

Looking back on the first A3 now, we’re incredibly proud of what we created together. As a team, and with you. You trusted us in our first year, and we’ll never forget it. Now our family is expanding, our team is growing, and so have you. We’re coming back bigger this year (just a bit), and we can’t wait to show you.

Roslyn Oxley has been a force in Australian contemporary art for more than four decades.

Since opening the doors to her eponymous gallery in Paddington in 1982, Roslyn Oxley has championed many of the country's most influential artists, including Tracey Moffatt, Patricia Piccinini, Bill Henson, Fiona Hall and Dale Frank, while introducing leading international voices to Australian audiences.

A long-standing exhibitor at Sydney Contemporary, Roslyn Oxley9 has participated in every edition of the Fair since its inaugural year in 2013.

This year, the gallery returns with a presentation by Jenny Watson and Mia Boe. Among the gallery's first represented artists, Jenny Watson will present significant historical works alongside new paintings, while recently represented Mia Boe debuts a new body of work that draws on personal history and broader colonial narratives. Both artists explore notions of self-hood, through interior worlds and dream-like imagery, each with a remarkably distinct voice evident in their visual symbology.

Belum setengah jam pintu JIExpo dibuka pada Jumat sore itu, antrean sudah memanjang. Gelang festival terpasang di tangan, tas-tas kecil dipeluk erat, dan sesekali layar ponsel terangkat merekam suasana yang mulai ramai. @pestapora 2026 kembali dimulai. Musik memang belum terdengar, tetapi keramaian sudah terasa langkah kaki yang tergesa-gesa, suara orang memanggil temannya, dan tawa yang pecah sebelum konser dimulai.

Di antara ribuan orang, masing-masing datang dengan alasannya sendiri.

Ada Najla, yang sebelumnya hanya bisa menonton keseruan festival lewat layar ponsel. Hari itu, ia memutuskan untuk bergabung langsung. Di tengah kerumunan orang yang tak dikenal, ia merasa hangat saat bisa bernyanyi bersama orang yang baru ditemuinya beberapa menit lalu. Di Pestapora, kebersamaan kadang tidak memerlukan perkenalan.

Hari berikutnya, Nanang membawa keluarganya jauh-jauh dari Lampung. Tujuan mereka hanya satu, menonton Sheila on 7. Bagi keluarga ini, lagu-lagu SO7 adalah bagian dari perjalanan hidup mereka. Malam itu, di depan panggung, suara mereka menyatu dengan puluhan ribu penonton lain. Kenangan keluarga ternyata bisa tersimpan dalam sebaris lirik lagu.

Sementara itu, Dita dan teman-temannya datang tanpa rencana khusus. Tidak ada daftar musisi yang wajib ditonton. Mereka hanya berjalan-jalan di area festival, membeli makanan, berpindah dari satu panggung ke panggung lain, dan tertawa bersama. Tanpa beban, malam yang biasa saja itu justru menjadi momen yang sangat berkesan.

Festival pada akhirnya adalah kumpulan momen-momen kecil, tangan yang bergandengan di tengah kerumunan, keringat di dahi, seseorang yang rela membawakan tas temannya, hingga orang-orang yang tetap bertahan menari meski sudah lelah. Kamera bisa mengabadikannya dalam sekejap, tetapi ada cerita yang lebih dalam tentang siapa yang mereka temui dan lagu apa yang mereka tunggu.

Pestapora bukan hanya tentang siapa yang tampil di atas panggung, melainkan tentang orang-orang yang bersenang-senang di bawahnya.

Bersenang-senang bersama mereka dibeberapa hari yang lalu 🍊🍓🍇

@emily.lamburd: All of my illustrations are inspired by whatever I’m deeply interested in at the moment— something I’ve studied, stumbled upon, or even discovered through a documentary. The Brisbane Illustration Fair is held at John Reid Pavilion (Brisbane Showgrounds), Gregory Terrace Bowen Hills, Brisbane. There are many options of how you may visit the fair:

🚗Driving/parking: There are three main paid parking facilities available in the area.

The Pavilion Car Park (Accessible via Gate 5 off O'Connell Terrace), The Royal International Convention Centre Car Park (Access via Machinery or Alexandria Streets), King Street Parking (Access at 600 Gregory Terrace).

Visit: https://www.brisbaneshowgrounds.com.au/exhibitors/directions-parking/ for prices and more information.

🚌Public Transport
Train: Bowen Hills and Fortitude Valley train stations are less than a 10 minute walk from the Brisbane Showgrounds.

Bus: Buses regularly run around the Brisbane Showgrounds. Main stops are on Bowen Bridge Road (outside The Old Museum) and St Pauls Terrace (near King Street). For more info, visit TransLink’s website.

John Reid Pavilion is fully accessible. Close to cafes and restaurants in King street.

Just announced: Congratulations to @renee_estee, winner of the 2026 MA Art Prize for her work ‘Empty Nest (we all wait for someone)’ presented by COMA, Booth C05.

Renée practice highlights myth-making and rituals surrounding mourning, celebration and commemoration. Her winning work, which will be on display at Sydney Contemporary with COMA, is a three-metre long diptych that considers the cycles of leaving, waiting and becoming that shape a life.

Now in its fourth consecutive year, the MA Art Prize was established by MA Financial Group, the Principal Partner of Sydney Contemporary, to celebrate and champion emerging and early-career artists exhibiting at the Fair. This year’s Prize increased to $25,000, and received a record number of submissions. 

See Renée’s work alongside works by the other MA Art Prize finalists at Sydney Contemporary, held at Carriageworks from 3-6 September 2026.

What started as an artist-run experiment has become one of Sydney's enduring contemporary galleries. Since 2007, CHALK HORSE has evolved from an independent project space into a commercial gallery recognised for its thoughtful programme and commitment to Australian artists.

Having exhibited at every Sydney Contemporary since the inaugural Fair, the gallery has grown alongside the event. This year, CHALK HORSE returns to Sydney Contemporary with an expanded presentation across two booths, bringing together painting, sculpture, ceramics and works on paper.

Galleries booth presents Adrian Jangala Robertson, Mechelle Bounpraseuth, Laura Jones, Emily Ferretti, Jasper Knight, Jason Phu, Allery Sandy, Danny Morse, Billy Benn, Harry McAlpine, Daniel Domig, Sam Doctor and Oliver Watts.

Works on Paper presents etchings by Robertson and Billy Benn, alongside works by Dean Brown.

See CHALK HORSE at Sydney Contemporary, 3–6 September at Carriageworks.

Nanda\Hobbs has been part of Sydney Contemporary since the beginning, exhibiting at every edition of the Fair since 2013.

This September, the gallery returns with a group presentation featuring Lottie Consalvo, Jonathan Dalton, Nicholas Blowers, Selma Coulthard, Roger Swainston, Anton Forde, Marie Mansfield, Matt Coyle, Floria Tosca and Andrew Sullivan.

Moving between abstraction and figuration, the presentation considers how landscape – internal, cultural and environmental – shapes contemporary practice, with works exploring memory, perception, Country, ecology and materiality.

See Nanda\Hobbs, booth A07 at Sydney Contemporary, 3–6 September at Carriageworks.

"It’s the tits! 

Delightful in name and nature, Sophie Delightful and Scarlet Tinkabelle bring the deep-seated roots of tease and taunt of vintage burlesque to the Darwin stage. Now, Darwin loves a cabaret, and they love boobs, this I know. But something that A Vintage Affair did differently was the addition of live vocals from the husky chords of Delightful. Paired with sensual contrast with Tinkerbell’s seemingly innocent persona we find quickly is anything butt. 
This tastefully naughty duo bring sugar and spice to the stage with audience cheers from the very top of the show. The sparkles and glittery gowns, with quaffed colourful curls set the stage for the vintage affair that takes up back in time. 

Delightful as the host interacts with the crowd, playing with cheeky charisma and a 1920’s finger wave curl she finds her mark early on and does not let go.  The bourbon warm vocals start as they Let Us Entertain You and we are as captivated by this modern day Gypsy. 

Followed quickly by the comedic and sensual striptease of Tinkabelle, in her first of seven costumes changes. The vintage influence can be seen in both her outfits and her movements as she masterfully commands both feather and fabric fans in hypnotic motion and flirts with the audience through the plumage of feathers."

At Sydney Contemporary, A Secondary Eye presents a sculpture-focused booth from Far North Queensland, featuring historical works from the Aurukun community and renowned Torres Strait Islander artist Ken Thaiday Snr.

This rare group of sculptures offers insight into the cultural, historical and political narratives of the Wik people of Cape York Peninsula, created before, during and after the landmark 1996 Wik Decision – a physical embodiment of ancestral narratives that continue to shape community identity and connection to Country.

Accompanying the works is previously unseen 1997 archival footage of Wik elders discussing the deliberations that led to the Wik Decision in the High Court.

Together, object, narrative and documentation highlight the enduring vitality of First Nations cultural knowledge, offering a rare encounter with the voices and stories behind these works.

When spoken word meets chaotic jazz, the world shares a collective in breath. As we are welcomed into the world of Under Skin, created and produced by local Darwin wordsmith Sophie Benkemoun, we hear the caress of the kit, flute and double bass of the Jazz Trio, with the warm vocal stylings of our producer herself. Sophie’s lyrical collaboration with our on-stage band allow a strong, and sensual introduction to the show. 

Flying in is hoop aerialist Shelley Eder, Sophie’s spoken words in song together with the full rumble of the band created a striking combination to the already enthralled audience. We find the musical stylings of Jack Tinapple (flute, saxophone and vocals), Lukas Lore (drum kit and bongos), and Adele Mammone (double bass). Our trio, clearly sharing a strong relationship with one another’s instruments to combine improvised jazz with just the right about of dissonance. The jazzy blues allow the shape of Eder’s contortion to stun the audience into appreciation, as the lyrics from Benkemoun caress and flow over the ensemble aligning with the Eder’s snake-like spins. 

Our MC, none other than local comedian Danielle Andrews, snaps us into a new world with direct address and audience polling about the Darwin Fringe Festival. “I can see the Fringe spirit is in your heart” she claims as the audience whoop and cheer for what is to come. A festival that allows artists to takes risks on stage and share pieces of their soul. Andrews riffs with the band who play back to fit the balance of smooth, yet playful improvised jazz that she busts a quick move to and educates the audience on how to claim your space on the dancefloor. Dance, being her chosen medium for self expression which sets the tone for the journey Under Skin.

グラフィックデザイナーが手がけるポスターを、作品として楽しみながら、暮らしや空間に取り入れることを提案する「POSTERS」。紙からデジタルへと媒体が移行するなか、丹念につくられたポスターを目にする機会は少なくなっています。一方で、一枚のポスターが空間や暮らしにもたらす豊かさは、今だからこそ大切なものになっています。
DESIGNART TOKYO 2026では、新たに川尻竜一、山口崇多、安田昂弘の3名が「POSTERS」に参加。それぞれが本展のために制作した新作ポスターをOFS GALLERYにて発表・販売します。異なる背景や表現を持つ3名が、ポスターという一つのフォーマットと向き合い、それぞれの視点から生み出す作品を紹介します。また、近隣のハウススタジオ「GREEN BOX」では、本展と連動したサテライト展を開催。これまで「POSTERS」で発表してきたデザイナーたちの作品を、室内のインテリアに合わせて展示します。
OFS GALLERYで新作と出会い、GREEN BOXでは暮らしに近い空間でポスターを楽しむ。異なる二つの会場から、ポスターの魅力や可能性を伝えます。時に社会を動かす力を持ち、大胆かつ緻密な表現を生み出すグラフィックデザイナーたち。その手から生まれた一枚のポスターが、個人の日常や社会の風景の一部となり、“小さな幸せ”をもたらす。そんな一枚との出会いを、ぜひお楽しみ

“POSTERS” proposes a way to enjoy posters by graphic designers as works of art while bringing them into everyday life. As media shifts from print to digital, opportunities to encounter carefully crafted posters are becoming rare, while the richness a single poster brings to a space feels more important than ever. 
For DESIGNART TOKYO 2026, Ryuichi Kawajiri, Takahiro Yasuda, and Agata Yamaguchi, join POSTERS for the first time, presenting new works created for the exhibition at OFS GALLERY. Each approaches the poster format from a distinct perspective. 
A satellite exhibition at nearby GREEN BOX will feature existing POSTERS works within a lived-in interior. Through these two venues, visitors can experience posters in different settings and discover how a single work can become part of everyday life and bring a “small sense of happiness.”

─────────────

森って、なんだろう。

世界には、900を超える「森の定義」が存在すると言われています。
どれくらいの木が生き、どんな動植物が暮らしているのか。
人はそこに、どのように関わっているのか。
見る人や目的が変われば、「森」の姿は変わります。

王子ホールディングスは、森を育て、森から製品を生み出してきた会社です。
私たちにとって森は、紙やバイオマス燃料などの原料となる木を育てる場所であり、
同時に、生物多様性をはじめとする自然環境や生態系を守り、
その価値を未来へとつないでいく場所でもあります。

けれど、森の価値は、本当にそれだけなのでしょうか。
私たちは、この展示を起点に、森の価値、
そして森と私たちの関係を捉え直すリサーチプロジェクトをはじめます。
その最初の試みとして、さまざまな分野の専門家に、
それぞれのまなざしから森を見つめてもらいました。
同じ森を見ても、見えているものは同じとは限らない。
本展が示すのは、そんな森への、多様なまなざしです。
森って、なんだろう。
答えをひとつに決めるのではなく、
森を見る新しい視点を、ひとつずつ増やしていく。
この展示が、その大きな問いをみなさまとともに考える、きっかけとなることを願っています。

What is a forest?

More than 900 definitions of “forest” are said to exist worldwide.
How many trees live there, what plants and animals make it home, and how people are involved. 
Change who is looking, or why — and the forest itself changes shape.

Oji Holdings has grown forests, and made things from them.
For us, a forest is a place to raise trees, and to protect the natural environment and its ecosystems for the future.

But is that really all a forest is worth?
With this exhibition, we begin a research project to reconsider the value of forests and our relationship with them.
We asked specialists from many fields to look at the forest through their own eyes.
What it offers is a diversity of ways of seeing.

What is a forest?
Rather than settling on one answer, we want to add new ways of seeing, one by one.
We hope it becomes a starting point to explore that question, together.

伝統と建築、そして海。三つの美が、一枚の絨毯に。

深いブルーを基調とするKeramatianの作品には、ペルシャ絨毯の伝統的な草花文様、イスラム建築を彩るタイル、そして海を泳ぐ魚たちが描かれています。古典的な文様と建築の幾何学に、自由に泳ぐ魚の姿を重ねることで、まるで深い海の中にペルシャの庭園やイスラム建築が浮かび上がるような幻想的な世界を創り出しています。異なるモチーフを独自の感性で融合し、伝統を新たな物語へと昇華する。その表現に、Keramatianならではの魅力があります。

一方、LAYA SAGHAEYが描く「DONYA」は、ペルシャ語で「世界」を意味します。

ここでいう世界とは、地図に広がる世界ではなく、ひとりの女性の記憶、精神、夢、そして生きてきた物語。顔という境界を越えて広がる、ひとりの「個」の宇宙です。ペルシャ絨毯に受け継がれてきた文様や色彩を背景に、文化や記憶を自身の感性で再解釈し、現代的な表現へと昇華しています。

受け継がれてきたHeritageと、そこから生まれるART。
KeramatianとLAYA SAGHAEY、異なる世代と感性による二つの表現を通して、ペルシャ絨毯が持つ新たな美の可能性を提示します。

Tradition, architecture, and the sea. Three forms of beauty woven into a single carpet.

Keramatian’s deep blue work brings together traditional Persian floral motifs, the tiles of Islamic architecture, and fish swimming freely through the sea. Classical patterns and architectural geometry merge with the fluid forms of fish, creating a dreamlike world where Persian gardens and Islamic architecture seem to emerge from the depths. Rather than simply recreating tradition, Keramatian transforms diverse motifs through a unique sensibility, creating a new visual narrative.

“DONYA,” by LAYA SAGHAEY, means “world” in Persian. Here, the world is not a geographical place, but the memories, spirit, dreams, and stories of a woman’s life—a personal universe extending beyond the boundaries of the face. 木は、かつて生きていた存在です。
その木が持つ量感や力強さを手がかりに、彫刻と機能のあいだにあるものを制作しています。

本展では、木を彫刻することから生まれたスピーカーと照明を展示します。
スピーカーは、乾燥と安定性を考慮して木を組み上げ、大きな身体として形づくり、照明は木の塊そのものを彫り出します。

音を鳴らす、光を灯すという役割を持ちながら、彫刻のように存在し、日々の暮らしの中で愛着が生まれ、そばに置き続けたくなるものを目指しています。

This exhibition presents sculptural speakers and lighting created through the carving of wood.
The speakers are built from assembled timber for stability and proper drying, then shaped into substantial, bodily forms, while the lighting pieces are carved directly from solid blocks of wood.

While functioning as objects that produce sound and light, each work retains the presence of sculpture. Through their continued place in everyday life, the works explore objects that gradually develop familiarity and affection.

Josh Ogle’s @oglecomponentdesign V3 titanium full-suspension was one of our favorite builds at @made.bike 
 
To bring his innovative, detailed vision to life, Josh teamed up with us at SILCA to 3D-print the frame’s custom titanium lugs at our Indy HQ. It gave him the perfect foundation to incorporate some wild details, like 3VO linkage platform, hand-bending rigid aerospace tubing for the brake lines, and embossing custom graphics into the metal throughout, like Pac-Man, Asteroids, and even torque specs.

This is what happens when two brands obsessed with perfection and cutting-edge manufacturing come together to create something cool.

Head over to the Marginal Gains Media link in our bio to read the full breakdown and drool over the crazy details on this special machine!

El Pebblito...Spanglish for gravel.
.
Much discussion in the Monē household about bringing a gravel bike to @made.bike . While fitting in isn't usually our thing , this prototype Pebblito was too spicy to keep to ourselves.

This is indeed a prototype...a sneak peek at what we're working on over here. The v2 pebby will be accompanied by a new svelte steel fork. We custom machined the steerer to make it one of the lightest steel forks on the market. Our people have spoken and steel is what they want.
.
UDH. T type. Sram transmission...while we're not crazy about all the new new...we ain't hopeless luddites either....and unfortunately it works pretty good...so yes, we t-typin. If it's any consolation, we've also figured out how to make a coaster work in there too.
.
New tension system...that's all we're saying about that.
.
All the same hotness as the last pebby...@columbus_official tubing. Flat mount or post mount. Front derailleur mount and internal dropper mount for full roadie or full rowdy.
.

「Schattenrequisit: Column」は、都市を構成する建築的要素である「柱（Column）」を、人の存在によって変化するものとして捉え直したインスタレーション作品である。
無数の透明な糸によって形づくられた柱は、一見すると均質で無機質な構造体として空間に佇む。しかし、人がその周囲を行き交うなかで、柱はゆっくりと回転し、糸の重なりや密度、輪郭を変化させていく。そこに光が重なることで、その変化は影となって床や壁へ広がり、実体とは異なるもうひとつの像を立ち上げる。
柱や直線といった規則的な建築要素によって形づくられる都市空間。その静的な構造とは対照的に、そこに生きる人々は絶えず移動し、出会い、離れ、それぞれの時間を過ごしている。本作では、本来は動くことのない「柱」が人の存在によって揺らぐことで、都市のなかでは捉えにくい人の動きや気配、時間の流れを、一時的な影の痕跡として浮かび上がらせる。
“Schattenrequisit”は、「影」を意味するドイツ語のSchattenと、「道具・小道具」を意味するRequisitを組み合わせた名称である。ここでColumnは、空間を支える柱ではなく、人、物質、光の関係を受け取り、その変化を影として映し出すための装置となる。
都市という静的な構造と、そのなかを絶えず移ろう人の存在。そのあいだに生まれる揺らぎを、光と影によって描き出す。

Schattenrequisit: Column reimagines the column—an architectural element of the city—as something altered by human presence.

Made from countless transparent threads, the column appears uniform and impersonal. As people move around it, it slowly rotates, shifting the overlap, density, and contours of the threads. Light extends these changes across the floor and walls as shadows, creating another image distinct from the physical form.

By allowing the normally static column to shift, the work reveals movements, traces of presence, and the passage of time that often remain unnoticed in urban space.

“Schattenrequisit” combines the German words Schatten (“shadow”) and Requisit (“prop”). Here, the column becomes a device that receives the relations between people, material, and light, translating them into temporary traces of shadow.

世界のモダンインテリアを牽引するイタリア屈指のインテリアブランド「Poliform(ポリフォーム)」。2026年4月にミラノ市内スカラ座の隣にオープンした、最新の旗艦店と同じラインナップとブランドの世界観を、東京・南青山の「Poliform TOKYO」でご覧いただけます。

注目は、2025年のミラノサローネで発表されたジャン＝マリー・マッソーのデザインによる、日本初入荷の新作「JOAN SOFA（ジョアン）」。不要な装飾を徹底的に削ぎ落としたミニマルデザインながら、滑らかな曲線と静かな存在感を放つフォルムは、ソファとしての純粋な本質を追求した、まさに究極のソファです。

また、アウトドアコレクションからはエマニュエル・ガッリーナ設計の「LAGOON」が登場。チーク材とテキスタイルの調和により、自然とシームレスに繋がる上質な空間を提案します。

常に進化を止めないPoliform。
今回も、単なる新作の発表にとどまらず、「Poliform TOKYO」のストア空間全体のストーリーを再構築しました。ブランドが追求し続けるタイムレスなエレガンスがどのように進化を遂げたのか、最新のマテリアル、計算し尽くされたプロポーション、そしてそれらを調和させる卓越した空間構成力を、皆様に五感で感じていただける貴重な機会です。

Poliform stands at the pinnacle of modern Italian interior design, shaping luxury living environments worldwide. Experience the exact lineup and brand vision showcased at our newest flagship store—opened in April 2026 next to La Scala in Milan—now on display at Poliform TOKYO in Minami-Aoyama.
A key highlight is the Japanese premiere of the JOAN SOFA, designed by Jean-Marie Massaud following its debut at the 2025 Salone del Mobile. Stripped of all excess ornament, its minimalist silhouette pairs fluid curves with a quiet, grounding presence—the ultimate expression of a sofa’s pure essence.

From the outdoor collection, Emmanuel Gallina’s LAGOON seamlessly connects indoor luxury with outdoor living. Warm teakwood and refined textiles create a serene sanctuary in harmony with nature. 

Poliform is in perpetual motion. More than a showcase of new designs, this exhibition completely reimagines the spatial narrative of the Poliform TOKYO showroom. We invite you to engage all five senses and witness how timeless elegance evolves through cutting-edge materials, sculpted proportions, and masterfully orchestrated architecture.
