Viaje en moto off road por Vietnam 2027 🇻🇳🏍️
¿Buscas un viaje organizado en moto por el norte de Vietnam?

 Del 6 al 16 de marzo de 2027 rodamos 11 días por pistas y caminos de montaña con Honda CRF 250/300, más campo que asfalto.

Así es un día cualquiera: a las 8:00 en marcha, curvas entre arrozales en cascada, un mercado colgado de la montaña a media mañana y, por la tarde, las gargantas de Ha Giang o el puerto de Ma Pi Leng.

 Caminos que no salen en ningún mapa y una cara al llegar que lo dice todo.

Qué incluye:
✅ Moto Honda CRF 250/300 y gasolina
✅ Mecánico y coche de asistencia
✅ Guía en español y guía local

Años después, regresamos a uno de los barrios más vinculados a la historia del festival. Pero volver no significa hacer lo mismo en el mismo lugar.

Festival Asalto 2026 se desplegará por San Pablo y Zamoray-Pignatelli a través de proyectos muy diferentes en escala, lenguaje y forma de relacionarse con el espacio.

El festival no pretende explicar el barrio ni construir un relato único sobre él. Propone acercarse a su diversidad desde múltiples miradas y generar situaciones en las que artistas, comunidades y espacios puedan encontrarse.

Habrá artistas que trabajarán a partir de objetos compartidos por sus habitantes; otros recuperarán palabras, recuerdos y observaciones surgidas durante múltiples conversaciones. Algunas propuestas imaginarán de nuevo ventanas hoy cerradas; otras entrarán en los portales de comunidades de vecinos o transformarán el Centro de Salud a partir de las experiencias de quienes lo utilizan cada día.

También construiremos un invernadero para preguntarnos colectivamente qué puede suceder en un espacio compartido. Habrá talleres y actividades que fomenten el encuentro, junto a intervenciones artísticas que modificarán, a diferentes escalas, el paisaje urbano.

Y hay algo de todo esto también en la propia imagen de esta edición. Las fotografías que construyen el cartel de Festival Asalto 2026 han sido realizadas por @eabad, fotógrafa y vecina del barrio, en casas de vecinos y vecinas de San Pablo.

Porque si este año Asalto vuelve a mirar el barrio desde cerca, tenía sentido que su imagen también surgiera desde dentro. 

Del 17 al 27 de septiembre . Nos vemos en las calles.

Berbekal gerinda dan bor tangan di bengkel, Ajies Sabara bersama tim F.Art 32 dari Bangkalan, Madura, membawa pulang enam penghargaan pada keikutsertaan pertama mereka di Kustomfest. Lewat motor “Pelor Angen”, mereka meraih Best Kustom Bike Show sekaligus trofi bergilir Piala Raja Kustomfest.

Motor berbasis Honda CB150R tahun 2013 itu sempat mangkrak akibat pandemi dan keterbatasan biaya. Dukungan Warung Nasi Bebek Sinjay kemudian membantu tim melanjutkan pengerjaan selama dua bulan penuh.

Nama Pelor Angen diambil dari nama sapi kerapan di Madura. Sementara perpaduan material metal dan kayunya terinspirasi dari senapan angin. Desainnya dirancang sendiri oleh Ajies, berangkat dari kegemarannya melukis.

“Jadi alat bukan menjadi penghalang bagi kami. Nomor satu adalah kemauan. Itu saja,” ujar Ajies.

Cerita penantian panjang juga datang dari Surya bersama tim 02 Garage asal Semarang. Chevrolet C10 tahun 1968 bekas kendaraan PLN yang proses pengerjaannya ia tunggu hingga sepuluh tahun akhirnya meraih Best Pick Up, Best Kustom Car Show, dan Piala Raja kategori mobil.

Kedua karya itu mendapat apresiasi tertinggi dalam Kustomfest ke-15 di Jogja Expo Center, Yogyakarta, pada 10–11 Oktober 2026. Direktur Kustomfest, Lulut Wahyudi, menyebut kompetisi ini tidak sekadar soal menang atau kalah, tetapi juga kesempatan agar karya para builder diapresiasi oleh orang-orang yang mencintai dunia kustom.

caption:
We are proud to welcome Weapon Records back to Earth Frequency Festival 2026, taking over The Vertex for an epic Sunday session for the ages 💥

Founded by pioneering Australian producer, vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Tetrameth as a platform for razor-sharp production and uncompromising dancefloor tunes, the beloved homegrown imprint continues to push the boundaries of high-grade psychedelic music both in Australia and abroad.

Earth Frequency’s connection with Weapon runs long and deep. Weapon artists have been an integral part of EFF’s musical fabric since the festival’s earliest days and have helped define the sound of Sunday on the Vertex. 

Their showcase features a stacked roster of both festival favourites and fresh talent performing at Earth Frequency for the first time. Built on a foundation of original psychedelic progressive trance and thick bush prog, this showcase is best served at serious volume in an outdoor location. Please use only as directed 🤘

Asturcones 2026 ya es historia. Y qué historia. 🐎
Tres días saliendo con el sol y llegando con él a punto de esconderse. Pistas, barro, collados y esa Asturias que solo se ve desde una trail con los neumáticos sucios.

Pero si algo nos llevamos de esta edición es la gente. Un grupo que se conoció el viernes y el domingo se despedía como si llevaran años rodando juntos. Esperas en las subidas, risas en la cena y alguna moto que pidió más cariño del previsto. Así se hace una familia sobre dos ruedas.

Gracias a todos los que lo hicisteis posible. Sois la razón por la que repetimos.

Y sí, repetimos 👇

Kustome Fest 2026 ini mengusung tema High Octane, di era ekonomi yang sedang lesuh ini. Kustom Fest hadir sebagai pemantik perputaran roda dunia kustom untuk tetap bisa bersaing di dalam negeri dan luar negeri.

#HumanOnWheels

Di bagian roda dua baik yang menggunakan mesin ataupun tenaga manusia, mereka memberikan beragam bentuk dan warna yang membuat setiap karya memiliki karakter dari pemilik kendaraan tersebut.

#HumanOnWheels

Pada bagian roda empat, banyak yang menampilkan mobil-mobil tua yang telah di restorasi mendekati ke original ketika di produksi. 

Beberapa mobil bahkan mendapatkan perhatian khusus dari tamu internasional karena keadaannya yang nyaris dengan kata sempurna.

#HumanOnWheels

Kustom fest 2026 ini juga memberikan manfaat kepada yang membutuhkan.

Penggalangan dana yang lebih hampir Rp1 Milliar ini di konversi menjadi bantuan pendidikan kepada adik-adik kita yang kesulitan membayar pendidikannya dan bantuan bedah rumah kepada rakyat yang rumahnya sudah tidak layak ditinggali.

#HumanOnWheels

Banyak hal yang di custom dalam acara ini, seperti diecast, helm, dan sarung tangan.

Bahkan acara ini menampilkan helm yang berukuran sangat BESAR.

#HumanOnWheels

Di outdoor stage kalian bisa menikmati balapan Flat Track dan konser yang dihadiri Seringai, Kelompok Penerbang Roket, Morfem, dan banyak lainnya.

All accommodation and extras go live and on sale when the full music line up drops this Wednesday. Get your crew ready as options are limited and won’t last long.

In 2026 we will also be offering 1 & 2 room pre pitched tents for those looking for a slightly more affordable and standard offering. These also include the basic extras needed to enjoy the weekend without having the hassles of setting up and packing up your tent and campsite.

All of the above options are perfect for those who may not have the resources to set up a tent and campsite, those wanting a hassle free weekend and those looking to catch the shuttle bus service in and out of the festival (which we highly recommend) This option may also be appealing to those looking to carpool with minimal space for tents and other equipment.

Expect a 14-hour journey through the full spectrum of underground bass music. While the signature low-slung drum and bass, halftime and 140 styles that built the label’s reputation remain at the core, expect a deeper exploration of downtempo bass, hybrid trap, breaks, and left-of-centre sounds. 

This is the broadest, most ambitious 8Ball Audio takeover to date and the perfect way to kick off a massive weekend of music 🔊🔊🔊

To mark NAIDOC Week, we’re celebrating extraordinary First Nations artists set to take the stage at Earth Frequency Festival. Today we shine a light on one of our headliners, Lisa May, a Dunghutti woman who grew up on Worimi Country 🖤💛❤️

With a career spanning two decades, Lisa May is one of the country’s leading techno artists. She is known for her dark, heavy, and uncompromising sound, and  powerful, flawless performances shaped by technical precision and deep musical understanding.

In 2023, Lisa joined the residents at Eat The Beat, performing major support slots for some of the world’s biggest names in techno and appearing at internationally recognised events including Amsterdam Dance Event, Carl Cox’s PURE showcase, Sydney Mardi Gras’ main party, Revolver Upstairs and Hardware’s Piknic Électronique.

On the production front, she has released three EPs on Volta Records, alongside tracks on Codex Recordings, FE Chrome, Reload Records and Kaligo Records.

Her music is supported by heavyweight DJs across the globe, solidifying her place at the forefront of Australian electronic music. We can’t wait to welcome her to Earth Frequency for the first time in 2026! 🌿✨

Earth Frequency Festival 2026 takes place at Woodfordia, on the  traditional lands of the Jinibara people. We are honoured the festival takes place on their beautiful Country, and express our deep respect for their traditions, ancestors, and elders, past, present and emerging. 

Jinibara people are the freshwater, rainforest and mountain people from the Jinibara nation. ‘Jini’ or ‘Yini’ is the lawyer cane, a vital resource, and ‘bara’ is we, the people. 

Jinibara is made up of four clans: Dungidau of the Kilcoy, Villeneuve, Woodford and Mt Archer areas, Dala along the Blackall Ranges, headwaters and tributaries of the Mary River, Nalbo from Blackall and much of the Glasshouse Mountains, and Garumngar from the rolling country of Brisbane River to Lake Manchester and Mt Crosby.

Earth Frequency recognises the Sovereign First Nations Community, whose history should be remembered and heard, and whose voices must be respected, elevated and considered in all respects when we walk on Country, care for Country and one another. We acknowledge that sovereignty was never ceded 🙌

caption:
Our relationship with the land is just as important as the connection within our community. Let’s nurture a culture of shared responsibility 🤝

Driving to the site is the single largest contributor to our carbon footprint. Carpool with mates, travel on the EFF Express bus or look for a ride online 🚌

Think smart before you pack. Cut back on useless packaging, use reusable containers, and swap out single-use items for recyclable tins or boxes ♻️

Broken bottles cause terrible injuries to people and wildlife. Keep our home safe by packing your favourite drinks in cans or reusable containers instead🥫

Keep our beautiful venue pristine and fire-safe. If you smoke, always keep a personal ashtray on you or head straight to the nearest bin 🚮

Cut down on the mountain of paper cups and plastic bottles bound for landfill. Bring your own cup for coffees and cocktails 🥤

Avoid cheap, disposable items that break after a single weekend. Invest in durable tents and gazebos that you will actually value and take home 🏕️

We actively invite your feedback, eco-ideas, and participation. Post your festival sustainability tips in the comments and help create a greener future 🌏

Born from the friendship of 2 childhood best friends of Iraqi and Maltese lineage, the pair explore the rave unconscious - blending mutated house, bush doof, dub techno and downtempo, bound to make you move.

STAGE 1: ‘RENAISSANCE’

Don't get us wrong, we're hype for the Dome but we do miss the Mansion. So, we're bringing the Mansion to Coburg 💥 

Inspired by the Renaissance Revival architecture of the Werribee Mansion, our first Cake stage explores the relationship between light, space, and reflection through a swaggy modular structure clad entirely in mirror. The frames will make sure your favs are directly in focus, while the surrounding environment and crowd will be echoed. Lit. 

We're happy to have a piece of Werribee with us this year despite the location switch. Yeow.

We are incredibly proud to announce that the Earth Frequency Festival Guild has donated $20,000 towards securing Woodfordia’s future as part of A Forest Of Goodwill 🌳
 
A Forest Of Goodwill is the Woodfordia Foundation’s fundraising campaign to buy back the amazing 500-acre block of land that hosts Earth Frequency and other vital Queensland festivals and cultural events, including Woodford Folk Festival. Securing Woodfordia protects artistic independence, safeguards environmental stewardship, and ensures it remains in community hands rather than private ownership.

Thanks to donations from the Earth Frequency community and the festival itself, our Guild has raised $10,000 for the cause, which was matched dollar-for-dollar by a group of generous Woodfordians, bringing the total up to $20,000. Our hats go off to everyone from the EFF community who has contributed so far and shown this worthy and important cause some love.
 
But we’re not done yet! There is still a way to go until A Forest Of Goodwill reaches its target and we hope that our wonderful community continues to donate to our Guild as we approach EFF2026 in October this year. Donations over $2 are fully tax-deductible and can be made via Humantix while purchasing tickets or standalone 🙏💚

Ada yang datang mencari referensi untuk membangun motor, ada pula yang jauh-jauh dari luar kota untuk bertemu kawan sesama pencinta dunia kustom.

Kustomfest ke-15 dibuka di Jogja Expo Center (JEC) pada 10 Oktober 2026. Mengusung tema High Octane, gelaran ini menghadirkan 150 motor dan 25 mobil kustom karya builder dari berbagai daerah. Pada hari pertama, pengunjung diperkirakan mencapai ribuan orang, memadati area indoor dan outdoor JEC.

Ale, pengunjung dari Tangerang, sudah tiga tahun berturut-turut datang untuk mencari inspirasi bagi motornya. Sementara Fira, asal Jakarta yang sedang kuliah di Solo, baru pertama kali hadir. Ketertarikannya pada bentuk kendaraan membawanya mengenal dunia kustom lebih dekat.

Penasihat Kustomfest, KPH Purbodiningrat, menyebut festival ini menjadi ruang bagi karya anak bangsa untuk menemukan karakter, identitas, dan panggungnya. Wali Kota Yogyakarta, Hasto Wardoyo,  juga mengajak anak muda menguasai teknik, memanfaatkan teknologi, membangun jejaring, dan berani memulai dari bengkel kecil.

Tiga tahun berturut-turut meraih Piala Raja Kustomfest, Yayak tetap menempatkan pelanggan sebagai kemenangan utamanya. Dari kepercayaan merekalah, dapur Queen Lekha Choppers di Karangkajen, Kota Yogyakarta, bisa terus mengepul.

Bengkel yang dirintis sejak 2010 itu kini dikerjakan empat orang, termasuk Yayak. Menurutnya, pelanggan datang dari berbagai daerah, mulai Jakarta, Medan, Bali, hingga Kalimantan. Ada pula yang berasal dari Thailand dan Malaysia. Karya-karyanya juga pernah dibawa ke Jepang dan meraih penghargaan selama tiga tahun berurutan pada 2017–2019.

Untuk Kustomfest 2026, timnya menyiapkan dua motor. Salah satunya berawal dari celetukan anak-anak bengkel yang melihat satu mesin menganggur. Mereka kemudian membangun sebuah chopper dari nol dalam 32 hari, jauh lebih singkat dari waktu pengerjaan yang biasanya memakan tiga hingga empat bulan.

Bagi Yayak, tumbuhnya dunia custom juga membuka pekerjaan bagi banyak orang. Ada tukang las yang menerima pesanan, hingga usaha pakaian dan sablon yang mengerjakan merchandise bengkel.

Itulah mengapa ia berharap semakin banyak pembuat motor baru tumbuh di Jogja. Semakin banyak yang berkarya, semakin besar pula kesempatan bagi orang-orang di sekitarnya untuk ikut mendapat penghidupan.

🎧💥 Artist Feature: @paul_abad 

Paul Abad has been a key figure in Australia’s vibrant techno, electronic music and festival culture for more than 25 years.  In that time, he has built his festival brand Earth Frequency to become one of the country’s premiere music, arts and lifestyle festivals, performed at countless festivals, clubs, parties and warehouses alongside some of the world’s most influential artists. and most importantly, developed a vibrant and connected community around everything he is involved with. 

After initially dabbling with a four-deck setup, Paul quickly embraced technology with a DJ/live hybrid approach via Ableton Live as early as 2004, allowing for more sophisticated and layered storytelling. The end result means Paul can effortlessly traverse through the different tones and moods of techno with both sonic consistency and ultimate flexibility, ensuring he has earned his place as one of Australian techno’s most experienced and dynamic DJs and live performers.

Kustomfest ke-15 berakhir dengan 225 karya, termasuk motor dan mobil kustom, sekitar 26.787 pengunjung, serta donasi Rp1.029.400.000 untuk bantuan pendidikan dan bedah rumah di Kota Yogyakarta.

Digelar pada 10–11 Oktober 2026 di Jogja Expo Center (JEC), Yogyakarta, festival bertema High Octane ini mempertemukan builder dari berbagai daerah, komunitas, dan pengunjung yang datang untuk menikmati karya sekaligus mencari inspirasi.

Rangkaian acaranya mencakup Kustom Bike Show, Hot Rod & Kustom Car Show, Motocumentary, hingga penghargaan bagi para pemenang kompetisi. Panggung musik turut diramaikan Seringai, Soloensis, Morfem, dan Rebellion Rose, dan penampilan kelompok musik lainnya.

Semangat berbagi juga hadir melalui riding bersama Ride For YK dan penyerahan donasi. Dana yang terkumpul menjadi dukungan bagi pendidikan dan perbaikan tempat tinggal warga Kota Yogyakarta.

Gelaran ini juga menghadirkan undian lucky draw berhadiah perjalanan ke Yokohama Hot Rod Custom Show 2026 di Jepang.

Dua hari pertemuan selesai, karya dan cerita dari JEC dibawa pulang. Buat kamu yang datang, momen apa yang paling membekas di Kustomfest tahun ini?

caption:
Di tengah kelesuan ekonomi dan persaingan dengan komponen otomotif produksi massal, KUSTOMFEST 2026 hadir dengan tema “High Octane”. Memasuki penyelenggaraan ke-15, festival budaya otomotif kustom ini akan digelar pada Sabtu–Minggu, 10–11 Oktober 2026, di Jogja Expo Center (JEC), Banguntapan, Bantul, DIY.

Tahun ini, KUSTOMFEST juga menjadi bagian dari rangkaian HUT ke-270 Kota Yogyakarta melalui kolaborasi dengan Pemerintah Kota Yogyakarta. 

Direktur KUSTOMFEST, Lulut Wahyudi, menyebut keterlibatan tersebut menjadi momentum baru setelah 15 tahun membangun ekosistem custom culture di Yogyakarta, sekaligus membuka ruang kerja sama yang lebih luas antara pelaku industri kreatif otomotif, pemerintah, dan masyarakat.

Lulut mengatakan tema “High Octane” menggambarkan kebutuhan akan energi baru untuk mendorong industri kustom Indonesia terus bergerak dan berkembang di tengah berbagai tantangan.

“Yang dibutuhkan adalah bahan bakar yang berkualitas, yang oktannya tinggi. Harapan kami dari Kustom Fest dengan menginject oktan yang tinggi itu bisa mampu membakar dan menggerakkan mesin dunia custom Indonesia ini,” ujar Lulut.

Melalui gelaran tahun ini, KUSTOMFEST ingin mempertemukan para pelaku industri otomotif kustom, UMKM, seniman, hingga generasi baru builder Indonesia. Ajang ini juga diharapkan menjadi ruang kolaborasi, pertukaran ide, dan pengembangan jejaring bagi pelaku industri kustom nasional.

Keranda jenazah jadi motor kustom? Wendy Purnama Putra mewujudkannya lewat “Mayit”, karya dari WBike Kustom Garage di Kotagede, Yogyakarta, yang membawa pengingat tentang akhir perjalanan manusia.

“Secepat apa pun kamu mengejar dunia, garis finish-nya tetap kematian,” kata Wendy.

Di balik karya-karyanya yang nyeleneh, Wendy juga pernah merasa jenuh dan buntu, bahkan ingin menyerah. Dukungan istrinya menjadi salah satu penyemangat untuk terus bekerja. Saat ide mentok, ia memilih berbagi cerita dengan teman-teman. Dari obrolan itu, bantuan dan jalan keluar kerap datang.

Bengkelnya pun menjadi tempat tumbuh bagi orang-orang yang bekerja bersamanya. Menurut Wendy, sejumlah pekerja yang dulu ikut dengannya kemudian membuka bengkel sendiri. Ia berusaha menjaga hubungan dengan prinsip “nguwongke uwong”, menghargai orang sebagai sesama manusia.

Dari bengkel di Kotagede itu, komponen buatannya juga sudah menjangkau Malaysia dan Singapura. Sementara untuk “Mayit”, ia memanfaatkan kembali komponen yang tersedia dan berkolaborasi dengan teman-temannya untuk mewujudkan gagasan tersebut.
Penasaran melihat “Mayit” dari dekat? Motor ini dibawa ke Kustomfest pada 10–11 Oktober 2026 di Jogja Expo Center.

KUSTOMFEST 2026 High Octane, dari Helm Raksasa, Dapur SPPC hingga Motor Mayit

Kustomfest 2026 bertajuk High Octane menghadirkan beragam kreativitas unik di Jogja Expo Center (JEC), Yogyakarta, Sabtu-Minggu (10–11/10/2026). Tak sekadar memamerkan motor dan mobil kustom, gelaran tahun ke-15 ini juga menyuguhkan karya-karya nyentrik dengan gagasan menarik.

Di antara karya yang mencuri perhatian, terdapat helm raksasa dari Trooper Helmet, dapur Satuan Pelayanan Pembangunan Chopper karya Queen Lekha yang mengingatkan pada SPPG, hingga motor Mayit karya Wendy Purnama. Ketiganya menunjukkan kreativitas pelaku kustom dalam mengolah ide menjadi karya yang unik.

Motor Mayit, misalnya, mengingatkan pengunjung pada garis akhir kehidupan duniawi, yakni kematian. Karya tersebut menjadi bukti bahwa dunia kustom tak hanya berbicara soal modifikasi kendaraan, tetapi juga dapat menyampaikan pesan dan refleksi kehidupan.

Direktur Kustomfest Lulut Wahyudi mengusung tema High Octane di tengah tantangan industri kustom, mulai dari kondisi ekonomi hingga persaingan suku cadang impor. Kustomfest diharapkan tetap menjadi ruang bagi kreator untuk menunjukkan inovasi dan karakter karya Indonesia.

Selain pameran motor dan mobil kustom, Kustomfest 2026 juga menghadirkan Flat Track Race, Art Island, Body Art, Paint Battle, serta partisipasi pelaku dan juri internasional. Berbagai agenda tersebut memperkuat Kustomfest sebagai ajang pertemuan komunitas sekaligus perayaan budaya kustom. #kedaulatanrakyat #krjogja #kustomfest #highoctane

CALLING ALL AUSTRALIAN MAKERS AND DESIGNERS | Complete the survey today before it closes on 2 October.⁠
.⁠
Australian craft & design practitioners: your experience matters.⁠
.⁠
We’re building a national picture of craft and design practice in Australia — and we need your voice.⁠
.⁠
This survey is an ADC Legacy Project, funded by Australian Design Centre in collaboration with the Australian Craft and Design Centres (ACDC Network), NAVA and Craft Australia.⁠
.⁠
The data collected will help sector organisations advocate for practitioners and make a stronger case for funding, opportunities, education, business support and policy change.⁠
.⁠
As ADC closes its doors after six decades of supporting Australian craft and design, this research is one part of the legacy we’re leaving behind: useful evidence that can help the sector advocate for its future.⁠
.⁠
The survey takes 9–12 minutes and is completely anonymous.⁠
.⁠
If you’re an Australian craft or design practitioner, take the survey and help make sure your experiences are part of the picture.⁠
.⁠
Complete the survey via the link in bio before 2 October 2026.

Naik kendaraan roda tiga buatan Jogja ini, rasanya disebut seperti “terbang rendah”. Namanya Retro Three Wheeler, karya Lulut Wahyudi dari Retro Classic Cycles. Pandangan Jogja ikut menjajalnya bersama Lulut, merasakan duduk berdampingan layaknya naik mobil, tetapi dengan ruang terbuka dan suara knalpot seperti naik motor Harley Davidson.

Idenya muncul saat Kustomfest Ride and Drive 2021. Lulut ingin memadukan pengalaman berkendara motor dan mobil, dengan desain terinspirasi kendaraan tiga roda yang populer di Inggris pada era 1930-an. Kabinnya yang terbuka juga mengingatkannya pada sensasi naik pesawat klasik.

Proses pembuatannya penuh perbaikan. Dalam pengujian awal sekitar 6.000 kilometer, mesin dan gearbox-nya sempat rusak hingga harus diangkut towing. Lulut kemudian menghabiskan sekitar satu tahun untuk mengembangkan kendaraan ini, termasuk menyempurnakan sasis berdasarkan pengalaman berkendara.

Dibangun secara handmade dari nol, setiap pesanan bisa membutuhkan waktu 9–10 bulan. Retro Three Wheeler menggunakan mesin Knuckle Head 1.500 cc dari S&S Cycle, transmisi empat percepatan, dan penggerak roda depan. Hasil pengembangannya sudah dibawa Lulut berkendara hingga Bali dan Lombok. “Ini karya Jogja ya, karya anak Jogja, jadi made in Yogyakarta,” ujar Lulut.

Pengin lihat langsung Retro Three Wheeler karya bengkel Jogja ini? Datang ke Kustomfest 2026 “High-Octane” pada 10–11 Oktober 2026 di Jogja Expo Center (JEC), Banguntapan, Bantul.

ABOUT THE MAKER⁠
.⁠
Sarit Cohen is an Australian ceramic artist whose practice explores porcelain, memory and cultural inheritance through sculptural vessels and objects. A graduate of the Australian National University School of Art and Design (Ceramics), Sarit completed a Diploma of Education at the University of Canberra, during which she was awarded the Doug Alexander Memorial Award for Decorative Surface.⁠
.⁠
Sarit’s practice has been significantly shaped by international residencies in Denmark, Switzerland and China, where she developed her exploration of porcelain manipulation and casting. Over the past two decades, she has exhibited widely in Australia and internationally, including exhibitions in the USA, Denmark, Hungary and Japan, with her work held in public and private collections across these regions.⁠
.⁠
‘The play with the form of the object is always a pleasure, and this play creates the building blocks of ideas to be represented. The exploration into the making of ceramics has absorbed me for 30 years. I am constantly refining my ideas to complete works that satiate my curiosity. It is still a wonderful experience witnessing the vessels taking shape.’⁠
.⁠
Sarit also has an exhibition at Craft + Design Canberra in the Gallery, Vessels of Dialogue until Saturday 12 September 2026.⁠
.⁠

EXHIBITION NOW UNTIL 12 SEPTEMBER | Fragile Structures: The Architecture of Decay by Fran Romano @franromanoceramics and Madeline Cardone⁠ @madeline.cardone⁠
.⁠
See the works in person and visit the Craft + Design Canberra Gallery, open noon to 4pm Wednesday to Saturday. Our Shop + Gallery are located upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra ACT 2601.⁠
.⁠
LEARN MORE | About the Exhibition⁠
.⁠
This exhibition is a collaboration between visual artists Madeline Cardone and Fran Romano. Working in glass and ceramics respectively, the artists share an overlapping conceptual and material language. Both are fascinated by the built environment, exploring ruins, decay, voids and architectural phenomenology through the deconstruction and reconstruction of space. They share a common cultural heritage that informs their practices and strengthens this collaboration. ⁠
.⁠
Both artists have recently been exploring abstraction of form and space in a sculptural context. Ceramics and glass have common material properties, and both artists work in processes that seek to highlight and challenge the dualities inherent in these materials, notions of strength, fragility, permanence and transience. They explore the qualities of each material that are unexpected, highlighting the process of discovery in the outcome of the works. ⁠
.⁠
For more information visit our website | https://craftanddesigncanberra.org/blogs/current-exhibitions/fragile-structures-the-architecture-of-decay⁠
.⁠

NAPIRELLY

2024年のLabyrinthに参加した方は、NapirellyがDelta FunktionenとのユニットImmediate ProximityとしてB2Bセットを披露していた姿を目にしたかもしれない。そして2025年のLabyrinthに来ていたなら、駐車場でボランティアとしてキャンプギアをシャトルバスへ積み込む手伝いをしていた彼女を見かけたかもしれない。前年に体験したLabyrinthに心を動かされ、「どんな形でもこのフェスに貢献したい」という思いで去年再び日本へ飛んできたNapirelly。DJであると同時にフィットネスインストラクターでもある彼女には、その体力を存分に発揮してもらった(笑)。

そんなNapirellyの姿勢は、多くの面で私たちの心を打った。今年の出演オファーを最初に送ったアーティストが彼女だった。
旧ソ連・レニングラード生まれ、世界で唯一、北極圏上に築かれた都市サレハルドで育ったNapirelly。そのワイルドで大胆、そして自由な精神は、そのまま彼女の音楽表現にも表れている。オランダのDeepgrooves Vinylレコードプレス工場で3年間働いた後、現在は再びサンクトペテルブルクを拠点に活動中。文字どおり、まったく異なる世界からやってきた存在だ。

現在は、サンクトペテルブルクのレーベル／イベントコレクティブRoots UnitedのレジデントDJを務める。プレイではテクノ、ブレイクス、エレクトロ、ベースミュージックを自在に行き来し、時代やBPMを軽やかに横断する。DJ、プロデューサー、トレーナー、そして世界を飛び回る旅人としてのエネルギッシュな日々は、そのプレイスタイルにも色濃く映し出されている。

今年はボランティアではなく、ステージの上へ。彼女の帰還を心から歓迎したい。

---

If you came to Labyrinth two years ago, you would have seen Napirelly play a tag-team dj set with Delta Funktionen as Immediate Proximity, their joint project. And if you came to Labyrinth last year, you might have seen her in the parking lot where she worked as a volunteer helping load camping bags onto the shuttle bus. Inspired by what she witnessed the previous year, she flew back, wanting to contribute to the event in any way she could. She's not only a dj but a fitness instructor, so we put her strength to work.

The spirit of Napirelly moved us in many ways, and she was the first artist we reached out to play this year.

Born in Leningrad, USSR, and raised in Salekhard—the only city in the world built directly on the Arctic Circle—Napirelly brings a wild, bold and free spirit to her art. After spending three years working at Deepgrooves Vinyl Pressing Plant in the Netherlands, she is now based once again in Saint Petersburg. She literally comes from a very different place.

She is currently a resident dj of Roots United, a record label and events team in St Petersburg. As a dj, Napirelly bounces back and forth between techno, breaks, electro, and bass music, juggling a wide range of BPM's and eras of music. Her high energy life as dj, producer, trainer, and global traveler is reflected in how she plays. We greatly welcome her return--this time to the stage.

caption:
Earth Frequency Festival is in Full Bloom 🌺

Over twenty years ago, we planted a seed. Small, intentional, but full of possibility.

We tended it patiently, season after season. Watered by community, nourished by music, art and shared values.

Roots pushed deep into the earth, finding strength in connection, resilience in care, and wisdom in time.

There were cycles of sun and years of hard weather. Moments of wild growth and times of careful tending.
Still, the roots held. Still, the garden grew.

From those foundations came shoots of creativity, leaves of expression, and branches reaching toward something larger than any one of us.

A living ecosystem shaped by thousands of hands, hearts and intentions.An  ever-evolving landscape of sound, light, movement and imagination.

Now, after more than two decades of cultivation, Earth Frequency has blossomed. 

This is the moment when everything flowers at once. When vibrant colour spills across the horizon. When past, present and future converge in a single, radiant unfolding.

Full Bloom is abundance without excess. Growth without forgetting our roots. A celebration of how far we have come, and the depth and richness of what we have cultivated. 

It is the beauty of maturity. The confidence of a garden that knows itself. A reminder that when we nurture what matters, growth is not rushed, it is earned.

In 2026, we gather not to chase something new, but to witness what has unfolded together.

To dance on sacred land. To reap the bountiful harvest of more than two decades of intention. 

To stand in gratitude, wonder and celebration, right here, in Full Bloom 🌺🌿🌞🌿🌸

LEARN MORE | About the Exhibitions
.⁠
Correspondence continues Jude Muduioa’s @judemuduioa interest in accumulation as both a making process and a way of thinking. Each element is formed by hand before becoming part of a larger whole, where no single component dominates. ⁠
.⁠
Dwell by Suzanne Knight @suzanneknight33 presents a body of tapestry weavings that explores the intertwined histories of migration, settlement and ecological change. ⁠
.⁠
Vessels of Dialogue by Sarit Cohen @saritcohenceramics is an exhibition of ceramics exploring architectural moments shaped by the artist’s memories.⁠
.⁠
Fragile Structures: The Architecture of Decay is a collaboration between visual artists Madeline Cardone @madeline.cardone and Fran Romano @franromanoceramics . Working in glass and ceramics respectively, the artists share an overlapping conceptual and material language. ⁠
.⁠
Thank you to our government organisational support from @artsact_ and @creative.australia. Thank you to our multi year partners @home.byhollyofficial, @artgroupdevelopment, @actparks, @institute_architectsact, @lawyerbank.com.au, @abyadina, @ale_mary_brewing_, Tailored Accountants and @lecheeserie⁠

MEET THE MEMBER | Fran Romano⁠ @franromanoceramics | Maker Member of Craft + Design Canberra
.⁠
A graduate of ANU School of Art Canberra (2013), Fran is inspired by memory, history and nostalgia, and the passage of Time. She investigates these themes through layering, experimentation with found materials and texture.⁠
.⁠
In recent years, Fran has begun to explore death rites and rituals from both an archeological/historical perspective and a human one. Aiming to create a quiet, contemplative space for the viewer.⁠
.⁠
An interest in the creative process has also found it’s way into her teaching practise and a series of ephemeral ReflectiveClay workshops she offers in the community. Uniquely combining her Social Work/Community Work background with her Art practise.⁠
.⁠
In 2018 she was awarded an Emerging Contemporaries prize from Craft + Design Canberra. 
.⁠
She has been a finalist in the Little Things Art Prize (2018), the Goulburn Art Award (2022), and the North Queensland Ceramic Art Award (2024).⁠
.⁠
She has undertaken special commissions for both giftshops at the National Gallery of Australia and the National Museum of Australia, to coincide with major exhibitions at those institutions.⁠
.⁠
Fran is also part of our current exhibition, Fragile Structures: The Architecture of Decay with @madeline.cardone on at the Craft + Design Canberra Gallery until 12 September.⁠
.⁠

Byron Writers Festival pays tribute to Lynda Dean OAM, festival co-founder and lifelong board member.⁠
⁠
It was a surreal and heartbreaking moment last weekend when, as our team gathered outside the packed Bay Street Stage for the festival finale, we received news that our beloved Lynda had passed.⁠
⁠
Lynda was a larger-than-life figure with an endless capacity for joy and living, a formidable tenacity and powerful intellect. She was someone who built things and, as a philanthropist, worked tirelessly for her community. She knew many of our team and board members for all their lives. ⁠
⁠
As part of the festival’s 30th anniversary a session was presented in honour of Lynda whose health had prevented her from joining us in person if not in spirit. This year that session was the Good Witch, moderated by festival Chair Courtney Miller, covering Lucianne Tonti’s book of the same name.⁠
⁠
With her passing, the festival will continue to honour Lynda with a named session each year in recognition of her legacy – and as a figure who embodied the spirit of the festival.⁠
⁠
Lynda, who co-founded Byron Writers Festival alongside Chris Hanley once said the festival "came out of a need for cultural events in the region. There was a hunger to have cultural events happening here."⁠
⁠
Speaking to The Echo earlier this year, Lynda traced its roots to the Aquarius Festival.⁠
⁠
"[Aquarius] brought so many people here with different ways of thinking. The main underlying thrust of that thinking is, if I want something to happen, if I want my world to have culture in it, it’s up to me to get off my backside and make it happen."⁠
⁠
We remember Lynda for making so many good things happen, and for sharing her vision, generosity, wise guidance – and especially, for her love of life.⁠
⁠
Our team received the news of Lynda’s passing as the Big Voice Choir closed out the festival weekend with a performance by Goanna’s Shane Howard and Bundjalung singer Benja Roberts. ⁠
⁠
As the news broke, a rainbow appeared in the sky. It seemed fitting. Lynda would have wanted us dancing.⁠
⁠
We will miss you, Lynda.

EXHIBITION NOW UNTIL 12 SEPTEMBER | Dwell by Suzanne Knight⁠ @suzanneknight33 ⁠
.⁠
See the works in person and visit the Craft + Design Canberra Gallery, open noon to 4pm Wednesday to Saturday. Our Shop + Gallery are located upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra ACT 2601.⁠
.⁠
LEARN MORE | ⁠
.⁠
Dwell presents a body of tapestry weavings by Suzanne Knight that explores the intertwined histories of migration, settlement and ecological change. Shaped as discarded plastic bottles, these woven forms examine the ways introduced plants, materials and settler traditions have become embedded within Australian landscapes, while reflecting on the layered relationships between domestic life, consumer culture and environmental transformation.⁠
.⁠
These works are woven from raw-spun and repurposed wool, and naturally dyed fibres using colour extracted from invasive weeds including ivy, St John's wort, hawthorn, briar rose, mullein, dandelion and thistle. Often introduced to recreate familiar European landscapes, these plants become both subject and material, their pigments embedded within the weavings. Other works draw on the native vegetation of the Murrumbidgee River corridor, recalling the pre-colonial riverbanks and open woodlands that were progressively displaced by pastoral settlement. Woven using raw merino wool, these ghostly forms reference both the original ecology and the sheep industry that transformed it.⁠
.⁠

【MIGHTY JAM ROCK】出演決定！
@jumbomaatch @takafin_reggaejam @mjr_boxerkid

大阪を拠点に活動するレゲエクルー。メンバーは、サウンドのKYARAとROCK。そしてDeeJayのJUMBO MAATCH、TAKAFIN、BOXER KID。サウンドシステムはDANCEHALL MECHA-DOG 、 レーベルはMIGHTY JAMROCK RECORDS。
1998年、大阪のサウンドがクルーの枠を超えて《謎のミックス集団》MIGHTY JAM ROCKとしてミックステープ「SOUND BACTERIA」シリーズを発売したのが起源だ。当時、レゲエのテープといえばジャマイカから輸入
された音質の悪い現場収録モノが主流であったが、「レゲエはいいぞ」を旗印に掲げ、クオリティにこだわったミックステープを制作。結果、レゲエファンのみならず、アパレルショップ、美容院、飲食店などでBGMとしても人気を博し、大阪・アメリカ村を中心に、街中に「SOUND BACTERIA」が大音量で鳴り響くというムーブメントを巻き起こした。またこの頃、ジャパニーズレゲエは近年のように確立しておらず、ダンスやサウンドクラッシュで日本語レゲエをプレイすることで非難の声が上がる時代でもあった。
悔しかった。「広くレゲエを聞いてもらいたい」「ジャパニーズレゲエの良さを知ってもらいたい」。その想いを実現させるべく、MIGHTY JAMROCKはいよいよ《謎の集団》の仮面を脱ぎ捨て本格始動を決意。それが1999年に開催された、当時まだ珍しかった生演奏のバンドでアーティストがパフォーマンスを行うビッグステージショー「HIGHEST MOUNTAIN」の第1回だ。以来「HIGHEST MOUNTAIN」は毎年開催され、8年目の2006年には大阪・舞洲で2万5千人を集客し、名実ともにレゲエフェスの代名詞ともなった。最近では大阪城野外音楽堂での開催を2年経て、2018年には開催20周年を迎え、家族連れにも優しいレゲエフェスティバルをテーマに舞洲で復活開催する。
また、JUMBO MAATCH、TAKAFIN、BOXER KIDの3人ユニットでのアルバムも、2001年より毎年リリース。シーンの筆頭を走り続け、2025年には25枚目のアルバム「DANCEHALL ROCK」を完成させた。ジャパニーズレゲエアーティスト最多のリリース量である。
大阪にレゲエあり! と日本中に知らしめた彼らは、20年を超える時を経てもなおカルチャーの核となり、レゲエの魅力を拡散する。「レゲエはいいぞ」の彼らの旗は、今日も大空になびいている。

OPENING NIGHT | Thank you to everyone that joined us for the opening of four new exhibitions at Craft + Design Canberra on Thursday 30 July.⁠
.⁠
You can now visit the exhibitions until 12 September 2026. The Craft + Design Canberra Gallery is open from Wednesday to Saturday from noon to 4pm.⁠
.⁠
LEARN MORE | About the Exhibitions⁠
.⁠
Correspondence continues Jude Muduioa’s @judemuduioa interest in accumulation as both a making process and a way of thinking. Each element is formed by hand before becoming part of a larger whole, where no single component dominates. ⁠
.⁠
Dwell by Suzanne Knight @suzanneknight33 presents a body of tapestry weavings that explores the intertwined histories of migration, settlement and ecological change. ⁠
.⁠
Vessels of Dialogue by Sarit Cohen @saritcohenceramics is an exhibition of ceramics exploring architectural moments shaped by the artist’s memories.⁠
.⁠
Fragile Structures: The Architecture of Decay is a collaboration between visual artists Madeline Cardone @madeline.cardone and Fran Romano @franromanoceramics Working in glass and ceramics respectively, the artists share an overlapping conceptual and material language. ⁠
.⁠

Before we introduce the new designers for March I wanted to introduce myself and the motivation behind Makers Market. It's Emma here, I'm a founder / director at Good Form with Dan. 

Design in New Zealand is punching above our weight in many sectors, especially architecture. When it comes to smaller objects and applied design it seems a lot harder to build your own practice. The few who make it to market are under huge pressure and it's tough to survive. It seems like there is a space to nurture design talent and give emerging designers some exposure. 

In honesty I'm trying to create the kind of event I want to go to myself. I've been fortunate to meet so many designers and creatives and I noticed there aren't a lot of platforms for exposure. Makers Market is something we started as a small way to share our local talent with you. We hope you will love the March event designers and come out to support them. 

Thank you so much to everyone who joined us in October and the wonderful vibrant crew who exhibited and supported the event. It was an exhilarating experience – I don't think I stopped smiling all weekend. We can't wait to do it again!

See you soon.

Emma Eagle

Between Land and Sea by David Ellsworth

In this sculptural work, a group of kangaroos is rendered in sharp, geometric steel forms, their familiar silhouettes reduced to structure and line. Set against the natural landscape of the beach, the kangaroos speak to endurance, balance, and quiet presence. The use of bright, reflective colour contrasts with the surrounding sand and sea, introducing a deliberate tension between the natural and the constructed. While their forms are static, the arrangement suggests movement and awareness, capturing a moment of stillness within an ever-changing environment.

The inaugural Rhoda Roberts Oration honoured the late, beloved arts leader with a deeply moving and significant tribute from proud Quandamooka man and Chair of Creative Australia, Wesley Enoch, which left few dry eyes in the crowd.⁠
⁠
Antoun Issa captured his mother's experiences of love, heartbreak and hope during the Lebanese Civil War in Rebirth, while Tom Forrest delighted audiences with Gone Bush, a funny, personable session with Mindy Woods that that spoke to Country and explored family connection through food.⁠
⁠
A full house was enraptured by Antoinette Lattouf, who brought Women Who Win to the stage with Louise Adler, a powerful and insightful look at women who took on the system and won.⁠
⁠
What was your favourite session from Friday? Share a photo or your thoughts in the comments.⁠

🔥 Un père, un fils, une aventure.
 Notre ambassadeur @jonwoodroof a repris la route du @grinduro Scotland cette année, 8 ans après sa première édition. Mais cette fois, son fils Otto, 15 ans, était de la partie. 

2 jours de voyage depuis la Hollande, vélo chargé + ferry de nuit 
100 km de gravel écossais, avec pluie et jolis cols au programme 
1 souvenir gravé à vie : Otto, plus jeune rider de l’épreuve 🏆 

« La veille, Otto et moi avons hésité entre le parcours de 65 km ou celui de 100 km. Finalement, nous avons choisi les 100 km, avec ma devise : “nous ne sommes pas venus jusqu’ici pour seulement venir jusqu’ici”. » 

Quand la fatigue s’est installée après 70 km, Jon a posé une main sur l’épaule de son fils et l’a aidé à grimper les dernières côtes grâce à son Dimanche 29 Gravel. 

Un moment simple, fort, où l’esprit du vélo prend tout son sens : partage, liberté, dépassement. 

📸 Crédit : @andrewleinsterphoto / @christinegei.ger / @doddstar1979 

🇬🇧 A father, a son, an adventure.
Our ambassador Jon returned to Grinduro Scotland this year, 8 years after his very first edition. But this time, his 15-year-old son Otto was part of the journey.

2 days traveling from Holland, loaded bike + overnight ferry
100 km of Scottish gravel, with rain and some tough climbs on the menu
1 memory for life: Otto, Youngest Rider of the event 🏆

“The night before, Otto & I debated the 65km or 100km routes. Ultimately, we went for the 100km with my motto: ‘we didn’t come this far to only come this far’.”

When fatigue kicked in around km 70, Jon placed a hand on his son’s shoulder and helped him conquer the final climbs with his Dimanche 29 Gravel.
A raw, powerful moment — where cycling means sharing, freedom, and pushing your limits.

The Dock chair by Clark Bardsley features New Zealand long-fibre wool sheepskin upholstered onto a soft, cylindrical backrest. The shape of the backrest supports the body in a warm, and highly tactile embrace.

caption:
Soplo a la vista en la Escuela del Océano Pichilemu! 🐋

Hoy celebramos el Día Mundial De Las Ballenas, guardianas de la salud del océano y visitantes ilustres de nuestras costas en Pichilemu. 

¿Sabías que su presencia no solo es un espectáculo natural, sino que son piezas clave para combatir el cambio climático? Al capturar carbono y fertilizar el fitoplancton, ¡nos ayudan a todos a respirar mejor!

Y eso no es todo! 

Nos visita en la Escuela del Océano está hermosa Ballena Franca Austral creada por el colectivo @tipichill_chilli  para el @surfestival la cuál recorrió La Serena y Pichilemu, inspirada en la ballena y su cría que nos visitó frente a nuestra escuela en octubre del 2024.

Esta ballena Franca Austral fue creada con madera reciclada y boyas interceptadas en la Reserva Nacional Pinguino de Humboldt. #NoaDominga 

 Agradecemos por esta donación a @surfestival y @los.lobos.records por facilitarnos está hermosa Ballena la cual puedes venir a conocer desde hoy, y concursar  respondiendo a la pregunta: 

¿Qué nombre le pondrías a esta ballena?
Todos los nombres concursan por un premio. 
Para eso debes: 

1. comentar la foto con el nombre más original 🫰
2. compartir este post en tus historias etiquetando @escueladeloceano_chile. 

Sorteo Martes 24 de Febrero a través de nuestras publicaciones. 
Sorteo sólo válido para chile.

En la Escuela del Océano Pichilemu, creemos que debemos conocer para proteger. 

Por eso, hoy te invitamos a:
🔸Respetar las distancias de avistamiento 👀🐋
🔸Aprender más sobre las especies que migran por nuestro maritorio 🐳
🔸No contaminar nuestras playas🚫

Artists are invited to be creatively brave, bold and daring when applying to be a part of SWELL 2026, Queensland's largest outdoor sculpture exhibition taking place at Currumbin Beach on the Gold Coast.

SWELL is a ten-day manifestation of conceptions and visual commentary, and presents small, medium and large-scale sculpture, installations, and digital works as a FREE outdoor gallery at Currumbin Beach, 11 – 20 September 2026.

📌 Your Perth Makers Market FAQ! ✨

Planning your visit to our next market on Sunday, 24 May 2026 at Goolugatup Heathcote? We’ve got you covered with everything you need to know before you arrive! 👇

❓ Is there an entry fee?
💰 Nope! Perth Makers Market is a FREE community event. Come for the good vibes and support incredible local creatives! 🛍️

❓ Where can I park?
🅿️ Parking is available right next to the market at the Heathcote Lower Lands. It’s managed by Applecross Rotary as a fundraiser—your kind donation helps support local non-profit initiatives. 🙌

❓ Can I take public transport?
🚉 Yes! Hop off at Canning Bridge Station (Mandurah Line), then enjoy a scenic 20-minute riverside walk to the market. It’s a beautiful way to start your day out!

❓ Is the market wheelchair accessible?
♿ Absolutely! Goolugatup Heathcote features step-free paths, accessible toilets, and ACROD parking. If ACROD bays are full, a drop-off zone is available—just ask our friendly staff for help.

❓ Can I bring my dog?
🐶 Sorry, no dogs allowed. Goolugatup Heathcote is a dog-free venue. Bringing pets could result in a fine if seen by a ranger—please leave them at home this time. 💜

❓ Are there vegan & gluten-free options?
🌱 Yes! There’s a great variety of vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free eats—from sweet treats to savoury bites, there’s something for everyone!

❓ Should I bring cash or card?
💳 Most stallholders accept card, but we recommend bringing some cash just in case. There is no ATM on-site, so plan ahead if you prefer to use cash.

❓ Got another question?
💬 Drop a comment below or slide into our DMs we’re here to help!

Join us this Sunday 24th May 2026 from 9:30am to 3:30pm at Goolugatup Heathcote, Applecross.

SPOTLIGHTON: Thammika Songkaeo⁠
⁠
Thammika Songkaeo is the author of Stamford Hospital, a debut novel selected as a must-read for International Women’s Day alongside The Handmaid’s Tale and The Second Sex. ⁠
⁠
Set over a single weekend, the novel follows a woman who hospitalises her barely-ill child − not out of neglect, but sheer exhaustion − using the institution as a temporary refuge from a life she had not expected: one defined by full-time motherhood and a sexless marriage in Singapore, a place she never agreed to be.⁠
⁠
Thammika Songkaeo will be in conversation at Byron Writers Festival this weekend.⁠
⁠⁠

Can you believe it's been more than 10 years since Perth Makers Market began? 🎉

Every item you find at our market is handcrafted by local artisans right here in WA. Our debut in 2016 featured 75 stallholders and drew a crowd of 1500 visitors. Since then, we've grown to hosting six markets annually in Applecross, along with our popular twilight series at Burswood Park. With strong ties to the community and a focus on giving back, we think there's something magical about Perth Makers Market.

Thank you to our amazing stallholders, customers and community for being part of our journey! Here's to many more years of creativity and community. 🌟

🚨SCAM ALERT – PLEASE READ🚨

We've seen an increase in scams targeting our stallholder community, so we'd like to remind everyone how to identify genuine communications from our team.

Official emails will ONLY come from emails ending in the following:
• @marketlife.com.au
• @perthmakersmarket.com
• @perthupmarket.com.au

⚠️ Common scams we're seeing include:
• Comments or messages claiming there are stallholder spaces available and asking you to DM someone privately.
• Fake emails offering stallholder opportunities for events we don't run.
• People pretending to represent our markets in Facebook groups.
• Emails offering to sell our stallholder database.
• Fake commission requests.
• Requests for payment via PayPal.

Please remember:
❌ We will NEVER ask you to message a staff member's personal Facebook account.
❌ We will NEVER ask you to pay via PayPal.
❌ We will NEVER request payment or personal information from an unknown email address.
✅ All market applications are made through the MarketLife website.
✅ All successful applications are invoiced via email from events@marketlife.com.au
✅ If you see different stall prices from those listed on our website, it's a scam.

If you receive a suspicious email or message:
• Don't reply.
• Don't click any links.
• Don't provide personal information or make any payments.

If you're ever unsure, please contact us directly at events@marketlife.com.au, before taking any action. 

Thank you for helping keep our stallholder community safe. Please share this post with fellow makers and report any scam posts or accounts you come across.

Nos vemos!

The First National Byron team visited Courtney Adamo at her beautiful Bangalow home to talk about the things that matter most to her – family, home, creativity, and the little details that make a house feel like a home.

In our conversation, Courtney shares the inspiration behind the family rituals and seasonal rhythms explored in her newest book, At Home in Every Season.

From her love of books and interiors to creating spaces where family and friends can gather, she gives us a glimpse into the ideas, rituals and inspiration that shape her approach to home and life in the Northern Rivers.

A few years ago, I never could have imagined writing this...

✨ One of my art pieces has been selected for the 2026 SWELL Sculpture Festival in Australia. ✨

This September, a 16-foot sculpture of mine will travel from California to Currumbin Beach on Australia’s Gold Coast, where it will be exhibited alongside artists from around the world as part of one of the country’s most celebrated outdoor sculpture festivals.

For 10 days, thousands of visitors will experience art stretched across miles of coastline—where the ocean becomes the backdrop and creativity becomes larger than life.

As a child, I remember standing in front of a monumental work of art and feeling something shift inside me. That moment changed the trajectory of my life.

Now, to think that something I created might spark that feeling for someone else is both humbling and surreal.

But what makes this public piece especially meaningful is that this artwork isn’t about me.

It’s about us.

Built from woven paintings and the hopes, dreams, and wishes of people from all walks of life this sculpture exhibiting at SWELL, will continue collecting wishes for the world—creating a living archive of connection, hope, healing, and humanity.

Over the coming months, I’ll be sharing ways for people around the world to participate this project called:

🌊 Wishes Across Oceans 🌊

A global exchange of wishes connecting Ahumanity through art, light, and human connection.

If you’d like to be part of the artwork, comment “WISH” below or send me a DM.

And if you’re new here, welcome. I’m so glad you’re along for the journey.

Australia, here we come. 🇦🇺✨

¡Todo un espectáculo! 😍✨

🐋🇨🇱Su figura se robaba las miradas durante el surfestival, convirtiéndose en un símbolo de admiración y respeto por el océano. No era solo una representación artística, sino un poderoso mensaje ambiental. Su presencia invita a reflexionar sobre la relación entre las personas y el mar.

🏄🌊La llegada de esta majestuosa figura hecha por @tipichill_chilli no solo fue en el Surfestival, ahora para conmemoración del Día Mundial de las Ballenas arribó en la Escuela del Océano en Pichilemu, un espacio dedicado a la educación y cultura marina. Su objetivo principal fue inspirar conciencia y compromiso con el cuidado del entorno marino.

🪵♻️El ejemplar, además de bello, fue creado con madera reciclada, reforzando el mensaje de sostenibilidad. Esta decisión no fue casual, ya que busca promover la importancia del reciclaje y la reutilización de materiales. Así, la obra une arte y educación ambiental en un solo proyecto. La creatividad se convirtió en una vía concreta para hablar de responsabilidad ecológica.

🐳🩵Las ballenas cumplen un rol fundamental en el equilibrio del planeta. Son capaces de capturar grandes cantidades de carbono a lo largo de su vida, ayudando a reducir los efectos del cambio climático. Además, a través de sus desplazamientos, fertilizan los océanos. Este proceso contribuye a la producción de oxígeno y al mantenimiento de la vida marina.

📍📸En Chile, estos gigantes marinos forman parte esencial del patrimonio natural. Cada año pueden ser admirados en distintas zonas costeras y en diversas épocas, atrayendo también el interés científico y turístico. Su presencia fortalece la identidad marítima del país. Son un recordatorio vivo de la riqueza y diversidad de nuestros ecosistemas.

👀🫶🏻Crear conciencia sobre la labor de las ballenas es urgente y necesario. No solo representan belleza y majestuosidad, sino también una solución natural frente a la crisis climática. Educar a través del arte es clave para que las futuras generaciones sigan maravillándose con su existencia.

ON UNTIL SATURDAY 18 JULY | Reclamation | Jessika Spencer (Wiradjuri)⁠ @jessikatona @ngur.ru⁠. Visit the Gallery from noon to 4pm, Wednesday to Saturday. 
.⁠
Reclamation continues Wiradjuri artist Jessika Spencer’s exploration of Indigenous feminine knowledge systems and material practice. Flowing on from her recent exhibition Rematriate, this body of work reflects a process of returning to softer ways and focusing on the quiet strength Aboriginal women have always carried.⁠
.⁠
Working across weaving, adornment, eco dyed textiles, photography and sculptural installation, the exhibition brings together woven coolamons, water carriers, reclaimed textile works and contemporary adornments that speak to survival, continuity and connection to Country.⁠
.⁠
Natural materials gathered from Country remain central throughout the exhibition. River reeds, raffia, shells, palm fibre and reclaimed fabrics are transformed through weaving, knotting and eco dyeing processes that honour cultural practises.⁠
.⁠
Historically, woven objects such as coolamons, dillybags and water carriers were not decorative objects, but essential cultural technologies tied to gathering, medicine, motherhood and survival. By reinterpreting these forms through contemporary installation and adornment, Reclamation honours ancestral knowledge while asserting its continued relevance within contemporary Indigenous life.⁠
.⁠
At its core, the exhibition is an act of reclamation, reclaiming space, ways of thinking, practice and cultural continuity through making.⁠
.⁠
For more information visit our website | Link in bio.⁠

Book Review: 100 Years of Betty by Debra Oswald ⁠
⁠
Reviewed by Amy L at The Book Warehouse Ballina⁠
⁠
One Hundred Years of Betty was such a beautiful surprise. I went in expecting a story about one remarkable woman, but it ended up feeling like a story about all the ordinary moments that make up a life. This was an excellent choice for our recent bookclub pick!⁠
⁠
Following Betty through an entire century was incredibly moving. As a character, she is resilient, funny, stubborn, and so wonderfully human. Debra Oswald has a way of making everyday moments feel just as important as the life-changing ones, and I found myself completely invested in Betty’s journey.⁠
⁠
There were parts that made me laugh, parts that made me cry, and plenty of moments that had me thinking about family, love, loss, and how much the world can change in one lifetime. It felt warm, heartfelt, and quietly powerful from beginning to end with a big emphasis on family in both senses of blood-related and found families.⁠

📍 See Debra Oswald at Byron Writers Festival next week, from 14—16 August. 
⁠

🎲Estamos felices, ayer recibimos la entrega de 55 juegos de mesa de LudiChile al Espacio Lector del Centro Cultural La Moneda.

📚Esta donación se enmarca en el Mes del Diseño, junto a la próxima exposición “Mesa compartida. El juego de mesa en Chile”, que invita a reflexionar sobre el rol cultural y social que han tenido los juegos de mesa en nuestro país desde mediados del siglo XX hasta hoy.

🤝El juego de mesa trasciende edades y contextos, es una práctica cultural que fortalece la convivencia, el aprendizaje y la comunicación.Pronto estarán disponibles para que todas las comunidades que nos visitan puedan disfrutarlos y encontrar en el juego un espacio de encuentro y diálogo.

Durante este hito nos acompañaron: Regina Rodríguez, driectora ejecutiva del CCLM, Trinidad Guzman, coordinadora del Área de Diseño y Servicios Creativos del Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio, Juan Pablo Vergara, curador de la muestra, Matías Castillo, LudiChile, Laura Mena, Fractal Juegos y Camila Parra de Ludoísmo.

Agradecemos a Within Play, Fractal, Fatuma, SJS, Flama Lama, Etherna, Circoctel, Niebla Games, Quimera Estudio, Pudu Juegos, Salta pal lao, Akanni, Tricípite, Ludoísmo y Holiplay.

ABOUT THE MAKER⁠
.⁠
Ferro Forma is the culmination of a long standing partnership between Alison Jackson and Dan Lorrimer. They are a metalsmithing workshop specialising in handcrafted small batch edition objects that capture the hand of the maker and the heritage of our craft.⁠
.⁠
Alison Jackson is a designer, maker and contemporary Silversmith based in Braidwood, Australia. Completing a Gold and Silversmithing degree at the Australian National University, Alison holds over two decades of artistic and technical metal forming expertise.⁠
.⁠
With an aesthetic best described as elegant, timeless, and minimal, Alison showcases her work through her fine jewellery, tableware, large scale installation, limited editions and exhibition work.⁠
.⁠
Alison’s work is held in both public and private collections, including a large acquisition by the Canberra Museum and Gallery. A recipient of numerous notable awards and grants,  Alison’s work has been exhibited widely within Australia and also internationally, including at Inhorgenta (Germany) and Milan Design Week (Italy). ⁠
.⁠
Dan Lorrimer is a contemporary sculptor, machinist, fabricator and toolmaker. With a degree in Sculpture from the Australian National University, Dan has since diversified his work, significantly developing his skills across a wide range of technical areas, specialising in metal forming.⁠
.⁠
Dan’s sculpture practice explores notions of movement, energy, solidity and illusion through minimalist sculptural forms, often located between the artificial and natural world. He has exhibited widely across Australia and has work held in private collections across the country. ⁠
.⁠
Photography by Leann Timms

Join acclaimed journalist and human rights activist Antoinette Lattouf in conversation with Louise Adler for an evening celebrating the courage and conviction of women.⁠

What happens when someone steals your story – takes the intimate details of your life and puts them on the page? It happened to Rafael Frumkin, American author and essayist, when she read her former mentor's novel and recognised fragments of her own life scattered throughout. But where is the line between theft and inspiration? And what does a writer owe the people whose lives they borrow from, anyway?⁠
⁠
On Friday, 14 August Frumkin brings these questions to Byron Writers Festival for 'Who Owns the Story?'. In a lively conversation with Chris Harrigan, editor of @thestory.au magazine, the pair will discuss the promise and peril of mining real life – real people, relationships and pain – for writing material, and who gets to decide what stories get told.⁠
⁠
To celebrate, the first 25 guests at the session will receive a free copy of The Story magazine. So mark Friday August 14 in your calendar and get in early.⁠
⁠
@FiresideAgency is the publisher of The Story and a valued Supporting Partner of Byron Writers Festival 2026.⁠

New session added! A Life in Books.⁠
⁠
Join Richard Fidler as he records a very special episode of Conversations in front of a live audience with publishing icon Louise Adler.⁠
⁠
Louise’s parents met in Australia, in the aftermath of WWII. ⁠
⁠
As an asthmatic child Louise spent most of Melbourne’s winters in bed with nothing else to do but read novels. A particular penchant for Enid Blyton’s boarding school series required parental intervention after a certain exchange at the dinner table. Thus began her deep pleasure in the world of books.⁠
⁠
Shaped by her family history, Louise grew up interested in questioning everything. She was 15 when she went to her first Vietnam moratorium and spent far too long in the lockup for her role in the protests.⁠
⁠
She went to Israel at the age of 17, which was a transformative experience for her.⁠
⁠
Back in Australia she began her career in publishing after working as an academic and arts administrator. She spent 30 years in the publishing industry including for Hachette Australia and as the CEO of Melbourne University Publishing.⁠
⁠
Louise was Director of Adelaide Writers’ Week from 2023 until the implosion of the 2026 festival.⁠
⁠
As well as talking about her life and some of the dramatic turning points she’s experienced, Louise will expand on some of the fascinating titles she’s worked on including Louise Milligan’s book on Cardinal Pell, Mark Latham's diaries, and Tony Abbott's Battlelines.⁠
⁠
‍This is a must-see live conversation. See it with a Three-Day Pass or Friday Pass. Tickets on sale now.⁠
⁠
🗓️ 9:00–10:00am, Friday 14 August⁠

From The Conversation – the world’s leading publisher of research-based news and analysis – comes a new season of their Making Of podcast series, The Making of One Nation.⁠
⁠
From a fish and chip shop in regional Queensland to the heart of Australian politics: over six episodes, this podcast series explores the unlikely story of the country’s most controversial minor party.⁠
⁠
For thirty years, One Nation and Pauline Hanson have been ridiculed, dismissed and shut out. Now, no one is laughing. This is the story of how a party built on fear and grievance thrived, died and rose again to upend Australian politics.⁠
⁠
The Conversation goes beyond the headlines and stunts to document how One Nation works and what it means for Australia’s future.⁠

LEARN MORE | About the Exhibition⁠
.⁠
This exhibition is an introduction to the STAUNCH. Collective, a collaboration presenting works created by seven Blak artists who connected through conversations about Culture as a resistance practice for/as First Peoples. ⁠
.⁠
Each of the artists have created work that speaks to their experiences of growth, connection and healing, opening space for discussion, discourse and joy. STAUNCH. invites you to consider what resistance truly looks like, how do you resist the colony and how do you uphold it? ⁠

Rewild | Artists-in-Residence Exhibition presents new work by artists Michele Grimston @michelegrimstonart and Hannah McKellar @hannnahmckellar, developed through the 2025 Craft + Design Canberra Artist-in-Residence program at Cinerea Cottage, located within Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve. The residency combines time immersed in the landscape with a dedicated research component undertaken in partnership with the National Zoo and Aquarium @nationalzoo.⁠

Framed by the theme of Rewilding, the program invited Michele and Hannah to consider ecological restoration and shifting relationships between humans and the natural world. MEET THE MAKER | Meet Rodriguez Nalorlman Pindiying @pindiyinq (Thyemirri Bininj, Djalama Clan Group, Mamadawerre homeland, West Arnhem Land (NT)) and listen to them discuss their artwork Kurrung (merebu) 2026. This work is part of STAUNCH., on at Craft + Design Canberra until Saturday 23 May 2026. 
.
Visit the exhibition and see the work in person at Craft + Design Canberra. Open noon to 4pm, Wednesday to Saturday upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra. 
.
ARTIST STATEMENT
.
This artwork depicts the traditional seasonal changes of colour harvested from plants on Djalama Country. It represents the six Bininj seasons, Kudjewk, Bangkerreng, Yekke, Wurrkeng, Kurrung and Kunumeleng, of the Kuwarddewardde Malkno Calendar. Each of the woven colours represent the seasons in which particular plants can be collected. This is a collaborative piece created with two djunkayi (Care Takers) for Mamadawerre, including Rosemary. Her knowledge demonstrates the seasonal changes through traditional weaving techniques.
.
The surrounding digital art prints depict the six specific colours from the calendar and the respective plants they come from. The prints document deep intergenerational knowledge inspired by interdisciplinary techniques. The artwork mixes traditional weaving techniques from West Arnhem Land and contemporary practices.
.
ARTIST BIOGRAPHY
.
Rodriguez Nalorlman Pindiying is a Thyemirri Bininj artist, educator, and cultural leader from the Djalama Clan Group in Mamadawerre, West Arnhem Land. His multidisciplinary practice bridges Country, knowledge sharing, and conservation exploring rock art, digital heritage, and the transmission of ancestral knowledge through contemporary forms. As a collaborator with STAUNCH. collective, Rodriguez celebrates the resilience and creativity of remote homelands, using art as a tool for education, identity, and cultural continuity. 
.
#staunchcollective #firstnations

MEET THE MAKER | Listen to Georgia Hoskinson @sovereign_archive @george.ah (Badtjala (Butchulla)) speak about their work, Silt, Salt, Sovereign 2026. This work is part of STAUNCH., on at Craft + Design Canberra until Saturday 23 May 2026. 
.
Visit the exhibition and see the work in person at Craft + Design Canberra. Open noon to 4pm, Wednesday to Saturday upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra. 
.
ARTIST STATEMENT
.
This series of nine lithograph and monotype panels explore littoral zones, shifting spaces and masterpieces of adaptation as agents of Indigenous Futurism.
.
The works were made by layering lithograph, trace monotype drawing, monoprint, and giclee techniques to create transparent sun-toned light and topographical, chitinous washes which collapse the distance between tide pools and cosmic nebula.
.
Silt, Salt, Sovereign honors the eternal unyielding presence of generations on the shorelines of the future.
.
ARTIST BIOGRAPHY
.
Georgia Hoskinson is a Badtjala/Butchulla (Wondunna clan) artist and arts worker, with East Prussian, English and Irish heritage. Based in Magandjin/Meanjin and working in the Gallery and Museums sector, Georgia’s practice employs print making and life drawing to explore narratives and ecosystems of Salt-Water Country, with an interest in the intersection of cultural practice and institutional ‘tradition’. 
.
#staunchcollective #firstnations

MEET THE MAKER | Listen to Marcus Maye Wright @mayemarcuswright (Wiradjuri-Gamilaraay) speak about their work, I have all this time with you 2025. This work is part of STAUNCH., on at Craft + Design Canberra until Saturday 23 May 2026. 
.
Visit the exhibition and see the work in person at Craft + Design Canberra. Open noon to 4pm, Wednesday to Saturday upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra.

ARTIST STATEMENT
.
I have all this time with you (2025) consists of four black and white prints on photographic paper, accompanied by a cut coolamon with the negatives mounted onto the outside. The work was a collaborative shoot with Dion Wait, a social media sensation and cultural practitioner who lives and works in Wagga Wagga, New South Wales.
.
The work is a message through time; the coolamon, the scar on the tree, the images and the negatives. Scar trees on Country are a message to us from the old people, and cutting one today is communicating back, it is our ability to speak with them, join them in culture.
.
I really want to thank Dion, who blesses me with a breath of Country and culture while I am tucked away into the city. I also want to compliment him on the perfection of 
his craft.
- Marcus Maye Wright (2026)
.
ARTIST BIOGRAPHY
.
Marcus Maye Wright (he/him) is a Wiradjuri (Wiradyuri) and Gamilaraay (Gomeroi / Gamilaroi/ Kamilaroi) man hailing from the Central Western tablelands, New South Wales and is an experienced digital producer focusing on film production with a passion in telling Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander stories. Marcus is interested in the complexities of film photography, as well as the intimate process of taking portraits.

A CELEBRATION OF 2025 | Results of our Annual General Meeting and Annual Report.
.
On 24 March 2026 Craft + Design Canberra held our Annual General Meeting (AGM), reporting on 2025. We are delighted to share some of the incredible achievements outlined in our 2025 Annual Report, which is now available on our website.
.
2025 was a landmark year for Craft + Design Canberra. Income to artists as a result of our programs reached $404,034, a 644% increase since 2023.* Exhibition visitors grew 133% to 6,178 people, and our public programs attracted over 10,000 people in person, a 616% increase since 2023, and more than 20,000 online. Our inaugural Undercurrent Design Market drew 4,279 visitors and generated over $302,996 in sales for makers across just three days, while shop sales increased by 53% from 2024.
.
The organisation is in a strong financial position, with our auditors confirming that our financial report gives a true and fair view of our financial position as at 31 December 2025. We also secured ACT Government funding for the 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Festival, themed Dissent, the result of more than ten years of advocacy, and we look forward to sharing our festival achievements and program in the coming months. With revenue growing 38% over four years, we head into our festival year in the strongest position we have ever been.
.
At the AGM we farewelled Board members Penny Boyer, Rod Bobeldijk, Kayannie Dennigan and Ashley Eriksmoen and thanked them for their generosity and passion, and welcomed new Board members Delephene Fraser, Ben Ennis Butler and Erin Hinton.
.
Thank you to our incredible community for everything they do to advocate for contemporary craft and design practice in the Canberra region and connect artists, community, partners and places.
.
None of this would be possible without the dedication of our incredible staff and board, the generosity of our sponsors and partners, and the ongoing support of our government funders artsACT and Creative Australia. 
.
*We measure against 2023 as it was our last comparable non-festival year. During festival years statistics fluctuate greatly.
.
Images | Photography by 5 Foot Photography

MEET THE MAKER | Listen to Sandy Harvey @sandycappuccino (Kalkadoon) speak about their work, Natives 2026. This work is part of STAUNCH., on at Craft + Design Canberra until Saturday 23 May 2026. 
.
Visit the exhibition and see the work in person at Craft + Design Canberra. Open noon to 4pm, Wednesday to Saturday upstairs in the North Building, 1, 180 London Cct, Canberra. 
.
ARTIST STATEMENT
.
Natives is a series of six works depicting Australian native flowers: waratah, Cooktown orchid, Sturt’s desert rose, Tasmanian wattle, golden wattle and royal bluebell. Each species is tied to a specific place, carrying the presence and memory of Country.
.
The series reflects on endurance as quiet persistence. Native flowers adapt and continue, thriving in environments shaped by change. Their resilience is gentle yet constant, grounded in deep relationships to Country. In this way, they become a metaphor for resistance, not as force, but as survival, 
continuity and care.
.
Together, the works form a dispersed map of STAUNCH’s homelands, connecting different places while holding space for identity and belonging. Natives considers how we remain rooted across distance, and how connection to Country endures.
.
ARTIST BIOGRAPHY
.
Sandy Harvey is a Kalkadoon artist and arts worker based in Meanjin/Magandjin/Brisbane, with a creative practice rooted in storytelling and connection, exploring the relationships between people, place and spirit. She is interested in creating inclusive and accessible spaces for artists where they can share their stories and connect with one another and their audiences. 
.

2026 ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE PROGRAM | In March, the 2026 Craft + Design Canberra Artists-in-Residence explored the National Film and Sound Archive @nfsaonline (NFSA), including getting a behind the scenes tour of the Mitchell warehouse. ⁠
.⁠
Lea Durie @lea_durie, Jeffrey Sarmiento @sarmiento_glass and Julie Bartholomew @juliebartholomewceramics joined NFSA staff to explore objects, records and gather inspiration.⁠
.⁠
ABOUT THE 2026 CRAFT + DESIGN CANBERRA ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE PROGRAM ⁠
.⁠
Since 2006, Craft + Design Canberra have collaborated with the ACT Parks and Conservation Service @actparks to offer residencies that explore the intersection of craft and nature. The residency provides artists with solitude and space for creative reflection, opportunities to engage in public workshops, and culminates in an exhibition at Craft + Design Canberra. ⁠
.⁠
In 2026 the research partner is the National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA) @nfsaonline, offering a two-week research period focused on Australia’s rich audiovisual heritage. Artists are now spending time at the Acton building and in the archives in Mitchell, engaging with archived voices and stories that capture our collective memories, cultural shifts and evolving identity. ⁠
.⁠
Following the research period, artists will spend three weeks at Gudgenby Ready-Cut Cottage in Namadgi National Park. Since 2006, this residency has offered a profoundly transformative environment that fosters reflection, inquiry and the development of new work. ⁠
.⁠
The residency will be followed by an Open Day at Ready-Cut Cottage in in Namadgi National Park on Saturday 28 March 2026. You can book your place now via our website by heading to craftanddesigncanberra.org and heading to the PROGRAMS page. ⁠
⁠

LEARN MORE | About the Exhibitions

STAUNCH.
This exhibition is an introduction to the STAUNCH. Collective, a collaboration presenting works created by seven Blak artists who connected through conversations about Culture as a resistance practice for/as First Peoples. 
.
Each of the artists have created work that speaks to their experiences of growth, connection and healing, opening space for discussion, discourse and joy. STAUNCH. invites you to consider what resistance truly looks like, how do you resist the colony and how do you uphold it? 
.
STAUNCH. is a cultural collective making works of art that generate Blak excellence, each artist with their own creative practice drawing from Country, Community and collaboration. 
.
STAUNCH. includes the artists Rodriguez Nalorlman Pindiying @pindiyinq (Thyemirri Bininj, Djalama Clan Group, Mamadawerre homeland, West Arnhem Land (NT)), Georgia Hoskinson 
@george.ah (Badtjala (Butchulla)), Sandy Harvey @sandycappuccino (Kalkadoon), Shanysa Jayde McConville @shanysajayde (Eastern Arrernte), Marcus Maye Wright @mayemarcuswright (Wiradjuri-Gamilaraay), Nic Ingram @nadi_yarns (Palawa and Wiradjuri ) and Maggie Douglas @maggiejean.douglas (Kabi Kabi and South Sea Islander). 
.

2026 ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE PROGRAM IS UNDERWAY | Meet Jeffrey Sarmiento @sarmiento_glass, one of three artists along with Lea Durie @lea_durie and Julie Bartholomew @juliebartholomewceramics, who have been selected as the Craft + Design Canberra 2026 Artists-in-Residence in partnership with @nfsaonline and @actparks. 
.
In this video, hear Jeffrey discuss how he is finding the residency so far. 
.⁠
Since 2006, Craft + Design Canberra have collaborated with the ACT Parks and Conservation Service @actparks to offer residencies that explore the intersection of craft and nature. The residency provides artists with solitude and space for creative reflection, opportunities to engage in public workshops, and culminates in an exhibition at Craft + Design Canberra. ⁠
.⁠
In 2026 the research partner is the National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA) @nfsaonline, offering a two-week research period focused on Australia’s rich audiovisual heritage. Artists have been spending time at the Acton building and in the archives in Mitchell, engaging with archived voices and stories that capture our collective memories, cultural shifts and evolving identity. ⁠
.⁠
Following the research period, artists will spend three weeks at Gudgenby Ready-Cut Cottage in Namadgi National Park. Since 2006, this residency has offered a profoundly transformative environment that fosters reflection, inquiry and the development of new work. ⁠
.⁠
The final part of the residency will see the three artists exhibit at Craft + Design Canberra in 2027. 
.⁠
