Glaze-making day begins long before the glaze itself.
The first step is preparing the ash — one of only three ingredients in my ash glaze recipe. This ash comes from my own fireplace and those of generous friends, gathered with gratitude and transformed into something entirely new.
The process is slow and deliberate. First, the ash passes through a gold-panning sieve to remove the larger pieces of charcoal. Then through a kitchen sieve, making it easier for the final stage — a 60# sieve, where it becomes soft, fine powder.
Many moons ago, I decided not to wash my ash. I enjoy leaving a little mystery in the mix. Each batch carries its own character, with subtle shifts in colour depending on the wood it came from. No two are ever exactly the same.
Collecting and sieving enough ash for a single glaze batch can take many hours. Once I have enough, I mix the glaze and let it rest overnight, allowing it to settle before one final sieving the next day.
Then comes the glazing.
Many of you know that I spray my glaze rather than dip it. I apply it in a way that mimics the path of flame in a wood-fired kiln, enhancing the contours of my sculptural forms. The result is movement, depth, and a surface that feels alive — carrying traces of fire, ash, time, and the stories of the wood from which it came.

Rising fuel costs are making it harder for remote First Nations artists to share their work nationally, with diesel prices reaching up to $4.40 a litre in communities like Papulankutja (Blackstone) in WA and Ramingining in the NT. 

For remote art centres, attending major events such as the Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair can mean travelling thousands of kilometres, transporting artworks and covering significant fuel and freight expenses. 

Despite the growing costs, art centre workers say attending these fairs remains vital for cultural connection, visibility and income, with organisers now appealing for support to help remote communities make the journey.

Featured Artist | Vanessa Inkamala

Born in Ntaria (Hermannsburg), Vanessa Inkamala paints alongside her younger siblings at Iltja Ntjarra (Many Hands) Art Centre. Working in the renowned Hermannsburg School watercolour tradition, Vanessa continues a style that has been passed down through generations of her family, carrying forward the artistic legacy of Albert Namatjira and the Western Aranda watercolour movement.Through her work, Vanessa contributes to a living tradition that remains an important expression of culture, Country and family connection.

Artist spotlight - Janet Fraser

Studio # 4

Janet loves the strength, plasticity and texture of stoneware clay, the metamorphosis through fire back to its origins of rock and stone. 

Most of her work is wheel thrown, some shapes and surfaces altered reflecting the natural formations and weathering of the landscape. 

Rock and ash glazes express a feel of place and colours of the Australian bush, the elements of water, wind and fire, a natural progression from raw, soft and sticky clay to rock hard pieces with textures of the land and seashore.

*SOLD OUT* Join @lor_saboourin (they/them) to practice “Falling on Gear!” This training addresses falling directly to help improve commitment. We do progressive falling practice followed by movement, breathing, resting, and body/mind awareness exercises. Students leave understanding how to take appropriate risks and how to commit to those risks. Students will practice the following skills during this course: fall properly, give a dynamic (cushioned) belay, break a climb into smaller risk events, assess risk effectively, distinguish between no- and yes-fall zones, engage no- and yes-fall zones appropriately, make appropriate risk decisions, improve body/mind awareness, rest effectively, improve breathing, create flow and momentum, deal with climbing stress, commit more deliberately, reduce fear, and more!
.
*** Must be able to comfortably top rope 5.8 in the Gunks or 5.10 indoors. Must know how to lead belay. Some experience placing trad gear (such as an Intro to Trad clinic) or leading trad is required.

Sam Haines (they/she) @sahaines has always been drawn to climbing. They started at 3 years old, climbing the banister and trees of their home, and quickly progressed to rock. As a teen, they found mentorship in the community and learned the skills to top rope and teach other youth. Over the years, they progressed from sport, trad, Ice, and alpine climbing in the Northeast and other ranges across the US. Sam has worked for 15 years in outdoor education with pre-k through 12th graders. They have also been working as an organizer and volunteer of the Adirondack Queer Icefest since its founding in 2021. With these experiences, Sam brings a passion for teaching others skills to empower their own pursuits and a dedication to expanding the climbing community for marginalized people.

In Rescue Skills 101, we’lll cover basic methods of ascending a rope to help a climber, assisting a climber through a crux, taking over a belay from someone else, and simple rappel techniques. We’ll use scenarios to explore improvised solutions and best practices, instead of just teaching a few cookie-cutter drills that might not apply in the real world, and you’ll leave with a solid set of tools to handle most situations that could happen at a crag. This is a skills intensive course, and we’ll focus on learning fundamentals on the ground, then practicing those skills in a low-risk vertical setting with review and feedback from our instructors. Most of our course time will be spent working on skills with very little rock climbing, so come prepared to spend time hanging in your harness!
.

This piece, ‘Nhamini baŋ’baŋ’’, is by artist Manunu #2 Munuŋgurr from Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka.

This carving represents Nhamini Baŋ’ Baŋ’, a woman spirit from a story told to children. She inhabits the dark forest after losing her child and is drawn to the sound of a baby boy crying.

Her name comes from ‘nhamini’, meaning breasts, and ‘baŋ’ baŋ’’, the sound of them hitting her chest as she approaches. Little boys are urged to quieten their cries with the warning that Nhamini Baŋ’ Baŋ’ may come and take them away.

Nhamini baŋ’baŋ’
Earth pigments on wood
49 × 6 cm
Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka

This piece, 'Yankuljunku', is by artist Nyungawarra Ward from @Warakurna_Artists. 

"I am painting Yankuntjuntju. It is my Grandmother’s Country, close to Patjarr. There’s a rockhole close. I like to paint my story, my Grandfather’s, my Grandmother’s. My Father’s Mother passed away at that rockhole, that is why I’m painting. My Grandmother had two sons, two daughters. [She] passed away right there, rockhole side. I also paint Karrku, that’s my Nyal-ku Tjukurrpa, (my dreaming) Porcupine dreaming in that place. I think about these stories and my family when I am painting. Proper story. Painting keeps my family, and these stories close to me." - Nyungawarra Ward

Meet our next teacher for the 5th edition of the Wander Yogi Festival. 🌿 Lara Lima 

Lara draws from the wisdom of Ayurveda, Vedic Counselling, and Internal Family Systems (IFS) to guide others back to their essential nature. Her work is an invitation to remember that true connection with others begins with inner harmony.

At the Wander Yogi 2026, Lara will be sharing:
✨ Workshop: Remembering the Thread — From Inner Harmony to Human Connection

What if the invisible thread that connects us to one another is the very same thread that connects us to ourSELF?
Just as countless waves arise on the surface of one ocean, we appear different on the outside while sharing the same essential nature. This workshop is an invitation to remember that — through guided experiential practices, meditation, and the compassionate lens of IFS, Ayurveda, and Vedic wisdom.
The journey from separation to connection does not begin in the world around us. It begins within. 🤍

Join us in the Rockies, PNW, or Northeast to learn what it takes to climb even higherrrrrr in our Multi-pitch 101 course series in partnership with @smilemountainguides @out_inthewild @riseoutsidecollective 🌈✨
.
*8/22-23: Boulder, CO
*9/26-27: Smith Rock, OR
*10/24-25: New Paltz, NY
.
Flash Foxy’s Multi-pitch 101 course equips climbers with the know-how to climb and descend from routes longer than one rope-length. This course covers essentials like building multi-pitch anchors, taking the roles of leader and follower, rappelling from a multi-pitch route, staying safe and organized during transitions at anchors, and solving basic problems on routes. Our instructors will provide low-risk environments for practice and review the skills you need to continue your practice after the course. We’ll also discuss navigation, what to bring, and how to plan for your adventures. This is a skills-intensive course, and we’ll focus on learning fundamentals on the ground, then practicing those skills in a low-risk vertical setting with review and feedback from our instructors. Most of our course time will be spent working on skills with very little rock climbing, so come prepared with comfortable but capable shoes!
.
Courses are offered on a sliding-scale starting at $50 thanks to support from @arcteryx ! Full scholarships are also available at the link in bio!

Meet our next teacher for the 5th edition of the Wander Yogi Festival. 🌿 Paula Andreewitch.

Paula’s work explores practice as a context to cultivate our felt recognition of interdependence.
Weaving somatic yoga, non dual philosophy and enquiry based pedagogy, she’s interested in how our bodies tell the story of ancient cosmologies, how interoception opens perception, and the way our practice can become a generous pathway for stimulating curiosity, cultivating awe, and honouring life as sacred.

At the Wander Yogi 2026, Paula will be sharing:
✨ Somatic Yoga and Embodied Philosophy Workshop
"Rhythms of belonging" weaves somatic movement, non dual philosophy and sacred sound as an invitation to explore interdependence as a sensory experience.

Revisiting some of the stunning works that sold during DAAF Online last month. A reminder that many of the Art Centres involved have online stores you can visit year-round.

This piece, ‘Yukuwa’, is by artist Djirrirra Wunuŋmurra from Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka.

Yukuwa is one of Djirrirra’s personal names and the subject of this work, with the motif described as almost a self-portrait and an expression of her personal identity.

Yukuwa is a yam whose annual reappearance is a metaphor for the increase and renewal of people and Country. The work also references Yirritja renewal ceremony and the kinship lines that connect groups together.

Yukuwa
Earth pigment on paper
56.5 × 30.2 cm

What if a single pastry could make you think about life? This book by Rio Christiawan wanders through the small, ordinary moments that quietly shape us, a trip to another city, a cup of coffee, an emoji, a friendship, a heartbreak, and turns them into invitations to pause and reflect. The cromboloni becomes its guiding metaphor: layer upon layer, sweet and crisp, never quite as simple as it looks, just like life itself, built from experience, failure, loss, and small surprises that shape who we become. 

This book won’t turn you into a philosopher. It just asks you to slow down, notice, and think again, since philosophy hides not in lecture halls, but in a cup of coffee, a message from a friend, or a pastry on the table. Step into the labyrinth, and savor every layer.

📍 Cucu Betutu
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October
⏰ 11 AM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunches

Bagaimana jika sepotong cromboloni bisa membuatmu berpikir tentang hidup? Buku karya Rio Christiawan ini menyusuri momen-momen kecil dan sederhana yang diam-diam membentuk diri kita, perjalanan ke kota lain, secangkir kopi, sebuah emoji, sebuah pertemanan, sebuah patah hati, dan mengubahnya menjadi undangan untuk berhenti sejenak dan merenung. Cromboloni menjadi metafora utamanya: lapis demi lapis, manis dan renyah, tidak pernah sesederhana yang terlihat, sama seperti hidup itu sendiri, tersusun dari pengalaman, kegagalan, kehilangan, dan kejutan-kejutan kecil yang membentuk siapa diri kita. 

Buku ini tidak akan menjadikanmu seorang filsuf. Ia hanya mengajakmu untuk berhenti sejenak, memperhatikan, dan berpikir ulang, sebab filsafat bersembunyi bukan di ruang kuliah, melainkan dalam secangkir kopi, sebuah pesan dari sahabat, atau sepotong cromboloni di atas meja. Masuklah ke dalam labirin, dan nikmati setiap lapisnya.

This Festival anthology, Stories From the Islands, brings together ten emerging Indonesian writers, selected through its 2026 Emerging Writers Programme, exploring lives suspended between inheritance and change across Indonesia’s thousands of islands. 

A grandmother’s folktales echo through generations; ancient myths linger in the shadows of modern life; love bends beneath the weight of custom; women challenge expectations placed on their bodies and futures; young people leave home only to find that distance cannot silence where they came from. Rich in local culture yet deeply universal, it reveals Indonesia not as a single narrative, but as a constellation of voices illuminating belonging, identity, and change.

📍 Indus Restaurant
🗓️ Friday, 23 October
⏰ 5.45 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist

Antologi festival ini, Stories From the Islands, menghimpun sepuluh penulis muda Indonesia, terpilih melalui Program Penulis Muda 2026, mengeksplorasi kehidupan yang terjebak di antara warisan dan perubahan di seluruh ribuan pulau Indonesia. 

Dongeng-dongeng nenek terus bergema lintas generasi; mitos-mitos kuno bertahan di balik bayang-bayang kehidupan modern; cinta melengkung di bawah beban adat; perempuan menantang ekspektasi yang dibebankan pada tubuh dan masa depan mereka; anak-anak muda meninggalkan kampung halaman hanya untuk menyadari bahwa jarak tak mampu membungkam suara asal mereka. Kaya akan budaya lokal namun sangat universal, buku ini mengungkap Indonesia bukan sebagai satu narasi tunggal, melainkan sebagai konstelasi suara yang menerangi makna keberadaan, identitas, dan perubahan.

Todo parece indicar que el último sábado del año lloverá en Jerez de la Frontera. Pero eso no es ningún problema para nosotros, ya que @labodegaskate cuenta con más de 2000 metros cuadrados de espacio para montar dos escenarios. Todo sigue igual, e incluso puede que haya más ambiente si cabe. Así que, si no tienes tu entrada, ve ya a por ella y allí nos vemos.

Gracias a todos nuestros patrocinadores en especial a la Delegación de Juventud del Ayuntamiento de Jerez.

This book follows Munin, a former political prisoner, who runs Blitar Magic Garage in Setiabudi, a makeshift settlement in central Jakarta. When whispers of redevelopment threaten the fragile balance of the neighbourhood, Munin and his neighbours are forced to confront a dark web of corruption, greed and political manoeuvring, their alliances strained as they grapple with their pasts and futures in an effort to defend the kampung against developers and the army. 

Will Suharto’s relentless vision of progress overshadow the dreams of Soekarno’s little people? As Munin repairs cars belonging to Jakarta’s elite with magic, spirit warnings suggest that trouble is brewing, whether from the land clearance, or something more sinister.

Buku ini mengikuti kisah Munin, mantan tahanan politik, yang menjalankan Blitar Magic Garage di Setiabudi, sebuah permukiman darurat di tengah Jakarta. Ketika desas-desus penggusuran mengancam keseimbangan rapuh lingkungan tersebut, Munin dan para tetangganya terpaksa menghadapi jaringan gelap korupsi, keserakahan, dan manuver politik, dengan aliansi mereka yang goyah saat mereka bergulat dengan masa lalu dan masa depan mereka dalam upaya mempertahankan kampung dari para pengembang dan militer. 

Akankah visi kemajuan tanpa henti ala Suharto mengalahkan impian rakyat kecil ala Soekarno? Sementara Munin memperbaiki mobil-mobil milik kalangan elite Jakarta dengan sihir, pertanda gaib mengisyaratkan bahwa ada bahaya yang mengintai, entah dari penggusuran lahan, atau sesuatu yang lebih gelap.

Broken Horses is an epic and personal story of female agency, set in the remote colonial world of 1920s Southern Patagonia. 

Georgie Carruthers breaks off her engagement with her wounded fiancé in the aftermath of the Great War, and racked with guilt, crosses the ocean to take up a post as governess to a motherless boy for the Creeds, a wealthy estancia family consumed by colonial expectations. Raul, a horse breaker, captures Georgie’s heart with his warmth and wisdom, while Mr Creed considers her a useful second wife, an unexpected love triangle that subverts narrative expectations and breaks into a world of politics. In the background, rebellion by the estancia workers intensifies as landowners, in terror of a Russian-style revolution, plan brutal reprisals.

⏰ 2.30 PM

Broken Horses adalah kisah epik dan personal tentang keberanian perempuan, berlatar dunia kolonial terpencil di Patagonia Selatan pada tahun 1920-an. 

Georgie Carruthers memutuskan pertunangannya dengan tunangannya yang terluka setelah Perang Besar, dan dilanda rasa bersalah, ia menyeberangi lautan untuk menjadi pengasuh seorang anak laki-laki yang kehilangan ibunya, bekerja untuk keluarga Creed, sebuah keluarga estansia kaya yang terikat kuat pada ekspektasi kolonial. Raul, seorang penjinak kuda, memikat hati Georgie dengan kehangatan dan kebijaksanaannya, sementara Tuan Creed menganggapnya sebagai calon istri kedua yang berguna, sebuah segitiga cinta tak terduga yang mematahkan ekspektasi narasi dan memasuki dunia politik. Di latar belakang, pemberontakan para pekerja estansia semakin memuncak seiring para tuan tanah, yang diliputi ketakutan akan revolusi bergaya Rusia, merencanakan pembalasan yang brutal.

In an era of data and information overload, this huge amount of information can either overwhelm us or offer valuable insights to support our decision-making. Drawing on the author’s academic and professional experience of over ten years working with data, this book offers an insightful look at our world today through the lens of data patterns. 

It explores strategic issues including poverty, education and health systems, climate change and planetary resilience, and corruption and governance, and their implications. It invites readers to see how transforming data into wisdom, followed by data-informed action, especially when making decisions that shape the course of a society, a nation and humanity, can lead to a better world.

This book follows two sisters from one of Jakarta’s most powerful Chinese-Indonesian dynasties, and the night that tears their family apart. At their grandfather’s lavish birthday celebration, Estella poisons every guest, and only her younger sister Gwendolyn survives. 

Drifting between consciousness and memory in a hospital bed, Gwendolyn pieces together the life they shared: her fierce bond with Estella, Aunt Sandra’s unexplained disappearance, and the grand mansion where tycoon Irwan Sulinado’s family hid its deepest secrets, secrets rooted in the fear that gripped Chinese-Indonesian families in 1998. Like the monarch butterflies the sisters once watched together, the truth must break open before it can finally take flight.

What if the most profound experience of a lifetime is already waiting to be found, simply forgotten along the way? This book follows one regular guy turned Balinese Hindu priest as he traces his journey from a single inexplicable moment on a Berkeley beach at age twenty to a life of deep, daily bliss. 

Part soul-stirring spiritual memoir, part practical guide, it draws on decades of searching across continents, cultures and traditions to offer a refreshingly honest, sometimes out-there invitation to stop settling for ordinary happiness. Through gratitude, self-discovery and ancient Vedic wisdom, it gently challenges what spirituality is supposed to look like, and opens doorways that can be walked through in one’s own way, at one’s own pace.

ABOUT LISA CAHILL⁠
Lisa Cahill is known internationally for her kiln-formed glass sculptures and installations including numerous public art commissions. After graduating from Monash University, Victoria in 2000 she has been an independent studio artist for 19 years having established glass studios in Melbourne, Sydney and now Canberra.⁠

Cahill’s glass installations create a discourse about the Australian landscape and her affinity with it, often entwined with her Danish heritage. THANK YOU | Launch + Artist Talk | Fallen Leaves by Rebecca Selleck @becselleck⁠
.⁠
Thank you to everyone who joined us for the launch of Fallen Leaves by Rebecca Selleck at Namadgi Visitor Centre on Saturday 6 December 2025.⁠
.⁠
ABOUT THE ARTWORK⁠
Fallen Leaves was commissioned by Craft + Design Canberra in partnership with ACT Parks and Conservation @actparks. This site-specific artwork by Canberra-based artists Rebecca Selleck, responds to the theme 'Fire in the Landscape’ and is a reflection on the evolving impact of climate change and the increasing severity of weather events in the ACT region. ⁠
.⁠
ARTWORK STATEMENT⁠
The Orroral Valley bushfire was so big and close we could see it from our backyard. I had my newborn in my arms. I could feel the thousands of choked breaths and splintering of great limbs as ecosystems collapsed. I was scared for my child’s future. For all our kids’ futures. ⁠
.⁠
The land wasn’t recognisable. The fires were so hot they destroyed too much. But still the charred eucalypts shot out their epicormic growth. Along with other devastating fires around Australia, the Orroral Valley fire was the catalyst for intensifying conversations across the country around climate change and human impact. ⁠
.⁠
For those of us who choose to remember, we go on with sorrow in our hearts and hope for the future. This artwork is a reminder. On a granite boulder, a child lays, tenderly touching the hand of a kangaroo joey. These figures are both at rest, facing towards Mount Tennent. Curved over them is the blackened bronze form of a burnt young eucalypt still in the act of sheltering, and below their young leaves form a glistening bed. ⁠
.⁠

Come find us this weekend @darwinartfair stall 64 🧡

Join us on Larrakia Country this August 6-9, where our Art Centre will once again be part of the annual Darwin Aboriginal Art Fair (aka DAAF), Australia’s largest Indigenous Art Fair. This is an action packed week you won’t want to miss - celebrating strong Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art, design and culture.

We’ll be joined by over 75 fellow First Nations Art Centres from right across the country, selling exclusive pieces that you won’t find anywhere else. Drop by for a yarn and meet the artists, hear the stories behind the work, get involved in a workshop, enjoy a cultural dance performance, look through some incredible artworks - and pick yourself up something special!
DAAF is grounded in community and culture, with First Nations Art Centres and ethical practice at the heart of the event. It remains FREE to attend from Friday to Sunday, with 100% of all art sales going directly back to the Art Centres, our artists and communities. 

See you there! 🌞

When: 6-9 August, 2026
Where: Darwin Convention Centre, NT and online
For more, head to: WWW.DAAF.COM.AU and follow @darwinartfair (@darwinaboriginalartfair on FB) for all the updates.

📷 Arts worker Chantelle Wunungmurra and managers Trevor Van Weeren and Gioia Johnson 

If you can’t make it in person we will also have Artworks available on the DAAF online portal….

This is the story of eight-year-old Jia, who, on a rainy afternoon at her grandfather’s home, discovers a weathered family journal filled with stories written by her elders. 

As she turns its pages, she meets a great-grandmother’s needlecraft, a Wowa’s thriving trade, and a great-grandfather’s tender hopes. Inspired to ask her own questions, Jia begins a new chapter, a tender, magical tale about memory, family and belonging.

📍 Rumah Kayu at Taman Baca Ubud
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October
⏰ 3.45 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunches

Ini adalah kisah Jia yang berusia delapan tahun, yang pada suatu sore yang hujan di rumah kakeknya, menemukan sebuah jurnal keluarga yang lusuh tersimpan di dalam laci tua, penuh dengan kisah-kisah yang ditulis oleh para tetua keluarganya.

Saat ia membuka lembar demi lembar, ia bertemu dengan seorang nenek buyut yang mahir dalam kerajinan tangan, seorang Wowa yang keteguhan imannya membangun usaha dagang yang berkembang pesat, dan seorang kakek buyut yang menuliskan dengan penuh kasih harapannya untuk cucu pertamanya. Terinspirasi untuk menemukan panggilan hidupnya, Jia memulai babak baru, sebuah kisah tentang ingatan, keluarga, dan rasa memiliki.

Kaja and Kelod is as relevant today as it was when first published by Oxford in Asia in 1981, the first book on the subject written by a Balinese author, offering a broad and well-organised perspective as well as the fundamentals and details for both scholars and laymen. It celebrates the eightieth decade of master dance and scholar Prof. I Made Bandem, and salutes the passion of his co-author and close friend, Frederik DeBoer. 

This third luxury edition is more compelling still, with a redesign and updated research that includes new illustrations, information on evolving dance forms, and an expanded introduction by cultural expert Bruce W. Carpenter, co-author of Masks of Bali (2024) with Bandem.

📍 DI SINI DI SANA by Rachman & Sons
🗓️ Thursday, 22 October
⏰ 11 AM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunches

Kaja and Kelod tetap relevan hingga hari ini seperti saat pertama kali diterbitkan oleh Oxford in Asia pada tahun 1981, menjadi buku pertama tentang topik ini yang ditulis oleh penulis asal Bali, menawarkan perspektif yang luas dan tersusun rapi serta dasar-dasar dan detail bagi kalangan akademisi maupun awam. Buku ini merayakan delapan dekade kehidupan maestro tari dan akademisi, Prof. I Made Bandem, sekaligus menghormati dedikasi rekan penulis dan sahabat dekatnya, Frederik DeBoer. 

Edisi mewah ketiga ini tampil lebih memikat dengan desain ulang dan riset terbaru yang mencakup ilustrasi baru, informasi tentang perkembangan bentuk-bentuk tari, serta pengantar yang diperluas oleh pakar budaya Bruce W. Carpenter, rekan penulis Masks of Bali (2024) bersama Bandem.

An island. A residency. And stories that have never been told before, coming to #UWRF26.

We are proud to partner with Cempedak Island to bring the Tulisan Nusantara Writers’ Residency to Ubud. On Cempedak Island in Indonesia’s Riau Archipelago, the residency gives writers time and space to turn the sea, wildlife and stories of the region into new work.

Residency lead Ken Kwek and inaugural writer-in-residence Pamela Ng join us across three sessions exploring who gets to tell our stories, and why it matters.

Swipe through to discover the sessions they will appear in, and secure your Festival Pass through the link in our bio.

—

Sebuah pulau. Sebuah residensi. Dan kisah-kisah yang belum pernah diceritakan sebelumnya, hadir di #UWRF26.

Kami dengan bangga bermitra dengan Cempedak Island untuk menghadirkan Tulisan Nusantara Writers’ Residency ke Ubud. Di Pulau Cempedak, Kepulauan Riau, residensi ini memberi para penulis waktu dan ruang untuk mengolah laut, satwa liar, dan kisah-kisah dari kawasan tersebut menjadi karya baru.

Pemimpin residensi Ken Kwek dan penulis residensi perdana Pamela Ng akan bergabung bersama kami dalam tiga sesi yang mengupas siapa yang berhak menceritakan kisah kita, dan mengapa hal itu penting.

Geser untuk melihat sesi-sesi yang akan mereka isi, dan dapatkan Festival Pass kamu melalui tautan di bio kami.

Beyond Sukawati’s famous art market lies a humble world of everyday Balinese life, where local markets and time-honoured recipes tell stories of generations past. Join us to taste crispy kerupuk tahu, learn the craft of tofu-making, savour lawar and jaja gambir, then enjoy iconic nasi tahu at Men Sarti before fresh coconut water at Artisan Village.

➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26CulturalWorkshops

Di balik pasar seni Sukawati yang terkenal, tersimpan dunia kehidupan sehari-hari masyarakat Bali yang sederhana, tempat pasar-pasar lokal, dapur tradisional, dan resep turun-temurun menyimpan kisah dari generasi ke generasi. Perjalanan kuliner ini dimulai dengan kerupuk tahu yang renyah di pasar lokal, sebelum mengajakmu melihat langsung proses tradisional pembuatan tahu, cicipi lawar serta jaja gambir, sebelum akhirnya menikmati nasi tahu khas di Men Sarti. DAY SIX OF CRAFTMAS | Join us as we continue celebrating local makers this festive season, including Ceramicist Margaret Brown @margaret.brown.427⁠
.⁠
Our Day Six feature is Margaret Brown, whose handcrafted ceramic pieces bring warmth and soul into everyday moments.⁠
.⁠
ABOUT MARGARET BROWN⁠
Working from her quiet studio in the Bega Valley in New South Wales, local ceramicist Margaret Brown crafts and designs a prolific array of domestic delights.⁠
.⁠
Brown is drawn to the medium of porcelain for its purity and translucency. These unique qualities allow her works breathe a sense of easiness into daily living through each mug, beaker, and bowl. Through her domestic vessels, she combines function with aesthetic.⁠
.⁠
No two pieces of Brown’s making are the same, each carries a unique character bestowed upon it through careful handcrafting by the artist. Brown porcelain forms are created through the Japanese technique of nerikomi, a thoughtful and time-consuming practice. The skillful patterns in her works have been created by hand-combining slices of porcelain of varying colours together. This process allows her to form purposefully coloured designs.⁠
.⁠
Brown completed a Diploma in Visual Arts (Ceramics) at the Australian National University School of Art and received a Technical award upon completion of the course. ⁠
.⁠

Fly Ranch is Burning Man’s living laboratory — a rural center for interactive arts, community participation, and land stewardship. You are invited to visit. Join a nature walk, explore the art, and taste the honey and vegetables from the garden.

On Saturday September 26th from 1 PM to 8 PM Fly Ranch will be hosting an open house: a relaxed day to bike, walk, soak, and connect with the land. Wander the Hualapai Flat and take in art pieces steeped in Burning Man history, including a chance to bike across the open playa where the Man burned in 1997. Make your way to the geothermal pools for a soak. Wrap up with a garden tour taste of what the land gives: honey from the bees, a pickled bite from the garden, and tea brewed from herbs grown right on site.

Debbie Argue’s book on her research about Homo Floresiensis or Flores Man. Archaic tiny humans that lived on the Indonesian island of Flores over 50,000 years ago. I was in Flores at the beginning of the year. It is an endless stretch of thick tropical forest. Based on human evolutionary lineage, Flores Man should not have been found on the island for Flores was never connected to mainland Asia. Argue discusses all possible theories. I nerded out!

Translated from Arabic, Lives in Pomegranate by Ali Al Shaali are short stories that delve between ecological collapse and cultural erosion that shape the lives of humans across the globe. Dark secrets to catastrophe-struck futures, one navigates through themes of identity, survival and loss.

Minor Detail by Adania Shibli is about the gang rape and murder of a Bedouin Palestinian girl by Izz soldiers in the Negev desert. Shibli then narrates a fictional investigation by a journalist who vows to find out what happened to the girl so the story is not forgotten. Endless and often unsuspected dispossession.

A Splintering by Dur e Aziz Amna is a bold book about a working class woman who rises from village to city girl while fighting patriarchal systems in Pakistan. Dealing with class, power, money, the main character is an amalgam of all things taboo in a conservative society yet demands empathy from the reader. The book takes a wild turn half way — I was not expecting it. A must read!

Michael Shaikh is a human rights activist and this book is his experience with travel and food as a journalist across war-torn borders and countries. What gets lost in the face of war? The food we eat and its ingredients and it strikes the autonomy of women,

Big, bold, dramatic, perhaps even thought provoking... 💭
This week's Honoraria feature large scale installations that invite your participatory presence. For a complete look at this year's art browse the full list of 2026 Honoraria artists. 🔗 in bio

"Notorious BIG Spinning Wheels" offers meditation, mesmerization, and whimsy through monumental spinning sculptures.
"Axis Mundi: Resonant Spire" rises from the desert as a 33-foot wooden tower of ever-evolving audiovisual interaction, translating participant voices in both sound and light.
"Aetheric Ascension Tower" carves the silhouettes of human souls into a cone piercing the sky from its roots in the earth.
"Elemental Dragon" emerges as a fractal wooden sculpture, inviting every observer to meet and co-create the mythical creature in collective imagination.
"LOOKOUT!" is a 48-foot fire extinguisher lookout tower, asking us to reckon with the scorching state of our world.
"Above and Below" reminds us of the artistic desire to cultivate spaces of adventure and connectivity in our homes through a beanstalk structure, suspending a glowing Victorian cottage 40 feet in the air.

Forty years ago on the solstice, friends gathered to burn a Man on a San Francisco Beach. In 1990 Burning Man founds its home on a vast lakebed, the Black Rock Desert.
An ephemeral city emerged, a nexus of Communal Effort and Radical Self-expression now 70,000 strong. Today around the world, Burning Man inspires more than a million people to live more creative, connected lives.

Burning Man is fueled by YOU. What will you create in the next 40 years?

If you thrive on the grit, the dust, and the beautiful chaos of building a city from scratch in the open desert, you belong with the Department of Public Works (DPW).

DPW is the backbone of Black Rock City. Ask any crew member — the experience IS the reward. You’re working hard alongside some of the most interesting people you’ll ever meet and playing hard when the shift ends like you’ve earned it. As a DPW member, you get to live the version of Burning Man that most people never get to see. It’s a golden ticket to the carnival, paid for in heart and sweat. 

> Choose your Adventure <
The DPW Roustabouts: Go where the work is! we need skilled hands — and those who want to become skilled — to help build the city. Commitments vary from 2-9 weeks and yes, your ticket and meals are part of the reward. 

DPW Crews: Not everyone wields hammers out there. DPW needs fuel attendants, dispatchers, drivers, LNT support, data trackers, and even some paid managerial roles and heavy equipment operators! There are many ways to contribute to building a city out of nothing.

Are you ready to join this dusty carny crew?

When the balance of power is distorted, Francesca Albanese speaks for the rights of Palestinians.

An international lawyer, scholar, and UN Special Rapporteur on the human rights situation in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967. Through rigorous legal analysis and fearless advocacy, she makes the case that a just future requires ending the genocide, the unlawful occupation, and apartheid, so that Palestinians and Israelis alike can live in freedom, dignity, and peace under international law.

Albanese knows that action means saying the hard thing plainly, and saying it again.

What’s the question you would want Albanese to answer, live?

🔗 Join us this October. More details in bio.

Ketika keseimbangan kekuasaan terdistorsi, Francesca Albanese menyuarakan hak-hak rakyat Palestina.

Seorang pengacara internasional, akademisi, dan Pelapor Khusus PBB untuk situasi hak asasi manusia di wilayah Palestina yang diduduki sejak 1967. Melalui analisis hukum yang cermat dan advokasi yang tanpa kompromi, ia berargumen bahwa masa depan yang adil memerlukan diakhirinya genosida, pendudukan ilegal, dan apartheid, agar rakyat Palestina dan Israel dapat hidup dalam kebebasan, martabat, dan perdamaian di bawah hukum internasional.

Albanese percaya bahwa aksi berarti mengatakan hal yang sulit dengan jelas, dan mengatakannya lagi.

Apa pertanyaan yang ingin Anda dengar dijawab langsung oleh Albanese?

Overlooking a bamboo jungle, the beloved Casa Luna long table lunch returns, asking Rumi's own question: are we mortal or divine, flesh or flame? In the kitchen, Sanjoy Roy is cooking up an Indian feast, slow-braised favourites, flatbreads and sambals mingling with fragrant curries and spice, alongside Casa Luna's legendary specialities. 

At the table, eight writers each bring something written in their pocket, a confession, an argument, a small act of defiance, to lay beside the dishes.

📍 Casa Luna
🗓️ Sunday, 25 October
⏰ 12 PM
🎟️ IDR 650,000
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26SpecialEvents

Menghadap hutan bambu, jamuan meja panjang Casa Luna yang legendaris kembali digelar, mengajukan pertanyaan Rumi sendiri: apakah kita fana atau ilahi, daging atau nyala api? Di dapur, Sanjoy Roy sedang meracik jamuan khas India, hidangan favorit yang dimasak perlahan, roti pipih, dan sambal berpadu dengan kari harum dan rempah, menyatu dengan hidangan khas legendaris Casa Luna. 

Di meja itu, delapan penulis masing-masing membawa sesuatu yang tertulis dalam saku mereka, sebuah pengakuan, sebuah argumen, sebuah tindakan kecil perlawanan, untuk diletakkan di samping hidangan.

Our Weapons Are Traditional Ceremonies brings together the voices of five Nausus, women long marginalised for their traditional knowledge, fighting for their homelands and standing on the front lines against environmental destruction and the seizure of communities’ living spaces, while working to restore nature. 

From the Mollo rock mountains protected by Mama Aleta, to the sorghum gardens pioneered by Maria Loretha in Adonara; from Sangihe Island defended by Jull Takaliuang, to the forests of Mount Kerasik protected by Mardiana, and the Kendeng mountains called upon to join Gunarti’s struggle through prayer and symbols connecting body and nature. 

This book grew out of a process of harvesting knowledge, uncovering wisdom embedded in memory, the body, and lived practices, expressed by the women themselves in their own words. Here, symbols and mantras become women’s cultural weapons for nurturing life, protecting food biodiversity, sowing hope, and carrying resistance forward.

Moderated by Olin Monteiro

📍 Threads of Life
🗓️ Friday, 23 October
⏰ 1 PM
🎟️ Register via tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunchRegist
➡️ Learn more tinyurl.com/UWRF26BookLaunches

Senjata Kami adalah Upacara Adat menghadirkan suara lima Nausus, perempuan yang lama terpinggirkan karena pengetahuan tradisional mereka, berjuang demi tanah air mereka dan berdiri di garis depan melawan perusakan lingkungan dan perampasan ruang hidup masyarakat, sambil bekerja memulihkan alam. 

Dari gunung batu Mollo yang dilindungi Mama Aleta, hingga kebun sorgum yang dirintis Maria Loretha di Adonara; dari Pulau Sangihe yang dibela Jull Takaliuang, hingga hutan Gunung Kerasik yang dijaga Mardiana, dan pegunungan Kendeng yang memanggil untuk ikut berjuang bersama Gunarti melalui doa dan simbol yang menghubungkan tubuh dengan alam. 

Buku ini lahir dari proses memanen pengetahuan, menggali kebijaksanaan yang tertanam dalam ingatan, tubuh, dan laku hidup, diungkapkan oleh para perempuan itu sendiri dalam kata-kata mereka. Di sini, simbol dan mantra menjadi senjata budaya perempuan untuk merawat kehidupan, melindungi keragaman hayati pangan, menyemai harapan, dan meneruskan perlawanan.

Moderator: Olin Monteiro

This is the story of Laura, a young woman from Florence who, like so many dreamers of her generation, travels to the heart of Africa in search of an authentic life, far from the hypocrisies of the modern world. There she meets Laconi, a young Indonesian dressed like a prince, with piercing eyes that belong to the wild, and together they begin a journey that will change everything. 

Years later, their daughter Geia sets out to understand her origins, a journey of memory and reconciliation leading her back to her father’s world and an ancestral lineage said to descend from tigers. This is the true story of a woman who rediscovers her identity through her father and her past, a portrait of a generation that dreamed of changing the world.

Ini adalah kisah Laura, seorang perempuan muda dari Florence yang, seperti begitu banyak pemimpi di generasinya, melakukan perjalanan ke jantung Afrika untuk mencari kehidupan yang autentik, jauh dari kemunafikan dunia modern. Di sana ia bertemu Laconi, seorang pemuda Indonesia yang berpenampilan bak pangeran, dengan tatapan mata setajam alam liar, dan bersama-sama mereka memulai perjalanan yang akan mengubah segalanya. 

Bertahun-tahun kemudian, putri mereka, Geia, memulai pencarian untuk memahami asal-usulnya, sebuah perjalanan penuh kenangan dan rekonsiliasi yang membawanya kembali ke dunia ayahnya dan garis keturunan leluhur yang dipercaya berasal dari harimau. Ini adalah kisah nyata seorang perempuan yang menemukan kembali jati dirinya melalui ayah dan masa lalunya, sebuah potret generasi yang bermimpi mengubah dunia.

Three days that felt like a fairytale, like stepping into a world where people were fully expressing themselves.

Dance everywhere.
Bodies moving freely.

Letting go through movement, freedom of expression and real connection.
Meeting new people, coming together in community, sharing presence.

The workshops were pure magic. I dove into belly dance, cacao ceremonies and breathwork, each one opening new layers. 💃🏽🍫

And it was so beautiful to simply look around.
People in costumes, colors, fairies, feathers, glitter, fully living their best and most authentic versions.
Freedom felt contagious!

May our daily lifes also feels like festival where we are free to be :)

This book opens with a fragile, thousand-year peace between dragons and leviathans now faltering, as the leviathan queen challenges the dragons’ dynastic supremacy, fomenting unrest and dealing with dark forces, while Black Corruption, an oozing shadow not seen since the Cataclysmic War, spreads once more across the land. The omen is clear: a being capable of destroying the world will soon rise. 

Amid this conflict, a young dragon prince burned by Corruption ventures out in search of the strength to overcome the evil growing within him, his journey intersecting with a lovestruck leviathan, a colourful band of mercenaries, and a human commoner with a mysterious connection to the ancient past, their interwoven fates deciding whether their world endures or falls into oblivion.

Buku ini dibuka dengan perdamaian rapuh selama seribu tahun antara para naga dan leviathan yang kini mulai goyah, ketika sang ratu leviathan menantang supremasi dinasti para naga, memicu kerusuhan dan menjalin hubungan dengan kekuatan gelap, sementara Korupsi Hitam, bayangan pekat yang belum pernah terlihat sejak Perang Kataklismik, kembali menyebar ke seluruh negeri. Pertanda sudah jelas: makhluk yang mampu menghancurkan dunia akan segera bangkit. 

Di tengah konflik ini, seorang pangeran naga muda yang terbakar oleh Korupsi memulai perjalanan mencari kekuatan untuk mengalahkan kejahatan yang tumbuh dalam dirinya, perjalanan yang mempertemukannya dengan seekor leviathan yang dimabuk cinta, sekelompok tentara bayaran yang penuh warna, dan seorang manusia biasa dengan hubungan misterius terhadap masa lalu kuno, takdir mereka yang saling terjalin akan menentukan apakah dunia mereka akan bertahan atau jatuh ke dalam kehancuran.

The sage Wisrawa’s forbidden passion for Princess Sukesi unleashes a cosmic imbalance, the origin of all human suffering. At the heart of this Javanese retelling of the Ramayana stands Anak Bajang, a misshapen dwarf child who restores balance through innocence and sincerity, herding the wind in search of meaning. A visionary epic where gods test mortals and beauty turns to ruin.

This tribute honours the poetry of Sitor Situmorang, one of Indonesia’s great poets. A bilingual selection, in Indonesian and English, translated and annotated by Prof. Harry Aveling, brings Sitor’s voice to English-speaking readers while celebrating the craft and difficulty of translating poetry. 

Join Warih Wisatsana, who speaks about the man, the writer and his poetry, and John McGlynn, who introduces Sitor to a wider audience. The launch also introduces the Sitor Situmorang Award for a promising young Indonesian writer, with 2026 Awardee Arianto Adipurwanto.

Persembahan penghormatan ini mengangkat puisi Sitor Situmorang, salah satu penyair besar Indonesia. Kumpulan puisi pilihan dalam bahasa Indonesia dan Inggris, yang diterjemahkan dan diberi anotasi oleh Prof. Harry Aveling, memperkenalkan suara Sitor kepada pembaca berbahasa Inggris sekaligus merayakan seni dan tantangan menerjemahkan puisi. 

Hadirlah bersama Warih Wisatsana, yang akan berbicara tentang sosok, penulis, dan puisi-puisinya, serta John McGlynn, yang akan memperkenalkan Sitor kepada khalayak yang lebih luas. Peluncuran ini juga memperkenalkan Penghargaan Sitor Situmorang untuk penulis muda Indonesia yang menjanjikan, dengan penerima penghargaan 2026, Arianto Adipurwanto.

スイスデザインを象徴するUSMが60年にわたり生産し続けているUSMハラーは、タイムレスなモジュラー家具システムの代名詞となっています。そのデザイン哲学は、流行に左右されることなく、あらゆる世代のニーズに適応しながら常に進化してきました。USMハラーは、遊び心にあふれた無限の可能性を秘めており、世界中でさまざまクリエイティブなインスピレーションを与えています。

USMは2025年ミラノデザインウィークでのインスタレーションにてテキスタイル製の新製品「USM ハラーソフトパネル」を発表。モジュール性、機能性、USMが60年以上にわたり培ってきた価値観を表現するプロダクトで3種類のサイズ、 3種類のパターン、10色のカラーバリエーションで展開されます。マグネット仕様により、組み立て作業や追加の固定具なしで、開閉、スライド、位置替えが簡単に行えるため、新しいデザインの可能性が広がります。

この度USM東京ショールームでは、その革新的なオプションの機能性とデザインを紹介します。

USM will unveil its new textile product, the USM Haller Soft Panel, at an installation during Milan Design Week 2025. The product, which embodies modularity and functionality, values USM has cultivated for over 60 years, will be available in three sizes, three patterns, and ten color variations. Its magnetic design allows it to be easily opened, closed, slid, and repositioned without the need for assembly or additional fasteners, opening up new design possibilities.
The USM Tokyo showroom will be showcasing the functionality and design of this innovative option.

街の風景をモチーフにした「情景 -scene (or memory)-」を発表します。街中のありふれた風景は無意識に個々の日常や人生と密接に結びついています。毎日歩く夜の帰り道、何気なく眺めていた窓、無意識に触っていた壁の凹凸。そんな風景から生じる些細な現象を丁寧に再構築することで、私たちの記憶の片隅にある情景を拾い上げます。

JOKEI -scene (or memory)- is a work inspired by the everyday scenery of the city.
Such ordinary cityscapes are unconsciously intertwined with each individual’s daily life and personal history.
The road home walked at night, the window casually glanced at, the uneven wall surface touched without awareness.
By carefully reconstructing the subtle phenomena that emerge from such scenes, JOKEI -scene (or memory)- picks up the fragments of scenery that linger quietly in the corners of memory.

Pyro PLA Project is a product series that utilizes textures created by directly heating the surface of 3D-printed objects with an open flame, melting and blending the layered traces. それは一見ただの散水ホースですが、内部に樹脂を流し込み硬化させたものです。ホースの弾力と重力の釣り合いが偶然に生み出す何気ない曲線を、カメラが一瞬を切り取るように固定化しています。そこには、偶然と必然、一瞬と永遠、一点物と量産品、重力と反重力、機能と装飾、創造と模範、日常と芸術といった一見相反する概念が同時に現れます。こうした曲線をNIESSINGのジュエリーが展示される空間にそっと紛れ込ませることで、バウハウスの思想から大きな影響を受けたNIESSINGのデザインをあらためて見つめ直し、その理解を深めるきっかけを作れればと考えています。

At first glance, it appears to be an ordinary garden hose, but it has been filled with resin and hardened from within. The subtle curves that arise by chance from the balance between the hose’s elasticity and gravity are fixed as if captured by a camera in a fleeting moment. Here, seemingly opposing concepts—chance and necessity, the momentary and the eternal, unique pieces and mass production, gravity and anti-gravity, function and ornament, creation and model, the everyday and art—appear simultaneously. By subtly weaving these curves into the space where NIESSING jewelry is displayed, we aim to offer a renewed perspective on NIESSING　design, which has been profoundly influenced by Bauhaus principles, and to deepen understanding of it.

世界に遍在しているCCTVカメラの映像を、ネットワークを使って時間と空間を整理して見てみること、それは、衛星から見る地球の姿とは違った、新しい地球の今の姿を捉えられるのではないだろうか。頭の中にある、統一感のある地球のイメージと、地表の複眼的な視点で捉えた世界とは、どのような共通点やズレがあるのだろうか。
インターネット上に公開されている世界中のライブカメラの映像をつなげることによって地球が動いていること（夜明けから日暮れへと変化していく影や景色）をあらためて認識し、宇宙ステーションや人工衛星のような外部からの視線とは違い、内部からの様々な複眼的視線で地球の変化をとらえた映像によって、見知らぬ場所の日常の光景、それらの離散的な情報の中から様々な欲望、それらのレイヤの変化、ズレが可視化される。
実際には行くことができないその場所を、カメラという「窓」を通して見ることにより、今この地球上に暮らす私たち・世界の人々とのつながりをも感じることができればと考えます。

A public artwork on the theme of “Liberation of vision” in the entrance lobby on the first floor. This work was created by Dumb Type, a progressive art collective that held an exhibition at the Artizon Museum in 2023, featuring their works from the International Art Exhibition, La Biennale di Venezia. A collection of publicly available live images from live cameras around the world is combined and displayed as if it were a single window, offering a sense of connection to the outside world even while inside the building. The unconventional perspective and shift in point of view encourage business people to change their mindset and behavior. This is the first public art piece by Dumb Type.

Dance of Darkness brings the haunting, rare art of Butoh to Browns Mart, transforming the space into a living, breathing stage. Born from the trauma of post-Hiroshima Japan, Butoh is a form of resistance, a poetry of the body, a language of what cannot be spoken. In Darwin, where this art is rarely seen, the performance becomes both mirror and pulse: reflecting the political, social, and economic pressures shaping local lives, and giving them shape through slow, explosive, visceral movement.

Created in situ with regional artists, Dance of Darkness amplifies voices often absent from mainstream stages, weaving stories of resilience, identity, and survival into every gesture. The performers inhabit the textures and atmospheres of Browns Mart, allowing the building itself to become part of the work’s memory and emotion.

This workshop is about what comes after the festival, taking your encounters with unfamiliar histories, voices, geographies and ways of seeing the world, and turning them into something lasting. We leave full of ideas and highlighted books, but in a world of constant information, how do we actually make sense of it all? Through guided writing, participants work through two questions: how do we let stories reshape the way we see the world, and who have we become because of this festival? One encounter from the festival becomes the starting point, carried through stages of awareness, perspective and personal meaning. 

The workshop is facilitated by four leading Modern Women in Bali writers, each guiding one stage of the journey before the group comes together for a collective reflection. These reflections form a living archive of how literature and human encounter continue to transform people, and participants leave with both a personal piece of writing and a shared, collective narrative.

Price includes a welcome drink and snacks.

One month to go until #UWRF26, and this September belongs to the ten finalists of this year’s Emerging Writers Programme.

Every Wednesday this month, our Shelfmates on Discord will meet these writers live, ahead of their appearance at #UWRF26 this October. Expect real conversations: their stories, their ideas, the worlds they are building.

Chosen from 634 submissions by writers across Indonesia, from Aceh to Papua, these ten made it through a curatorial process built to spotlight new voices and fresh perspectives in Indonesian literature. Their short stories dig into the many layers of contemporary Indonesia: local issues, social relations, history, and life in a digital society. These stories will be published in the Festival Anthology by Penguin Random House SEA.

The sessions are free to join. Registration details and important links to join our Discord community are available here: bit.ly/Meet-EmergingWriters

gekitetz Inc. は「void reconstruct (ykgw); / ヴォイド リコンストラクト(ヨコガワ);」と題しフィールドワークによって採取した環境音を可視化したインスタレーションを行います。サウンドから浮かび上がる街の輪郭を再構築し、人とまちの関係性や情緒的な風景を探ります。

本作は、2024年に広島県横川エリアでの地方創生プロジェクトの一環として「ARTIST IN RESIDENCE プログラム」に参加し、現地で滞在制作を行ったものです。会場では、このプロジェクトから生まれたヴィジュアライゼーションによる作品を中心に、株式会社歴清社とのコラボレーションによる、その図像をアーカイブし金銀箔紙を活用した、デジタル技術と伝統工芸の融合による平面作品展示も行います。

gekitetz Inc. presents void reconstruct (ykgw), a work that visualizes environmental sounds collected through fieldwork. By reconstructing the contours of a city revealed through sound, the relationships and emotional landscapes between people and their urban surroundings are explored. This presentation, part of a regional revitalization project, was created during “THE ARTIST IN RESIDENCE” program in the Yokogawa area in Hiroshima in 2024. It is centered on a sound visualization installation collected  from this residency. Alongside of this installation, graphic works archiving the visualized imagery are on display. Recording sound and preserving its archive - this is where a new dialogue with the  city begins.

Free art, in this economy? Yes, at Sydney Contemporary!

As part of this year’s Installations program, Sydney Contemporary celebrates pioneering pop and conceptual artist Billy Apple® (1935–2021) with a new edition of his BILLY APPLE ART FREE FOR THE TAKING print.

The print is one of three Billy Apple® projects appearing at Carriageworks this September, continuing the artist’s enduring exploration of how art is made, valued, bought, sold and circulated.

Take home a Billy Apple® print at Sydney Contemporary, taking place 3-6 September at Carriageworks.

Billy Apple is represented by 1031SW | STARKWHITE. Installations is curated by José Da Silva.

This August, we celebrated the women whose stories cross borders and find new life in other languages.

For Women in Translation Month, we shine a light on women writers and the translators who carry their words across languages and cultures, opening their work to new readers and new ways of seeing the world.

Today, on the final day of the month, we celebrate the translators, editors, and advocates who make these crossings possible, often behind the scenes and with little recognition for the skill, care, and creativity they bring to the work.

Here is a selection of women whose skilful translations help stories travel further, reaching readers and places far beyond their original language.

—

Agustus ini, kami merayakan perempuan-perempuan yang kisahnya melintasi batas dan menemukan kehidupan baru dalam bahasa-bahasa lain.

Dalam rangka Women in Translation Month, kami menyoroti para penulis perempuan dan penerjemah yang membawa karya mereka melintasi bahasa dan budaya, mempertemukannya dengan pembaca baru dan membuka cara-cara baru dalam memandang dunia.

Hari ini, di penghujung bulan, kami merayakan para penerjemah, editor, dan mereka yang terus memperjuangkan karya-karya ini, yang memungkinkan perjalanan lintas bahasa tersebut terjadi. Sering kali bekerja di balik layar dan tanpa banyak pengakuan, mereka menghadirkan keterampilan, kepedulian, dan kreativitas yang begitu penting dalam proses ini.

Berikut adalah pilihan perempuan-perempuan yang melalui terjemahan yang terampil, membantu karya-karya para penulis menjangkau lebih jauh, hingga menemukan pembaca dan tempat-tempat yang jauh dari bahasa asalnya.

Built up, erased and built again, Luke Brennan’s paintings carry the traces of their own making.

The Sydney-based artist works through repeated cycles of creation and removal, producing layered, relic-like surfaces that sit between the organic and artificial, microscopic and lunar, sublime and degraded. Drawing on entropy and decay, the works resist a single reading, appearing at once ancient, otherworldly and strangely familiar.

See Luke Brennan presented by LAILA at Sydney Contemporary, 3–6 September at Carriageworks.

At Sydney Contemporary 2026, Five Walls Gallery pairs Australian artist Max Lawrence White with Tokyo-based Shuhei Fukuda for a dialogue in minimalist abstraction through systems, materiality and process.

White's practice uses a random sequence generator to select colour combinations from 210 studio hues, structured within a consistent geometric framework – a balance of chance and control.

Fukuda works with traditional Japanese materials, including washi paper and silver leaf, letting natural oxidation transform the surface over time – blurring the line between painting and object.

Together, the two practices trace complementary paths through abstraction: one built on chance and system, the other on material and time.

See and buy the works at Sydney Contemporary from 3-6 September, Carriageworks. Buy tickets through the link in bio.

Mohammed Massoud Morsi turned his journalism experience in conflict-ridden regions into human and hopeful stories to last forever.

An Egyptian-Danish-Australian photographer, journalist, and writer whose work has been published in all three of his native languages. After discovering that journalism made people yesterday’s news, Morsi turned to writing novels instead, reaching for the heart of existence in a complex world. His photographer’s eye for detail and passion for speaking out for the suppressed, shape a body of work that challenges and breaks common narratives all at once.

Morsi knows that awareness starts with looking for the current you cannot see.

Whose story deserves more than a headline?

O Coquetel Molotov (@noarcm) lançou uma nova coletânea que reúne vozes femininas em ascensão na cena pernambucana. O projeto nasce a partir da Incubadora Musical e apresenta faixas inéditas de Dimitria (@dimitria_______), Renna (@costadarenna), Luísa Cunha (@_luisacunha), Dandara MC (@dandaramc_) e Rayssa Dias (@rayssadias_oficial).

Gravadas em imersão no estúdio Criatório, em Gravatá, as músicas refletem a diversidade estética das artistas — que transitam entre rap, rock, pop, indie e brega — sob produção de IDLibra e mixagem de Benke Ferraz. Além das gravações, o programa também ofereceu mentorias e oficinas, fortalecendo o desenvolvimento artístico e profissional das participantes.

A iniciativa, viabilizada pelo Edital Inova Mulher da Sudene, reforça o compromisso com a valorização de novas vozes femininas na música, criando espaço para experimentação, troca e protagonismo dentro da cena local.

Mais do que uma coletânea, o projeto se consolida como plataforma de impulso para artistas que vêm redefinindo os caminhos da música contemporânea em Pernambuco.

A Pakistani-American writer, composer and performer best known for his raga-pop blockbuster single Pasoori, called by The Guardian UK the biggest song to come out of Pakistan this century, and praised by The New Yorker for its stealthily subversive edge. Drawing on Sufi poetry and Western pop, his recent work includes the Nicolas Jaar-produced album Intiha and his solo debut Love Language.

Sethi knows that action means turning defiant metaphor and music to songs that everyone will sing.

Ali AlShaali didn’t just write stories. He built a house for them.

An Emirati poet, novelist, and publisher, author of five poetry collections and several works of fiction. His recent works include the novel My Name is Alya and the short story collection This is My Father and Lives in Pomegranate. He was named Poet of the Year at the Sharjah Festival of Arabic Poetry in 2024, and his poetry has been translated into Spanish, Turkish, and Greek. An engineer by training, he now leads Al Hudhud Publishing Group, which he founded in 2011. AlShaali knows that action is what a writer owes the writers who come next.

What does it take to build a home for stories?

Ali AlShaali tidak hanya menulis kisah. Ia membangun rumah untuknya.

Seorang penyair, novelis, dan penerbit asal Emirat, penulis lima koleksi puisi dan beberapa karya fiksi. Karya-karya terbarunya termasuk novel My Name is Alya dan koleksi cerita pendek This is My Father and Lives in Pomegranate. Ia dinobatkan sebagai Penyair Tahun Ini di Sharjah Festival of Arabic Poetry pada 2024, dan puisinya telah diterjemahkan ke dalam bahasa Spanyol, Turki, dan Yunani. Seorang insinyur berdasarkan latar belakang pendidikannya, ia kini memimpin Al Hudhud Publishing Group, yang ia dirikan pada tahun 2011.
AlShaali percaya bahwa aksi adalah apa yang dimiliki seorang penulis untuk diberikan kepada penulis-penulis berikutnya.

Sindhunata went to the refugee camps so the rest of Indonesia couldn’t look away.

An Indonesian novelist, journalist, cultural thinker, and Jesuit priest. His landmark novel Anak Bajang Menggiring Angin, published in 1983 and now translated as Anak Bajang Herds the Wind in 2026, draws on Javanese retellings of the Ramayana to explore passion, remorse, grace, and the human struggle for meaning. As a journalist, he reported directly from the 1999 East Timor refugee crisis, publishing his account in Jembatan Air Mata. He has long edited BASIS, a Yogyakarta magazine sustaining Indonesian cultural and intellectual life since the early 1980s.
Sindhunata knows that action means going to where the story hurts the most.

What is a book that took you somewhere you couldn’t turn away from?

Sebagai jurnalis, ia melaporkan langsung dari krisis pengungsi Timor Timur pada 1999, yang dituangkannya dalam Jembatan Air Mata. Ia juga telah lama menjadi redaktur BASIS, majalah asal Yogyakarta yang menopang kehidupan budaya dan intelektual Indonesia sejak awal 1980-an. Sindhunata percaya bahwa aksi berarti mendatangi tempat di mana kisah itu paling menyakitkan.

Returning to Sydney Contemporary after a standout presentation at Photo Sydney 2025, Blender Gallery marks its 25th anniversary with an extraordinary exhibition of rare, iconic and never-before-seen photographs.

Presented as part of our 10th edition, the showcase moves beyond mass editions to focus on scarce vintage prints, unique archival images and museum-quality works that capture defining moments in music, culture and photography.

A major highlight is an exclusive presentation of works by legendary Australian photographer Gary Heery, alongside the world premiere of a new collector's book featuring his intimate photographs of Madonna.

Featuring works by renowned photographers including Mick Rock, Brian Duffy, Dominique Tarlé, Norman Seeff, Allan Tannenbaum and Michael Cooper, this is a rare opportunity to experience, and collect, some of the most influential images of the last 50 years.

See it at Sydney Contemporary, 3–6 September at Carriageworks.

Idanna Pucci didn’t just visit Bali. She let it rewrite her.

An Italian writer and cultural historian exploring social justice and cross-cultural exchange. She grew up in Florence, watching her uncle, Emilio Pucci, weave Balinese and Javanese motifs into his fashion. In 1985, she settled in Walter Spies’ former studio in Iseh, beneath Bali’s Gunung Agung volcano. Her books include The Epic of Life, on the ceiling paintings of Klungkung’s royal court of justice; The Lady of Sing Sing, her great-grandmother’s fight to save a condemned woman in 1890s New York; and The World Odyssey of a Balinese Prince, the story of her mentor, Dr. A.A. Made Djelantik. Pucci knows that empathy is what happens when a place stops being foreign and starts being home.

What’s a place that changed how you see the world?

Idanna Pucci tidak sekadar berkunjung ke Bali. Ia membiarkan Bali mengubah dirinya.

Seorang penulis dan sejarawan budaya asal Italia yang mengeksplorasi keadilan sosial dan pertukaran lintas budaya. Ia tumbuh besar di Florence, menyaksikan pamannya, Emilio Pucci, memadukan motif Bali dan Jawa ke dalam karya fesyennya. Pada 1985, ia menetap di bekas studio Walter Spies di Iseh, di kaki Gunung Agung, Bali. Buku-bukunya termasuk The Epic of Life, tentang lukisan langit-langit pengadilan kerajaan Klungkung; The Lady of Sing Sing, kisah perjuangan buyutnya menyelamatkan seorang perempuan terpidana di New York pada 1890-an; dan The World Odyssey of a Balinese Prince, kisah hidup mentornya, Dr. A.A. Made Djelantik. Pucci percaya bahwa empati adalah ketika sebuah tempat asing berubah menjadi rumah.

Tempat mana yang pernah mengubah cara pandang Anda terhadap dunia?

The Lucky Dumpling Market is back at Elder Park and it is such a fun way to spend an afternoon or evening by the river. The whole space feels festive and relaxed with colourful stalls, live entertainment, and that classic Adelaide spring energy in the air. You can smell sizzling dumplings, hear music drifting from the stage, and watch the river shimmer as you wander around deciding what to eat next.

♿️ Accessibility wise, it was fairly wheelchair friendly. The grass was not too bumpy, although there are some slightly steep spots so it is worth taking your time. It does get busy after around 5pm, so if you prefer a quieter experience and more space to move, going between 2pm and 5pm is ideal. Waitatiri wrote a children’s book. Harvard turned it into a lesson plan.

An Indonesian writer and Harvard graduate on an LPDP scholarship. As a survivor, she has dedicated part of her life to advocating against bullying. Her book The Missing Colors uses color as a metaphor for a bullied child’s emotional journey. Since 2024, it has become a free teaching resource on Harvard REACH, used by educators in the US and Indonesia alike. Her forthcoming book expands that research, examining bullying through the eyes of victims, perpetrators, and bystanders alike.
Waitatiri knows that awareness starts with realizing bullying isn’t a child’s problem. It’s ours.

What’s a story that helped you heal?

🔗 Join us this October. More details in bio.
🎟️ Early Bird Sale ends 18 August.

Get your Festival Pass before prices go up at ubudwritersfestival.com/tickets (or link in bio).

—

Waitatiri menulis buku anak. Harvard menjadikannya bahan ajar.

Seorang penulis asal Indonesia dan lulusan Harvard melalui beasiswa LPDP. Sebagai seorang penyintas, ia mendedikasikan sebagian hidupnya untuk memperjuangkan pentingnya mengatasi bullying. Bukunya, The Missing Colors, menggunakan warna sebagai metafora untuk menggambarkan perjalanan emosi seorang anak yang mengalami bullying. Sejak 2024, buku ini menjadi bahan ajar gratis di Harvard REACH, digunakan oleh para pendidik baik di Amerika Serikat maupun Indonesia. Buku terbarunya memperluas riset tersebut, membahas bullying dari sudut pandang korban, pelaku, maupun para saksi. Waitatiri percaya bahwa kesadaran dimulai dari menyadari bahwa bullying bukanlah masalah anak-anak semata. Itu adalah masalah kita semua.

Apa kisah yang pernah membantumu pulih?

🔗 Bergabunglah bersama kami bulan Oktober ini. Info lengkap di bio.

Louis Grant's new sculptures bring together blown glass, textiles and reclaimed materials in intimate sculptural arrangements.

Forms lean, hold and support one another, creating moments of connection, care and transformation. For Grant, glass is both a material and a metaphor: fluid, unstable and resistant to fixed form. These qualities become a way of exploring queer embodiment, alongside memory, vulnerability and the relationships that shape us.

Presented as part of Installations, Sydney Contemporary's program of 14 ambitious contemporary art projects transforming Carriageworks and iconic locations across Sydney, curated by José Da Silva.

Experience Installations at Sydney Contemporary, 3–6 September. Book your tickets via the link in bio.

Matthew Campbell chased the story of stolen gods across continents and their journey home.

A Canadian reporter for Bloomberg Businessweek and author of The Man Who Stole the Gods: A True Story of War, Obsession, and a Global Art Conspiracy. His previous book, Dead in the Water, co-authored with Kit Chellel, was named a Book of the Year by The Economist, the Financial Times, and The Times. Matt has reported from more than twenty-five countries on crime, corruption, terrorism, economics, public health, and the environment, earning some of journalism’s most prestigious honours.

Campbell knows that awareness starts with asking who a treasure really belongs to.

What’s a story that made you question who owns the past?

🔗 Join us this October. More details in bio.

Matthew Campbell mengejar kisah tentang dewa-dewa yang dicuri melintasi berbagai benua dan perjalanan mereka pulang.

Seorang jurnalis asal Kanada untuk Bloomberg Businessweek dan penulis The Man Who Stole the Gods: A True Story of War, Obsession, and a Global Art Conspiracy. Buku sebelumnya, Dead in the Water, ditulis bersama Kit Chellel, dinobatkan sebagai Book of the Year oleh The Economist, Financial Times, dan The Times. Matt telah meliput dari lebih dari dua puluh lima negara dengan topik kejahatan, korupsi, terorisme, ekonomi, kesehatan publik, dan lingkungan, dan karyanya telah meraih beberapa penghargaan jurnalistik paling bergengsi.

Campbell percaya bahwa kesadaran dimulai dari mempertanyakan kepada siapa sebuah harta sesungguhnya dimiliki.

Kisah apa yang pernah membuatmu mempertanyakan kepemilikan masa lalu?

Story Time - Wild Horses 2025 

After many years of hearing amazing things of this Doof and not being able to make it. Seeing that @persona___official  was on the line up and after listening to him for years and waiting for his Australian debut. I knew now was the time.. 

THE PROBLEM?
I had 2 weeks to figure out how to make this happen and get myself there, after a week of brainstorming and putting together the pieces I started coming to the realisation that this actually might not work out.. but I knew that missing out was not an option. 
I had 1 week left to make up my mind and get a move on. So while I was at work cooking up a storm. my brain was zooming with thoughts and ideas but I came to the conclusion that I will miss out on this. And as that thought came up I notice in the background a song playing… it was ( Wild Horses by Rolling Stones ) *goosebumps* 

THE SOLUTION? 
I knew in that moment exactly what I had to do, so while on break I wrote up and handed in my resignation with a week’s notice. As the week goes by the excitement builds, and on my final day I packed my belongings stacked up my car and made the move from Lismore NSW back to VIC. After 20 long hours on the road with minimal stops. With such short notice this was my first time solo at a Doof but I MADE IT! 

I was feeling very anxious and worried on how things will go though, I wasn’t sure how I will handle being alone but as I was setting up camp I was approached by my neighbours with very familiar faces that I hadn’t actually personally met yet but in that moment every little bit of worry and question on being alone instantly disappeared.

Thank you @anujktl @zionbawa and your crew for such a beautiful experience it’s such a pleasure to finally get to know you all, and Anuj your story about the time you were at a festival feeling anxious or distant from the crowd and the little  boost from that wise lil girl really touched me man 🫶 thank you deeply for your pure energy and blissful presence. You are a big part to this new door I’ve opened in life without even knowing 
 
@yaro.ck this experience is unlike any other ❤️

O No Ar Coquetel Molotov foi incrível.
E os dados de impacto do festival provam isso.

Na 25ª edição, aplicamos o Protocolo ManiFESTA! com uma operação Lixo Zero, garantindo monitoramento em tempo real e destinação correta dos resíduos.

Foram mais de 600 kg de recicláveis recuperados, fortalecendo três cooperativas parceiras, e 100% dos resíduos orgânicos enviados para compostagem, retornando ao ciclo da natureza. O que não pode ser reciclado ou compostado teve destinação correta. 

Com essa operação, evitamos a emissão de 3,47 toneladas de CO₂ e reduzimos significativamente o impacto ambiental do evento.

Sustentabilidade se faz com dados, responsabilidade e ação coletiva.

Ajen Angelina adalah seorang dosen dan penulis yang lahir di Ruteng, Nusa Tenggara Timur. Saat ini, Ajen sedang menempuh studi PhD Keperawatan di Curtin University, Perth. Sementara itu, Hamran Sunu adalah penulis asal Palopo, Sulawesi Selatan, yang kini bermukim di Makassar. Akan menarik untuk mengetahui perjalanan mereka dalam menulis, cerita-cerita yang mereka bawa, serta bagaimana pengalaman hidup membentuk cara mereka menulis.

For the first session of the Emerging Writers Programme 2026, Shelfmates will meet Ajen Angelina and Hamran Sunu, two writers with distinct backgrounds and writing journeys.

Ajen Angelina is a lecturer and writer born in Ruteng, East Nusa Tenggara. She is currently pursuing a PhD in Nursing at Curtin University in Perth. Meanwhile, Hamran Sunu is a writer from Palopo, South Sulawesi, now based in Makassar. He currently works as a freelance screenwriter and editor, and has been writing since the early 2000s.

It will be interesting to hear about their journeys as writers, the stories they bring with them, and how their life experiences have shaped the way they write.

Meet Ajen and Hamran in a live Shelf Therapy session on Discord this Wednesday.

Karuna Ezara Parikh turns the personal into the political, one page at a time.

A British-Indian author and poet whose novel The Heart Asks Pleasure First explores the forces that shape identity and belonging. Her 2021 poetry collection, Where Stories Gather, gave language to the causes closest to her, gender, secularism, and climate. An active political voice, she has spoken openly about staying present in difficult conversations, even amid backlash. Her writing has appeared in The Wire, Vogue, and Dazed.

Parikh knows that awareness starts with the questions we are willing to ask out loud.

Karuna Ezara Parikh mengubah hal personal menjadi politis, satu halaman demi satu halaman.

Penulis dan penyair asal Inggris-India ini menulis novel The Heart Asks Pleasure First, yang mengeksplorasi kekuatan-kekuatan yang membentuk identitas dan rasa memiliki. Kumpulan puisinya tahun 2021, Where Stories Gather, memberi suara pada isu-isu yang paling dekat dengannya, gender, sekularisme, dan iklim. Sebagai suara politik yang aktif, ia telah berbicara secara terbuka tentang tetap hadir dalam percakapan-percakapan sulit, bahkan di tengah kecaman. Tulisannya telah dimuat di The Wire, Vogue, dan Dazed.

Parikh percaya bahwa kesadaran dimulai dari keberanian mengajukan pertanyaan dengan lantang.

Join a masterclass with Chaitanya Srivastava, exploring how authors can build a meaningful presence online. In an increasingly crowded publishing landscape, writing the book is only one part of an author’s journey, as readers discover, discuss and connect with books and writers across a vast digital ecosystem, from TikTok and Instagram to newsletters, podcasts and long-form platforms such as Substack.

As part of Art + Dine, Sydney Contemporary’s new program bringing art, food and hospitality together across the city, Saison has collaborated with artists Reko Rennie, Ramesh Mario Nithiyendran, Michael Zavros and Joan Ross to create a series of limited-edition drinks inspired by their practices, palettes and personal tastes.

We spoke with Saison co-founder Dave Verheul about the craft behind the bottle, the natural crossover between art and hospitality, and what happens when an artist’s work becomes something you can taste.

Xu Xi is a veteran diasporic writer of Asian stories, particularly stories from Hong Kong. She has built her body of work one book at a time.

One of Hong Kong’s leading English writers and author of seventeen books, including five novels, ten prose collections, a memoir, and a co-authored textbook, having also edited four anthologies of Hong Kong writing. Her works include the novel That Man in Our Lives, the essay collection This Fish Is Fowl: Essays of Being, and The Art and Craft of Asian Stories, co-authored with Robin Hemley. Her newest title is the fiction collection Horizon: Hong Kong Selected Stories. A diehard transnational, Xu long inhabited the flight path connecting New York, Hong Kong, and New Zealand, and now divides her time between New York State and the rest of the world.

Xu knows that action means writing the seventeen books no one else was going to write.

What’s the hardest thing you’ve ever finished?

🔗 Join us this October. More details in bio.

Xu Xi adalah penulis diaspora veteran untuk cerita-cerita Asia, khususnya cerita dari Hong Kong. Dia telah membangun karya-karyanya satu buku pada satu waktu.

Salah satu penulis berbahasa Inggris terkemuka asal Hong Kong dan penulis tujuh belas buku, termasuk lima novel, sepuluh kumpulan prosa, satu memoar, dan satu buku ajar yang ditulis bersama, serta telah menyunting empat antologi tulisan Hong Kong. Xu percaya bahwa aksi berarti menulis tujuh belas buku yang tak akan ditulis oleh orang lain.

Prabal Gurung refuses to be someone else’s cautionary tale.

A Nepali-American fashion designer and author whose memoir Walk Like a Girl charts an immigrant’s journey through discrimination and reinvention. Growing up in Nepal and India, he was written off as indulging in fantasy. 

In New York, he rose through the fashion world facing relentless adversity. His memoir, released May 2025, exposes the truth beneath the glamour with brutal honesty: 95 percent hard work, 5 percent sparkle. He reclaims every insult and speaks every truth he was told to bury.

Gurung’s journey proves that action changes everything. 

What question would you ask Gurung?

Prabal Gurung menolak untuk menjadi cerita peringatan orang lain.

Seorang desainer fashion dan penulis Nepal-Amerika yang memoarnya Walk Like a Girl menggambarkan perjalanan imigran melalui diskriminasi dan reinvensi. Tumbuh besar di Nepal dan India, dia dianggap hanya memanjakan diri dengan fantasi. 

Di New York, dia bangkit melewati dunia fashion menghadapi kesulitan yang tak kenal lelah. Memoarnya, dirilis Mei 2025, mengekspos kebenaran di balik kemewahan dengan kejujuran yang brutal: 95 persen kerja keras, 5 persen kilau. Dia mengklaim kembali setiap penghinaan dan mengucapkan setiap kebenaran yang diperintahkan kepadanya untuk mengubur.

Perjalanan Gurung membuktikan bahwa tindakan mengubah segalanya.

Pertanyaan apa yang akan Anda tanyakan kepada Gurung?

Meet Louie Buana, who writes history back to life.

An Indonesian writer and history researcher at the Institute for History, Leiden University, Louie excavates the stories colonialism tried to erase. His work spans customary law, Southeast Asian maritime networks, and the lives that fell between empires.

But Louie doesn’t just publish in journals. Since 2011, he has brought the La Galigo epic to young generations through the Lontara Project, a youth community preserving this South Sulawesi treasure as a UNESCO Memory of the World.

Louie builds awareness by bringing forgotten histories to life.

What history gives you hope?
